If you like games similar to Battlefield, you will enjoy this game.  If, however, you **don't** like games like Battlefield, then you will not enjoy this game.  I do not like Battlefield, hence I do not like this game and it's why I'm giving it a thumbs down.
Pros - it's free and you absolutely cannot go wrong with that.  It plays and offers things for free that I didn't get in $60 games, so that's a good thing.  Game seems to run well (movement seems sluggish though) and I did not experience any lag, crashes, or anything like that.  Game offers three different factions you can play for along with the generic "class" of soldiers offered by most of these games nowadays (infantry/assault, medic, engineer, heavy assault, etc.).  The game seems to offer the basic garden variety gameplay (capture A, B, C wash rinse and repeat).
Cons - this is basically my issue with the game and it's the reason for the thumbs down.  The game is massive, probably the most massive game that I've played thus far in terms of the map size, players, etc. and that is either a good thing or a bad thing depending on your personal likes.  Like Battlefield, I think that is its first fault.  Sure, you can "instant action" into a bloody mess of an all out battle and probably not last 30 seconds because someone is camping and doing spawn kills or someone is hovering overhead in some gunship shooting everyone who shows up with reckless abandon.  OR you can just spawn at a normal respawn point and then spend time hoofing it across a vast expanse of land to get to the action hoping that a passing gunship (or whatever they are in this game) doesn't get you or that you don't get sniped, etc.  I had (and still do) a relatively difficult time trying to differentiate my team from the other teams (having three different factions playing at once doesn't help either).  Identifying markers don't really seem to show up until you are right on top of someone and by then, it's usually too late.  In game movement just seems sluggish (this may go back to the framerate issue I've heard about) and that's even if I dumb down the settings.  I don't like the UI and I don't like having to use in game terminals to unlock items, equip, get vehicles, etc.  I've only got about an hour and half into the game and it's enough that I want to pull my hair out already.
I could go on, but why bother?  Like I said, if you like the Battlefield series you will probably enjoy this game.  I basically just can't get  to grips with what's going on in a game of this scale and by time I do, I'm usually dead.  My idea of a good time in a game is not having to respawn every 30 seconds.  This is also one of those games where people are telling me you need to join a good team (or clan or whatever) to really have a positive experience and I simply don't have time for all of that nonsense.

Max Payne 3 is simply put, a medium quality game gone very very wrong. A game made wrong by terrible decisions all along.
For me the Max Payne 3 experience started poorly soon after installation. I had to jump into the hoop of using the Rockstar Social Club system to actually have game linked to an account on their platform. Big companies tend to do that, no one likes it because we are basically forced into it once the product is purchased, it's nothing more than abusing the consumer and very bad commercial practice. As if it wasn't enough, the "Social Club" is the source of a very well known bug sticking you into an infinite loading screen from the get go.
Despite how old the game is now on PC, it still hasn't been fixed, which is unforgivable.
The only way to actually circunvene that is to launch the game from your folder, not via Steam. So basically you purchase a game on Steam and can't use it via Steam. I'm surpised Valve hasn't settled that yet, because Rockstar by doing that prevent Steam users from using Steam service, which is a really bad thing when you're supposed to have a buisness relation.
Now, when I finally managed to make the game work, my screen is cropped with a big black zone on the right of it, and the left of the image "out of screen". So I have to fiddle with the menu blind in the hopes of managing to correct that. Which I managed to do.
Now, for an other problem, the game is in french, and I want it in english. There is no language option, so the only way to change that is to create a command file so I can enjoy the game in the language I want.
I still haven't started playing, and already ran into 4 problems, 2 of them potentially making the game unplayable. It makes me doubt if Rockstar even listened to their testers(assuming they were doing their job).
Now, for the game itself. The game is rigged with thoses unskippable cutscenes which made it famous for being a terrible thing for replay value. Some of them are actually skippable now, but guess what? Doing so have high risks of CRASHING THE GAME. Great, hey?
The game is also rigged with some weird visual effects adding a sort of blur or light effect during both cutscenes and gameplay. Thoses things serve no purpose whatsoever except making you feel nauseous or annoyed, if not both.
As for the gameplay itself, gone is the pleasure of the old Max Payne. Dive rolling into things will cause collision you take ages from recovering. You take insane damage from any source even in medium difficulty. Painkillers are scarce, nothing like the first 2 games. And the game tends to remove the ones you have for "scenaristic reasons". Because the game try to be "realist" in a game involving bullet times and a hero enduring enough pain and punishment to down an army of elephants, and take enough lead in his body to make a real size copy of the Titanic. Said game also only allows you to hold 2 handguns weapons and a big gun, instead of letting you enjoy a full inventory like the first two did. Also, Max will drop his big gun if he uses akimbo style. The game also loves to switches you to only one handgun style every time a cutscene pop up, which is almost all the time.
Basically you have to fight the game even more you're fighting the ennemies.
The game also loves to punish you for wanting to explore the level(which is a necessity for some collectibles) by giving you an automatic gameover if you take too long to do some things.
This game is basically a trudge in a swamp, it's annoying, it's slow, and it's simply not fun. Some sections are so ridiculously difficult you will have to restart them 6 to 10 times.
As for the story, well, it's basically making Max an idiot and punishing him for that, despite the fact the guy was a professional cop with a strong investigation sense. They try to cover something absolutely unbelievable by putting it on the account of Max being a drunk. Even if he's drunk and full of painkillers, I doubt he can be that oblivious. Point is, it isn't believable at all. It doesn't help the way the game is made only give you "answers" very late, despite the fact it's pretty easy to piece things.
Game is also very short, expect to finish it in less than 15 hours, and that's only if you chase every collectible, crash a lot and redo some sections a lot.
New York Minute mode has been made a terrible terrible thing. If for some reason you die in a level, you have to restart the whole level. Also cutscenes are still there and as unskipable as ever. Enjoy the same 4 minutes long cutscene mid level every time you want to play in that mode. Of course seeing the large amount of scenarised reasons to lose your game(like escort missions and such), expect to have to restart levels a lot.
I haven't even tested the multiplayer, because it's only competitive, and must be repetitive and boring.
Bottom line, it's a terrible game made by terrible people, and ported by even more terrible persons.
At least Max voice acting is good, but that's not enough to save the game. I'm a bit sad Lazlow produced that piece of garbage, he too, used to be cool. But I guess everyone needs money. At least he had fun coming to south america to supervise voice acting for the numerous brazilian pedestrians.
I bought the whole game for 7 euros at a -80% sale. I still consider for a product of such a low quality, it's far too much. 3 euros is at most, what I consider the game worth. Assuming you actually make it WORK to begin with, that is.

It's the break of dawn: July 16, 1946. Everything's gone to♥♥♥♥♥♥ The Nazi War machine is advancing at an astonishing rate. We can't catch up, our tactics are failing, outclassed and outgunned, and no-one knows why. People are getting desperate. Not me, I'm here to see an old friend and settle a score.
In July 1946, U.S. Special Forces operative William "B.J" Blazkowicz, Fergus Reid and Probst Wyatt take part on a massive raid against the fortress of Deathshead. Which serves as a giant weapon laboratory for the Nazis. The three get captured by Deathshead, and forces Blazkowicz to choose between Fergus or Wyatt. Based on your choice, Fergus or Wyatt die a horrible death. Blazkowicz and the survivor barely escape the compound, but not without injury. Blazkowicz suffers a critical head injury, which brings him into a vegetative state for fourteen years. After he wakes up from his vegetative state, the Nazis have taken over the world.
Wolfenstein: The New Order has some very fun first person shooting mechanics, making it ever so satisfying to kill waves of Nazis. You can upgrade special skill trees by doing certain tasks, this will allow you to play how you want. You can stealth your way through certain levels, which is surprisingly well done. The game has a lot of different settings, which are all very fun to play through. Based on your choice at the start of the game, Fergus or Wyatt will live throughout the game, which gives the game some replay ability. The game has sixteen chapters, which will take the average gamer around twelve hours to complete. You can carry an unlimited amount of weapons, with some you can even duel-wield. Some weapons are upgradable by finding items, like a grenade launcher to add to your machine gun.
The surprisingly good B-Movie story and likable cast of characters make Wolfenstein: The New Order really worth playing by this fact alone. The gameplay is also extremely fun, with lots of weapons to shoot some Nazis with. Even the stealth take on the game is a welcome bonus. Most levels are very linear though. And it may sometimes feel like you're on a rail. The game has a ton of replay ability  which add some extra hours to your play time. And keep shooting, stabbing, strangling Nazis.

I guess it's about time I made a review, time hasn't been on my side, sadly. Anyways what better to review than the much beloved (and hated, for some reason) Max Payne 3!
Developed by Rockstar, you immediately can see the high production values with it's astonishing graphics, effects and cutscenes which are the best I've ever seen in any game. Hair looks really good, which is strange because only like 3% of videogames do hair good (even better than Tomb Raider imo, though TR does the physics of the movement better, but in 2012 there wasn't tesselation I think...). I also need to add that this game has one of the BEST PC Ports I've had the pleasure to try out!
The attention to detail beats any other game out of the water, which surprisingly detailed papers, photos, brands and other stuff you may find in your 10-12 hour journey.
Scenarios are very varied (even though they happen in the same country: Brazil (in portuguese it's Brasil with an "S" which makes more sense to me, but english isn't my prime language so maybe it's just me)!
There are level in the Disco, night forests, day forests, abandoned factories, luxury boats, etc. etc. Which really does make the game a nicely paced gem.
Audio is just amazing, nothing there to criticize so I won't talk much about it: Voice acting is superb (as are the facial animations), so is the gun sounds and even the enemies in the middle of a gun-battle will outright say tactics (but most of the times they just curse) that most people won't understand but me, understanding portuguese as clear as pure water, had a blast listening and understanding everything without the need of subtitles, too bad it's pretty much just "Matem esse filho da♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; or &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥quot;, but oh well, it helps the player get immersed in the♥♥♥♥♥♥world Max got himself into, once again...
One part of the game I can't discuss well is the story because it's a mixed bag for me and didn't cause me a predominat feeling about it: It's filled with MANY plot holes and weird choices to tell the story, BUT at the same time it was interesting paced well enough to make me want to finish the game and still want to replay the game, though I want to replay it more for the (you guessed it):
-Gameplay! It's superb in every aspect! It's old school goodness with small - almost non-existant HUD and non-regenerating health.
Bullet-time is back and it's awesome as you would expect, because who doesn't like taking a "layed-back-beach pose" while being half-in and half-out of a shattering window while headshotting 4 guys in a matter of fractions of second? No one, that's who! :DD
Anyways, the gunplay is great, this is easily one of the best feeling 3rd Person Shooters I've had the pleasure to waste my time in! You also have collectibles which are golden gun-parts for every gun in the game, so if you callect all 3 parts, you get to use a golden gun, and HOLY♥♥♥♥♥♥ it actually looks like gold! *Eyeballs to MW3*
Besides gameplay itself, you (or most of you anyways) should be happy to know the game is hard in a good way! I played on the hardest difficulty possible at the start, finishing after 11 hours with a smile and many scars on my face while looking at the credits and thinking about the 500 or so deaths I had by the ending cutscene while smilling like a retard for accomplishing this hard as balls game.
Why is it so hard? Enemies actually know how to aim, just like a real player would, thus 1 well placed shot to the head will kill you instantly if you so much as peek outside cover during an intense firefight! Thinking fast and strategic use of your bullet time ability as well as good shot placement is key to survival!
Side note: As a portuguese, it makes me so proud that portuguese is actually in a video game! I just loved the idea of incorporating something different rather than Russian or Arab!
Oh! Almost forgot about the multiplayer! - It's♥♥♥♥♥♥ Moving. Right. Along!
Overall, I think pretty much everything is covered... except the fan's reactions, which are... somewhat dumb, mainly due to the lack of reasons for their criticism, just because it "lost" the noir, when it should! Max Payne is a broken man, in his shoes, the last thing I'd do was to stay in that sh*thole of an apartment and waiting for death to slowly take me...
Also, how is Max a bad character that ♥♥♥♥♥es all the time? He's been through a lot, everyone like that is supposed to be (and feel) miserable! His everything died, so I don't think he should be watching family guy in a party-hat for a living, so I guess the painkiller and alcohol addiction makes sense and add a nice deep characterization to Max that the first 2 games missed completely!
Nevertheless, the game is pretty much flawless, except Rockstar's Social Club DRM, which still requires online log-in to play the single-player, which is bullsh*t! And the worst is that it will only log-in if it's in a good mood, otherwise, you'll have to play something else. It's weird that companies still add these DRM's to their games that no one ♥♥♥♥ing asked for in the first place! And for what? Stats? I can live without them, don't worry because I won't lose any sleeping hours because your DRM didn't count the amount of ♥♥♥♥ing painkillers I took in a mission! So, thank you but no thank you, RockStar, Ubisoft, Microsoft, ...
Also, the story, while interesting enough to elevate in in most shooters (which have bland stories most of the time), it has more (plot) holes than a slice of swiss cheese! Not as inconsistent as Sleeping Dogs, for example, thankfully enough!
9/10 sounds about right, buy it below 30€, the collectibles and the great gameplay are good enough to make you want to replay it again, thus making it more worthwhile at a higher pricetag of 30€!

Max Payne 3 is a well-crafted, worthy successor to the series. The aspect I found most enjoyable was the gunplay - bullets felt like they had a lot of force to them, and on hard difficulty or above, good aim is absolutely vital to getting through the game. Most of your enemies aren't very resilient - but neither are you, and this lets a skilled player perform extremely satisfying maneouvers. In a fun way, the imminence of death and the quick repeatability of many scenes reminded me of Hotline Miami, another game which I also loved for being fast-paced and brutal.
It is also worth mentioning that although cover is important in many areas, you can also get through many situations by being full-on aggressive. The AI is very finely tuned, and will often try to charge you when you hide in the same spot for too long; it also sports very good aim, but reacts humanly to you pulling sudden moves.
The writing fumbles here and there - it seems everyone is "leading an army" - but it succeeds at being unpredictable on several memorable occasions.
I would recommend this game to anyone looking for a solid, challenging experience backed up by a good story.

Good shooting action, cool weapons, and the reincarnation of BJ Blaskowitz was well done.  Lots of things to look for, some fun "easter eggs", and two different main story lines depending on a choice you have to make early on, which is a crappy choice to have to make in the story line, but there it is.  There is some fairly explicit sex in the game, about which I don't recall seeing any prior warnings, so beware if you have issues with that sort of thing, and/or if you have younger kids who might want to play this game.  Otherwise you'll get to answer the "Daddy, what are they doing?" question.  :)
Technically, there are a lot of problems .  I have a top of the line Alienware machine with two GPU's and my system checks out perfectly using Dell's diagnostics, but the rendering in the cut-scenes, of which there are many, was simply awful.  Weird colors, people with hundreds of little colored lights on their heads, weird shapes extending from NPC's to the ground as they move, many NPC's rendered without bodies, just clothes and eyes...or sometimes just disembodied heads.  The soundtrack in the cut scenes rarely matches the scene on screen. Since many key elements of the story occur in these scenes, it takes away a great deal from enjoyment of the tale.  Also, on a PC you'll have to disable V-sync just to get the game to run at an acceptable frame rate.
If you play at anything but lowest difficulty, you will die a lot; we're used to that in FPS games, but the game uses the ported-from-consoles auto-save system and you can't save the game on your own.  That is tolerable if reloads take a reasonable time, but in this case, reloads take way too long, in some cases as long as three minutes--and again, this is on a very high-end system.  The time wasted on reloads was unacceptable.
As a big fan of the Splinter Cell, Hitman and Deus Ex series, I appreciated the attempt to insert real stealth action opportunities into a more or less standard over-the-top shooter, but the execution left a lot to be desired.  There is no way to hide bodies, and I suppose the developers decided to make up for that by making the enemy NPC's totally stupid or blind or both.  You can pick off an enemy commander from a distance with a silenced pistol or knife throw (and you REALLY want to kill the commanders ASAP, since as long as they live the enemy keeps spawning more reinforcements) and leave his body lying in the middle of a room or walkway.  No problem; other enemies will walk right past the body without batting an eye.  The same goes for close-up takedowns with the knife--just leave the body out in the open, because nobody will notice it.  I appreciate the fact that ralism often has to give way to making a game playable, but if you're going to "do stealth", you need to do it with at least some semblance of reality.  Also, there is no "radar" to keep track of enemies, and the lean-from-cover system is decent but not great, so you often end up getting spotted and having people shooting you, doing real damage, without having any idea where they are, since there also is no system for indicating the direction of enemy fire.  You can very easily end up dead (and awaiting an endless reload) before you have a clue where the enemy fire was coming from.
Last but not least, this game is touted for its story.  The premise is very interesting--resistance fighters against the evil Nazi Reich after they have managed to win World War II (although exactly how they did this is never explained very well, just some hints here and there; history buffs will be disappointed in that, as I was.)  And throughout most of the game, the story holds up pretty well.  There are numerous newspaper and magazine clippings scattered around that help to describe what the world is like under the Nazis in 1960, and the developers did a nice job with the visuals in that regard, especially in London.  But not to put too fine a point on it, the ending absolutely, completely stinks.  It ruined the entire experience for me.  I won't do an outright spoiler here, although I am sorely tempted, but I've never liked this kind of ending to a story, and unfortunately there are a fair number of writers out there who love to perpetrate this kind of crap on their audiences.  Some people think it makes for great art, or something, but I strongly disagree.   I won't go any further on that point as it would reveal more than I want to about what actually happens.
Overall I would rate this game around 5 on a scale of 10, just for the quality of the shooting action and the variety of weapons.

Probably the most infuriating FPS game in my library.
1. No balance in mercs. At all. Play around for a few hours and you'll find there are no counters to any merc's special ability, like Fletcher's atom bombs (sticky bombs on the ground that usually one shot.) or Skyhammer's air raid (he calls bombs from the sky). Did I mention Kira's orbital laser (laser of death from the sky that can be controlled)
1.5 No balance in maps. It's either extremely defense sided or offense. No in between. The only way to get around this, of course, is to stack levels.
1.C Did I mention players can take control of turrets and shoot at you from out of sight and deal high damage before you realize you're being shot at? Fun stuff.

2. No ranked, not even casual. The average casual game: Your team all single digit level players, enemy team all double-triple digits. There is no segregation of newbs and seasoned vets, and that sucks eggs. There's the option to call a vote to shuffle based on skill, but what team crushing would vote yes on that?
3. Yes, shut up, it is pay to win. The best mercs all cost cash. "But wait!" You say. "You can buy them with in game credits!" 50,000 in game credits. The average 20 minute game yields about 200 credits. "But wait!" You say. "There's a free rotation of three different mercs!" This does more harm than good. For one, you get just a crap ton of the mercs in each game with no diversity on your team. If an OP merc is in the rotation, good luck having fun during a game against 6 naders or 5 fletchers and a pheonix.
4. The loadout cards make no sense. Each merc has cards as loadouts. You pick one before you start a game and you're forced with it. Cards have a variety of weapons and augments (abilities like 66% faster health recharge or such). You can't mix and match. If you really like a shotgun on one card but hate the pistol for a merc, you're stuck with it. Also, the cards are earned very slowly through grinding for case drops. The cards are tiered so of course, you're stuck with the crap cards unless you want to buy higher ones. Higher ones have the same weapons but more augments (up to 3). If you're lucky, you'll get a decent card. If you're tremendously fortunate, you'll get a card for a merc you ACTUALLY OWN.
If the game had balance and a decent loadout system it could be actually fun. It has some decent things going for it, like nice aesthetic, interesting movement, a non-garbage secondary objective system, and a way to revive dead teammates.
But don't take it from me, try it yourself and form your own opinion.

So Max Payne is back - I know it's been a while, but I never got around to playing this. So bear with me.
Max, Max, Max... I never really forgave you for the fact that your face had changed. With Sam Rivers inspiring the first model in the opus that started it all, one really got the feel for a skinny, slighty damaged look that was beautifully topped off by Johnny Knoxville's eyes (could not be unseen). A determined look, needless to say. Then, for the encore, the noir feel was just about still there - but you just beefed up all of a sudden! You stopped being those damaged good running on painkillers and booze and became yet another Bogart-type who had a seemingly unlimited resistance to booze and pills. Now you pull this Walter White act? Breaking Bad fans will appreciate. Nonetheless, you looked like a hard piece of work, you were vicious and determined and you blamed yourself for everything (seriously? They barely managed to get away from you as it is - good thing they all had armies at thier disposal). So when faced with those odds, you just straight up owned the lot of them. There's only so much a man can do: the self-loathing was a bit much. That Panama ♥♥♥♥-up could have been avoided if you hadn't been boozing, though.
Handling was a bit weird. It took some time to get used to, but in the end, worked a charm (what I mean is that I had to get used to not jumping with SPACE - it began to get detrimental to your cause very quickly), but I can't complain about that.
What I will complain about is the laser sight being a handicap to shooting. It stripped my crosshairs away and left me with a strobe effect. You end up avoiding weapons with those attachments because... Well you're already a drunk, I don't want to put you on an Parkinson's watchlist, do I? Other than that, it's still the head-shot bullet fest it's always been. And I love it.
The scenery was beautiful. As much as I liked what I saw, what I heard was even better. I played with subtitles on, thinking that if I play with portugese voices, I'll want to understand what they're calling and just exactly *what* lewd acts they engaged in with my mother. But no: no translation in the subtitles. It made me feel like a goddamned tourist and it was a gorgeous spin. Amazing. Now I can insult my portugese co-workers. You really get the feel for how much trouble you're in by making feeling for everyone you can understand: I was actually glad I didn't speak the language. While it didn't share the same atmosphere as its predecessors, I still enjoyed all nine hours of the time it took me to complete on Hard.

Have to say that I was extremely disappointed with this game.  I immediately loaded up on the "uber" difficulty... and felt like I had accidentally put it on "daddy, can I play?" difficulty.  This game provided no challenge at all for me, and maybe it would have gotten better later on, in that regard at least, but I'll never know.
The game fairly early on forces you to make a decision.  Normally I like this.  It adds to the feeling of your actions having meaning in the game.  The issue is the choice and that you are FORCED to make it.
************SPOILERS****************
You have to choose between two of your allies on who lives or who dies.  If you refuse to make the choice everybody dies and the game reloads at the point where you are told to choose.
**********end spoilers*******
I despise this and refuse to choose who lives and dies, thus my time with this game is done.  I would have put in a random choice generator for people who refuse to choose so that the game could progress without feeling like I killed an ally and friend.
On the other hand, the portions of the game that I did play were very good looking.  I like the fact that I didn't feel like I was walking through the same hallway over and over again.  That is, unfortunately, the only positive I have for this game.  If you don't mind making those choices and playing a game that you can almost litterally walk through on the hardest difficulty then you might give it a shot; just definitely not for sixty dollars, and I feel like I wasted my money even though I got it on sale for half that.  I give it 3/10.

This game reminded me of the time when I still liked shooters. They just don't make 'em like this anymore. You can expect a solid 15 hours of gameplay (give or take up to 5 depending on your playing speed) for your first playthrough, that said the game makes itself replayable by having a choice in the first level which will slightly alter the gameplay and minorly affect possible routes you can go in levels. It's not much, but it's enough to give you an excuse to spend another 15 hours on it when you're bored some months (or years) after your first completion (or if you are just starving for more after you finish the game).
My only problems with the game were performance issues, I have a pretty high end machine but it seems that the game is very poorly optimized, for example it does not support triple buffering (so one of my major performance issues was that my framerate was jumping between 15/30/60 all the time when Vsync was enabled, the solution is to disable Vsync in the game options and to force Vsync with triple buffering on in your graphics drivers. Blame iD Software for this one.) And it also seems to have some caching issues. Load times between deaths can get extremely long as well (up to more than a full minute) but after dying an X amount of times in the same spot (2 or 3 times) it seems the game starts to load it faster. Don't ask me why.
Besides the performance issues, the game was great all around, from the gameplay to the story, and even the characters. I also loved the entire soundtrack. The protagonist was your typical classic FPS type (like you'd expect from Wolfenstein or Doom games) which was kindof a nice kick in the nostalgia. It's an oldschool game making use of the capabilities of modern game development tools. A must play if you are or ever were a fan of shooters.

I am a big fan of the ex-Starbreeze guys, but something is missing from Wolfenstein that keeps it from being a strong GOTY contender. The technical problems on PC when trying to activate basic functionality like MSAA were a big hassle, but more importantly, the old school teleportation solution to transitioning between levels felt really detrimental to the experience of playing the game.
For example the much hyped train story sequence - it looked really impressive in preview videos, but in the actual game the sequence felt crammed in between two levels. They tried to create an oppressive world, but the constant teleportation between story sequences and geographically distant locations (even using ridiculous stealth helicopters) made it really hard to immerse yourself in the world and feel the oppression.
I mean, imagine how effective that train sequence would have been if it had been preceded by escaping the military checkpoint of the previous level, hiding with a fake identity among other civilians, presenting forged paperwork to get on the train and getting to explore the train as a detailed location. All of this while being paranoid about being detected and with various stealth gameplay elements to make it possible to actually be detected. But instead of doing this, the game just cuts to the story sequence in question, which completely lacks tension as a result ...
Many of the levels that you "teleport" to could have been edited to be physically connected to the resistance headquarters hub, which would have required some effort from the developer, but would have vastly improved the immersion into the game world. Exploring the secret tunnels around the resistance headquarters in some short missions was a really fun experience, and I just wish that the developer had made more of an effort to facilitate that kind of connectedness between the hub and all the missions in the game.

This is what happened the very first time i played this game:
The first time i played this game i had a basic old gaming laptop, so i couldnt play very well.... still, i decided that i should give it a try. on my first 15 mins i tried all races, a little bit of that and so on. when i finally decided to play NC, i joined in the defence of a base far to the northeast. little did i know then that the TR wanted that pass....badly, but the mayority of the NC decided to move to juicier grounds.
here i was, in this outpost overlooking a massive desert, with bare minimum defenders. suddenly i realize some weird objects on the distance. being a complete noob at the time all i could tell is that it was some sort of tank, maybe and some oversized schoobuses.
I looked back at the base and saw multiple cannons, that looked perfectly suitable to deal with the threat at hand. i was just waiting for them to move ahead and get in range. little by little though, those "easily countered" tanks started to multiply.
it took less than 5 minutes for my situation to change from manageable to♥♥♥♥♥♥hit the fan. whoever the commander was at that time decided it was time to assault the fortress, and so, over 20 tanks, several schoobuses and a multitude of fighters started bombarding the base relentlessly.... in mere seconds all those magnificent turrets and defences that made me feel safe melted. what i thought were engineers at the time were working hard to keep the defences up but to no success. soldiers kept dying left and right from this relentless bombardment, missiles were shot in the air attemping to shoot down enemy fighters dogfighting with the ocasional air support. Enemy firghters in return would rain hell on any solder unlucky enough to be caught outside. all we could do was hope for reinforcements.
After a few minutes, enemy troops started to pour in from the left, in a massive attempt to destroy the shield generators and allow their overwhelming number of tanks into the installation. we fought tooth and nail, but we knew this was a battle we could not win...
then, out of nowhere, NC fighters retook the skies, not long after, a long line of armored vehicles started rolling in from the outpost behind us, pushing back the enemy forces. We held the fort.
after this i turned around, grabed my cellphone, and started to look for a new pc. while i played.
No matter what, if youre a PC player, you should at least try to play this game a couple hours. this is one of those games that you should try at least once in your gaming life. and be sure to play it with a clan or something.

Since steam sale late autumn last year I've been playing Max Payne 3. First I focussed on the single player. The story is intense and keeps you hanging during your first playthrough. I found it most annoying to have to see cutscenes even more than actual gameplay but like I said, the story is both interesting and intriguing.
Max Payne is an anti hero that easily fits for your imagination. Having lost all that's dear to you, I would do the same as he probably. His weaknesses, pills and booz, are kind of cool. In fact, Max is telling you a story, and while he does you may take his place in heavy shooting action. Whether you're on a boat, deep in the jungle, in the Favella or breaking out a cellblock in the local police station, you'll always find yourself between a massive amount of bad guys, that all have their looks and appearances as if they just walked out of the real life to act in your computer game.
Shooting these fine gentlemen is what's the basic point in the game. And Max has his adrenalin loaked soul set to be the top shooter, which grands you so called bullet time and shoot-dodge abilities. Time will slow down while you can still aim and shoot on your own time. If you get good at this, you'll feel like Max himself and every new group of enemies is another rush of joy through your connected brains ;)
I completed the entire story numerous times, enough to get all the most difficult challenges and achievements. The hardest are to collect i nthe arcade section of the game. You can play seperated levels with differetn goals. New York Minute is the most challenging. You have to complete a level with just one minute on your watch. Killing enemies will add time, but if you die, you loose. Once you complete all you can do a "One Hot Minute Harcore". That is the entire playthrough, with the same principles. On quite a hard difficulty level. So, no dying, not even once, an entire playthrough. I managed to do that after a few weeks of practicing. One of the hardest achievements I've accomplished in my gaming histiry so far :)
Now I'm playing multiplayer. A bit less then I'd hoped for. Rockstar has designed a great way to use bullet time in a multiplayer setting. If you get used to it and learn the game mechanics how this will appear to other players, you can sure get advantage out of it, but the game remains fair. The multiplayer maps are all story related. The choice is huge. The graphics and gameplay are good. The problem though with the multiplayer is there's not enough players online. And the pistols are over-powered. You can easily shoot everything to shreds with a dual wield pistol loadout. They are much more powerful than a machinegun. But, if you like to use assault or precicion weapons, you can make advantage of your distance. Pistols have limited range so it's possible to get an answer to those running maniacs with their dual wield murdermachines.
There are cheaters though. Some people seem to always have an advantage of a second or so, and they have a kill-death ratio that can't be explained with just good gaming. I'm no sore loser but I'm quite sure there's guys who use certain cheats to always get on top. Too bad.
Many people are negative about the MP but I do like it. Could have been better but it's good playable and very entertaining.
The graphics in the game are overall incredible. So damn realistic, and now that I'm using my new GTX780 it's even better. The detail and the realistic design are outstanding. I can easily say I haven't seen beter so far. That's not too difficult of course with a game that only loads quite small corridors, but then again they pushed everything to the max.
All in all I'd give this game a
for sure! The graphics, the joy, the realistic design and excellent story make this game to the best single player game I've been playing the last few years. The multiplayer could have been better, but without cheaters and with more ppl online, it would be defenitely worth a try or two, or more :)

There are really only two gripes I have about this game, and one of them is purely just me being not-so-good at multiplayer games. One is the absolutely ridiculous download size (32gb! no joke) and the multiplayer is a bit on the difficult side. Other than those two things, this is probably my favorite game in the series. I own all of the Max Payne games, and I've played through 1 and most of 2 and 3.
This game has some incredible atmosphere, watching cutscenes feels like I'm watching a movie, even with graphics on low because I had some trouble running this game. The places you visit and walk through feel like people actually live and work there, or just go there to have a great time. And the characters are all distinct from what I've seen so far. And Max is really something in this game. Some people may say he's a bit whiny and although that's true, I can't help but to like him and want to help him. He's a character I actually care about, and there's only a few video game characters I can say that about.
If you've ever complained about a game being too short, you will not have that complaint with this game. I've put what I felt to be quite a bit of time into this game (around 8 hours at time of writing, I believe) and I'm only in like Act 2! All of the acts are very distinguished though, and they have a great transformation that follows Max and what few people he interacts with that survive through this whole situation. The story is somewhat confusing if you play in bits and pieces like I do, but it is good, just pay attention.
The gunplay is solid and all, but it is a little wierd to get used to with a keypad, but that's my thing. The inventory system is refreshing in a way, mainly because of the direction the rest of the game is taking. The whole game has this feel of all of this is actually happening in real life, whereas the first two games had less of that. Max can hold two one handed guns in holsters and one rifle. But if you dual wield the two one handed you drop your rifle because your hands are full. And it makes sense, but it's a little wierd at first.
One more thing, and I feel this should be said, because it will affect some people. Violence in video games is always controversial, and I am always a fan of video games that are violent. But remember when I said this game is more 'real'? The violence feels that way, and it may just be me, but when you shoot people, its a lot different from other games. The impact looks real, and they just drop. Blood spray and splatter matches it, and blood pools make you track footprints and such. I guess for a long story short, its a very violent game, but in a more realistic fashion. And this can turn people away, because some people are very particular about this stuff. I only mention it because if you really take the time to watch it and notice the things like that, it's slightly disturbing.
I have to hand it to Rockstar Games for making such a great end to a trilogy. If you want a great third person shooter, or just love Max Payne, you should definetly pick this game up. It's well worth it.

I'm glad I didn't pay the full retail price for it when it came out. It's a pretty average shooter and it's console heritage really shows, particularly with the over-reliance on sticky cover (something that is a big departure from the previous 2 Max Payne titles, and not an improvement - gone are the elegant bullet time gun battles, replaced with sticking behind some cover, hitting bullet time and picking off enemies, rinse/repeat).
The story is pretty mediocre and brazenly telegraphs the major plot points if you are paying attention and the cut scenes, especially the infuriating visual effects, are headache inducing. Which is too bad because this game seems to have equal time cut-scenes and then shooting gallery levels.
I was actually baffled at the really high review scores this game achieved, but then upon reflection I suppose it's because of the fact that there have been very few good story based shooter to ever appear on a console, so in that light, I suppose it's definately one of the better ones.
Anyway, the game is decent value for money at the super sale price, but otherwise it's pretty forgettable. I find it marginally more entertaining than the Deus Ex remake, which I got bored with and never completed. If anything, this game made me go and purchase the Max Payne 1 and 2 bundle so I could replay Max Payne 2, which is seriously a better game than this one, despite it's obviously old technology.
Why does it seem that every "modern" remake of a classic FPS franchise seems to fall on a scale of "terrible" to "mediocre"? I'm not really saying this is a bad game, just that it's not a particularly stand-out one.

TL;DR: Definitely worth trying if you like massive FPS battles.
The game itself looks fairly good. Graphics are not breathtaking, but they do not feel rigid or clunky in any way.
Considering the amount of players, gunshots, explosions and stuff in your vicinity the frame rate is very solid.
I am running the game on med settings and have a steady 30-40fps.
My specs for comparison:
AMD Phenom II X4 955 @3.2Ghz
Nvidia GeForce GTX 660 2GB (Zotac? Not sure after all those years)
12GB RAM
Windows 10
Anyway, first a few words about the gameplay and stuff.
There are 4 continents in total on each server.
On each continent, there are 3 factions fighting each other. The goal of each faction is to conquer the whole continent.
Easier said than done if the whole map is as big as your mum's left♥♥♥♥♥♥cheek.
Usually there are 2-3 big fights going on at each faction-front. Your faction might be about to take a factory from Faction Blue (Forgot the faction names), while at the same time you are losing an outpost to Faction Purple.
So technically all people on one server are not directly fighting each other. Though, if you happen to participate in a big offensive, the scale of the battle is immense.
If one faction happens to actually conquer a whole continent, said continent is locked for some time and you have to switch to a different continent to conquer it.
Actually conquering a continent can take a few hours, but usually its days or weeks, sometimes even months. It basically is a constant back and forth of the frontline.
The best part: It is not Pay2Win at all.
You may buy ingame currency for actual money, with which you can unlock new weapons and stuff, but all weapons are somewhat balanced and no gun has a big advantage over another one.
There are a few DLC out there that include guns that you cannot unlock by just playing as far as I know (Might be wrong on this one), but those guns are not OP in any way.
Anyway, all in all I'd give it a 8/10 because I love huge, smooth battles, and since even if you have a small squad of people you can actually have a big impact on the frontline since teamwork is far superior over sheer numbers.
Only thing I dislike to some extent is the levelling system.
I actually like the 'level up to get different (maybe better) guns'-approach. That way there is a motivation to rank up and it feels more rewarding.
The current system works like this:
'Play, gain credits, and unlock whatever gun you like.'
But that is a minor thing, so definitely a recommendation on this great game.

To start off, Max Payne 3 is a game that may not be the most graphically beautiful game on the market, but it's one of the most detailed. The game really shines when you stop and look at all the small things around you. While this isn't prevalent on lower display settings, on medium up, the little things start to shine. Noting that I'm only 2 hours into the game, what I can say is that if you're on the market for an all out shooter with minimal cutscene time, sorry, but this isn't the game for you unfortunately. Combat in this game is amazing, fluid and needlessly brutal, which given the atmosphere, gives a huge boost to the overall performance and feel of the game. This game is heavily a story based game, with the majority of the game using cutscenes as a transitional scene, instead of running from point A to B (at times) which works to it's strengths and weaknesses. There's a decent amount to go back to, looking ahead, as there's an additional 2 difficulty levels that can be unlocked on beating the game on hard, and the difficulty unlock from beating that. And on top of that, there's a multiplayer component. I'm not able to say much about that as of yet, but I've heard several good things about it. With collectibles, a powerful story and brutally amazing combat, Max Payne 3 is quickly becoming one of my most loved games. If you're not into excessive brutality, or a majority of a game being cutscenes and the 30GB download, I would warn you about this, but if you don't mind the listed, I cannot recommend the game enough (especially how the game is on a nice sale at the time of this posting)

Despite a lot of criticisms, I found Max Payne 3 to be a very enjoyable game. You take control of Max Payne a retired cop who is fighting the depression for the loss of his wife and daughter. Also fighting his addiction to alchohol and pain killers. In the game Max Payne is a body guard for a rich family, that forces Max to find their daughter after being taken by terrorists.
The things i loved about the game were of course the iconic bullet-time feature that allows Max to leap through the air in slow motion and kill enemies at the same time. Which never gets old. Also I loved the difficulty of the game. The game is suprisingly really hard. You could be killed with one bullet depending on where you get hit. The script was another thing that I loved, there are so many awesome phrases and one-liners in this game.
The things I disliked was the story, I felt it was a pretty generic action movie storyline. Also the game doesn't have much replay value. The only thing that would make you replay the levels was to find all the golden weapon parts to get golden guns.
Overall it's a very fun and action packed game, I recommend giving it a try, especially with the Rockstar sale going on at the time. Give it a try.

There is no other game that offer's such large scale battles in a never ending war.
Where you, your platoon and many other players can be deffending a base against 2 other factions consisting of hundreds and hundreds of players each. Attacking with a wide variety of armoured vehicles, aircraft and Infantry. One soldier can make a big difference if he knows what he's doing.
You can have a massive dog fight going on overhead battling for conrol of the skies allowing their galaxy (Troop dropships)  to reinforce their team below. Hundreds of infantry fighting for control for individual buildings, in some cases one faction will have the top floor and the other the bottom, being bombarded by armoured convoys / blockades as each faction battles it out for control of the roads to support (Or farm) the capture of a base.
You can have intense squad Vs Squad battles for a base that will grow into a full on war, going from 15-20 players to 90+ on either side as your team comes to aid the capture or deffence.
It accommmodates the whole range of warfare be it you like to be a sniper or get up close and personal with a shotgun, ace fighter pilot to ground pounding bomber, tanker to logistics.
Yes it has "Zerging" issues where 2-3 rivaling forces meet at a fix point and battle it out for hours on end with it only moving on when one side looses aload of players from boredom of fighting in the same area - Or one force just dwarfes the other in size of numbers just stomping over anything and everything that they come into contanct with.
There are also copy & paste bases, facilities & buildings but I personally don't mind it so much. There is still a vast array of bases that are completely different from one another and it aids in PC performance.

Yes, Skillbasedness isn't a bad thing, but too much skillbasedness is. A single skilled player
can effectively take out an entire 8-mediocre-player-team on his own, luck can help you
injure them, but killing them requires about the same amount of skill. This is mainly due to the
other points a problem.
- ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Spawnsystem.
Respawning becomes available in regular intervals, which depends on the Size of your team
(eg. 10 seconds in 2-player-team, 30 seconds in 8-player-team (not precise values)).
"That doesn't sound so bad" you might say, "you spawn as a group instead of alone".
Yes, the idea is not bad, but the implementation is ♥♥♥♥ed. Wether you die now or half a second
later decides about if you can respawn instantly or have to wait half a minute, and some
♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s find our your teams respawn cycle and always kill you just as the cycle starts anew,
giving you the maximum respawn time every time.
There also is no Spawn protection, which makes a ♥♥♥♥ed match even more ♥♥♥♥ed, when you
FINALLY spawn and the entire group gets killed by spawncampers.
So the effective playtime in a 15-minute match that is lost by minute 3 is about 20 seconds.
Total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t and a pretty common occurance.
- Massive merc balance issues (at least I think so).
Some might disagree with me on this, but this game has massive balance issues regarding the
weapons and skills of the characters. Snipers for exsample are for my taste way too strong
(I hate snipers anyways), and a single skilled player can take basicly everyone out from afar.
And if you manage to play Sparks properly, you pretty much already won the game.
- And finally the biggest issue, the one everyone knows about: Team balancing.
In combination with the skillbasedness: Absolute bull-♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥
This has been around for ages, too, but despite all the complains SplashDamage does
NOTHING to fix it.
Remember how I complained about DB being too skillbased? Yeah, the game doesnt at all
balance the teams, it just adds the joining players. That's why you will quite often end up in a
7-player-team with an average level of 15, highest level of 23 and lowest of 11, VS a
8-player-team with an average level of 40, highest level of 80 and lowest of 20.
Leave game and find another? Yeah right, joining running matches always results in joining the
losing side of a match that was like the one just described.
Particularry annoying when you need to defend an objective: the attackers can attack for 15
minutes, you have to defend for 15 minutes, if you dont manage to, the games to 1/3 lost.
So what does the game decide, put the Lvl 50 guy who just joined into the 2-player-attackers

attacker joins.

negative fun on losing side, mediocre fun on winning side.
And the solution? "Shuffle Team"-votes. These effectively give everyone a 50/50 chance to be
in the winning team after the vote passed and the teams were shuffled, since balance is not
possible, causing the majority of all games to escalate into ShuffleTeamVotes until the
4-minute-mark prevents you from doing so.

First off, if you've ever played battlefield and/or destiny then you will enjoy this game.
In PS2, you fight representing one of the three factions; Terran Republic (TR), New Conglomerate (NC) or Vanu Sovereignty (VS). Each faction has it's own distinct weapons, Main Battle Tanks (MBTs) and Main Air Fighters (MAFs). If you prefer high damage with above-average fire rate, I suggest you join TR. VS features a faster fire rate with medium damage, and NC weapons are focused around shotguns with lower rates of fire.
The planet you fight on, Auraxis, has four continents; Esamir, Hossin, Indar, and Amerish. Two new continents called Searhus and Oshur are planned to be added in a future update, with Searhus being a large volcanic map and Oshur a highly-destructible environment map. Additionally, there is a "beginners only" continent called Koltyr if you are not ready to head into the real-deal.
These continents have many "regions" or bases that you must defend or take. Taking a region will move you one step over to conquering the continent, and your faction will be rewarded with a benefit for a limited time. The more regions you capture, the higher amount of Victory Points (VP) your faction will have. Additionally, there are tasks such as "Capture 3 Biolabs to gain 3 VP" that will help you in your quest to success.
Overall, Planetside 2 is an immersive fps with stunning graphics and amazing landscapes. You can fight together with your comrades and Zerg base after base, or act sneaky-beaky like and stealth-cap bases as an Infiltrator. The race of who caps the continent first is ultimately in the hands of your factions' communication's skills and your cooperation.

I always wanted a game where you could customize every aspect of your robot with trade-offs, advantages, and disadvantages. The closest I got before was Armored Core, but there wasn't exactly a bustling online community for that game, which means it never presented me with the opportunity to fight my customized thing against other people's customized things.
In Robocraft, you can make planes, tanks, cars, mechs, blimps, wall-climbing spider-bots, and even crazy combinations of any of those. You can equip lasers, rail guns, plasma launchers, gatling guns, lock-on missiles, flak guns, and so on. Then you've got modules that let you go invisible, blink teleport, or emit an EMP blast. The amount of customization allowed by all of this is staggering, and with few exceptions, there's no single right way to use any of them effectively.
You build your bot using a bunch of blocks and parts that drop while playing and, like Hearthstone, you can break down old parts into pile of dust (called Robits) that you can then forge new items out of if you want something specific. While building, you'll have a certain amount of CPU pFLOPS which is basically the game's balance juice to make sure that you can't make anything overpowered. Depending on what parts you use, and how many, you can fine-tune your speed, health, and damage output.  Then you can launch into the default Battle Arena objective-based mode or an old-fashioned Team Deathmatch. There's a great amount of strategy both during the build phase and in the middle of a match, and somehow there's enough depth to make me stick with this game for well over two years. The last time I did that was Halo 2 back in the mid-00s.

Getting ready for another playtrough, this time on old school difficutly. I thought to myself; I think I should write a review, because I am truly in love with this game!
I have seen many complaints about this game being a "railshooter with 90% cutscenes". Yes there are a lot of cutscenes and atrocious loading times. In your first playtrough these load times don't really matter because they are covered up with pre-rendered cutscenes important to the story and this leads me to...
* Minor spoilers
(and my English isn't that good)
The story:
You are Max Payne. A middle aged drunk that escaped New Jersey in fear of retribution after killing the son of a mob boss. A friend -Passos- Get's you a job in Brazil, working as a body guard, protecting a rich Brazillian business man and his socialite wife. The lower class gangs living in the slums see the opportunity to kiddnap the wife for a ransom. But things go way deeper. Corrupt politicians, corrupt cops and people dissapering from the slums.And in the centre Max payne.
The best moment in the story is when Max realizes that the alcohol and pills are clouding his judgement. He quits cold turkey, shaves his head, dons a Hawaian shirt and takes off to safe the girl and find the truth about him really being there.
The gameplay:
The gunplay and bullet time is smooth. The game punishes you for bad aiming. You health goes down quickly (on harder settings and I recommend playing it on hard). Headshots are the way to go. They are instant kills on most enemies.
Like I said. The game can be hard. The times of spamming bullet time and shooting up a room, leaving you untouched is over. Use cover and use your bullet time for the harder parts. There are some goodies to pick up, but the game is pretty linear.
Graphics:
First of all, once again... The load times are awful. Switching from a low res pre-rendered cut scene to the pretty graphics of the ingame engine. I have a decent rig and the game runs smoothly for me on it's hights settings on a resolution of 1920X1080. The textures are sharp and the enviorments detailed. It is almost a shame this game is so linear because you really feel like exploring.
Max's jacket moves like a jacket should and details, like sweat dripping from max's face are done beautifully and are done just enough to let you appreciate the effort.
One thing that bothers me is the flashy.. uhm static? popping up and the the text popping up (watch some video's on youtube, you will understand what I mean). I wish I could turn it off. Sure I understand why they put it in, but it doesn't really work for me.
The facial animotions are what we would expect from rockstar. They compliment both the visuals and the voice acting.
And the voice acting... it is some of the best I have heard in a while. The actor playing Max Payne gives a believable performance and is riddled with little details. I would have bought the game, just to listen to his voice.
Multiplayer:
I have tried MP and I had fun. But I am not a MP kinda guy. From what I have seen; the servers are a bit empty, so it takes a while to get in. If more people played, I would too.
Verdict:
If you like shooting and a good story. Buy it. 10/10

Max Payne 3 can be summarized in one sentence: Shooting Brazilian gang members and paramilitary forces with the use of slow motion and John Woo's Hard Boiled in one hell of a game. I used to play the previous two Max Payne games back in my original Xbox and the third game is hard to describe. The genre of the game is a hybrid of crime thriller with a sheer blend of intense firefights, containing the cinematography of Tony Scott's 2004 film, Man on Fire. Strangely enough, Max Payne is more cynical about himself and his surroundings. If you know what happened in the first two games, then you should know why he acted in such attitude. The story in the game is rather...complex up to the point that it is confusing on what's happening and who's who. The narration mixes up to Max's current situation in Brazil and his past in New Jersey and Panama Canal. Unfortunately, the story progression tends to go back and forth of Max's past and present, ruining the mood on certain points of the story. Without a doubt, the gameplay is highly impressive with excellent body movement and human flexibility for Max to fire his weapon at any position. However, the game does feel a bit repetitive and can be difficult for some gamers to not play the entire game in one sitting. Overall, the game is recommended to those who like slow motion, action movies particularly John Woo's Heroic Bloodshed films, and gun play. However, the game may not be for some gamers who are more story centric (even though there were some surprising moments in the story). The story's good and may feel a bit "uncomfortable" in certain parts of the story. It has my recommendation.

First of all i just want to say that i played this game way back in the day when it was released and i loved it so much. Back then you had no way of tracking how much time you played but il bet anybody i played over 1000 hours eaaaaasy! Then when the expansion disc came out i just had to have it omg i was so addicted back then.
So now that im 25 years old and probably hadn't touched this game for over 10 years, i see that this game is on Steam and for Nostalgia reasons i decide what the hell i loved it back then i can love it again on Steam!
Since this game has been released on Steam the developers have included the Conquerors expansion disk (DLC) with the original game and also included Workshop support. It was due to this Workshop support that the modding community for this game created such a vast epic amount of content that the Developers had decided to even release further DLC to this game that i believe was created by the community. However since i bought the game on Steam after this point for me it has always had all the DLC included.
So playing this game again for the first time in probably over 10 years brings back so many memories and im soon remembering how i used to build my bases and quickly picking up the hotkey buildings. With this i jump straight into a couple of Deathmatches and Random matches against the NEW Computer AI which is considerably harder than the disk versions Conquerors AI. I get killed off pretty early and quite easily but im not phased at all because the memories playing this game are flooding back to me and im absoloutly loving playing this game once again.
Unlike the PS2 version this is Steam and therefore it also now has achievements of which there are around 300 i believe, so if you are wanting those then there will be no using cheatcodes like back in the day when you were a little low on a resource :P
Also one thing i will add since having bought this game it has very regularly been Updated with many Stability fixes and Lag fixes. Due to the age that this game is now considering it was first released in '99 the support from the Devs is just fantastic especially when they could just ignore this game and focus on their much newer games. Speaking of which i also have AoE 3 but haven't played it on Steam yet, it doesn't seem to have Achievements or Workshop content like this game does for some reason so maybe that doesn't get the same support this game does i don't know, either way if you are looking at buying an Age of Empires game i highly recommend you buy this one!
So this game since being released on Steam has Multiplayer - Something which i at least never had on my PS2 version although we never had an Ethernet cable to connect to it back then so maybe there was Multiplayer back then too. I personally have not yet even managed to touch on the Multiplayer side of things since im progressivly working my way through completing all the Campaigns in the entire game and its DLC. Multiplayer i can only imagine would even more so greatly increase the overall number of hours played in this game, especially when you look at playing through some of the Workshop Scenarios together too.
So this game has Workshop content, what does that mean? It means that the Developers have given the AoE community the power to create thier own graphical texture improvements and share their scenarios that they have created for this game with everyone else that owns the game.
For me so far i have grabbed a couple of graphics improvements that give the water textures a more colourful, realistic feel and new cliff and grass textures. This gives the game a whole fresh, modern HD feel to the game which still has or at least looks like it has the original graphics from 1999. That is what im assuming from still having not played the disc version that i still have with the PS2 :P
There are like i said before many hundreds of Custom Scenarios all created by the Community Workshop that i haven't even touched on myself yet that could add upto hundreds of hours of extra gameplay. I have seen scenario remakes of Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones to challenging scenarios and some other very creative scenarios!
There are graphical mods that allow you to completely change the entire feel of the game so you can have Crystal Trees and huge Veins of Gold and Stone Mines with a Space like terrain if you wanted. This is the kind of things you can experience on a game this old that breathes new life into it and could easily see you play over 10,000 hours in this game.
If you played this game back in the day and loved it - BUY IT NOW! You will not regret buying this game, i only have a meagre 200 hours so far in this version, i expect to be easily dropping 1000 hours in eventually. That is ontop of what i could only guess would be at least 1000 hours on the PS2 version back in the day :P

When I started playing Robocraft it was amazing. It was fun, entertaining, enjoyable, a stress killer, and honestly, it was actually addicting. But like they say; things change. And boy oh boy, do they. First;
I played back when classes were a thing still, and the "10 second recharge system" changed things too much. Before when we had classes, teamwork was involved. Your team would split up into small squads and tatically approch the enemy in different ways, usually with a medic. (Snipers went off on their own to give range support)
Now you just have many players abusing the system. They charging in and die instead of staying with allies, just because if nothing damages them for 10 seconds, they heal. This can hurt the whole team depending on the game mode.
There's not much to say except; the crates you get at the end of battles need better reward drops. Getting a reward for your hard work, shouldn't bore you. That's what crates did for me.
This is honestly the only thing I "hate" about the game. Here's why.

I also played back when we got in game currency (RP was the name) from simply having fun and playing matches. I usually got 500k RP from one match. With premium it'd give me 900k. This gave players room to not only build robots, but waste their money on parts to test robots or even "perfect" their already beautiful works of art.
Even if you were a low level, new player, you could have those parts you wanted in just Two - Three matches. With premium? One battle depending on how good you are. This was more fair to players raising up in the ranks. It also made fighting Pay To Wins less painful for noobs. Now, that's gone.
At this point you need to build robots and sell them to get anything, but prices are usually very high. High to the point of only buying robots if you either Pay To Win, or grind your fingers to dust. This also takes away having your own original one-of-a-kind robot design; what Robocraft was all about from the start.
Eh, this one isn't a big deal. I'm not against change, but too much isn't good. I'll be blunt, things were fine before but now they're just a weird cluster ♥♥♥♥.
Plasma Launchers: They're good and balanced because you have to actually aim and get skillful to use them right.
SMG: Same as above. Placement may effect spread and accuracy.
Rail: The sniper. Placement certainly effects weapons.
Proto-Seeker: No. Stop. You'd literally hurt someone more shooting them with a pistol, loaded with grains of rice.
AreoFlak Cannons: A cheap, exploding energy blast that cuts your flying bot out of the air. Does barely noticable damage to your robot itself, but ♥♥♥♥s your jet wings/Heli Rotar Blades. Even if you have back ups on the bot that aren't in the blast.
Lock On Missle Launcher: Dude, what even in the actual ♥♥♥♥. It's literally just aim, shoot, and that person you're shooting at is RIP. If avoiding was easier, or if they did less damage it'd be fine but.. no. So much for proper balance huh?
Ion Distorter: Hahahahahahaha.......just kill yourself and save the enemy the trouble.
For the sake of length, I'll wrap this up. This doesn't even feel like Robocraft anymore. What Robocraft was meant to be when I first played it, and I'm very dissapointed with the direction this going so far; down the drain. If the game improves, I'll probably touch it again. But until then I simply can't recommend it.
If you like Robocraft, or want to try it despite my review, please go ahead. I hope you have a different, better expriance than I've had.

When I started playing Robocraft it was amazing. It was fun, entertaining, enjoyable, a stress killer, and honestly, it was actually addicting. But like they say; things change. And boy oh boy, do they. First;
I played back when classes were a thing still, and the "10 second recharge system" changed things too much. Before when we had classes, teamwork was involved. Your team would split up into small squads and tatically approch the enemy in different ways, usually with a medic. (Snipers went off on their own to give range support)
Now you just have many players abusing the system. They charging in and die instead of staying with allies, just because if nothing damages them for 10 seconds, they heal. This can hurt the whole team depending on the game mode.
There's not much to say except; the crates you get at the end of battles need better reward drops. Getting a reward for your hard work, shouldn't bore you. That's what crates did for me.
This is honestly the only thing I "hate" about the game. Here's why.

I also played back when we got in game currency (RP was the name) from simply having fun and playing matches. I usually got 500k RP from one match. With premium it'd give me 900k. This gave players room to not only build robots, but waste their money on parts to test robots or even "perfect" their already beautiful works of art.
Even if you were a low level, new player, you could have those parts you wanted in just Two - Three matches. With premium? One battle depending on how good you are. This was more fair to players raising up in the ranks. It also made fighting Pay To Wins less painful for noobs. Now, that's gone.
At this point you need to build robots and sell them to get anything, but prices are usually very high. High to the point of only buying robots if you either Pay To Win, or grind your fingers to dust. This also takes away having your own original one-of-a-kind robot design; what Robocraft was all about from the start.
Eh, this one isn't a big deal. I'm not against change, but too much isn't good. I'll be blunt, things were fine before but now they're just a weird cluster ♥♥♥♥.
Plasma Launchers: They're good and balanced because you have to actually aim and get skillful to use them right.
SMG: Same as above. Placement may effect spread and accuracy.
Rail: The sniper. Placement certainly effects weapons.
Proto-Seeker: No. Stop. You'd literally hurt someone more shooting them with a pistol, loaded with grains of rice.
AreoFlak Cannons: A cheap, exploding energy blast that cuts your flying bot out of the air. Does barely noticable damage to your robot itself, but ♥♥♥♥s your jet wings/Heli Rotar Blades. Even if you have back ups on the bot that aren't in the blast.
Lock On Missle Launcher: Dude, what even in the actual ♥♥♥♥. It's literally just aim, shoot, and that person you're shooting at is RIP. If avoiding was easier, or if they did less damage it'd be fine but.. no. So much for proper balance huh?
Ion Distorter: Hahahahahahaha.......just kill yourself and save the enemy the trouble.
For the sake of length, I'll wrap this up. This doesn't even feel like Robocraft anymore. What Robocraft was meant to be when I first played it, and I'm very dissapointed with the direction this going so far; down the drain. If the game improves, I'll probably touch it again. But until then I simply can't recommend it.
If you like Robocraft, or want to try it despite my review, please go ahead. I hope you have a different, better expriance than I've had.

The original Max Payne games were fantastic, and still fun, but show their age a little. Max Payne 3 successfully manages to modernise the gameplay and the character himself.
This is one of the few game series with a large focus on story but set in the time of their release. So Max ain't what he used to be. Max's drunken drugged face looks suitably like♥♥♥♥♥ The majority of the locations are completely different to what you would expect in a Max Payne game. The heat of Brazil in contrast to the snowy nights of New York. The story itself is not related to Max's past but the arc is personal to Max. It's satisfying. Cutscenes are very nicely edited and at a good length. I was quite happy sitting back watching these scenes in-between the action.
The gunplay is just a joy. There's slow-mo you can activate anytime but only acquire from hitting your shots right. There's also unlimited slow-mo by diving around everywhere which may sound like a cop-out but, depending where you jump, you may be exposing yourself and you need to get  back up. That might sound funny, Max takes a moment to get back up. Old ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Despite the slow-mo capabilities the game is not easy. The latter half there are many parts where you are very limited with ammo. Areas can be swarming with enemies, at different heights, and with little cover and little ammo it's just thrilling. You need to nail every bullet near the end. Or on Hard. The Hard difficulty truly is elitist stuff here. There was one moment which was a bit cheaky but excused due to the quality of the full game. Having all these odds pit against you and throwing yourself into these areas all to the beat of the sweet gun porn in action, it's fantastic stuff. It forces you into becoming a good player by taking big risks.
Noir monologues, guns and imperfect people. It's worth playing.

I can't compare this to the original two games because it's been years since i've played them but it's pretty similar as far as i remember. The big problem to me in this game is how easy it is to die and all the side things.
It's understandable for a person with no armor on to be easy to kill but Max Payne 3 really pushes that with the healthbar that seems to have vanished from modern games. In order to heal you need pain pills which you automaticly use if you die, whenever you run out of health you go into slow-motion and get a free shot at whoever killed you, if ou kill them before you hit the ground you simpl get back up with one less pain pill bottle. Now that's all pretty nice but i have only had a max of maybe 5 pill bottles at once in a single chapter and one bottle does not fully heal you, it might restore 1/3 of your health which is a problem when you're in a huge shootout with only one bottle. Now of course yu'd imagine the shootdodge thing would balance that out but it didn't for me because all it does is slow things down and it is on a meter that has to recharge and on the hardest difficulty it does not recharge. If you are low on health and have several enemies to kill and go into shootdodge here is what is most likely to happen: you manage to kill a few only to find the rest in cover and a stray bullet is drilling through your skull.
Another problem is collectables, there are these things called Grinds that are small tasks like "Shoot this many people in the leg" and "Shoot this many people while on your back" the problem with Grinds is that they are just that, a grind, some you never really get a chance for and the all of them take several kills to level once and they all have 4 or 5 levels. Aside from the Grinds there are also clues that only the players who explore will find and even then most will need help to locate them. There are also golden gun parts, every gun in the game has 3 golden gun parts that once all are obtained you will get a golden version of that gun whenever you pick it up giving it a bigger magazine and a higher damage which is needed towards  the end of the game.
Now of course the crown jewel of this game is the story. It is well writen, told very well and ends in a way that made me very happy and made me felt like i did something with the story. Now typing out th story or even a summary would probably end up with a book and i don't have that much time on a steam review so go hear it for yourself.
Overall i give Max Payne 3 a 9/10, it's a fun game with nice controls and a great story but collectables are an issue and so is health but the autosaves keep it to a minimum degree.
