I've put a good amount of time into Dirty Bomb. and I may as well give it a good review to help others understand why I would put so much time into this game.
First things first, the game IS free to play and you lose nothing but time for trying the game out. However for those first couple of matches the game doesent explain a lot of things to you. The recently added tutorial and assault course (make sure you go throug those by the way) does a good enough job explaining mechanics, but the characters, classes, and loadout system is never explained, which is a big issue.
Loadouts, loadouts, loadouts.
I honestly like parts of the loadout system, and I dont mind having preset weapon and augmentation combos. I feel its a viable way for developers to avoid players creating completely dominant setups leaving no use for many weapons and augmentations, so A+ for that. Thankfully bronze+ tier cards have no bonus gameplay advantages, but its not quite clear about that to new players, so they should really get to that. Also the cosmetic part of loadouts bears a problem. Getting loadouts is random, and you (majority of the time) cannot decide what loadout you'll be getting, or what cosmetic options itll come with. This means that if you saveu p all of your credits and resources to get a cobalt card for your favorite merc, but get a gun youre bad with and in the color you dont like, you're♥♥♥♥♥♥out of luck.  When unboxing crates you cant even decide what merc youll be getting a card for, so you can end up with plently of flat out useless cards. Overall if they seperate the cosmetic part of the cards from the randomness of getting cards, it might end up better
Characters.
This game has a good variety of characters, and no one character really feels overpowered to me right now. You've got your engineers who do objectives faster, your medics who keep people alive, your recon who are good at ranged fighting or being a♥♥♥♥♥♥to the enemies, and youre normal fraggers who dish out lots of damage in spectacular ways. The characters youre given to start with are very good and easy to learn, so Im glad they start you out with those. Problem is they dont start you out with an engie, meaning a lot of new players dont touch objectives and it can be a bit infuriating. The characters do have a good range of nationalities, personalities, and abilities, and I really do think its one of the strongest parts of the game. Everyone feels unique with maybe the exception of Arty being a mini Skyhammer. Overall great characters and fun abilities.
Unlocking characters has never been a problem for me either. It can take 30'000 to 50'000 credits to unlock them (or 10$ but I dont reccommend that) which can be a lot, but if you do your daily wins / plays and complete missions you can quickly and easily rack up those coins. Just try not to spend too much on loadout cards if you want new characters. Theres also a free rotation every 2 weeks or so, so you can always try out characters you might not otherwise buy.
As for those mechanics and gameplay, I think theyre one of the most standout parts of the game. Time to kill feels perfect and it really rewards landing headshots (which feel oh so good to do). Movement is fantastic being able to wall jump, long jump, and get around quite well. You feel in control of your character and pulling off wall jumps to get to parts of the levels feels fantastic. Weapons have just the right amount of punch and recoile and are incredibly satisfying, the gameplay is one of the parts that really keeps me coming back.
However the future of this game is looking bleak. Its been a good year+ since we've had a new character or map release, and the 6 normal + 3 execution maps can get a bit bland after 150+ hours of gameplay. Splash damage is working on a lot of projects and I can understand dirty bomb not being on the backburner, but the game feels so close to being out of beta and being done. The player base is slowly dropping, but still has a good 2000+ players online at any time, so you will have no problems finding a match to play in. Who knows how long those numbers will last, but as long as they do and you can play the game, I'd say its worth a shot

I was a huge fan of Max Payne when it came out.  I really enjoyed MP2, but it left me feeling as if they hadn't really 'gone anywhere' in the intervening time. I've waited so many years to find out just how it turns out for Max, and to see if it's possible to improve on Max Payne.
Well, MP3 is an absolutely amazing experience beginning to end.  It's not a DooM-like first-person shooter!  Beginning-to-end, this is the story of a fallen man, finding that what seems like the perfect dream job to escape his past,  turns into a nightmare, dragging him back to square one.  It's a lovingly-told experience, which you have to just get a beer (or coke), and sit back and experience.  Take it at the pace it's delivered, and don't try to rush it.  If you do, it'll be over before too soon, and you'll regret it.  The cutscenes and dialogue are LONG.  Longer than any other game I've played.  Some of them can be skipped, but a lot of it is used to hide 'loading' screens, so you can't bypass them.   The dialog is great, though, so just enjoy it :)
I've now finished it, and I'm seriously considering buying the DLC for it, which (if you know me), tells you more about the game than anything I could write above.  The story is reminiscent of some Bruce Willis moves, and the pacing too.  The voice acting is perfect, and the way the game gradually kicks-in the help system when you hit a hard point is very refreshing.   They've definitely taken hints from console games, which tend to be more forgiving than PC games, to keep up the 'casual' nature of the game.
The game isn't perfect by any means.. The controls can feel 'sluggish' at times, and the way his body changes direction when you move can leave you slightly frustrated in firefights, but the cover system, guns, music, bullet time, and shootdodge are all just as good as MP1.  In my opinion, you have a lot less bullet-time than you did in MP1..  Maybe I'm just getting worse at shooting, but I remember clearing whole rooms in MP1 in bullet-time, watching the bodies suddenly all collapse when normal time-flow kicks back in.  In MP3, the enemies are all spawned sequentially, so your bullet time can help for the first 'wave', but you're left on your own for the next few waves.   Other than that, everything else about the game is lush.  Get it. Now.

I was a huge fan of Max Payne when it came out.  I really enjoyed MP2, but it left me feeling as if they hadn't really 'gone anywhere' in the intervening time. I've waited so many years to find out just how it turns out for Max, and to see if it's possible to improve on Max Payne.
Well, MP3 is an absolutely amazing experience beginning to end.  It's not a DooM-like first-person shooter!  Beginning-to-end, this is the story of a fallen man, finding that what seems like the perfect dream job to escape his past,  turns into a nightmare, dragging him back to square one.  It's a lovingly-told experience, which you have to just get a beer (or coke), and sit back and experience.  Take it at the pace it's delivered, and don't try to rush it.  If you do, it'll be over before too soon, and you'll regret it.  The cutscenes and dialogue are LONG.  Longer than any other game I've played.  Some of them can be skipped, but a lot of it is used to hide 'loading' screens, so you can't bypass them.   The dialog is great, though, so just enjoy it :)
I've now finished it, and I'm seriously considering buying the DLC for it, which (if you know me), tells you more about the game than anything I could write above.  The story is reminiscent of some Bruce Willis moves, and the pacing too.  The voice acting is perfect, and the way the game gradually kicks-in the help system when you hit a hard point is very refreshing.   They've definitely taken hints from console games, which tend to be more forgiving than PC games, to keep up the 'casual' nature of the game.
The game isn't perfect by any means.. The controls can feel 'sluggish' at times, and the way his body changes direction when you move can leave you slightly frustrated in firefights, but the cover system, guns, music, bullet time, and shootdodge are all just as good as MP1.  In my opinion, you have a lot less bullet-time than you did in MP1..  Maybe I'm just getting worse at shooting, but I remember clearing whole rooms in MP1 in bullet-time, watching the bodies suddenly all collapse when normal time-flow kicks back in.  In MP3, the enemies are all spawned sequentially, so your bullet time can help for the first 'wave', but you're left on your own for the next few waves.   Other than that, everything else about the game is lush.  Get it. Now.

Even though it's not as good as
and
,
still manages to be a thrilling experience with a dark and gritty story and incredibly solid third person shooter mechanics that offers immense satisfaction while playing.
The Good:
· Bullet Time Is Back: after being gone for many many years, the coat-wearing, pills-nibbling ex-cop is back. The gameplay feels authentic to the original while delivering something entirely fresh to the current standard third person shooter formula; Bullet Time. The player can slow down time to land more precise shots, or dive through the air in an iconic actionmovie-esque way while you can feel the bullets missing you by just a hair...
· Incredibly Detail: ... and every single one of those bullets is individually rendered into the game. The AI will react to where you shoot them, Max Payne himself can 360° around himself even while laying down on the ground and the game cuts from cutscene to gameplay flawlessly. Overall
has an uncanny amount of detail to it, from the textures to the precision and the the movement among many others.
· A Surprisingly Large Amount Of Replayability: after the lengthy story is completed and all of the campaign collectibles are collected you can get into the multiplayer or the New York Minute mode that gives you a minute to complete a level and rewards you with bonus time for every enemy you kill... without any chechpoints along the way.
· Superb Voice Acting: Max's original voice actor is back and every other personage in the game is beautifully voiced. Their tones and accents fit the situations and the character's movements, making for incredible voice acting that I've rarely seen done this good before.
The Bad:
· The Story Doesn't Live Up To The Previous Games: previous games had plenty of memorable characters (Mona Sex and Vinni Gognitti among others) but the characters in
feel flat and uninterresting. The story had me in its grip long enough, but in the end I cared too little for anyone else besides Max. The overall quality of the story in dumbed down by these uninterresting characters, which is unfortunate but not too troublesome.
The Ugly:
·
is downright gorgeous. Rockstar is generally known for their open-world games with amazing visuals, but with the linear
they put a lot of extra effort into the visuals and detail. From the lightning to the materials and the uncanny amount of detail, this game is one of the prettiest of its year.
Final Verdict:
· Compared to most third person shooters,
stands out due to its authenticity and fresh mechanics for the genre with tons of content that will keep you coming back long after the first time. 8/10

This is a really fun game, if you're willing to sink some hours into it. Starting out in Dirty Bomb is extremely hard. The matchmaking is less than adequate, it has one of the steepest learning curves I've seen in a while, and getting new mercs can be a grind. I reccomend manually browsing servers, and looking for a server where the level cap is 5. This way you'll play against other players who are close to your skill level. As for getting new mercs, this is what breaks this game for a lot of players. They're hard to get. But if you simply complete your missions and play daily, you'll get a new merc in no time. Finally, once you've really gotten used to the game, have unlocked a couple mercs, and can hit some headshots, you'll find Dirty Bomb is stupidly fun, challenging, and especially rewarding.

Short review:
It's absolutely brilliant, one of the best shooters in years, buy it now, you won't be disappointed!
Longer review:
I'm stingey when it comes to PC games these days, I don't buy at full price simply because by the time I get round to playing a game it'll be on sale.
Wolfenstein is a rare game that's absolutely worth the full price. The levels are large, the visual effects are great, the sound likewise and most importantly the gameplay is superb!
So may shooters feel 'wrong', like you're on roller skates all the time gliding through levels. In Wolfenstein you feel yourself running, you fling yourself behind cover when under fire only to have chunks of it blown out around you (which you can then shoot through). It's absurd, over the top and thrilling.
There's so much else to recommend though...
The cutscenes and acting are some of the most realistic I've ever seen and really pull you into the story.
There's upgrades so you can enhance skills!
Finally...once you finish the game...play through it all again making a different choice at the end of the first level, I'm doing that again now and seeing characters I hadn't seen before, it's a great idea!
Absolutely finally...the achievements are sensible and quite easy to get, this is definitely a game you can avhieve the perfect game rating in Steam.
As I write this it's even on offer as part of a weekend deal...don't hesitate at this price.
Needless to say, I'm really hoping they make a sequel!

Probably the best single player campaign I've played in a long time.  It really makes you care about the story (which is very pleasantly surprising in a Wolfenstein game)  The gameplay is exciting, the voice capture and acting and characters are all great.
There were some hitching problems at times when I was playing, but those seemed to have been fixed before I finished the campaign.  I don't like the id Tech 5 engine--it's not ugly, but the textures up close are fairly crummy, and once again (as with Rage) the engine often has an inability to "remember" textures that are behind you--if you turn quickly they have to fade in to compensate, which nearly kills the immersion (thankfully the characters and the story and the great gameplay mitigate this a bit).
There's secret to find the game, and as such there's replay value--I missed a good bunch of things.  Secrets and trophies are not merely for posterity however: they are used to unlock aspects of the game that you wouldn't otherwise see.  But for me the replay value is already there because the campaign is so good.  The devs spent a lot of time honing it, and it shows.  Highly recommended.

You make another bot, and that will also stay at X rank. You don't really take a bot through the higher levels of play anymore.
Loot boxes are trash. Literally the worst part of the game. Oh you want a wheel? Good luck finding a loot box with one. Oh and did I mention some items in the loot box are premium locked? Yeah. So chances are, it'll be locked out anyway. Want to actually buy the wheel instead? Well there's no currency. You heard me right, there's no currency besides galaxy cash which you have to pay for with real money. There is robobits or whatever, but you only get them by recycling parts you have already. Games that are F2P, should reward you for putting some money into the game, but not making the game unplayable if you don't.
Honestly if this game just put tiers back, removed loot boxes, and removed all those broken weapons, maybe I'd give it a good review. But the developers have gone super greedy and desperate for this game to succeed, if not evident by the loot boxes, look at how many times they've payed Yogscast to play their game. They are desperate for money and players.
TL:DR; Game used to be good, isn't anymore.

text:
Max Payne 3 is a very special Max Payne game. Its no longer in the dark setting of the streets of new york in winter, it now plays  in ♥♥♥♥ing Rio de Janero. Max Payne is no longer a cop, he's now a bodyguard for a wealthy family, but that does not mean he has stopped the drugs, the booze and the smokes. The story is about a gangster clan wich kidnaps the daughter of your boss. While Max risks his life often enough to find her, he discovers the streets and "background"-crimes of brazil and also a few plot twists about bad guys lying and♥♥♥♥♥♥
The story is a bit thin compared to the previous games, especially those moments where you don't really care about a few important characters of the story.
The gameplay is very similiar to the previous games. Max shoots his way through tons of badies while using bullet time and pain killers, a very fun combination that has always worked good. One point is a bit sad though: You can only carry 2 handguns and a 2 handed weapon (and if you dual-equip the 2 handguns you actually drop your big gun). I personally think the massive amounts of guns you could carry and use whenever you wanted from the previous games were a better solution. Also there are no more grenades for you to use. Allllllso: no more quicksaving. A bit stupid if you have to fight the same hoard of enemies again and again :C
The game has a very high graphic standard. Most of the time you'll have high quality textures and good exploding effects. The voice acting is good, especially the monologues of Max burn into your memory. The soundtrack on the other hand is a "funky" version of the original soundtrack. I kind of dislike this, the "hawaii five-o"-theme song would probably been better...this is no longer a "sad" max payne, its a "depressed and angry" max payne in a zoo full of partying gay flamingos.
Conclusion: I recommend the game for the sake of having max payne gameplay, while I dislike most of the setting of the game. There are a few flashbacks that play in New York, but its just never the same anymore.

Max Payne 1 and Max Payne 2 set the bars for graphics quality and storytelling when they first came out in the early 2000's, The new game, Max Payne 3, once more sets a high standard for graphics, with incredibly cinematic textures and lighting and some horrific kill-cams. The core gameplay is updated for the 2010's but retains the Max Payne hallmarks of epic weaponry and ridiculous bullet-time sequences - in one scene, Max throws himself sideways and shoots a rocket from a helicopter out of the air, just because he can!
Whilst the storyline for the first two games was incredible, Max Payne 3 leaves me cold. The narrative is scarcely believable and most of the characters are one-dimensional and unrelatable. In one sequence, we are asked to feel sorry for one character purely because she is a woman. Max himself is a broken man - and we know why having played the first two games - but his motivations are unfathomable because there is no one left he cares for. There are some flashbacks to New York but all they provide is a change of setting (and some more hair for Max).
The developers do away with the graphic novel-style storyboards in the first two games in favour of more traditional cutscenes - albeit rendered in Max Payne 3's spectacular graphics engine. Max retains his deadpan, world-weary delivery and sardonic edge, which does deliver a few laughs.
Fans of the previous two games will not be impressed with Rockstar's narrative for Max's middle age, but if you take the storyline as an excuse for incredibly fun gameplay and eye-popping graphics then it certainly is a great buy. Newcomers for the genre who don't know anything about Max Payne will probably enjoy it because they haven't been spoiled by the previous two games.

I would get, from each battle, parts not money. These I would slowly and arduously break down into materials, and then be frustrated as I get no-were near my goal. I would play a game, and have every single kill by my new, weak robot stolen by a massive machine with better weapons, stopping me from getting beyond the most basic of crates. I dont know what the develpers have done, but I know that they have destroyed Robocraft as it used to be, with no hope of restoration. All I can say is to not bother putting any time, money or effort into this game, as one day all your hard work might be reset with the currency, money spent in reality wasted as it's in-game feature you bought is taken, and the mechanics that once made your machines powerful make them into paper trash, as the game dies around you. And since so many new players have come not knowing what the game was like before, they dont complain, and so the developers are not likely to ever change this spiral of... ruin.

While it certainly isn't a perfect game, Planetside 2 takes the (in the words of a certain British-Australian fellow) spunk-gargle-wee-wee modern shooter genre and makes something useful out of it. This is a war game with actual war.
Whilst games like Call of Duty would plonk you down into a little square map with two teams of 30-some-odd other people to duke it out until your arbitrary number is higher than the other team's arbitrary number, PS2 plonks you into the middle of a giant army of at least a thousand other soldiers on one of four continent-sized maps, points you toward the other two teams (three factions total) of bad guys and says "Go get 'em!"
This is a game that requires teamwork between vast platoons and small squads. The game is based around territory control, and when I say territory control, I don't mean controlling one of a map's three goal posts. These are actual facilities that have an impact on your faction's war effort. Each base is unique, and you and your friends must figure out the best way to attack it, or risk many a floor being wiped with many a you. Additionally, the objective of territory control means there is always a push forward (except in defensive scenarios, which still require mobility), which in turn means that there is very little hiding behind chest-high walls, suckign your thumb, and popping out periodically to spray bullets and profanity in random directions.
The gameplay is fun and complex (but not terribly overwhelming), the factions are clearly defined beyond color schemes, weapons and upgrades are balanced and serve specific roles rather than simply being better than each other, and the game awards bonuses to people who show new players the ropes. At times, battles can be hopelessly frustrating, but very few games are without frustrating bits.

Through questionable design choices, I watched as each update ruined the game more and more, and had to endure through the game I enjoyed become an abomination. They removed the tech tree's purpose first, and then completely. They removed the currency and turned it into... something worse. I now had to grind for DAYS to get what once took me hours. I would get, from each battle, parts not money. These I would slowly and arduously break down into materials, and then be frustrated as I get no-were near my goal. I would play a game, and have every single kill by my new, weak robot stolen by a massive machine with better weapons, stopping me from getting beyond the most basic of crates. I dont know what the develpers have done, but I know that they have destroyed Robocraft as it used to be, with no hope of restoration. All I can say is to not bother putting any time, money or effort into this game, as one day all your hard work might be reset with the currency, money spent in reality wasted as it's in-game feature you bought is taken, and the mechanics that once made your machines powerful make them into paper trash, as the game dies around you. TL;DR: A absolute blast to play, well worth it on sale, even without multiplayer. 9/10
So I was half expecting this game to be another Triple A rehash of old ideas with a new skin. And thats actually kind of what it is. Its just a REALLY GOOD version of that. It is based in the same Wolfenstein universe as you would remember from the older games, but just a bit different. Basically, America lost to the Nazis, and the Nazis now rule the world under the command of the madman known as Deathshead. Thats about it for story really, the rest of the game is just you kicking♥♥♥♥♥in as many different places they could think of to make the game flow semi-coherently.
Gameplay-wise, Wolfenstein: The New Order is amazing. Gunplay is super satisfying, all the weapons feel hefty and powerful, and sound awesome too. Each set of weapons can be duel-wielded without penalty to aim, which makes doing so a blast as you mow down Nazis with twice the power and in half the time. Stealth is an option from time to time, but is less of a sneaky "Kill him, then him, etc." and more of "Stand behind him and Quicktime event him to death". Still super satisfying to twist a neck or stab several times, but could've been a bit more engaging. Several times I found myself trying to sneak and standing clearly in someones view. Panic would set in and I would just mash the melee key until the enemy went down, which can be a little frustrating and takes you out of the immersion.
The Graphics in this game are actually pretty amazing. Its not without occasional texture pop in due to the engine its on, and it seems to be optimized a little less than adequately for PC, but rarely did I find fps drop to be an issue in only the most intense scenes, and I use a fairly mid-range PC. Animations can be a bit iffy sometimes, but thats really only in cutscenes so it doesn't matter as much.
Basically, its a great game. No Multiplayer (Yet?), but it shines through that all the time was poured into making the Single-Player experience an absolute blast. It took me about 9-10 hours to beat the game once, and I was ready to dive back in for a harder difficulty just to be able to blast some Nazi's. If you enjoy single-player and high octane fun, this is for you.

One of my top games of 2014, no doubt. After Wolfenstein from 2009 and RAGE disappointed some fans, id Software and Machine Games decided to once again revamp Wolfenstein once again to do the franchise justice. The graphics are great and the framerate runs smoothyl (for my PC at least), the level design is fantastic with fresh new areas almost each chapter, starting with a D-Day-esque invasion of General Deathshead's fortress, then going to far as a submarine and onto the moon. The gunplay is excellent, with the ability to dual wield almost every weapon except for the Laser Kraftwerk (my favourite weapon in the game) and any turrets you can carry around. The gameplay is solid as well, with four different "perk trees" to upgrade by completing challenges. Each tree is different, ranging from stealth gameplay to demolitions for those who like to run and gun. The bosses were fairly fun, although certain bosses was disappointingly easier than I expected. Overal the game is a great new installment to the Wolfenstein franchise and is perfect for those who want more old-school shooters and for those (like myself) who love the idea of alternate history and history all together.
TL;DR Version:
Pros:
-Great graphics and framerate (on my PC, not certain about others)
-Excellent gunplay
-Variable gameplay
-Awesome setpieces and level variety
Cons:
-Some bosses easy while others are a good challenge
Overall rating: 9.5 Nazi Skulls out of 10
Recommended to: Shooter fans, history buffs, and those who crave old school nostalgia

Immediately it becomes clear that time has moved on and Max no longer is comprised for 12 pixels, and the game is no longer driven by the art noveau comic book strip. Suddenly its far more "future-CSI" esque, and the game is being driven in a completely different way.
Here is where the review will divide opinion - on one hand, this is a Max Payne title, so it should be reviewed inline with the rest of the series and with this in mind it is the weakest of the three, one the other hand this is a great story-shooter game which is non stop action with some eye-popping graphics!
It's easy to liken the story to CSI as well, there were plot twists, there was blood and between the action scenes you were dragged through the story. But, drag it did. Due to the cut up gameplay there are times where it was almost infuriating , you want to progress but the story was going to bring you back to attention and force you listen. The areas felt limited in this sense, you would bust a gut fighting through a zone, when suddenly you had a 5 minute cutscene to observe. It really takes the edge off the adrenaline rushes it could have had.
Traditionally MP had large gameplay areas, a short storyboard explaining the events and then another large gameplay area. Somewhere during the transition from MP1 & 2 on to MP3 they have lost this. It's a shame, the game has lost its charm because of it and has become a little generic.
It was clearly intended to help it sell, few people have played 1&2 in recent years and the change in art direction etc would have helped the title sell. So as a standalone game borrowing another titles name, it has a lot of strong points. A Huge 35GB download gives you super graphics, smooth gameplay, some legendary bullet time moments and some pretty sweet voice acting and character models!

There are so many things wrong with this game, I'm not even sure where to start.  It is insulting to the Max Payne franchise the same way that Aliens Colonial Marines is insulting to the Aliens franchise.  In its current state, it would have been better off as a movie with a cinematographer who wasn't high on mushrooms during the entirely of the game's development like this one seems to have been.
The most obvious problem is the "cinematic" design of the game.  This game has an absurd number of cutscenes.  Enter room, cutscene, shoot bad guys, repeat.  Sometimes you get more than one cutscene per room.  These cutscenes often unequip and even completely remove your best weapons before dropping you in front of enemies in a vulnerable position.  Cutscene transitions are so seamless that if it weren't for the HUD suddenly appearing, you wouldn't know the cutscene was over.  Others start action movie slow motion sequences which you encounter every couple levels and are the one redeeming feature in this otherwise dreadful game.
The other main issue with the cutscenes is their overall design.  The game frequently shrinks the screen by about 5% during cutscenes, leaving a black border around the edge and distoring the graphics.  On top of that there's constant bright color flashes and distortions, like the cinematographer watched a marathon of Michael Bay movies while on mushrooms and decided that all the flashing colors would be the best thing to use nonstop in a game.  This even invades gameplay at times.  I feel like it would be a very good idea to give people considering purchasing this game a strong epilepsy warning because of this.  The game attempts to emulate the previous games' noir storytelling style by taking random freeze-frames of the cutscene and pushing them to the side, yet they never seem to relate to what's going on in the cutscene and appear entirely random, so it ends up being just another distracting graphical effect.  On top of that, the cutscenes also draw random words that are spoken on the screen in the same manner.  I can hardly even remember what the overall story was about due to how poorly the cutscenes were done.
Moving onto the gameplay, the game basically plays nothing like the previous Max Payne games.  This one retains bullet time, yet the charge drains so fast that you're lucky to be able to shoot two enemies before it drains completely.  Shoot-dodge works, but the levels seem to be designed to make it as difficult to use effectively as possible with barriers in every possible location blocking your fire, and after the dodge is complete you are laying prone on the ground.  You take less damage there, but standing up leaves you extremely vulnerable until you are completely upright, which is fairly slow.
Related to bullet time, there is a new "last stand" feature where taking lethal damage triggers bullet time, automatically turns towards the enemy who killed you and gives you one last chance to kill your attacker.  If you do so it automatically uses a painkiller and you survive.  While it sounds like a cool feature, it feels more like it was introduced to the game to have an excuse to allow the enemies to do even more damage to you.  Starting about halfway through the game on hard just 2-3 shots from most enemies will kill you which is often an instant death from full health.  Somehow there are TWO higher difficulty levels.
The game also introduces a cover system.  Taking cover often seems to benefit your enemies more than it benefits you since aiming out of cover isn't exactly fast and leaves you as vulnerable as if you were standing out in the open.  You are unable to shoot dodge out of cover without manually leaving cover first which makes mobility a huge problem.  Blind firing out of cover retains a small amount of protection (you will still get hit a lot) but is the least accurate method of firing I've ever seen in the game.
Now on to the camera...At first glance the camera is great.  The FOV is pretty good for a third person shooter and it's manually controlled with no automatic nonsense.  And then you discover that it likes to randomly switch from the right side to the left which throws off your aim.  And then you discover that it sometimes drops the camera to waist level so you can't see over cover to shoot the enemies while they fill you full of lead.  WHY?!?
As for the technical aspects of the game:  The graphics are decent, but nowhere near as good as I would expect from a 33 GB install.  You can tell that a ton of work was done on animation and it shows for the most part, yet for some reason Max Payne running looks fake and robotic, almost identical to Max Payne 2 (not to knock Max Payne 2, there wasn't any better animation technology when it was made.)  I don't know if this was done on purpose but it looks really out of place compared to the rest of the game.  The game has full DX11 support but it microstutters badly so I was forced to use DX9.  On the other hand performance is very good and I was able to maintain a constant 120 fps on all but one chapter with near maximum settings.  KB/M control works great with no mouse acceleration.
I only paid $2.50 for this game and it is being filed with my most regretted purchases.  If you want to play a cinematic game, get Tomb Raider.  If you want to play Max Payne, get Max Payne 1 and 2.  If you want to play a third person cover shooter with a good story, get Spec Ops.  If you don't want epilepsy, play anything else.
As an additional note, this game requires Rockstar Social Club.  A lot of people have trouble using this to activate their game.  The other day, it managed to crash the game so badly on my computer when I started it that I couldn't even kill the process in the task manager.  The next day I started it up and was forced to reactivate the game because it had apparently forgotten.  Luckily it worked, but it gave me flashbacks of the nightmare that is Games For Windows Live.

i get that the developer has to make sure that the 'Wallpaper Engine" works without any serious issues.. but it does feel like a finished product already.. and i had no issues running this Early-Access on my i3-2120 with GeForce GXT640Ti..
i used Stardock's "DeskScapes" for over 2 years..
'Deskscapes' has a good number of animated wallpapers, but when i saw what the "Wallpaper-Engine" can do.. i was blown away like a young kid trapped in a toy-store alone all night..
i am browsing the workshop for hours non-stop and i am still discovering new things to add to my collection of animated wallpapers..
- what makes the 'Wallpaper Engine' a winner is the workshop..
the software's official animated wallpapers are too conservative compared what people share on Steam workshop.. FORGET ABOUT the video posted by the developer on Store Page.. go to youtube, and if you search for 'wallpaper engine' on youtube, make sure that you watch videos that are posted by people from Asian countries (China, Japan, Thailand, the Philippins etc), they'll show you the variety of what this software can do..
while most English speaking videos do not do enough justice to what this software can do..
by comparison..
'DeskScapes' from Stardock has stunning official animated wallpapers, but the community website (the equivalant of Steam Workshop) has very few good animated wallpapers that were made by fans..
'Deskscapes' always felt to have few good choices..
but on 'Wallpaper Engine', i am struggling to choose which animated wallpaper to be on.. there are so many good choices to choose from..
- the length.. some shared wallpapers on 'Wallpaper Engine's workshop, are 7-10 minutes long before wallpaper gets repeated; that's more than enough for music-videos, trailers and short films..  compared to 'Deskscapes' animated wallpapers that rarely go above 20 seconds before they are repeated, like a Gif animation..
- what i hope to see in the future updates of 'Wallpaper Engine", is the ability to tweak the wallpaper more.. for example, 'Deskscapes' has the ability to invert a wallpaper vertically or horizontally, and apply filters like black&white, darkening and old-film.. i for one, prefer to make my wallpapers darker, so i can better read the lables on my desktop icons..
and other features like the ability to automatically cycle between selected wallpapers with a shuffle option..
- at the moment, this  Early-Access is about US$3.00 compared to Stardock's Deskscapes which is standing at US$10.00..
and i cannot emphasize more on the fact that the Steam Workshop is what makes the Wallpaper Engine great..
in conclusion..
this is a great software and a great addition to my collection..
but you have to remember that this is an Early Access, and they are still trying to iron-out the kinks in it..
so make sure you read the system requirements for the app, and 'how to fix common incompatibility issues' that is posted in the 'Discussion' before buying..

The game is quite addictive and very entertaining from the start but soon enough you get to see and feel the real face of the game:
Downsides:
-matchmaking is horrible: You will often be matched with folks who are way over your level and who know almost every nook and cranny of the maps.
-plagued with AFKers: Almost every match you'll be forced to play with folks who are AFK. Pair that with the following...
-team balancing: you'll be 1 man short for a good part of the game. This might not seem that bad but if combined with the previous points, it's horrible. It also takes a while for the spot to be filled but chances are, the game is already lost by then.
-the grind is horrible... If you want something out of this game, a better weapon or a better trait set, get ready to grind your back end off! Crafting of load-out cards is a game of Russian roulette; you'll either get something that's kinda handy but not really and you'll spend a decent amount of credits that you had to lose quite a bit of matches to accumulate
-toxicity among players: Yes, it's an online game and it's free. What else to expect. It's still here and it's annoying as heck.
-Map balancing: some maps are way too easy for the defenders, some maps are way too easy for the attackers. E.g. map "Chapel" Incredibly easy to defend, quite problematic to attack.
Special bonus! Meh point: It's a game that heavily relies on team play. If you luck out and are forced to play with a team of 7 which consists of 2 snipers, 1 afk guy and 1 guy who's sat on the machine gun at the spawn point, best of luck winning. However, when you finally get queued with folks who know what they are doing (or are at least trying), it will be awesome (had that happen once in 17-18 hours of play).
Upsides:
+looks okish
+runs smooth
+fast paced
+voice acting is really good
TL;DR - if you want to try it out, do. It's a good thing the game is free or else it would be a massive disappointment for the spent money. But get ready to be infuriated by the problems within the game.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is set in a Nazi controlled world, where the Nazis won World War 2 and now have power over the world. The campaign tells a fantastic story, one of the best I have ever played, where you feel as if you get to know the characters in a mutual way. The gripping story is fantastic with many different items to collect and is all good, but once you have finished the campaign, that's it you have finished. There is nothing else to do when you complete the campaign and is most certainly not worth £34.99 (approx $59.99) due to there being nothing else to do once the campaign is complete.
In some missions, the game gives you the choice of either going in guns blazing or playing stealthily which both have their pros and cons depending on how you want to do it. This gives the player some freedom and I personally find this very good as you choose how you want to play the game. The gunplay is also responsive and fluid but I found that the gun models were a bit big and took up most of the space on the screen, but I wouldn't let this put you off.
I was running this game with these specs:
AMD FX-4300 @ 3.8GHz
8GB RAM
AMD R7 250 DDR3 2GB OC
The frame rate was relatively stable with only some lag on huge explosions, but the frame rate is stable 99% of the time. However, whilst I was playing the game in some missions I found that it took a little while to render some textures when I moved the camera and this was frequent throughout the game and bugged the hell out of me!
In conclusion, I think that anyone who loves fighting Nazis and who loves First Person Shooters with a gripping and compelling storyline will adore Wolfenstein: The New Order. I think that Wolfenstein: The New Order deserves an 8/10 as the storyline is one of the best that I have played, however once the campaign is complete, you won't touch this game for a long time. However, I would wait until the next Steam sale as this game is definately not worth £34.99 ($59.99) for the short hours of gameplay that it has.

This program is not a novel idea.
Many programs before have offered "live" desktop backgrounds in the form of 3D weirdness or .gif and video support. Even Windows Vista, at a time, supported the concept natively. But what makes Wallpaper Engine revolutionary in my opinion is that it is the very first time this idea has finally been executed successfully.
No program before has managed to ever make this great idea more than a gimmick. Programs before had limited support, it was impossible to find wallpapers, the UI was confusing and it was difficult to create custom backgrounds. In comparison, Wallpaper Engine, only being a few months old on Steam, already has thousands upon thousands of different background options available for free, and all easy to install with one click - just subscribe through the Workshop as you would any mod on Steam.
Not only is there a breadth of backgrounds available, but the program also proves exceptional in its resource usage. Programs of past failed in this respect, as they'd clog valuable CPU and memory resources to keep the background going, which defeats the purpose of a background in the first place. Wallpaper Engine has none of those woes, and its resource footstep is nearly invisible.
The idea of a program enabling users to have live, animated, and lush desktop backrgounds is not a new one, its decades old, but Wallpaper Engine is arguably the first to, at last, make it work.

The original Max Payne was a much-loved attempt to marry noir detective fiction with some intense third-person action: it was particularly notable for its bullet-time game mechanic which allowed you to briefly slow down the action and pick off the bad guys action-movie style. But the shooting was combined with some genuinely classy genre storytelling in the best hardboiled tradition, and it made for a classic. A rather lackluster second installment (which I still played through anyway out of affection for the first game as much as anything else) saw the series placed on ice for several years, but its been resurrected for this third episode. Sadly, despite the excellent graphics, a lot of the things that made the first game special are missing. Max's voiceover completely overplays things, veering into self-parody as the man with nothing to lose. It's hard to sympathise with him this time around. The gameplay also feels repetitive, with nothing to do but take out endless waves of thugs. Cutscenes frequently remove control from the player, and you can end up with a different weapon in your hand after the cutscene from the one you were holding before, very irritating when you know there are a ton of enemies just around the corner. It's a visual treat, with the Brazilian favela level in particular catching the eye, but if you're thinking of playing this and you're not a hardcore fan of the series, only pick this one up if you see it on sale.

This game is a legend among RTS gamers. Many AoE fans prefer this game over AoE III. AoE II is suppose to have the theme of the Dark/Medieval Ages to the Age of Imperialism/Colonialsim. The civs in the base game include the Celts, Britons (British), Franks (French), and even the Huns. Like Civ different civilizations have different special units. Unlike civ, they have unique technologies and also a degree of historical accuracy (i.e. Aztecs not having calvary units) or access to certain techs or building that goes into the accuracy. With it being an RTS that means no waiting around for the other players in multiplayer. Both RTS and Turn Based strategy games have their advantages and disadvantages so I'd consider it not fair to compare AoE and Civ and determine which are better. With that said the only gripe I have is in AoE II it's harder to get supplies and AoE III improved upon issues as well as brought in new ages and civs as well as many new features. Both are great but AoE III is $40 and it's 10 years old (originally released in 2005). So get AoE III when it's on sale and as for AoE II HD, if you prefer more of a challenge collecting rescources and the Medieval theme then this is up your alley.

Wolfenstein TNO is good, lots of weapon variety and fun mechanics, but a lot of it goes to waste when the game essentially boils down to hiding behind cover, emptying your laser gun at whatever robot is holding the biggest gun, and then ducking back down to recharge the gun. A lot of the freedom you'd think you'd get to enjoy is removed once the bigger baddies start showing up; instead you'll find yourself camping out by the nearest glowing yellow wall outlet and charging up a wanna-be Metroid arm cannon and emptying it into boring hulks of metal. The enemies have about 3 weapons (in different color varieties of course); automatic weapons with perfect accuracy and splitsecond reload times, grenades/rocket propelled grenades, and shotgun guys that shoot the UT flak cannon exclusively.  Occasionally, a big robot or mech will pack a sort of bright sticky grenade, which is lobbed at you and then hangs around long enough for you to calmly walk out of range and allow to detonate. And every enemy, including the final boss, can be positioned in such a way that they will stick to a piece of the scenery while you unload everything in your arsenal at them.
The game is absolutely beautiful & does some amazing stuff with Depth of Field, the weapons are unique and fun, the story is great, (until the final chapter; don't get me started on the ending. Ugh.) but the enemies are 100% boring bullet sponges with no confirmation that you're doing damage to them at all, (seriously; every shot you take at a boss/ large enemy will look and feel like you did absolutely nothing to it) it misses a lot of cool opporotunies for interesting combat, (you know the part I'm talking about) and overall leaves you wanting more.
Final conclusion: Play it, but play it on the easiest difficulty or one above and try to play with the mechanics to do cool stuff with the weapons. Lots of cool options for interesting gunplay are available, but if you play on even Medium or higher you'll be too busy using the same 2 weapons and hiding behind cover to really enjoy it. Get invested in the story, but don't be surprised when you get to the end and want to facepalm into the fourth dimension. 7.5/10, due to the lackluster ending and "up the health and lower the player's ammo" method of increasing difficulty.

I am so anxious to review this game. Ladies and gentlemen, I think I have found a new favorite.
Being a testosterone filled man with deep-seated cravings for violence hard-coded into my DNA from my primal, dinosaur hunting ancestors I of course lose my mind when I come across something that's hardcore, violent, action-packed and overall manly. Wolfenstein: The New Order of course, does not let me down.
Starting off with the basics: Wolfenstein is a revisit of the classic shooter series of the same name, taking on the role of Captain B.J. Blazkowicz you start the game in a desperate final push against the German war machine in 1946 (this is an alternate timeline of our history, so don't be upset if the game isn't historically accurate). Wolfenstein has amazing gunplay, a good story that is much more gripping than I expected, excellent level design and all-around great variety.
The gameplay is mostly focused on the shooting, as you can expect from a classic FPS revisit. The firearms have a steady and satisfying punch to them and enemies react appropriately when shot, making for some very nice gameplay. You also have the option to dual-wield most of the weapons in the game, firing two at once by holding down both mouse buttons increasing your overall damage per second but draining your ammo supply faster, but who cares? Manliness brotha. After each shootout the level is noticably affected by it, where most first-person shooters would leave a small handful of bodies and a few splashes of blood on the walls, Wolfenstein has great bullet-impact decals, destructable cover and very nice gore effects, making the area immediately after the slaughter look like it has been completely decimated by the shootout, again, making you feel like an unstoppable bad-@ss.
However, the gameplay is not just restricted to you being an unstoppable killing force. You can also play with a more stealth-minded approach, using a silencer attachment to your pistol, satisfying melee takedowns and even being able to throw your knives for an instant and silent kill. The game is pretty adaptable and while the AI isn't too suited for stealth it still gets the job done well enough. There are four different skill-trees in the game that unlock perks for the player as the game progresses, but unlike most skill-tree based games there isn't some level-up system followed by going into the menu and selecting which perk you want, instead the perks are unlocked based on challenges such as X amount of stealth kills, X amount of pistol kills etc. so the player does not need to concern themselves with carefully selecting perks based on an in-game meta, instead simply play the game the way you like to play it, and everything else will fall into place.
And before I get off the subject of gameplay, I want to make a quick sub-note: The enemies in this game just look badass. I love the Panzerhunds, the giant robot wolves with dagger-pointed teeth, and the frankenstein super-soldiers. Just. Wow, I feel my testosterone levels going berserk just thinking about it.
Level design in Wolfenstein is also very well made, with a fine balance between being fluid and controlled when it wants to be and switching to tight and intense when it needs to be. The transition between them is flawless, and each and every level has a unique design to them, making every chapter memorable and avoids being repetitive. In each level also are several hidden secrets, easter-eggs and collectables, creating a very welcome replay value to the game. I do indeed look forward to playing through again.
Now to the story: I wasn't expecting a huge impact with the story when I bought this game, similar to my expectations with Shadow Warrior. I was anticipating a mindless, shut-off-my-brain bullet and blood shower. But to my pleasant surprise Wolfenstein did in fact create a mighty well done story, not the best I've seen in any regard but surpassed all my expectations. B.J. Blazkowicz was taking part in the final push hoping to end the war in 1946, but events did not go according to plan and he and his team are captured and barely manage to escape, B.J. suffering a severe head injury in the process, putting him into a coma for 14 years. 1960, the war is over and the world is now under the iron-fist of the Third Reich, B.J. is in a vegitative state in a hospital in Poland when he is suddenly awoken by the scent of Nazi blood (MANLINESS). Seeing the world under control of the enemy he dedicated his life to destroy with extreme prejudice, he sets off to find any form of resistance to take the Reich apart piece by piece and take down his rival, a bitter little saurkraut known to most as Deathshead.
While the story did exceed my expectations it also left a few disappointments as well. There were missed opportunities to create some very powerful and emotional moments that the game just slid over, but there are other times where the game doesn't shy away from doing just that. The story is surprisingly good, not exactly the most original of scripts but it was a very interesting idea and it did leave a memorable impact. Now that said, there are some sour-points with the story: Out-of-nowhere plot devices that are never mentioned again in the entire game, just serving no purpose other than to make the story advance. Sometimes the game will try to create some dramatic moments with some characters who are no better than cut-outs: Some examples include obvious love-interest girl, obvious trust-issues guy with a shady past, obvious Jewish guy who does everything to remind you that he's Jewish, obviously Hodor from Game of Thrones, and B.J. himself is for the most part just the heavily-muscled jarhead who always means well but will not let anything get between him and his mission. The ending was also very vague and left way too much unanswered, but there's DLC coming in so maybe that'll change, assuming you're not a cranky anti-DLC activist.
So to wrap all this up: Wolfenstein: The New Order is a game that met and exceeded all my expectations, it was a great joy to play beginning to end. I highly recommend Wolfenstein: The New Order.

Do you like old school FPS'ers?
Yeah me too. If you are looking for a deep storyline or crafting system definately look elsewhere. This game reminded me of playing through a 90's action movie. The story was a bit cheesy but I loved it for that. They even tossed in some Easter eggs for the people who played their older games, I'll let you play to figure out what they were. Most collectables were easy to find and kept the game at a fast pace.
The play style of the game itself is simply run and gun. There is an element of stealth you can apply like older Wolfenstein games, which is very satisfying to sneak up and gut an enemy. Although there are sections where you can't avoid being seen, it's still fun to see how long you can go while messing around with the AI.
There isn't much weapon selection but the weapons are all varied and most can be dual wielded. You are awarded perks based on your performance in the game rather than having to gain exp. I loved this part because I think exp has no place in a game like this.
The health bar is mostly fixed with a slight recovery. Meaning you'd get shot down to 10/100 then recover to 20/100. Nothing like most shooters now which you're back to full health after getting riddled with shots.
I played this game because I loved all the Wolfenstein series. This game definately does do it justice and you feel like every bit of a badass playing it. There are even some scenes thrown in that are reminiscent of the 60's alternative history you end up playing. The only drawback is that this game is a huge 40gb, but I didn't have any compatibility issues or even one crash since downloading it. Extremely stable build.

Wolfenstein TNO is good, lots of weapon variety and fun mechanics, but a lot of it goes to waste when the game essentially boils down to hiding behind cover, emptying your laser gun at whatever robot is holding the biggest gun, and then ducking back down to recharge the gun. A lot of the freedom you'd think you'd get to enjoy is removed once the bigger baddies start showing up; instead you'll find yourself camping out by the nearest glowing yellow wall outlet and charging up a wanna-be Metroid arm cannon and emptying it into boring hulks of metal. The enemies have about 3 weapons (in different color varieties of course); automatic weapons with perfect accuracy and splitsecond reload times, grenades/rocket propelled grenades, and shotgun guys that shoot the UT flak cannon exclusively.  Occasionally, a big robot or mech will pack a sort of bright sticky grenade, which is lobbed at you and then hangs around long enough for you to calmly walk out of range and allow to detonate. And every enemy, including the final boss, can be positioned in such a way that they will stick to a piece of the scenery while you unload everything in your arsenal at them.
The game is absolutely beautiful & does some amazing stuff with Depth of Field, the weapons are unique and fun, the story is great, (until the final chapter; don't get me started on the ending. Ugh.) but the enemies are 100% boring bullet sponges with no confirmation that you're doing damage to them at all, (seriously; every shot you take at a boss/ large enemy will look and feel like you did absolutely nothing to it) it misses a lot of cool opporotunies for interesting combat, (you know the part I'm talking about) and overall leaves you wanting more.
Final conclusion: Play it, but play it on the easiest difficulty or one above and try to play with the mechanics to do cool stuff with the weapons. Lots of cool options for interesting gunplay are available, but if you play on even Medium or higher you'll be too busy using the same 2 weapons and hiding behind cover to really enjoy it. Get invested in the story, but don't be surprised when you get to the end and want to facepalm into the fourth dimension. 7.5/10, due to the lackluster ending and "up the health and lower the player's ammo" method of increasing difficulty.

I am so anxious to review this game. Ladies and gentlemen, I think I have found a new favorite.
Being a testosterone filled man with deep-seated cravings for violence hard-coded into my DNA from my primal, dinosaur hunting ancestors I of course lose my mind when I come across something that's hardcore, violent, action-packed and overall manly. Wolfenstein: The New Order of course, does not let me down.
Starting off with the basics: Wolfenstein is a revisit of the classic shooter series of the same name, taking on the role of Captain B.J. Blazkowicz you start the game in a desperate final push against the German war machine in 1946 (this is an alternate timeline of our history, so don't be upset if the game isn't historically accurate). Wolfenstein has amazing gunplay, a good story that is much more gripping than I expected, excellent level design and all-around great variety.
The gameplay is mostly focused on the shooting, as you can expect from a classic FPS revisit. The firearms have a steady and satisfying punch to them and enemies react appropriately when shot, making for some very nice gameplay. You also have the option to dual-wield most of the weapons in the game, firing two at once by holding down both mouse buttons increasing your overall damage per second but draining your ammo supply faster, but who cares? Manliness brotha. After each shootout the level is noticably affected by it, where most first-person shooters would leave a small handful of bodies and a few splashes of blood on the walls, Wolfenstein has great bullet-impact decals, destructable cover and very nice gore effects, making the area immediately after the slaughter look like it has been completely decimated by the shootout, again, making you feel like an unstoppable bad-@ss.
However, the gameplay is not just restricted to you being an unstoppable killing force. You can also play with a more stealth-minded approach, using a silencer attachment to your pistol, satisfying melee takedowns and even being able to throw your knives for an instant and silent kill. The game is pretty adaptable and while the AI isn't too suited for stealth it still gets the job done well enough. There are four different skill-trees in the game that unlock perks for the player as the game progresses, but unlike most skill-tree based games there isn't some level-up system followed by going into the menu and selecting which perk you want, instead the perks are unlocked based on challenges such as X amount of stealth kills, X amount of pistol kills etc. so the player does not need to concern themselves with carefully selecting perks based on an in-game meta, instead simply play the game the way you like to play it, and everything else will fall into place.
And before I get off the subject of gameplay, I want to make a quick sub-note: The enemies in this game just look badass. I love the Panzerhunds, the giant robot wolves with dagger-pointed teeth, and the frankenstein super-soldiers. Just. Wow, I feel my testosterone levels going berserk just thinking about it.
Level design in Wolfenstein is also very well made, with a fine balance between being fluid and controlled when it wants to be and switching to tight and intense when it needs to be. The transition between them is flawless, and each and every level has a unique design to them, making every chapter memorable and avoids being repetitive. In each level also are several hidden secrets, easter-eggs and collectables, creating a very welcome replay value to the game. I do indeed look forward to playing through again.
Now to the story: I wasn't expecting a huge impact with the story when I bought this game, similar to my expectations with Shadow Warrior. I was anticipating a mindless, shut-off-my-brain bullet and blood shower. But to my pleasant surprise Wolfenstein did in fact create a mighty well done story, not the best I've seen in any regard but surpassed all my expectations. B.J. Blazkowicz was taking part in the final push hoping to end the war in 1946, but events did not go according to plan and he and his team are captured and barely manage to escape, B.J. suffering a severe head injury in the process, putting him into a coma for 14 years. 1960, the war is over and the world is now under the iron-fist of the Third Reich, B.J. is in a vegitative state in a hospital in Poland when he is suddenly awoken by the scent of Nazi blood (MANLINESS). Seeing the world under control of the enemy he dedicated his life to destroy with extreme prejudice, he sets off to find any form of resistance to take the Reich apart piece by piece and take down his rival, a bitter little saurkraut known to most as Deathshead.
While the story did exceed my expectations it also left a few disappointments as well. There were missed opportunities to create some very powerful and emotional moments that the game just slid over, but there are other times where the game doesn't shy away from doing just that. The story is surprisingly good, not exactly the most original of scripts but it was a very interesting idea and it did leave a memorable impact. Now that said, there are some sour-points with the story: Out-of-nowhere plot devices that are never mentioned again in the entire game, just serving no purpose other than to make the story advance. Sometimes the game will try to create some dramatic moments with some characters who are no better than cut-outs: Some examples include obvious love-interest girl, obvious trust-issues guy with a shady past, obvious Jewish guy who does everything to remind you that he's Jewish, obviously Hodor from Game of Thrones, and B.J. himself is for the most part just the heavily-muscled jarhead who always means well but will not let anything get between him and his mission. The ending was also very vague and left way too much unanswered, but there's DLC coming in so maybe that'll change, assuming you're not a cranky anti-DLC activist.
So to wrap all this up: Wolfenstein: The New Order is a game that met and exceeded all my expectations, it was a great joy to play beginning to end. I highly recommend Wolfenstein: The New Order.

I recently finished the final chapter of the Max Payne story and I think I liked it! However... I have come away with some mixed feelings...
So firstly what is Max Payne 3? Well you play as the Max in the title, an ex NYPD cop who after the events of the first two games finds himself with his wife and baby murdered, his best friend dead and another woman he grew to care about shot in the back. Sooo understandably, this leaves Max carrying some hefty emotional baggage around with him, a suitcase made of scar tissue, full of regrets.
He's life weary cynicism personified, he's been through too much.. seen too much and no matter how hard he tries to find redemption or a way out of his own internal pain... things just seem to get from bad to worse.
Max Payne is probably the most apt name for a character ever conceived.
However he is also hard as nails and a master of film noir metaphor, believe me you'll come away from this game with a gritty one liner for nearly any situation. For example...
Max - “I didn’t know what to think any more. This town had more smoke and mirrors than a strip club locker room."
Use that one next time your confused about something, it will be fine trust me.
We start the 3rd game with Max now out of the NYPD as I say, pretty much propping up a local bar in New Jersey and trying to find some answers in the bottom of a Whisky glass.
During a drunken fight with some apparent hoodlums, Max tries to do the right thing... and ends up killing the only son of local mob boss Anthony DeMarco, who puts a price on his head.
So! It's off to Brazil for Max ..to a new life of private security, and the scene is set for Max Payne 3. Enjoy the sunshine!
Now... about those mixed feelings I have.
On one hand this game oozes style. The gun play and fire fights just "look" cool and at times almost appear choreographed in the way they play out, it's quite a spectacle to behold. When you combine that with Max's gravel voiced narration and an attention to detail which only Rockstar can provide, the game can feel like you're in the middle of greatest action movie ever made, which is brilliant!
On the other hand, I really felt like it dragged on way too long and as a game it could have been over in half the time really. It introduces utterly nothing new after the first 5 minutes. Beyond different locations, different weapons and harder enemies you'll pretty much be standing in cover shooting bad guys, or doing the same but in slow motion, for roughly 10 hours.
The slow motion is excellent by the way. I did a short video of one sequence which might demonstrate, which is on my profile I'm sure.
I'm not saying I didn't enjoy it, but paradoxically I'm not saying I did. The highs were few and far between for me, as were the lows, and for the most part I just went through the game shooting people in cool looking ways. Wading through bullet casings and stepping over dead bodies.
The story feels like it should take centre stage, but it doesn't, the gun battles is where the spotlight is firmly shone. The narrative technique is the same all the way through and the pacing is rigid in that in never changes. At no point did I feel like I was on the edge of my seat racing to climatic plot point.. or kicking back soaking up words to flesh out the story...
That isn't to say it isn't well acted, well animated or well written, it is. High production values are apparent throughout, and Rockstar have done a stellar job of making places seem real. Some of the locales are amazing in their detail, the airport level for example feels like an airport should.
Its layout, the fake adverts on the walls, the sounds of the jets, the PA systems the baggage conveyor... just marvellous.
And yet, with all this high praise, Max Payne 3 will remain an average game in my eyes, just because it was an average experience for me, which ultimately boiled down to the game lacking variety.
Whether you love this game or not, as always, it's personal taste and in this case how much you love a cool gunfight.
It's good! But, is it for you?

I came into this situation expecting a fun game, and I was certainly given that. Robocraft is nicely organized, runs smoothly even on my garbage computer, and looks good to boot. However, what I did not expect was a majority of content being locked behind a subscription-based paywall. Without buying premium membership, which only lasts for a limited time depending on how much you're willing to throw at the developers, Robocraft is extremely limited in its options. Numerous useful items are extremely difficult to obtain, free daily items are unavailable, and without a premium membership you are given four basic colors to customize your robots with, in a game centered around customization.
Is Robocraft a good game? Yes. Is it worth your time? Yes. But, is it worth your money? No. Ignoring my previous statements, my problems would be less so if a permanent premium membership were available, as the finite periods given feels like a disappointment and reflects on the developers badly.

4. At this point, we all know the deal as far as gameplay.  You get a portal gun. You shoot portals at two surfaces and you can traverse between those two points instantly. You use this and a few other mechanics that are introduced along the way to solve 3D environmental puzzles. Huzzah!
5. The puzzles here are not too tough. I suspect most relatively patient gamers will be able to plow through w/o looking up solutions in a walkthrough. I did! And I am dumb enough to spend like a hundred hours a year writing game reviews on Steam for zero compensation and zero recognition.
6. The reason they are not too tough, I think, is because they add new mechanics rather than burn the same few to the ground. I have mixed feelings about this since I do like hard puzzles but it avoids the trap of repetitiveness that many puzzle games fall into.
7. This games plot is you wake up in a secret science facility and try not to die until you win.
8. There is more to it than 7 though. There is storytelling here but it's not really tied so much to what you are doing. This is more about world building and this is just fine.
is more about world building than storytelling. You learn about the history of this secret science facility as you go through it. The picture you are given is imperfect but compelling. At the end of the game, you will inevitably want to know more about it than what you were given. This makes for a memorable experience.
9. J.K. Simmons's performance as Cave Johnson really makes this aspect of the game. If you want a complete Portal experience for as little time possible. Play the first game and then listen to the Cave Johnson parts on YouTube.
10. The music is also fantastic. You can download the whole thing from the game's website as MP3s for free. Thanks Valve! I mean it!
11. There is a co-op mode here which I really want to play but just makes the fact that I have no friends painfully unavoidable in my case.
12. I found the ending here just a touch disappointing. Story-wise, it was fine. It just wasn't very hard. I will take this over a super-frustrating final boss for sure but I think it could have been done better.
13. To save the answer the $64,000 question for last: yeah, you should play the first
first. There is nothing stopping you from playing this first, really. The plot is not that important and it's well hashed out here anyway. That's my advice. Take it or leave it, nerds.

65/100: Practically shooter on rails. To that end it achieves what it seems to have set out to do, but the combat is extremely repetitive. Shortcomings of AI design become especially apparent on highest difficulty where soldiers vary between mindlessly running into a hail of gunfire and other times having transcendent senses when stealthing. It's an old game.  Reworking the graphics in HD doesn't change the fact that it's an old game.  It is sadly missing some of the major RTS improvements that came out immediately after its release (mostly in Starcraft), like Attack-Move, but on the other hand, it has some mechanics that were not only missing in Starcraft but in the entire generation of RTS which followed Starcraft, appearing only in Starcraft II and its ilk many years later, like different unit-types dealing increased or decreased damage to other unit-types (polearms do extra damage to cavalry, but are weak against infantry).  On the other hand, this was one of the most fun, and most uniquely fun, RTS ever made.  The real jem of this game is the ability to build fortifications and attack/defend them, which makes great use of the aforementioned mechanic of varying damage for unit-types.  Units not designed to attack buildings (like infantry, or archers) deal such miniscule damage to walls and castles that it is virtually useless to attack such structures with them.  Likewise, catapults, canons, and trebuchets are useless against units but devastating against structures, requiring the player to vary their forces in order to be successful.  The AI (while inferior to that of Starcraft which closely followed it) is quite good, with multiple "personalities" and strategies to battle against.  I love picking maps with defensible terrain and playing against multiple, overwhelmingly numerous AI opponents, building detailed in-depth fortifications and spending hours defending them with networks of castles and towers, using rapid-response teams to sortie out and destroy attacking siege weapons while building my own invasion forces to decimate the enemy's fortifications and cities piece by piece.

The Lowdown:
A reboot to the FPS that pretty much started it all! The New Order frops the ironsites style shooting, in favor of old school shoot from the hip was the best idea for the game. This presents a non stop action game that is fullfilling as well as a blast to play. All the guns pack a bunch and nothing is more fun then dual weilding assault rifles and blasting nazis at point blank instant gibbing them. The upgrade system in place is great to as it only rewards you for doing certain types of feats and kills, so you feel accomplished when you unlock perks.
The story is your standard kill the evil leader of the nazis to end his regime. From storming the beach of his fortress ala Normandy style to a Nazi concentration camp to the moon! It never is a dull moment.
There are a few short commings though, since the game uses IDtech engine you will have some varation in graphic detail. While characters, guns, objects will look great there is always that wall texture that looks like its from the nintendo 64 era with pixelated painted on posters or pipes. But this was no where as bad as it was in Rage. And while I'm not a multiplayer kind of person, the lack of it really hurts the value of the game as it was on the short side,. At about 9 hours I was able to complete the game on normal. With the way gunplay worked it would of been a fun arena style shooter to waste a few hours in if multiplayer had existed.
Verdict:
While definitly a fun game, due to the lack of multiplayer or any real replay value its best to wait for it to go on sale. But I found good value for it at $30

=========================================================================
first i need to state i have over 800 hours on this game, so i would like to think i know what im talking about, i have been part of this game since beta.
this review may seem pretty negative, or pretty subjective, but in the end i would recommend you try this game, but you should be informed of what you are getting in.
there will be 3 types of people in this game you will encounter:
-Newbies, guys he need help to get into the game
-Chill dudes, people who are there just to play the game, are usually helpful
- Hardcore people, who think they have something to prove, and rub it into your face when they get the chance, and take the game way too seriously. luckily there are not that many of them around.
first thing to know about the game, this is a game to played with friends or a game to make friends in, this is not a game to play solo. those who do, end up with 1 one of 2 outcomes, they join this game, get to maybe battle rank 10-15, then get fed up with feeling overpowered by high ranking BR players. or they eventually learn that it's better to work as a team, and start playing as a team.
there are 3 factions to choose from:
Vanu sovereignty- xenu lovers
New Conglomerate - Space Freedom
Terran Republic - space "omg why are our guns so op"
before i get into negative things about this game, there is “good” opinions i have for this game.
firstly, for the most part this game is balanced (excluding what i talk about later) with infantry weapons being well balanced and each faction having their own focuses on infantry guns.
each faction has their guns designed around a set group of faction oriented things, such as:
- NC has a high damage, low ammo count, and medium to short range for most of their guns.
- VS has medium damage, low ammo count, and short to long range for most of their guns.
