mostly my negative quips are due to the fact that i was probably not taking my own advice and just treating this game as a game, and getting into the game too much.
Im sure as you saw above i have a certain prejudice to one of those factions. my main faction is NC, tho i have characters on all factions, and play all factions. i will contain this to 1 paragraph as i don't want to really focus on this.
The really big deal i have with the “balance” of the game is due to the latest update to add vehicle weapons, they gave each faction a Tank/Harasser(transport vehicle) weapon to “balance” the gameplay gap of vehicles, but as usual they gave TR the most OP vehicle weapon, a gun that has no recoil, little to no drop, high damage, and a fire rate that puts both faction equivalent weapons 6 feet in the ground. so as it stands, the TR has the most OP faction specific weapons for their vehicles, the 2 most prominent being their Vulcan (minigun) and their gatekeeper (what i talked about before) followed by Vanu and their sauron (3 shot high damage laser gun), and then dead last is NC, with the only really “good” faction specific gun the NC has is a vehicle shotgun that does no damage to vehicles, the before a nurf the enforcer was okay, but now the dropoff on it it terrible.
the other main issue i have with this game is the way the developers treat rebalancing, the most apparent change to this game would be the complete removal of splash damage, when this game first started out there was a lot of splash damage from grenade launchers, or rocket launchers, but now you literally need to be hit directly with a grenade or rocket for it to even drop your shields. less then a year ago, sticky grenades were back to their previous form, they did double the damage then they were “supposed to” but that was actually what they used to be set to back when they were first introduced then they caught their mistake and dropped them down to half damage, basically making the splash damage non existent. at what point does that seem like an intelligent decision? well it's because enough players said “this is so unfair nerf this” and the developers are pretty much forced to listen to the players.
as for the subscription option, i did not invest in that until i was level 50, so this game is completely playable without it. the pay 2 win for this game is untrue, as almost all the important things, implants, utility slots, abilities, and whatnot need to be bought with the game currency not the real money one.
all in all, this game needs to make some changes, but i feel those changes will never return. what's the saying? “ you go to war with the army you have, not the army you might want or wish to have at a later time” so all i can say is this, some of my best friends i made on this game, and we have one hell of a time playing it. so to sum up this super ♥♥♥♥ing long opinion piece, play this game, if not for the possibility of a new game to enjoy

Still my favorite competitive shooter ever. This is all out war, seriously. The openess of the maps and the base setups create situations you will never experience in single map deathmatch games no matter how many people you pack in them. Lines of troops, tanks, airships punching through an enemy line and rushing the next base in a huge wave of chaos is something like I have never experienced before in a game. It really feels like sometimes I am on a Total War battlefield with how the action takes place on this grander scale. You can feel it when you and your friends are making a difference busting that choke point, and suddenly the tide turns and theres that rush of BOOM, MOVE OUT SOLDIERS!
As you get to know the maps and how the bases are tied together, you will understand this more. There is a particular area of a map where two bases can see each other with a vast stretch of open land between them. I have been part of tides trying to wave across this field to the next base with utter chaos all over, with gunfire flying from each base and tanks in there positions on either side, hundreds of troops battling out in between hiding behind rocks holding the line. AMAZING. In another area though you may have to fight your way up a hill, creating new situations and different strategies. The maps are varied and the areas have many ways to approach and take on a situation. You can go from these extremes down to going after that base thats available for the taking, but people are not looking at much, creating a smaller deathmatch like situation that can suddenly grow as people see the opening and push it.
This is truly a massive scale game when it comes to these crazy moments, but there is alot of depth to the classes and vehicles as well. Many upgrades and weapons to get, and alot can be done earning the in game certificates, the free to play model is done very well. Much like a good free to play, you will want to spend the money at some point, but you have plenty to do before, and do not feel forced into it. This game can be harsh, because due to its very chaotic and open nature, you will die ALOT. You as a single player will never dominate anything or anyone for a length of time, its the teamwork that counts here. To me in this game repairing a Sunderer is totally as good as a kill, because ANYTHING you can do to help your teamates will help you win that base. This makes support classes really stand out in this game, but all classes really have a place in the action, with each able to make special contributions to whats going on in the battlefield. The same goes for the vehicles, from the Sunderer mobile spawn point and nasty tanks, to troop dropping airships and fast agile dogfighters, this is a game not to be missed!
This game easily makes my top 10 list of games to play before you die.

Don't bother with them, they don't really enhance gameplay at all. Game has several higher difficulties than the initially locked ones, but unlike previous Max Payne games, there's no real reason to play them once they unlock (does not generate a different ending like previous games.)
The ....?

Wolfeinstein: The new order is the latest take on one of the most memorable FPS sagas of all time. If I had to describe what's the most significant characteristic of this game it would be the production. The game feels like a complete experience where everything has been carefully polished.
The story is set in a dystopian 60´s where nazis have won the war and completely taken over the world. It feels believable and there are lots of elements that make this setting very inmersive. The plot and characters follow every stereotype you could expect, but they're solid and fit right in, keeping it simple but gripping and enjoyable.
The gameplay is plain fun mayhem, if you want to go that way. You can also go for the sealthy approach, but the game encourages you to combine both to advance in a perk system that gives you some extra objectives and motivations to kill your enemies in this or that way. The difficulty is nicely balanced in my opinion, with some struggle here and there, nothing frustrating. There are also secrets and unlockables, not always easy to find but not unfair.
It all adds up for a great game. I really enjoyed it from start to finish. I'm glad they focused on delivering a good single player campaign instead of branching out the development and getting lost into multiplayer modes, RPG-ish additions or whatever. I got this game in the last summer sale and I'm very happy about it, it's a must-have for every FPS fan.
TL:DR
Good Stuff:
- Surprisingly good story
- Very satisfying gameplay
- The fake music bands and their background
- Top-notch production overall
- Plays fine even in average rigs (I've got an i5, ATI HD7870 and 8Gb RAM), no problems whatsoever
Bad stuff:
- stereotypical characters
- Not a lot of replay value

Update after two years and over 1,000 hours:
[
This game has stood the test of time. It's still running strong. The devs seem to be engaged with the game. Construction was rolled out sucessfully, and aircraft were nerfed.
This game is worth a try, it is free after all. You don't pay with money, you pay with your time. This is by far the closest game I have found to full mixed-arms war simulation. Base building, territory capture. It's got it all.
]
Original review:
I have played this game for 87 hours at the writing of this. Not as long as some other games I like, but this game is great. I cannot hesitate to write about it. However, as with all games, it has it's pros and cons.
Pros:
-Massive Multiplayer FPS Battles
-Fast paced combat
-Choice of non-combat roles
-Extensive vehicle combat
-Population high enough for real battles
-System fine tuned for the most dynamic battles possible
-Zergling rush all the things!
-Mobile spawn points
My favorite part of this game is the Sunderer. It is a hippie-bus with weapons, ammo, and turrets. Not only that, but it can be deployed as a spawn point. Essential for spawning troops to siege enemy bases.
Cons
-Terrible Flight controls (I can hardly fly. Others seem to do very well in aircraft. Expensive as well)
-Teamkilling (I am in NC, arguably the most dangerous team due to teamfire. They should reduce friendly fire a bit)
-Cost of upgrades (I have played for over 100 hours to get what I have, that is modest at best. Most of my classes and vehicles still have stock armor, weapons, and abilities. I also purchased some points and a membership. It does increase XP substantially, but I still feel starved of credits.)
There may be more, but it seems a solid game. It as an instant actions button for those who just want to zerg rush. If you're in doubt, follow the herd. Look for territories with the highest allies detected and stick with them.

Max Payne 3 turns out to be such a better adventure than i expected it to be. Like most i picked this up cheap during a steamsale just to have it placed in my backlog for a long time. The stories on the internet about 'repetitive shooting galleries' and 'endless amounts of unskippable cutscenes' didn't really excite me to say the least.
Now, after having completed about 2/3 of the game, i have to give this game the praise it deserves. Yes, you are basically playing in a movie where you get to do only and all the shooting, but who cares if it is this good in both aspects.
Normally, i'm the guy who say's i'd rather read a book or watch a movie than have to follow a story in a videogame. I just think 99% of the stories in videogames suck, and that mostly has to do with the flat robotic characters in those stories that the game expects me to 'care about'. Well s***, i still don't care that much about the characters in MP3, and they don't have the depth of a novel based person either. But at least they come across as true badasses with raw sentiments and gritty jokes. Rockstar proves to me, just like in GTA, that i can be amused by a story in a videogame and  that i can even put up effortlessly with a lot of cutscenes.
Perhaps because they also so perfectly set the stage for the dark scenes in wich we get to actually play the game. Especially the favelas feel so utterly hopeless and raw, despite being in tropical brazil. It gave me the exact same atmosphere as portrayed in the awesome movie-series Tropa Elite/Elite Squad.
And then the game itself. It was a bit hard for me to get into, because honestly, during the first few hours i really struggled with the controls. I just fumbled my way like an idiot from scene to scene, while needing a good amount of luck to survive. But as the story progressed i started to learn how to take on the enemy in various creative ways, preciously timing my bullet-time for the right moments. Then it starts to occur why this game is being able to give you shooting gallery after shooting gallery without feeling repetitive. Every gallery in itself turns out as an opportunity to showcase your skills in different and more importantly, beautiful ways. I don't think i ever played a game where the shooting feels this good. So no, even after 2/3 of the game i'm feeling anxious, perhaps even moreso than ever, to continue my killing spree.
Rockstar has really proven for me once more why they are King of the Hill in the videogame industry for me. They actually bring a level of rawness to games that can honestly compete with some of the action-movies in Hollywood. So far they are the only one for me, but i hope their games show the direction for other studios to follow.

Starting off with the good, gameplay in Wolfenstein: TNO is fast paced and simplistic. Levels consist of areas of run-and-gun goodness and areas of sneaky goodness. If sneaking isn’t for you then you can run-and-gun through the sneaky portions as well, however it may be far more difficult than taking the quiet route. For someone that sucks at this genre, Normal difficulty was a good challenge for me during the run-and-gun areas. At later levels there are some rather annoying difficulty spikes, but nothing game stopping.
There are four skill tress that a player can specialize in by simply playing with whatever gameplay style they want. Love throwing grenades in the fray, the skills that will increase your damage and accuracy will naturally be acquired as you use them. Want to mow down enemies by dual wielding assault rifles or shotguns? You’ll gain more accuracy and damage as you do so. Gameplay isn’t halted to examine and determine the path of least resistance down a skill tree. That job has already been done for you, all you have to do is kill enemies to acquire them.
Wolfenstein doesn’t really do anything innovation for the FPS genre, it just does the basics very well. The level design is perfect and each location has it’s own distinct look and feel. The world looks lived in and you can tell that special attention went into the design and overall look of the levels. When Wolfenstein: The New Order excels on its level design, it fall flat on its face in the story department.
The main story and missions fall apart in this similar fashion from the halfway point on. I can suspend my disbelief only if the rules established are followed throughout the story. Wolfenstein establishes that the Nazis have all this power and control over all of the land and sea, yet expects me to believe that the resistance can waltz right into these places with absolutely no problems and wreck havoc on them. The issue is the game plays the Nazis winning the war with uber technology with a straight face, but then expects me to believe that these plans created from an episode of Kim Possible will work. It’s the constant clash of tone, along with terrible character building, that keep pulling me out of the immersion of the game.
If you simply smile and nod at some of the craziness in the storytelling, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a fun game to play. The gameplay is tight and polished to a shine, and the action is mostly non stop. There is a massively annoying hub system that turns Blazkowic into an errand boy from time to time (he even mentions this in a monologue), but outside of this the game is loads of fun to play.

Probably my favorite shooter of this year, Wolfenstein The New Order does a great job of combining old school and new school mechanics of shooters into an awesome FPS game.
The thing which surprised me the most is the story, it's really well written with many intreasting and memorable characters, honestly i think the reason I'd recommend this game is primarly due to the story.
It's one of the rare games where i actully enjoyed reading logs,newspaper articals or diary entries because i was intreasted to see how different this world is since the Nazis won the war.
The shooting mechanics are solid and filling Nazi bodies with bullets never gets old during the 8 to 10 hour single player campaign, which is well worth re-playing a second time since an early decision at the start changes a fair amount of the dialog in the game and even cutscenes.
The game even offers you a sneaking mechanic, alot of (but not all) parts you can sneak thru by stabing nazis silently or killing them with a silenced pistol but it's never required, it's an optional playstile. Personally i would switch all the time, some parts I'd sneak around and try to find hidden areas that will help me get by unnoticed but other times i just wanna let go and kill every Nazi scumbag with my trusty shotgun.
The health system is very old school, you have 100HP, you can overheal yourself above the maximum HP for a short time and you pick up armor around the map to take less damage however there is a lil bit of HP regeneration but not much, you will always regenerate about 10 to 20HP, so if you drop to let's say to 5HP after a fight it will slowly go up to 20 so you at least can take a bullet or two if you bump into someone and have not managed to find a health pack, i think it's a very nice combo of old and new.
It's well worth the money during an okay sale, imo it's worth picking up even for 25 or 30 Euros but full price (50 Euros) is imo a bit to much for an 8 hour (or so) Single Player campaign, yes it's worth replaying a second time but still theres other games which would offer more hours of entertainment for less money or the same amount.
So yeah, pick it up even during a small discount sale , it's totally worth it.

This game is pretty trash and here is my long detailed explanation why, I hope this helps in your decision to either DL or not DL the game or whether or not to make a micro transaction within the game (basically is it worth it).
This game has 3 game types that vary slightly by map basically (not a single one being TDM... its an FPS without TDM...) 1 type is a CS:GO 1 life, plant bomb, per round kinda game, 2nd type is escorting a vehile you have to repair and the other team destroys it followed by taking an EMP from within the vehicle and planting it in a building... why in the world did we have to escort this super slow vehicle that was blown up 10 times by the enemy to an elevator just to open the car and grab an emp from within... logic please... And lastly you basically plant C4 on 3 objectives (the next objective becomes available when you blow up the previous one).
I tell everyone that this game is a bullet sponge game. 4+ shotgun shells to kill someone. 3+ headshots with any weapon besides a sniper. If you are a heavy character you can live through a sniper headshot. Also when you get killed, you actually just get knocked down essentially... gives your team a chance to rez you (pick you up). I have mixed feelings about this... I really only hate this when I literally kill someone 5 times because their healer stayed hidden and rez them faster than I can finish off the knocked down player (which is very inconsistent on how much dmg the downed player needs to take to actually be killed). This game also makes it pretty hard to shoot while aiming down sights, so basically this is a hip-fire type game (except sniper)... however hip-fire is more acurate in my opinion...
Matchmaking is the worst I have ever seen in any game. The game does not match you by skill... rather it uses RNG... so 4/5 games you play will either be a complete annihilation of your team or their team. For instance, I'm level 11 (has taken over 80 hours to get to 11) in the game and my whole team consisted of players under 10... while the other team had 5 players over lvl 60... So the other 1/5 game will be either a draw or a close win/loss (only because the RNG put good players on both teams). It does allow you to vote mid game to "shuffle teams by skill"... Still RNG... AND to get this vote to pass, you need people from your team and their team to vote on the shuffle!!! Which will never happen because their team is winning!! So why would they vote to have the teams RNG shuffled and potentially loose!!! ...
As I read other reviews... I forgot to talk about HACKERS... Yeah this game has quite a few. This game has long distance C4 planting objectives so people use movement speed hacks. When I confronted one... he said, and i quote, "uhh i think its a perk in the game man" NO SUCH THING! LOL! Characters have enhancements through their character cards but nothing that makes them move so fast you question seeing anything till they get in a gun fight with somone behind you... And of course the aim-bots. Don't need to explain that... you can confirm this buy watching players screens on your team while the repawn timer counts down... crosshairs instantly snapping to players heads.. uses pistol for more acuracy and 3 shots later dead.
I could keep going but I'll just say, give it a try but don't expect much. You will soon see the disappointment I speak of. I think the game has a really solid idea and foundation but needs massive overhaul of the mechanics. I really want to play this game becasue of all the characters and their unique skills but I just can't get past how horribly trashtastic the mechanics are...

Starting off with the good, gameplay in Wolfenstein: TNO is fast paced and simplistic. Levels consist of areas of run-and-gun goodness and areas of sneaky goodness. If sneaking isn’t for you then you can run-and-gun through the sneaky portions as well, however it may be far more difficult than taking the quiet route. For someone that sucks at this genre, Normal difficulty was a good challenge for me during the run-and-gun areas. At later levels there are some rather annoying difficulty spikes, but nothing game stopping.
There are four skill tress that a player can specialize in by simply playing with whatever gameplay style they want. Love throwing grenades in the fray, the skills that will increase your damage and accuracy will naturally be acquired as you use them. Want to mow down enemies by dual wielding assault rifles or shotguns? You’ll gain more accuracy and damage as you do so. Gameplay isn’t halted to examine and determine the path of least resistance down a skill tree. That job has already been done for you, all you have to do is kill enemies to acquire them.
Wolfenstein doesn’t really do anything innovation for the FPS genre, it just does the basics very well. The level design is perfect and each location has it’s own distinct look and feel. The world looks lived in and you can tell that special attention went into the design and overall look of the levels. When Wolfenstein: The New Order excels on its level design, it fall flat on its face in the story department.
The main story and missions fall apart in this similar fashion from the halfway point on. I can suspend my disbelief only if the rules established are followed throughout the story. Wolfenstein establishes that the Nazis have all this power and control over all of the land and sea, yet expects me to believe that the resistance can waltz right into these places with absolutely no problems and wreck havoc on them. The issue is the game plays the Nazis winning the war with uber technology with a straight face, but then expects me to believe that these plans created from an episode of Kim Possible will work. It’s the constant clash of tone, along with terrible character building, that keep pulling me out of the immersion of the game.
If you simply smile and nod at some of the craziness in the storytelling, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a fun game to play. The gameplay is tight and polished to a shine, and the action is mostly non stop. There is a massively annoying hub system that turns Blazkowic into an errand boy from time to time (he even mentions this in a monologue), but outside of this the game is loads of fun to play.

What can I say about Dirty Bomb? Well, I have a respectable amount of hours, and have done quite a bit. Have I gotten anywhere close to playing every single character to be able to grasp their abilities?
No. Not even freaking close. You are definitely, not so gently, persuaded to purchase the characters. It can take anywhere from days to weeks of grinding to get a character. Based on my skill, it falls to the week side of the coin. That said, thats one of my only serious complaints about the game. Yes, there were a lot of bugs. They got fixed... eventually. Yes, there are new characters coming.... eventually. New maps as well.... but I think you get the idea.
The gunplay is fast, challenging, and usually skill based. 9 times out of 10, a well placed headshot will win a gunfight. Are there still tweaks that need to be made to characters? Yes.... and they're actually happening in a somewhat timely manner. I won't pretend to tell you that Splash Damage made the best, top of the line shooter. It has problems. The community can be toxic at times. But it's a cut above the usual garbage, and gave a unique spin on the usual gameplay. Tactics are more important than abilities... again, usually. I would say, try it out, but don't expect to be doing well in every single game right away. The skill curve will be hard. You will get used to seeing players over a hundred levels above you. And eventually, you will get used to seeing those high level players fall by your own hand, with the satisfaction you killed them.
Try it out, but buyer beware, it won't always be fun.

Max Payne 1 and 2 are great games, they have nice pacing to them and action that you'd be hard pressed to find anywhere else. It was nice to go through levels/maps while taking down badguys with excellent gunplay and see the comicbook like cutscenes with voice acting.
This game falls short of being a good game by itself, never the less part of the Max Payne series, to keep this short I'll list bullet points on why this game is terrible.
-Long drawn out, unskippable cutscenes with annoying video effects that flash, flicker/distort the screen often...that are 80% of the time unskippable because they are masking MASSIVE load times. It actually hurt my eyes after a while, really load up a youtube video, turn it to 1080p/full screen and watch for a bit, you'll see what I mean. This game felt more like Metal Gear 4, more cutscenes than gameplay.
-You don't feel like you're playing a game; you know how some games you run to an designated area for shooting and it's rince and repeat? This game does that, but worse, often the cutscenes will take you to right into the next fight- which may sound like a good way to break into more action but you cannot skip a lot of the cutscenes. So there's no real exploring, not a lot of running around. Cutscene, battle, 4 steps, cutscene, They really tried to make this play like a movie, and it didn't work. It's also a lot more cover focused this time around, you'll find yourself doing less awesome and fun diving around the battlefield and more hiding.  ( I played on hard mode so it may be different on lower settings)
-Glitches can be frequent, I dove for cover behind a car, Max stood up and then fell through the world, I had the game crash a few times too, meaning I got to see more of those cutcenes I mentioned that literally hurt my eyes.
-The game is 35GB, it's massive.
-You have to create another account with rockstar to play the single player game
The positives
+Well it LOOKs very nice, some character models that aren't important to the story look a bit wonky but there's no denying, the game is pretty; and it better be for 35GB+
+The gunplay is fun, they have a cool engine that makes the fights feel a bit more dynamic with bullets knocking enemies around differently on where you hit them. The game even has a lot of destructable stuff, making fights more exciting.There's a lot of fights to be had as well in different locals, but again it's hard to get into because of long load times covered by irritating filter covered cutscenes.
+You get to see all sorts of areas, it's got nice voice acting and has lots of polish in the details.
Other thoughts:
If- IF they didn't have the ammount of long cutscenes with these insane video effects constantly blasting your eyes I'd be more inclined to reccomend it, every time I felt myself getting into the game and being interested I got taken out.
Edit: I fully understand that the cutscenes mask load times, but that does not excuse them for being so effect heavy they physically hurt your eyes.
I'd honestly 100% rather have a load bar fill up than to be forced to watch a long cutscene again with excessive effects, you can skip this crap in DVDs but not games? Inexcuseable.
Because of the excessive frequency and length of cutscenes that cut into the gameplay I can't reccomend this game, not even on a LP. There's a game here, it's just buried under crap no one wants to be forced to sit through so they can play.
Still a better love story then Twilight. <|:^)

~THIS REVIEW DOES NOT HAVE SPOILERS!~
This game is pretty good! Not without its flaws of course, but ultimately a satisfying game. Wolfenstein: The New Order only has a single-player campaign, and ultimately benefits greatly from it. Since the focus was aimed all on that experience, the mechanics, story, and little details are polished to a shine unseen in many other First-Person Shooter campaigns.
The overall gameplay mechanics satisfied me greatly. You move fast and loose, and are encouraged to run around and firing at people while strafing. Your accuracy doesn't suffer while moving, so you can easily be on the move as you fight enemies. This is a great departure from many FPS game's desire to make you use cover as a major factor of combat, whereas you only use it as something to dodge bullets and reload before you're on the move again. The stronger enemies make you want to stick to cover more, but by the time you start dealing with them you'll be very familiar with how to fight.
The health usage also hearkens back to the old days of numerical health. You have to get healthpacks in order to heal yourself, although there is a nice anti-frustration regenerating health system. If you are between two multiples of 10 (for example, between 30 and 40 health), if you don't take anymore damage for a second you will heal back to the higher fence of 10. Say, you got left at 34 health, you would heal back to 40 if you didn't take damage for a few moments. Also, if you fall below 20, you will heal back to 20 again eventually. I found this to help validate the use of healthpacks as a way to more permanently get your health up, encourage more active gameplay and minimize usage of cover to gain HP back. I feel this kind of system is one of the best health systems in an FPS yet.
The story engaged me much more than many do, especially in that it made Nazis look like total scumbags. They already are of course, but there's something about seeing Nazis torture people in coldly efficient ways and kill innocent people that really fires one up. The nazis sometimes show off moments of humanity when you hear them talk about their families or they try to help each other, but I found these moments to show off even more how evil they are because they only care about their own and willfully turn a  blind eye to the suffering of their fellow non-Nazi humans. The recurring Nazi characters especially exemplify this, as they show vestiages of personality and class yet enjoy being cruel to everyone else; they explicitly take pleasure in torturing and killing anyone they deem of "impure blood". It's very cathartic when you get to deal with them.
As for the arcs the story goes in, they are satisfying and full of spectacle in the right way. You are driving the story, and you get the feeling that without your character everyone else would be still pretty screwed against the Nazi regime. Not to say the other characters are unnoteworthy; each of them adds flavor and personality, and you can tell how tired and worn they've become from being under such a terrible regime.
Lastly, I just want to gush for a moment over the game's subtle details. For starters, you can pick up objects near you without looking at them; this little feature saved me a LOT of frustration in trying to look at objects the "right" way to pick them up. Secondly, the focus on single player resulted in plenty of collectables to obtain. You can find music records (and listen to them!!), Nazi gold, Enigma Codes that unlock a new game mode, and plenty more. Lastly, you can find lots of newspaper clippings that fill in the details about what happened in between World War 2 and the Nazis taking over the world. I don't think these things would be in the game if Machine Games was pressured to make a tacked-on multiplayer.
I did have some complaints of course:
1) One of the more annoying things I had to deal with during combat is that it's difficult to tell sometimes if you are taking damage, and the degree you are taking it, until your screen is grayed out when you are near death. This is probably due to the high difficulty, but oftentimes I took focus from enemies and lost a majority of my health. Granted, such damage soaking is mitigated by being careful, but some more obvious notifications on how hurt I am would be nice.
2) The story went from believable to absurd from time to time. There are moments where I felt like you just did something that would warrant the entire Wehrmacht breathing down your neck, but only got a small squad going after me in response. Furthermore, some of the ways you "even the odds" are just straight up silly. They definitely are satisfying as hell to witness, even if they threaten suspension of disbelief.
3) The second phase of the final boss fight was obnoxiously obtuse. You can't fight the boss directly yet, so you have to do something that isn't intuitive and only vaguely implied. I don't exactly want handholding here, but better map design could have prevented this issue.
4) Very nitpicky point, but your ability to dual-wield weapons is an awesome yet impractical ability. You'll burn through ammo without careful shooting, and the single weapon does the job against most enemies. The only time I felt encouraged to dual-wield was when facing the most tanky of baddies, but sometimes it's not even necessary.
5) Also nitpicky, but this game features a "overheal"; if you grab health that would give you more health than your cap (100), you get the difference added to your health anyway but it will tick down your health until it settles on 100 again. This is ideal when you want to go toe-to-toe with lots of enemies or the really fat ones, but I honestly felt like it was a waste. I found it a better idea to wait until my encounter was over, then grab the health later to get back to 100 if I was injured severely.
Overall, Wolfenstein: The New Order impressed me on how powerful the story was and mechanically sound the game played. If you're looking for a cohesive, detail-filled, and just plan fun single-player game, you're looking at it.

What can I say about Dirty Bomb? Well, I have a respectable amount of hours, and have done quite a bit. Have I gotten anywhere close to playing every single character to be able to grasp their abilities?
No. Not even freaking close. You are definitely, not so gently, persuaded to purchase the characters. It can take anywhere from days to weeks of grinding to get a character. Based on my skill, it falls to the week side of the coin. That said, thats one of my only serious complaints about the game. Yes, there were a lot of bugs. They got fixed... eventually. Yes, there are new characters coming.... eventually. New maps as well.... but I think you get the idea.
The gunplay is fast, challenging, and usually skill based. 9 times out of 10, a well placed headshot will win a gunfight. Are there still tweaks that need to be made to characters? Yes.... and they're actually happening in a somewhat timely manner. I won't pretend to tell you that Splash Damage made the best, top of the line shooter. It has problems. The community can be toxic at times. But it's a cut above the usual garbage, and gave a unique spin on the usual gameplay. Tactics are more important than abilities... again, usually. I would say, try it out, but don't expect to be doing well in every single game right away. The skill curve will be hard. You will get used to seeing players over a hundred levels above you. And eventually, you will get used to seeing those high level players fall by your own hand, with the satisfaction you killed them.
Try it out, but buyer beware, it won't always be fun.

Max Payne 3 by Rockstar Games, Creators of the popular GTA and L.A Noire certainly didn't hesitate in making this third person shooter game, into something straight out of an action movie, while still having a very decent storyline to go with it.

The game features a mechanic refered to as "Bullet Time" which activates at the press of a button or when performing "Shoot Dodges" Which allows you to slow down time for those action headshots, as well as featuring a "Bullet Cam"

I got it on a Steam sale for $30....and I feel like I got my money's worth. And it's good enough as a game to even be worth a couple of replays....it has a small branching storyline which tells two slightly different stories based on an early choice you are forced to make.

I honestly can't reccomend this game to the average player. It's very difficult to pull off a MMOFPS like this well, and unfortunately Daybreak falls somewhat short of the bar. In short, this game is ahead of its time. The graphics and sheer amount of activity (there's several hundred players on a given continent at any time, and each continent is similar in size to the Oblivion world) cause many players to be forced to play at minimum resolution and graphics settings, which for an FPS is detrimental because it becomes difficult to aim at distant targets. In addition, the servers frequently lag, you rarely feel as though you're accomplishing anything, and battles for control of an area (especially biospheres and tech centers) can take hours. There are no "bot games" to play to get used to things- you are given a basic controls tutorial for your chosen faction and then dumped into the game immediately. For new players, this can be incredibly overwhelming. Throw in the fact that colors are somewhat muted and NC and TR armor looks similar at a distance, as well as friendly fire being on, and you get a huge cluster♥♥♥♥ everywhere there's fighting. It's hard to tell if you're "winning", because there's no objectives other than "capture this area" which can be completed by any faction at any time, provided an area is adjacent to one of their controlled areas. In summary: Too graphics intensive for most players, no sense of accomplishment, no adequate preparation for newbies, and no clear objectives other than "kill everything that moves that isn't [insert team color here].

Disclaimer: Beat main campaign on "I am Death Incarnate!" (2nd highest difficulty) in 9 hours.
~THIS REVIEW DOES NOT HAVE SPOILERS!~
This game is pretty good! Not without its flaws of course, but ultimately a satisfying game. Wolfenstein: The New Order only has a single-player campaign, and ultimately benefits greatly from it. Since the focus was aimed all on that experience, the mechanics, story, and little details are polished to a shine unseen in many other First-Person Shooter campaigns.
The overall gameplay mechanics satisfied me greatly. You move fast and loose, and are encouraged to run around and firing at people while strafing. Your accuracy doesn't suffer while moving, so you can easily be on the move as you fight enemies. This is a great departure from many FPS game's desire to make you use cover as a major factor of combat, whereas you only use it as something to dodge bullets and reload before you're on the move again. The stronger enemies make you want to stick to cover more, but by the time you start dealing with them you'll be very familiar with how to fight.
The health usage also hearkens back to the old days of numerical health. You have to get healthpacks in order to heal yourself, although there is a nice anti-frustration regenerating health system. If you are between two multiples of 10 (for example, between 30 and 40 health), if you don't take anymore damage for a second you will heal back to the higher fence of 10. Say, you got left at 34 health, you would heal back to 40 if you didn't take damage for a few moments. Also, if you fall below 20, you will heal back to 20 again eventually. I found this to help validate the use of healthpacks as a way to more permanently get your health up, encourage more active gameplay and minimize usage of cover to gain HP back. I feel this kind of system is one of the best health systems in an FPS yet.
The story engaged me much more than many do, especially in that it made Nazis look like total scumbags. They already are of course, but there's something about seeing Nazis torture people in coldly efficient ways and kill innocent people that really fires one up. The nazis sometimes show off moments of humanity when you hear them talk about their families or they try to help each other, but I found these moments to show off even more how evil they are because they only care about their own and willfully turn a  blind eye to the suffering of their fellow non-Nazi humans. The recurring Nazi characters especially exemplify this, as they show vestiages of personality and class yet enjoy being cruel to everyone else; they explicitly take pleasure in torturing and killing anyone they deem of "impure blood". It's very cathartic when you get to deal with them.
As for the arcs the story goes in, they are satisfying and full of spectacle in the right way. You are driving the story, and you get the feeling that without your character everyone else would be still pretty screwed against the Nazi regime. Not to say the other characters are unnoteworthy; each of them adds flavor and personality, and you can tell how tired and worn they've become from being under such a terrible regime.
Lastly, I just want to gush for a moment over the game's subtle details. For starters, you can pick up objects near you without looking at them; this little feature saved me a LOT of frustration in trying to look at objects the "right" way to pick them up. Secondly, the focus on single player resulted in plenty of collectables to obtain. You can find music records (and listen to them!!), Nazi gold, Enigma Codes that unlock a new game mode, and plenty more. Lastly, you can find lots of newspaper clippings that fill in the details about what happened in between World War 2 and the Nazis taking over the world. I don't think these things would be in the game if Machine Games was pressured to make a tacked-on multiplayer.
I did have some complaints of course:
1) One of the more annoying things I had to deal with during combat is that it's difficult to tell sometimes if you are taking damage, and the degree you are taking it, until your screen is grayed out when you are near death. This is probably due to the high difficulty, but oftentimes I took focus from enemies and lost a majority of my health. Granted, such damage soaking is mitigated by being careful, but some more obvious notifications on how hurt I am would be nice.
2) The story went from believable to absurd from time to time. There are moments where I felt like you just did something that would warrant the entire Wehrmacht breathing down your neck, but only got a small squad going after me in response. Furthermore, some of the ways you "even the odds" are just straight up silly. They definitely are satisfying as hell to witness, even if they threaten suspension of disbelief.
3) The second phase of the final boss fight was obnoxiously obtuse. You can't fight the boss directly yet, so you have to do something that isn't intuitive and only vaguely implied. I don't exactly want handholding here, but better map design could have prevented this issue.
4) Very nitpicky point, but your ability to dual-wield weapons is an awesome yet impractical ability. You'll burn through ammo without careful shooting, and the single weapon does the job against most enemies. The only time I felt encouraged to dual-wield was when facing the most tanky of baddies, but sometimes it's not even necessary.
5) Also nitpicky, but this game features a "overheal"; if you grab health that would give you more health than your cap (100), you get the difference added to your health anyway but it will tick down your health until it settles on 100 again. This is ideal when you want to go toe-to-toe with lots of enemies or the really fat ones, but I honestly felt like it was a waste. I found it a better idea to wait until my encounter was over, then grab the health later to get back to 100 if I was injured severely.
Overall, Wolfenstein: The New Order impressed me on how powerful the story was and mechanically sound the game played. If you're looking for a cohesive, detail-filled, and just plan fun single-player game, you're looking at it.

The FPS genre is really overused these days with nearly all games are first person shooters. but not that it matters to Wolfenstein, why? because this game is just unique in the story itself, the way it is presented to you. how william whispers to himself, communicating his thoughts to you. it is just brilliant. its nice smooth and well executed. I finished the game with a smile yet sad face, a smile on my face because I enjoyed the game. a sad face because the ending crushed my heart.
Gameplay:- Now Wolfenstein isn't any different from other FPS games. you point and shoot. pick up ammo, pick up health and go destroy some nazi's. in any brutal way you see fit. what's different in Wolfenstein however, is its perk system. You dont have to accumulate some exp and waste its point on the perk. you actually need to fulfill some objectives to each perk in order to activate it and unlock the next on the line. I find that system a bit challenging. specially when I try to sneak and assassinate. I dont have the patience to sneak anymore... so I go in guns blazing and shooting the hell out of the nazi's.
Sound/Music:- The Voice acting is amazing. everyone did their roles perfectly. and so much that sucked me in the game. This is a critical part for me. if voice acting sucks, I wont be dragged in and I will probably lose interest in the game. Wolfenstein however did not disappoint, the cast was brilliant. The music also was great. well done, well placed. gets you hyped in locations where you need to be hyped.
Graphics/animation. Wolfenstein is not a major leap  in future graphics. the graphics are just well done. Not amazing, not eye candy, Just normally right. it feels like the people who made it poured their souls into it. these kind of games I really like to support. Unlike the crap crysis 2 and 3... sheesh. these games are graphically nice, but felt dull and boring.
Overall, Wolfenstein The new Order is a great game. I enjoyed it fully. Not disappointed. money well spent! would totally recommend it!

I'm glad I got this when it was only a $1 and change... sold some trading cards and got it, well.. got what I paid for. Seemed like a fun premise, but alas... once you start playing, you see it for what it is. The style and art are pretty good, but the humor is just 10yo toilet crude, with your first introduction to humor being reoccurring poop gags that you have to wait through. Oh,, an owl is pooping, hah.. oh.. now a bear is pooping all over.. there's a point where you have to ride deer with rocket poop. You get the idea.
As for game play, it's repetitive as all hell without bringing anything new to the table as you progress. All enemies are pretty much the same. Either spam a melee, spam a ranged projective (and I mean really really spamming them, or the rare, spam melee then throw a ranged projectile before spamming melee. The bosses are all single or double mechanic gimmick fights so after a few, it's really the same thing. Run around avoiding ranged or projectile, dodge the "big" attack, spam your same attack over and over, rinse and repeat.
At least multi player should be fun right? Not even. It might be fun if you have 3 other friends at your house, all with xbox controllers, and your pc dragged down to your tv.. then it might be, but that's not really what pc games are about. There's an online mode for sure. Does it work.. not at all. There are no lobbies, just host a game and wait, or search for a game and hope there is one. No list, no ranks, no searching. When you do finally find a game, it's generally with an afk host who's been sitting so long waiting for someone to join, that when the game does fill, you have 3 players simply spamming the ready button until everyone quits.
so lets say you actually find a game, you join, it fills, and everyone actually accepts. Tada.. the game is awesome right? Nope. The experience makes me think that the 3 other people I'm playing with are on tethered sat-phones in the Philippines, or on some some terrible dial up in South America. No matter how good the ping bar shows in the lobby (if you can call it that) the game rubber bands and lags like hell. 2-3 second lag time while waiting for other players... The game crawls to a halt, and button presses don't even register.
I really wanted to like this game, but I just can't recommend it anyone.

Ah, Portal 2! Y'know, it must have been really difficult to work out where to take the series after the first game. New puzzles, obviously, but what about Glados? What about the protagonist? How do you take a simple story (with great subtlety), and expand on it, without making it seem stupid (like most sequels)?
But wouldn't you know it, they did it! They gave us a new character AI to talk at you. They gave us Glados. They gave us the backstory to Glados. They gave us the backstory to Aperture Science. They expanded the world. The new song isn't as great as "Still Alive", but it's still sung with as much gusto.
Portal 2 also has a cooperative mode (which I suppose would be the sequel to the single-player campaign), which I haven't tried (because I generally don't do multiplayer), but it's certainly a step in the right direction.
Along with new puzzles, there are new mechanics, including different types of gels, different ways of moving around, and lasers. I wish there were more lasers. I love lasers.
So, yeah, great game, especially if you like multiplayer. Even if you don't, the main campaign is worth it, especially if you get the game on sale.

What a disappointment!
I loved both the first and the second part of the series (made by Remedy Entertainment) which both are third person shooters with a serious film noir touch and a focus on slow motion gameplay. One prime element of their goodness was its dark story taking place in winter themed New Jersey and was being told mostly in comic panels, voice-narrated by the depressed cynical drug addict Max Payne himself. The nightmarish flashbacks about his murdered wife and child which occured multiple times in the original games are probably the first thing most people relate to the Max Payne games.
The third part of the series (developed by Rockstar Vancouver) lost its winter and film noir visuals almost completely and replaced them by strange and unpleasant random color blurs and plays mostly in São Paulo at bright daytime, which alone is a big shame and never really appealed to me.
Although the character Max seems still to be pretty much the same cynical drug addict and the story still features some darker elements, overall it doesn't feel like a true Max Payne storyline anymore. The worst thing they did to the storytelling was to replace the comic panels with game engine rendered cutscenes, insane amounts of cutscenes. It felt like I was watching more cutscene than actually playing. Even worse: There is no way of knowing what triggers the next cutscene, which forced me multiple times to progress to the next area even if I wasn't finished exploring the one before. Even though exploration in this ultra-linear game wasn't the biggest theme, sometimes I could have really needed some more painkillers or ammunition which I could have found hadn't the game forced me to abandom them.
What I was also forced to ignore were large amounts of collectibles. You can find "clues" throughout the levels which trigger a bit more of spoken information about what currently happens in the story and you can pick up parts of golden weapons. I generally dislike the idea of hiding story elements in linear games in which I cannot go back if I missed something. Those golden weapon parts on the other hand are an horrific, immersion-breaking element. If you collect three of the same kind of these odd contraptions which obviously don't belong where they are lying around, one of your weapons will be changed into a golden skin version, which I think is butt ugly, useless and totally doesn't fit in a Max Payne game.
The gameplay itself felt wrong all the time. I consider myself quite an experienced shooter player and played the game on "Hard" at first but I constantly died. This didn't change so much after reducing the difficulty to "Medium". The game just doesn't feel fair at all and a lot of the times the controls just did't do what I intended. I think this heavily frustrating aspect is related to Rockstar producing their games primarily for consoles and this being optimized for gamepads with aiming help. Even though I own a gamepad I would never ever want to play a shooter with it. Another unneccessary annoyance: After cutscenes most of the time you had different weapons in your hand than the ones you had chosen before and often your heavier weapon simply disappeared for no particular reason. Also I was placed in strategically questionable locations after a lot of cutscenes, which resulted in a lot of frustration by dying again. Don't let me start about the chest-high walls cover system which had to be in this game because it needs to be in every console shooter nowadays, with the twist that in plenty of situations the cover doesn't work at all.
The graphics are overall matching, but are technologically not on the level for a game of 2012. Especially the animations in the cutscenes looked clunky, which seem to be a constant problem in all Rockstar games I played in the last years. Moreover, the game engine crashed multiple times and caused problems with missing textures and models multiple times in my playthrough. As usual for bad port of a console game, there is no way to save your progress where you want. Sometimes when I died I respawned but couldn't see myself or my enemies while still being shot at and dying again. This cycle could only be broken by exiting the game and starting anew from the an earlier saved point. I didn't experience so many technological problems in a single game for quite a long time. I suspect the developers didn't have enough interest in the PC platform to test and fix this game properly. The game also requires to be registered to an Rockstar Social Club account and to be connected to their systems while playing. This also caused problems when I first wanted to start playing and is basically nothing more than just another layer of annoying DRM legal customers have to suffer from, it also means you can't share this game via Steam Family Sharing.
My conclusion: This game is just at the brink of not even being mediocre anymore. The only partially interesting part is the story and the character. The gameplay is just annoying and lost everything good from its predecessors. I can't say anything about the multiplayer part, but I wouldn't bet on it being worth it.
I wouldn't buy this again nor would I recommend anyone to buy this game.

Starting off, if you do not have a decent computer, then this game probably is not the game for you.
Planetside 2 is a MASSIVE online multiplayer, strategic first-person shooter, where the goal is simple and the answer is anything but. The goal: capture more territory for your faction, which is one of three themed teams. Territories are captured by captureing points points in a king of the hill and CTF kind of way. Each territory has between 1 and 3 points that are captured by being withing a ccertain distance of a point. After that, it can take up to 5 minutes for the territory to be completely captured. The only hard part is how you achive this goal and fend off players who are constantly running back from their spawn room or Sunderrer (a truck) Mobile Spawnpoint. This is the hard part about this is the route that you take to do this.
First off, there are 3 factions who each have their own benefits, art style, and specalizations.
The Vanu Sovreignty (VS) are a spandex peoples who believe that technology is the most important thing when it concerns the evolution of society. Their weapons boast little bullet drop, and quick reload speeds. They also have some AOE guns (exploding plasma shots).
The New Conglomerate (NC) are the liberators, fighting for freedom. They have low fire rates with hard hitting weapons combined with huge magazines. Just be prepared for the rediculous reload times. Also the NC are VERY fond of shotguns.
The Terran Republic (TR) are fighting for something (justice I think???). They have high fire rates and are very fond of chainguns.
Personally I specialize in being a close range infiltrator (they have lower health but have sheilds). SMGs while expensive, are excellent killing machines. The other classes are the light and heavy infantry, engineer, medic, and MAX. Each class has it's specific guns, abilities, and uses.
The difficult thing about Planetside 2 is that positioning is vitally important. After about 250 hours I started getting the flow of the game. By 400 hours I was finally starting to mantain a KD above 1. This game has a steep learning curve and will take a lot of getting used to. However, I see the 500+ hours completely worth it and can't wait till summer so I can play this a lot more.

Planetside 2 is a very open multiplayer fps where you will see battles of 100+ players fighting over an objective or base, which may take hours to finish. Which brings to another good point. Planetside 2's battles never truely end. It's a constant war between three main factions vying for territory control in four massive maps (As of rite now there are four main maps which there may be more at a later date) and even when one faction controlls the majority of the map that map is locked and the battle continures elswhere. All items excluding cosmetics are obtainable though the in game currency gained by playing the game. My only note with this is the currency can be quite grindy to get if you wanted to purchase bigger things like vehicle attachments, and heavy weapons. Playing with friends is quite enjoyable in this game and to me makes those big battles much more fun. If you play by yourself you can join squads and platoons to decrease the likelyhood of you getting squashed by a band of enemies ambushing you on a road. (small battles can erupt almost anywhere which adds lots of variety in where your fighing in the map. For example you could be fighting in a vast open grasslands or in a small chokehold inside a dessert canyon) Some things do need a little balancing from vehicles and ground based combat, but I feel in time it will be really close and fair in it's gameplay. Overall Planetside 2 delivers exactly what I think it set out to accomplish. Really expansive and open fps combat with massive amounts of players. If that sounds like it interests you in the slightest then I recommend this game. After all this is free to play and won't cost you a penny to get in on the action.

Wolfenstein is back.  After the very disappointing 2009 game I thought the series was done for.  Not only did Bethesda bring it back in style, they showed the world how to make a modern oldschool FPS.  The New Order is fast, over the top, lengthy, and oozes style.
The New Order takes place in an alternate history where the Nazis won WWII.  It has a retro-futuristic vibe with some very advanced technology, but still styled after the time period.  While it is highly implausable, it's a very interesting world to explore and there are lots of newspaper stories scattered throughout the game you can read to learn more about it.  They even went and recorded German versions of classic music to fit in with the alternate history timeline.
The game plays like an amalgamation of the best parts of classic and moderns games, combining fast satisfying gunplay, clever and interesting level design, quality graphics, great story and voice acting, and a long campaign.  You can duel wield shotguns and rocker launchers to fight giant mechanical dogs.  You can even sneak around stealthily and silently stab enemies with your knife.  After all the carnage is done, you still get a great story and voice acting.
Two things I greatly enjoyed about the game that I'd like to point out are the health system which is a hybrid regenerating / non-regenerating health system.  Your health only regenerates up to the next increment of 20 and you have to find health packs to heal any more.  This helps avoid the modern game design trap of having to duck behind cover constantly to regenerate health while also avoiding the oldschool game design trap of finding yourself helpless if you take too much damage.  The other element I wanted to point out is the almost complete lack of quicktime events (I believe there are two in the whole game.)  At least one developer realizes how terrible they are.
The only drawback I found with the game is the difficulty.  Even on Über difficulty the majority of enemies don't hit very hard and there are tons of health packs around.  The only really dangerous ones are the heavily-armored shotgun-wielding troopers because they have ricocheting ammunition that's nearly impossible to avoid.  There are a few special unlockable game modes however, some of which will offer a larger challenge for those who want it.
The other issue which may concern some people is that this game runs on the id Tech 5 engine, and hence is very prone to texture popping.  The textures are much higher quality than in RAGE however so don't expect a big blur of compression artifacts when looking at objects up close.  I also experienced pretty serious stuttering if I dropped below 60 fps but it wasn't too difficult to keep the game at 60 on my system.
I heartily recommend Wolfenstein The New Order.  It's the most fun I've had with an FPS in quite some time and well worth playing.  I hope it serves as an example to other developers and publishers on how to make an FPS.

Age of Empires 2 is, without a doubt, my favorite game of all time. Its not just nostalgia talking, either. It may lack a few quality-of-life features that more modern RTS like Starcraft 2 have, and the meta has been relatively unchanged for almost the lifespan of the game (Although, the new expansion changed it up a lot, and fan made balance mods are quite popular, so look out for those if playing online) but it still stands as a masterpiece of the RTS genre in both mechanics and single player creative value. It still has a pretty big online playerbase for a 15 year old game, too.
Now, dont expect a huge new overhaul for the HD version. Its pretty much just a widescreen mode and a resolution bump, a new largest pop cap at 500 and a new larger map size, "Ludakris", but there are tons of good texture and unit packs in the workshop if you want your game to look a bit more shiny than a 1999 release title :p
The issues, however, are noticeable. The game does not run very well for its age. Now, just speculation, I think that may have to do with the fact that it cant use more than one CPU core at a time. This problem only gets more noticeable when you add more players, higher population caps and larger maps, and more AI players. Playing a 4v4 on a Ludakris size map can tank your framerate VERY easily. Now, I dont really see that as a huge issue myself, but it may♥♥♥♥♥♥off other people, and understandably so.
Still, these problems aren’t too terribly huge. AoE 2 is still a fantastic game, and one that is worthy of any RTS fan's time.

My Review:
Setting/Story - The third part of the series takes place in Brazil. Some players might see this as a poor decision to relocate the hero outside of New Jersey, but there was really no way to create a new story in the same setting. There are a few parts that take place in Panama and New Jersey in order to spice things up. The story could have been improved. The first Max Payne was well written. Wife and kid were killed by a junkie, kill all junkies and their suppliers. In the third part, Max Payne is hired to protect a rich family in Brazil that he does not really like... So there is a fundamental problem here. Who does Max Payne care for in this part? The blonde bimbo sister? The brunette bimbo sister? The spastic brother in law? The people of Brazil? We don't really know...
3/5
Shooting - Max Payne is known for the bullet time action. However, there have been a few changes in each part. In the first Max Payne you were limited to the "Dive" bullet time. The second one added more options for bullet time, and in the third they expanded even more. This is where the problems occur... The environment in this game is a lot more complex (due to the taking cover feature) and it stops you from using the dive bullet time efficiently. Not only that, but even the last chance bullet time is bugged due to objects that stop you from turning around and spraying down your target. The part that was really impressive was the cover feature. Shooting baddies from behind a desk with no aim like a baddie is something that I could do all day/night long.
3/5
Graphics - Really impressive for the most part. The environment is rich with details and this adds to the shooting experience. Intense gun battles make wood and glass chunks fly all over the place creating an intense environment without really reducing the visibility. However, all these cool things make the game file uncool. If you have slow internet and you have to download the game. CYA HICK. You will need a pretty decent PC to run this baby, but it is worth it.
5/5
Overall - Straightforward third person shooter that will provide you with a few days/weeks of entertainment. Don't expect an open end world with puzzles and freedom. This is a classic hallway cleaner. Enjoy

Sums up this experience. Great when you haven't seen the cutscenes that "covers up" the load times, but when you just want to play the goddamn game, forget it. You'll be denied control 50% of the time playing in favor of small cutscenes. Even in the challenge and arcade modes it's the same since it's basically playing the story in small chapters. So Max moving from one area to the next will often to ♥♥♥♥ing always be a unskippable cutscene full of dialogue you've already heard. These can be anywhere from 5 seconds to 5 minutes.
The load times have proven to be complete bull. 3 minutes through a cutscene it will tell you it is still loading. But go back to the main menu and just resume from last checkpoint, bam, less than a minute.
Multiplayer has no lag compensation, no dedicated servers, no server browser, only matchmaking. The guy with the lowest latency wins. To make it even better it doesn't show pings. So you never know what to expect till you lie dead from a player that hadn't even entered your line of sight yet.
Weapon balance also feels broken, but that might be the lag at play. I still want to try it over LAN, which is, surprisingly, available. The character customization is fun. Lots of ugly mugs to put shades and scarves on.
It's crippled by the need to be a movie experience. It is undoubtedly fun the first time, the story is a good bit above the average; but by no means close to its precedessors. The new interpretation of Max Payne is grittier, more shallow, less likeable. Were the old Max has some self-awareness of the insanity of his story, this one will just spout dark/sarcastic metaphors using mostly stripclub and/or bar related nouns.
At a sale price it's worth it. The gunfights are fantastic, shame they don't like to let you enjoy them for long streaks.

After playing this game for about 136 hours now, I think I can review it now. :)
So lets begin....
Dirty Bomb and what is it?
Well Dirty Bomb is a first person shooter that is team and objective based. You goal is to defend the objective from being blown by a dirty bomb or the attackers planting the dirty bomb. Thus its name I believe.
The gameplay in terms of mouse and keyboard is superb, you can map the game to a controller via a third party program, but I don't recommend it at all in my humble opinion. What I like about this game is its humor, let me explain further.
The overall dialouge with each character is funny to me and I get enjoyment out of each mercenaries dialouge.
The balance of this game is way way better than when I first played two years ago. This game overall is what I'll consider to have a cult following or a small but dedicated community of a few 3,000 or so during peak hours.
The maps are well designed and the newest update has been nice so far when compared to its initial release back in June of 2015. I can say that this game is worth a try and consideration if looking for a alternative to cs:go if cs:go isn't your thing or you simply want to try something different. Like any multiplayer focused game, always be prepared to come across some rude players or teammate afk during matches and so forth with the shennagins.
In the end, I do recommend this game if and only if you have the time to invest in this game. As it can be a grindfest.
I have 1.45 million xp and am only level 10 after 136 hours which can be seen as a negative but doesn't take away from the overall feel and vibe of the game.
Not sure how long I will continue to play this game as it appears the community has gotten smaller since its 2015 release so as of writing this review on July 24, 2017 I might say goodbye to Dirty Bomb to focus on other games in my library.
But I will never forget the great times I've had in this game and thank Splash Damage for a good run and great game overall.
I give Dirty Bomb a 8.5 out of 10.

Ah, Portal 2! Y'know, it must have been really difficult to work out where to take the series after the first game. New puzzles, obviously, but what about Glados? What about the protagonist? How do you take a simple story (with great subtlety), and expand on it, without making it seem stupid (like most sequels)?
But wouldn't you know it, they did it! They gave us a new character AI to talk at you. They gave us Glados. They gave us the backstory to Glados. They gave us the backstory to Aperture Science. They expanded the world. The new song isn't as great as "Still Alive", but it's still sung with as much gusto.
Portal 2 also has a cooperative mode (which I suppose would be the sequel to the single-player campaign), which I haven't tried (because I generally don't do multiplayer), but it's certainly a step in the right direction.
Along with new puzzles, there are new mechanics, including different types of gels, different ways of moving around, and lasers. I wish there were more lasers. I love lasers.
So, yeah, great game, especially if you like multiplayer. Even if you don't, the main campaign is worth it, especially if you get the game on sale.

"Max Payne 3" is an awesome game. That's the bottom line.
Why? I'll tell in more detail. It's the same old MP, but then again it's very different, too. It's made by Rockstar instead of Remedy, and it's visibly a Rockstar game. And for me personally, Rockstar means top quality.
GAMEPLAY
Unlike most modern third-person shooters, MP3 harkens to the older days in some of the gameplay mechanics. Your health does NOT REGENERATE after a while. You have to use painkillers to restore health. Gone are the quick save function from the previous games, and MP3 introduces regular CHECKPOINTS which are pretty close in between - but due to the challenging difficulty and use of painkillers you have to be careful if, even if you survived, you want to continue or perhaps restart the checkpoint in order to do better and preserve more painkillers for later on.
Gone is also the comic book-style narration, and is replaced by CUTSCENES. There's plenty of them, and they're lengthy ones and extremely cinematic. As someone who considers Metal Gear Solid his favorite game, I was delighted. And rightfully so, because they're so well-directed and immersive. I don't even need to mention the stellar VOICE ACTING by all involved, but mostly - of course - the one and only James McCaffrey as the titular hero.
MP3 retains the BULLET TIME and SHOOTDODGE mechanics. It's just that they don't give you that much of an edge over your enemies. The bullet time depletes quickly, and its use is now a much more tactical affair than before.
A new mechanic is the brilliant LAST MAN STANDING. If killed with 1 or more painkillers in possession, time slows down as Max topples to the floor. In these few seconds you can aim at the guy who shot you, and if you kill him, you regain full health at the cost of 1 painkiller and your bullet time meter.
Max can now also remain PRONE endlessly, and shoot in all direction while down, until you chose to stand up.
MP3 introduces the COVER mechanic, also. This, I admit, could've been implemented a little better. As it is, its pretty rudimentary, but gets the job done and adds another dimension to the game.
Also making a first appearance in the franchise is the BLIND FIRE. And blind here really means that - blind. When blind firing, there's no reticle to show you even the general direction you're aiming at, so blind fire is largely guesswork.
The WEAPON EQUIPMENT has undergone a rather realistic change I've never seen before in video-games. You can carry 3 weapons: 2 one-handed weapons snugged into two shoulder holsters, and 1 two-handed weapon carried in the free  hand (+ you can dual-wield the 2 two-handed weapons). What confuses some players is the fact that, when wielding a one-handed weapon (for example a pistol) in the left hand, Max carries the two-handed weapon (let's say shotgun) in the other hand by the barrel (and can't fire it). But if you then select the other pistol in the other holster, the one for your right-hand, Max will drop the shotgun and then pull out that other pistol. The same goes if you chose to dual-wield your pair of one-handed weapons when currently holding a two-handed weapon - Max will discard the latter. In other words, there is no way to holster your two-handed weapon "for later".
The PHYSICS in this game are amazing, ranging from Max's animations as he leaps and collides and falls, to that of enemies (alive or dead) reacting to being shot with different weapons in different places. Marvelous.
And lastly, the DIFFICULTY. It's punishing, but I do like to dedicate my time fully to a game when I choose to play it, and I like a challenge, And MP3 is a challenge! I've only played on Hard and Hardcore difficulties, and the latter especially is unforgiving. A single bullet will most likely kill you, two will for sure. This makes some action set-ups later in the game truly a teeth-grinding experience, but it's not as impossible as some reviewers led me to believe. On the whole, it took me about 15 hours to beat the game the first time around (on Hard), and another 15 hours the second time (on Hardcore).
As for REPLAY-VALUE, there's plenty of it. There are little secrets to find during the gameplay, easter-eggs, as well as in-game achievements (called 'Grinds'), like "Kill 250 enemies with shotguns" and the likes. In addition to the STORY mode, there's ARCADE which offers Score Attack mode, a NY Minute (sort of time-trial) mode, Challenge mode, etc. And, of course, there's MULTIPLAYER (which I've not as of yet touched, so can't comment on that).
GRAPHICS
MP3 looks beautiful, in short. But it's also very customizable and well-optimized. Even on average hardware (like my HP ProBook 4740s laptop) I could play it on 720p, high details for everything, anisotropic filtering x 16, FSAA, V-sync on, with the framerate constantly ranging from 35-60.
SOUND
The soundtrack was made by a noise-rock band called HEALTH. I admit I was skeptical, since I couldn't envision how MP fit with noise-rock. But, HEALTH being smart as they are, didn't impose their musical style on MP. Instead, MP dictated their approach to the music. The result is an immensely powerful and epic score that adds another dimension to the whole experience (some scenes are unforgettable because of it), and is certainly one soundtrack that's worth getting to be listened stand-alone.
OVERALL: An amazing game all around, with very high production values. Along with "Spec Ops: The Line" my favorite TPS, and definitely in my Top #10 games of all time.

If you ever have played an FPS, you will know what to do by instinct. It has puzzels that unlock safes or hidden rooms that give you boosts or weapon upgrades. You have plenty of collectibles. Littered all over the world are newspaper clippings where you can learn more about the world around you. There are side-quests. It's all up to parr and forfills exactly what you expect and demand of a game like this.
But it's not the reason why you stay up and continue to play. That would be because Frau Engel must die. Painfully.

Fantastic game, 9/10.
Story: almost half of the game is consisted of narrative cinematics, giving you an insight of the situation and presenting the though processes of Max and his internal struggles as he uncovers a series of crude betrayals. voice acting is captivating and dialogues are well written.
Gameplay: brutal. One second you are watching a cinematic and a second later you are thrown into a room giving you 5 seconds to headshot 10 people or you die a merciless death. Unlike most modern shooters, there is no regenerative health, forcing you to be very aware of your situations and any reckless moves will cost you greatly. The AIs aren't necessarily the smartest, but they will try their best to flank you and shotgun you to the face. Even with his Bullet-Time skills, Max never felt too overpowered and still requires you to take cover and plan your moves accordingly.
Presentation: The game takes place in Brazil, and interestingly the developers decided to keep the game authentic and make all natives speak Spanish instead of broken English, and just like Max, your inability to understand what the people are saying makes you feel foreign and secluded, which makes the game that much more immersive.
Thoughts: for a 30+ GB installation, this is actually a rather short game, with just a bit over 12 hours of campaign. The gameplay is fairly linear and there really isn't much to explore. there are also occasional rag doll problems where you'll see Max flail his arm around and not being able to shoot anyone, giving you a frustrating death. Overall this game is incredibly well polished and enjoyable, highly recommended.
