What if Hitler had won the second world war?
This is the story in Wolfenstein: The New Order where Germany wins with strange superior weapons somehow made by the games antagonist in this alternate universe.
Gameplay wise Wolfenstein: The New Order doesn't run from its roots or tries hard to be something it isn't. Instead it embraces dual wielding assault rifles, and whatever you can think of would be in a Wolfenstein game is there. There is even the occasional stealth routine you can do, but you're not punished for simply taking out your biggest gun and start killing those evil nazi your way. All the weapons in the game also have their merit isn't thrown in just to be there, but all have their strengths and weaknesses. Despite having such relatively simple gameplay it is done really well, and I was entertained the entire way through this game, which was much longer than I first thought as well. The atmosphere also plays a part in this game, and really brings the world to life with nazi propaganda and presents you with a quite obscene future where nazi ideology rules the world.
If you're looking for a beautiful and fun FPS title Wolfenstein: The New Order should certainly be taken into consideration.

Today I am wearing lacy black underwear
For the sole purpose of knowing I am wearing them.
And underneath that?
I am absolutely naked.
And I’ve got skin. Miles and miles of skin;
I’ve got skin to cover all my thoughts
like saran wrap that you can see through
to what leftovers are inside from the night before.
And despite what you might think, my skin is not rough; nor is it bullet proof.
My skin is soft, and smooth, and easily scarred.
But that doesn’t matter, right?
You don’t care about how soft my skin is.
You just want to hear about what my fingers do in the dark.
But what if all they do is crack open windows?
So I can see lightening through the clouds.
What if all they crave is a jungle gym to climb for a taste of fresher air?
What if all they reach for is a notebook or a hand to hold?
But that’s not the story you want.
You are licking your lips and baring your teeth.
Just once I would like to be the direction someone else is going.
I don’t need to be the water in the well.
I don’t need to be the well.
But I’d like to not be the ground anymore.
I’d like to not be the thing people dig their hands in anymore.
Some girls know all the lyrics to each other’s songs.
They find harmonies in their laughter.
Their linked elbows echo in tune.
What if I can’t hum on key?
What if my melodies are the ones nobody hears?
Some people can recognize a tree,
A front yard, and know they’ve made it home.
How many circles can I walk in before I give up looking?
How long before I’m lost for good.
It must be possible to swim in the ocean of the one you love without drowning.
It must be possible to swim without becoming water yourself.
But I keep swallowing what I thought was air.
I keep finding stones tied to my feet.

Max Payne 3 tem ótima jogabilidade, trilha sonora boa, um enredo interessante (com algumas influências claras de filmes famosos) , gráficos bons e física bem trabalhada. Quanto a ambientação, o jogo se passa no brasil, em SP especificamente, e como brasileiro, não dá pra deixar de perceber algumas gafes cometidas, como as favelas parecerem que são do Rio, e não de São Paulo, ou até msm referências de camisetas de times cariocas nas favelas de SP. Também tem a questão da dublagem, que está até bem feita, mas vc ouve coisas meio bisonhas como "you're gonna die, meu camarada", o que soa estranho para nós. Mas, no fim, o trabalho feito pela Rockstar foi positivo, como se é de esperar, sem dizer que um fazer um jogo que se passa totalmente no nosso país já é um passo a frente na indústria dos vídeos games para nós, tupiniquins. Vale a pena sim: no nosso caso, além de se divertir, dá pra analisar a visão estrangeira sobre alguns aspectos e esteriótipos do Brasil.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

Max Payne 3 is one of the greatest third-person shooters I have ever played. Max Payne 3 is also hindered by gaping flaws that might turn many people off. It is an absolute riot when the game actually gives you control. The game is moving constantly, implementing loading sequences in the cutscenes themselves. It is fast paced, brutally violent, and very satisfying. Unfortunately, the game is also rife with problems, including unskippable cutscenes, DRM, and poor writing.
Pros:
+ Wonderful gameplay and mechanics. Very smooth and almost bug-free, the gameplay complements the fast pace of the sequence of events. Although Rockstar has changed quite a few mechanics, like the addition of taking cover and the exclusion of jumping, the game still feels very straight-forward and simply Max Payne: shoot the bad guys in very stylistic ways. Although there are collectibles scattered around, the game usually doesn't encourage exploration either, which is good for the pace (even though I miss it).
+ Amazing engine. The physics are impressive (if you've seen a ragdoll in this game rolling down a flight of stairs, you'll know what I mean) and the violence is superb and satisfying. Not many games pay such attention to violence, and I really appreciate Rockstar's implementations here.
+ Great graphics. The game has a lot of attention to detail and so many different props and things to shoot, it's incredible. You can also see wrinkles moving on Max's clothing.
Cons:
- Unskippable cutscenes. Why do we see so many games that allow you to skip every cutscene, yet MP3 was not able to pull this off? I doubt some parts are actually loading, because the skip button appears at the exact same moment every time...and I've played this game through about ten times now. The first time playing, the cutscenes are nice, but this game is so fun that I want to keep playing it, and I don't want to watch the cutscenes every time. (there are even cutscenes you can't skip in the arcade modes. What the hell?)
- Poor writing. For those that are looking for a simliar quality of writing to the first two Max Payne games, you'll have to look elsewhere. Writing in this game is pretty bad and comes off like the writers were trying too hard to capture Max's true essence. Instead, dialogues and monologues are mostly cringe-worthy and are not up to par to Remedy's fantastic work.
Closing: I don't have much else to say. This is a very fun game when you are actually playing it. The constant cutscenes might turn some people off, but the first time playing was pretty fun and engaging - I really didn't mind at all. A very solid third-person shooter. All future shooters should take examples off of the sheer detail in this game, especially the violence.

Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I did not see this coming.  When I first saw the trailers of this game and the initial gameplay reveal during E3 2013, I almost immediately wrote it off as another half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥attempt to cash in on the Wofenstein name.  Boy, was I wrong.  Not only does the gameplay feel perfectly matched to the legacy of this game, but the story is surprisingly adult and mature without relying on the standard "mature" cliches and tropes (although there certainly ARE some there; lots of cursing, lots of blood, two sequences of fairly explicit sex, etc).  Somehow, the writers at Machine Head were able to take B.J. Blazkowitz, one of the most cliche and two-dimentional characters in all of gaming history, and make him feel like a living breathing human with wants, needs, memories, hope; the list goes on.  The dialong is some of the best-written I've heard in a game period.  All of the characters talk like real people and no line comes across as cheesy or poorly delivered.  Actually, I should talk about the background characters too.  Every character is driping with human personality.  From the lowly Nazi guard in a labor camp to a lovable invalid to a former Nazi-turned resistance fighter (who has an extremely simpathetic and beliveable backstory, might I add) to the Nazi leaders who want to see you squirm to even B.J.'s obligatory love interest.  Every character feels perfectly fleshed out and doing so just adds to the deep, oppressive atmosphere of the game.
I've gone on about the story long enough.  The gameplay is surprisingly satisfying.  Each gun feels weighty and powerful; Automatic rifles fire with a mechanical "chunk chunk chunk" as you see your foes torn into equally powerful-looking pieces, shotguns feel like a dragon breathing fire, mounted guns feel like giant buzzsaws of death.  Most weapons even have the ability to be dual-wielded for even more shooty fun (including knives and shotguns.  Yes, you can dual-wield shotguns) and most weapons even have alt-fire modes that you can unlock later in the game.  The assault rifle has a mounted grenade launcher, the shotgun has bouncy shells which basically turns this gun into the flak cannon from Unreal Tournament and the pistols have attachable suppressors.  There is also a stealth system in the game, but it's not very fleshed out as you can just sneak up behind any enemy and stab him in his little German throat without anyone else noticing, the Nazi's won't notice you unless you are RIGHT in their line of sight, if they DO notice you and you hide behind a trash bin, they won't gome to investigate it and if the alarm DOES get sounded, every Nazi in a 3-mile radius will find you.  The only other things that don't work in this game are the upgrade system and the multi-choice system.  The upgrade system unlocks various perks for various things by doing very specific things (get X-many headshots with an assault rifle, stab Y-many Nazis, etc.).  However, the main problem with this is that these are all things that you'd do in-game normally.  They don't really make you try new playstyles and just feels pointless.  The multi-choice system basically stems from one choice that you make about an hour into the game and the only things that chance are either an upgrade to your health or armor, some different characters show up and some lines of dialog are different.  Nothing else changes and it feels like it was put in to add some variety and replay value without really changing anything.
That being said, if you want an old-school feeling shooter with a truly adult story, then you could do a HELL of a lot worse than Wolfenstein: The New Order.

This is my favourite RTS game of all time, besides Age of Mythology. If you're a fan of the genre, love history and the idea of team-based or lone wolf style gameplay, then this is up your alley. For most, this game is a nostalgic gem which I can relate to.
The idea of the game is to progress through a series of ages (dark, feudal, castle and imperial) with a selected civilization, which has their own traits and bonuses. Each age will advance your economical, technological and military branches, as you construct multiple units to create a large society and become a powerful civilization, potentially overthrowing your opponents via battles, wealth and scavenged resources. However, if you're playing with a team mate, you can also combine both societies in order to further aid one another, especially offensive or defensively if opponents raid your village(s). Another important task is the trade system with markets, as sharing between two or more allies is important for resource income, which can boost your economical status and allows you to produce more units and massive armies.
There are a wide variety of scenarios to choose from - whether it be the hot desert of Arabia, the eerie woodlands of the Black Forest, or the accessible seas of the Norse Lands where navy battles can occur. There's a map for everyone, each with their own style and resource contents. Also when you load up a scenario, there's a 25% chance it will be any season (i.e. summer or winter.)
The AI in game are relatively smart, but certainly not clever. Every game once they manage to reach the Feudal Age and build a market, the computer's focus is the constant production of gold and food using the market so that they can reach the Imperial Age very quickly. I find that to be rather silly and unfocused, especially if you want to build a tough economy first with lots of villagers and gradually make your way through each age. That way you have lots of resources in the end to generate plenty of military units and upgrades. However, gameplay style on this part will vary when playing online, as you'll never know what strategy your enemies could be planning. One thing to remember is that you can switch between two AI modes in the lobby, the other being 'Original AI'.
In conclusion, Age of Empires II is a fantastic RTS game whether you're playing alone or online, and it will provide hours of fun.

This is (I believe) my third review for this game. Hopefully I'll be able to update it as the time goes on.
Dirty Bomb is a free to play FPS from the developer Splash Damage. If this name sounds familiar, you've probably played some of their older games, including Wolfenstein: Enemy Territory(W:ET) or Enemy Territory: Quake Wars(ET:QW). Sure, there are many more games they developed and/or contributed to, but those are in my opinion the most famous ones. I used to play W:ET few years back and it was great fun. If you're not familiar with the game, it was /and still is/ objective based FPS (steal documents, escort truck/tank, destroy barriers) - sounds familiar? Dirty Bomb is basically W:ET's successor - but this time in London with more variety of characters with abilities.
• Art style
• Characters
• Multi objective maps
• Gameplay
• Active YouTube channel with weelky dev videos and trailers
• New content coming at a faster rate than before
• Events like Double Credits, Double ranked points, First edition week...
• Crafting system is still bad. It's been too long.
• Bugs, that are in game for months/years.
• Menu is slow, case opening is choppy
• Dirty Bomb's merch STILL isn't avaible for purchase
• Unfair, unrewarding bigger events with exclusive content that's impossible to get unless you pay real money or play 5+ hours every day unless you're super lucky.
Dirty Bomb is truly unique game. Not only because of it's fun gameplay (and other pros I wrote), but it was also capable to retain my attention for so long. No multiplayer FPS ever did that before (most of them are pay to win and / or boring).
But 2020 London has some issues too (other than that Jackal v CDA war going on) - some annoying bugs are present for far too long and crafting system needs to go ASAP.
Dirty Bomb DEV team is still hiring new people and you can see it's paying off - faster map and merc development, more bugfixes.
But it feels like certain things still require more people or attention, because devs are active on reddit, answer to questions but it doesn't reflect that in game.
Game should leave Open Beta in 2018, so hopefully the most "pain in the a**" issues will be resolved.
Overall, I'm not sure if there is any other free 2 play FPS that is so fun and not pay 2 win.
So give it a try! :-)

Let me start out by saying that I loved Max Payne 1 and 2...I didn't expect a sequel after number 2, (after all it was nearly 10 years prior)...and holy ♥♥♥♥ it should have stayed that way...
Max Payne 3 is a complete disgrace to the whole series! The last two were set as dark, and a bit edgy, action thrillers, (even if number 2 was trying a little too hard sometimes), but in this one, it's set mostly during the daytime, in some of the most bright and colourful settings on offer, Max Payne this time around sounds more like the writing of a 13 year old emo fan fiction interpretation of what max payne should be, it attempts to be "artsy" by makeing the game screen flicker and blur every so often during the cutscenes, which do in fact run for longer than the actual ♥♥♥♥ing gameplay as well as having random words from the dialogue pop up in captions, and if that wasn't enough, a good chunk of the dialogue is in spanish, and there is NO OPTION FOR TRANSLATING IT! Max isn't really likable this time around, in fact he seems just as much of a cardboard cut-out as the rest of the "characters" in a story that's so far removed from the previous two, that to make it feel at all like a Max Payne game, they have to reference what happened occasionally, otherwise you'd just think you were playing a poor mans copy of a hybrid of hitman and kane and lynch. And remember the bullet time shoot dodging in the last two? That is available in this one, although it's horribly executed. You snap out of bullet time if you dive into ANY solid object, it feels clumsy and delayed, and it feels like the developers are pushing the player to use the cover system more than anything else...yes, you heard right...the blood opera shoot dodge style has more or less taken a back seat to cover based combat. Don't get me wrong, I have nothing against cover systems, but in a Max Payne game? That's kind of like having a knitting mini game in a Mortal Kombat game...but the nail that seals the coffin shut is the quicktime events...I can't even believe I'm writing this...Max Payne now has quicktime events. It almost didn't seem real...
This game is a great tragedy too, the graphics are good, and the attention to details that went into the weapon mechanisms and how much stuff you can shoot up is good, but that could have been used in a much better game to feel much more at home. It's not charming, it has long lost the noir feel, when you're first introduced to most of the main characters in the game, the main feeling towards almost every single one of them is "who is this? and why the hell should I care about them?" A game is generally meant to engage your mind, give you a challenge to overcome, make you want to press on, reward you for overcoming said challenge, and if done right, make you want to play it again. Rockstar? What the hell happened? Most of your previous games were pushing the bounderies in terms of playability and mature content, but this? A good half of the game just feels like stock, recycled plot, characters and gameplay, there are a few good things that work, but the flaws? They grossly out-do any fun or enjoyment that could have been had. Please learn the lesson that Valve needed to learn with half life 2...good graphics does not a game make, and it's even worse when you♥♥♥♥♥♥on a series that was so well loved by so many people.
Some might agree with me, some might not, but all I can say is, if you truly loved Max Payne 1 and 2, then stay as far away from this trainwreck as possible, it will almost ruin great memories of a once great franchise.

Stands out amongst the numerous multiplayer focused fps' which include weak single player campaigns. This is single player only and you can feel the sheer amount of effort and gloss that has been applied. The story is B-movie stock which when looked at as a whole might raise an eyebrow but it's action beats, charicatures and enviroments are simply propped up by the plot and for them it is worth it, The voice acting is superb, the set pieces exciting and feel natural(such as the mecha dog chase scenes.)
The weapons are all a pleasure and the perk system (quite novel for a SP game) encourages you to play with them all rather than getting your hands on your favourite and ignoring the rest. The perk system does a great job of spicing things up, perks that encourage duel wielding or cover based headshots force you to change your playstyle if you want to claim them all which helps prevent the whole experience becomming stale. Another element that helps in that regard is the openess of the levels, while not reinventing the corridor shooter philosophy simply giving the oppertunity to have more than one path (2 or 3 in most cases) is a godsend. The element of control and desicion making for the player forces you to stop and contemplate how to proceed rather than blindly charging through the enviroment. It really makes you apprieciate the gameplay and map design with even a few routes.
Now I have to admit the visuals are excellent but I played this on both my laptop with a nvidia laptop gpu and my gaming pc with AMD. I found the game ran better with my laptop! apparently there are some issues with ATI gpu's I had stuttering a few times after I toned down all the effects and an annoying lip sync error that I removed by uninstalling the latest beta catalyst drivers. I am a bit dissapointed that a lack of testing for ATI gpu's and that an obvious issue hasn't been fixed after release. The game still ran well but with many of the effects toned down to much lower than my machine could handle and it was a bit dissapointing to have to do that, expecting the best performance and visuals from my dedicated gaming desktop. Another disspointment goes to the lack of varitey of weapons, quite early on you get to test out the old WWII weapons then afterwards the modern day equivelents and...that was it. Sure you get a shotgun and a rocket launcher etc but I felt like a variety of pistols or assault rifles would have been great to spice up the weapon choice but I do love the old school choice of allowing you to carry all these weapons at one time. THis feature is sorely missed in new games since Halo pinoeered the limited weapon carry.
All in all this is a great single player action experience and a welcome return. Marred by some optimization issues depending on your system set up and a bit of a floaty plot that fails to bring any emotional response (not for lack of trying!) is otherwise a steller title with excellent ensemble or characters, lovingly retro fps game design and action that'll keep you hooked.

Months before the game's release I thought this would be a good game, yet basic like the other one's within the franchise.  Shoot everything, kill bosses, defeat the Nazi's, for a lack of better statement on it. What happened in the nearing months to release & my complete time with the game astounded me.
It beat what I expected of a modern FPS game. Leaning, dual wielding, great accuracy when hipfiring, different classes of attack for each gun, stealth (What!? In a Wolf game? What the hell is this game?) that actually works great, & lastly, open missions while still linear. Basically you can take multiple paths but it still goes in the same direction, I loved trying things new in approach with my differing playthroughs.

It worked well with my Nvidia GTX 670m & Intel Core I7 - 3610qm laptop running on Windows 7 amazingly on everything on ultra - 30+ FPS. I recently switched to Windows 8.1 & did my second playthrough of the game on Uber difficulty. There is stutter every 10 or so seconds SOMETIMES, & if it does happen, mainly in combat. The GeForce 344.11 drivers decreased that annoyance but didn't remove it completely.
One thing I did notice within the performance matter was the fact that close-up-in-game character interactions decreased frames way more than being in hectic combat. The character details are very, very beautiful. With every wrinkle and every skin imperfection visible in conversation, it was obvious why the performance drops were happening.
I was blown away at the fact that I actually cared for the characters in a Wolfenstein game. I won't spoil anything here, but let's just say that the character development was absolutely gripping. People had backstories, I wanted to learn more about everyone, even the villains.
The best cutscene in the game so far both emotionally and gripping in itself was
Please keep in mind that character development from everything before this is key, watching this now before playing up to that point won't spoil anything but it won't give as much of an emotional effect as if you did play up to that point.
You watch and play as this group of characters progresses, has ups and downs with personal life and life backstories & you also can piece parts of the story together by finding collectibles and reading news articles within the game. I definitely recommend doing that as the story is gripping and provides insight into why, and how the Nazi's rule the world.
Playing in a world where the Nazi's won the World War's was depressing, but at the same time technically & architecturally amazing. If that could be stated as a true alternate reality anyway, in itself it was marvellous.
As I said initially, I cared for the characters & almost cried at the end. Watch the character development, engross yourself in the ever expanding environments and how they affect the characters themselves and you will be having similar emotions. All this is even subconsciously happening while you play by the way, just like every other game. So even if you want to look for the story & character development, it just happens. No need to look for it within cutscenes.
Wolfenstein: The New Order is a fresh take on the FPS genre & provides an overall great experience. There are some performance issues on Windows 8.1, but the lack of persistence with said performance issues means that it doesn't pull too much away from the game. Wolfenstein: The New Order beats many games this year, is the biggest surprise of the year & is Game Of The Year for me.

This is what happens when you give a series to a development team that had nothing to do with the earlier entries and basically give them a small sheet of paper with some basic gameplay mechanics, and a note saying "cast James McCaffrey as the title character": A game that doesn't feel like Max Payne, doesn't play like Max Payne, and actively punishes you for trying to play Max Payne. Oh, and don't forget needing to sign up for some obnoxious PC-only DRM service because Rockstar expects its paying customers to be treated like untrustworthy criminals! At least the PC version has some nice enhancements. Sure, they're only in the graphics department, and maybe in being able to actually customize controls assuming the console versions have that feature removed for no reason.
After this, you get to watch a long, unskippable cutscene that tells you "game is still loading!" if you try to skip it... all before you're allowed to get to the main menu.
Want to watch it again, so you can see the story when you're not just trying to set up your controls and graphical settings? I hope you're technically inclined enough to find the .bnk file in the install directory, otherwise you can forget about that.
You're given a bland onslaught of in-your-face tutorials during the first chapter because clearly people who play games are too stupid to learn basic mechanics on their own, or in a separate tutorial- an option Remedy's titles offered. You're also given an introduction to the horrendous input lag this title has! Press a button to move, and Max pauses before doing so. Let go of the button, and Max keeps going for a second before deciding to stop. Try to shootdodge, and Max will pause before the effect actually begins. Everything feels delayed, even the simplest things like mouse movement. (I refuse to try using a controller to see if it's more responsive. I didn't buy a PC game to play with a controller. Outside of vehicle-related games, that's a bit like buying an HDTV to watch VHS cassettes on.)
Get used to seeing cutscenes, as there are a lot of them. Out of the playing time that's surely displayed with this review, I've probably gotten to spend under half of that in actual gameplay. I had bad flashbacks to Inversion while playing with the amount of "30 seconds of gameplay between multi-minute cutscenes" that was going on! Inversion at least had the benefit of not being a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ization of an existing series of games. The rest is cutscene, cutscene, cutscene, with obnoxious and pointless effects plastered everywhere. Color desyncing, scanlines, freeze-frame of Max's face pushed to the side, the multiple-PiP effect of 24 fame, flashing lights, certain words that were
needlessly printed to the screen... It's constant, erratic, and nauseating, especially when you're trying to actually
. Thanks Rockstar, I appreciate being given migraines when I try to play your games. There's also a strange anomaly regarding the cutscenes: each one phases between pre-rendered and real-time rendering for no particular reason. (This is most noticeable if you have recording software that reports framerate running, as the pre-rendered are thankfully very high quality despite the graphics clearly being below what the real-time graphics are capable of. Pre-rendered cutscenes "run" at an incredibly higher framerate than the real-time cutscenes.)
Remember how I said the game punishes you for trying to play it as if it were a Max Payne game? Veterans of the series will see, in the rare gameplay segment, that trying to remain mobile and use bullet time and shootdodging will end up getting you killed as quickly as standing in an inferno. Instead, you're clearly expected to cling to cover like some Gears of War/Kill.Switch player and play it that way- including switching back to your main gun from your pistol because you're most likely in this situation straight out of a cutscene.
A few more horrendous gameplay changes are ones clearly decided upon because Rockstar wanted to make an Xbox game out of a historically PC-based series. Gone is Max's ability to hold an arsenal of weaponry and grenades that provide a variety of options for how to shoot up the next mook. Gone are even the names of the weapons! Max can now only hold two pistols, with the option to use either one of the two, or dual wield them (Ingram-style machine pistols count for this). You can pick up a two-handed weapon, but if it runs out of ammo or you want another two-handed, you have to drop the gun. If you get into a cutscene, you will have to switch back because you're forced to use a pistol again. Your weapon selection is a radial menu, clearly designed for a joystick. Painkillers now take effect near-instantly rather than healing over time, but it doesn't really matter since unless you're huddled behind cover like a generic modern TPS game your health's going to run low just as fast anyway.
Run out of health, but have painkillers? Rockstar took a page from Call of Duty's book like so many other unoriginal people and give you a variation of "last stand" - kill the person who "killed" you and you get to stand back up. Fun! Challenging! Pointless!
Oh, and your ability to quicksave or save from the menu where
would like? Rockstar ignored that idea too. Can't give
much control to the player, right?
Overall, someone unfamiliar with the previous entries in the franchise and can stomach the awful input lag (or the thought of playing a PC game with a controller) might enjoy this, so long as constant cutscenes with nauseating effects aren't a problem. As a fan of the older games, and someone who just went through the entirety of Max Payne 2 again, I have to say this is the
Fall of Max Payne. My only consolation was I spent less than $5 on this thing during a sale, because I don't think I can be bothered to go any further.

tl,dr: A reasonably good game though not a big step forward for the series. Worth picking up for a few bucks (more if you like Max) but there are probably better games out there if the hammy dialogue doesn't appeal to you.
Max Payne is not the kind of series everyone can enjoy. It's chiched, over-the-top noir characterization of the greiving cop protagonist is played surprisingly straight and might be too brooding for some people. The first game(MP1) set the psycho-drama in motion by killing off pretty much everyone Max Payne cares about... although since it was in the beginning, there was little reason for the player to care, so Mp1 was mostly a revenge shooter draped in noir on the snowy deserted street of NY. Still, even the attempt at a plot and some stylistic cut-scenes set it apart from most shooters... that and bullet-time, of course. What is now a standard convention was largely started by Mp1, where Max would run through a door and create a slow-motion ballet of death with bullets dancing through the air as he floated cinematically. I can still remember watching bullets spiral and handgun slides reciprocate in slow motion, an impressive graphical feat at the time. Mp2 was the "Fall of Max Payne" but it had characters that developed and were worthy of caring instead of having them introduced just to get killed for an informed motive (as in the first game). By the end Max is able to make emotional connections again even though the betrayal and death of those he cared about.
Unfortunately, in the world of Mp3 the second game might as well have not existed.Mona, the interest of the second game (who died or lived depending on the difficulty setting) is relegated to someone Max wanted to grief-bang, despite her being a compelling character with more than one dimension in Mp2. Max has gone backwards to where he was at the end of the first game, losing the interesting development he underwent. Cheap way to a sequel.
The plot of MP3 is somewhat convuluted, perhaps purposefully so. Unlike the first two games, this plot is not about Max; instead he's a badly working cog in a stupidly created conspiracy, with little individual motivation. There are lots of different characters and organizations that are difficult to tell apart. It's sometimes difficult to figure out who is trying to kill you at any given moment. To be fair, this is the usual with the series and not a big problem to me. Worse is the fact that there are many cutscenes you cannot skip in the regular game mode (because it's 'loading). The reality is that this loading is not optimized for higher-end computers and is implemented poorly. I'd rather see a 'loading' screen for 10 seconds than have to watch the same cutscene 3 times. MP3 is also bad about letting the player quit; particularly galling is when the annoying 'last stand' mode is activated so you get one last shot at the enemy but Max is placed in such a way that he can't possibly succeed... you still have to wait and wait to die instead of loading.
MP3 seems to be a case of the devs throwing everything at a wall to see what sticks. There's the now-ubiquitous bullet-time that has been badly gimped by the fact that Max now crumples into vulnerability whenever he touches a wall or other object. Instead they (of course) added a cover system, which takes away much of the beauty of the combat the previous games displayed. Naturally to balance the cover the enemies are more numerous and harder, making it difficult to play like Mp2, particularly because if you're trying to move through a room you keep running into waist-high cover barricades. Regardless of if you're on easy or hardcore, there are some spikes in difficulty throughout the game that get annoying. The game also promotes a console like system of changing weapons that doesn't work well; speaking of which, cutscenes often have Max switching to a pistol for no reason other than to frustrate the player once the scene is over. Cutscenes in general have Max acting very incompetent and tend to be at odds with the rest of the game.
Max occasionally has a 'partner' in his travels who is useless except to demand the player 'hurry up' every fifteen seconds. This is annoying and gives bad pacing to these levels. Speaking of which, developers who put 'collectables' in a game and then demand that you push through without looking around should be put in the stocks (Mafia 2 devs, you're next). The guns are varied and look great as usual, with some nice nods to the setting like changing the ubiqitous Beretta to its Brazilian Taurus brand. Shotguns are comically ineffective at anything but close range, which is unrealistic to anyone who has seen a pattern of buckshot at 15 yards, but this may be a balancing mechanic.
I find it disjointing that after a gunfight even though he's standing, Max clearly should be dead judging from the bullet holes all over his chest. It's really silly looking and immersion-breaking. Better ways to represent this would be visual impacts to a kevlar vest (Max gets one at one point but leaves it behind for some reason) or maybe to have non-lethal wounds look "grazing" and treat health more like "luck" so that only the last round results in a lethal-looking wound (since this is how the game treats it anyway). There is a dissonant part of the game where Max is wounded in the arm in a cutscene and suddenly is near death, despite being shot in the chest every other minute. While the game lampshades this a bit, it reflects how poorly the wounding mechanic works.
The graphics are quite good, the gore is in place with the Max Payne world and the settings were masterfully done. The desolate noir New York of Max Payne was great for its time, but we've moved past the technical limitations that made it so useful for the development. While Mp3 spends a little time back there, most of the game is spent in a beautiful and well-renditioned Brazil. There is no magical English-speaking here, so unless you speak Portugese you're out of luck... just like Max, a gringo out of water. The world is well-populated and feels gritty without having the 'brown tint' of some other shooters. I will say the stylized "Man on fire" visual effects got to be a bit much.
Is MP3 a good sequel? Eh. In terms of characters and plot, the second game probably should have ended the series. At least the writers should have done better than rebooting back to the first game, which is basically what happened. But it's not terrible as a sequel and it is a good game. James McCaffrey again does a great job voicing Payne and most of the other actors are good, as well. It's a beautiful looking game that recaptures a lot of the feeling of the first two games and even if it doesn't really expand the series, fans will probably enjoy it. That's why, even though there's a lot of criticism above, I still find myself drawn to it even after finishing. Non-fans of the series could probably find better products in the genre although it is a good chunk of gameplay that can be had often for a bargain price.

An absolute blast, and a true successor to the Wolfenstein legacy.
Mac Gameplay First Impression - Written review below
The gunplay is top notch, true for many id games, and it's simply in a league ahead of others FPS games of the last few years.
It's rather astounding  what they managed to do with the rather old idTech 5 engine that still runs OpenGL 3.2.
The story is gripping, and hooks you in right from the start. Mixing fast paced action, and detailed plot to keep the player engaged the entire time.
My only issues with the game are purely down to the engine. Sadly Crossfire support is only there in fullscreen mode, and with some Profile tweaking in the drivers. Which means if you run the game in windowed mode one of your GPUs is disabled. Not an issue for many, but it means streamers and people recording gameplay lose a substantial amount of performance, and game detail as a result.
The other issue is good ole texture popping, even after RAGE and the creation of MegaTextures, the issue is still there. Even with two GPUs with 6GB of VRAM each.
Even so, it doesn't take away from the gameplay and excitement at all. It simply plays brilliantly, and I would happily recommend the game to any FPS lover.

Personally I do enjoy this game and while this game certainly does have its ups and downs, I am not here to praise or criticize this game. I am here to offer a phenomenal 4 Cheese Ravioli recipe!
Here are the ingredients you will need!
Ravioli Dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 pinch salt, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 2 eggs, 1 1/2 tablespoons water.
Ravioli Filling: 1 (8 ounce) container ricotta cheese, 1 (4 ounce) package cream cheese, softened, 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, 1/2 cup provolone cheese, shredded, 1 egg, 1 1/2 teaspoons dried parsley.
Pesto-Alfredo Cream Sauce: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 cloves garlic, crushed, 3 tablespoons prepared basil pesto sauce, 2 cups heavy cream, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 (24 ounce) jar marinara sauce.
1. Mound the flour and salt together on a work surface and form a well. Beat the teaspoon of olive oil, 2 eggs, and water in a bowl. Pour half the egg mixture into the well. Begin mixing the egg with the flour with one hand; use your other hand to keep the flour mound steady. Add the remaining egg mixture and knead to form a dough.
2. Knead the dough until smooth, 8 to 10 minutes; add more flour if the dough is too sticky. Form the dough into a ball and wrap tightly with plastic. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
3. While the dough is resting, prepare the ravioli filling. Combine the ricotta cheese, cream cheese, mozzarella cheese, provolone cheese, egg, and parsley and mix well. Set the filling aside.
4. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and pesto sauce and cook for one minute. Pour in the heavy cream, raise the heat to high, and bring the sauce to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the Parmesan cheese and stir until the cheese melts. Remove the pan from the heat and keep warm.
5. Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, warm the marinara sauce over medium-low heat.
6. Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Beat the egg with the tablespoon of water to make the egg wash.
7. Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets no thicker than a nickel. To assemble the ravioli, brush the egg wash over a sheet of pasta. Drop the filling mixture on the dough by teaspoonfuls about one inch apart. Cover the filling with the top sheet of pasta, pressing out the air from around each portion of filling. Press firmly around the filling to seal. Cut into individual ravioli with a knife or pizza cutter. Seal the edges.
8. Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the ravioli, and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the ravioli float to the top and the filling is hot, 4 to 8 minutes. Drain well.
9. Grease a baking sheet. Place the cooked ravioli on the sheet pan and bake in the preheated oven until brown, about 4 minutes.
10. To serve the ravioli, divide them among four warmed serving bowls. Drizzle the marinara sauce over the ravioli and then top with the cream sauce.

To explain this game would be...a bit hard. I'll try my best to explain how the community works to the best I can.
There are three different factions:
The Terran Republic (Military Dictatorship wanting to unite the lands)
The New Conglomerate (Almost total Anarchy type of freedom trying to bring freedom to all sectors)
The Vanu Sovereignty (Cult of Technology)
The Terran Republic usually has the regular bullet-like technology at the beginning and basically through the game. The people who are usually these guys are rather new to the game, as I played as them at first. They don't usually get along with one another, but the players usually accomplish whatever goal they need to accomplish with good heavy infantry and Maxes (Basically mechsuits)
The New Conglomerate, to sum it up, is basically if a bunch of shotguns got together and decided to turn into people. They excel in light assault shotgunners and heavy assault, but lack stealth. The people on this faction usually are nice people, but they don't usually cooperate that much with one another (results may vary). They end up, though, helping one another in the end by basically swarming with sheer manpower and excellent air power.
The Vanu Sovereignty is a cult of technology. They have some of the better later guns while lacking in beginner equipment. From my experience, they seem to have the better people tactically and they usually all get along, but they lack manpower. The beginning guns are basically crap, but as you play more as them you unlock some of the most overpowered weapons in the game. Basically, they are good at strategy and teamwork, terrible in numbers, bad beginning guns but some of the best later guns, and better technology than the rest of the factions.
For the combat, this game is full-on chaotic at times, but can also be quiet but deadly. You can end up in just a small skirmish against another faction, but you might also end up transforming that small skirmish into a huge battle to turn the tide of the fate of the continent.
The continents can be controlled by different factions, giving certain factions certain abilities. JUST REMEMBER THAT THIS GAME IS NOT A PAY-TO-WIN GAME! The things you can get on here with money can be gained with gameplay. This isn't like any other massively multiplayer shooter. This is NOT Call of Duty or Battlefield! This game will be, instead of 32 vs 32, will be about 200 vs 200 vs 200 just in one area alone. There are many servers and with each server there are continents. Within these continents are regions and these regions are fought over. This means that there is CONSTANT war between people. These servers hold about 2000 people each, most likely more, and each continent is full of warzones. There will be kamikazes, airstrikes by other players, snipers who snipe you from the other side of the map, basically everything.
This game is fun and frustrating. I cannot stop playing, but I also cannot stop getting♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off at times. The community is amazing, and this game balances the frustration of wanting to achieve as well as the fun of playing greatly. The only think I recommend is that you have a good computer to run this game.

Shooting is core to this genre, Wolfenstein defined FPS back in the day, and TNO devs shoots true. The gun play is spot on with quick response, snappy peek-cover mechanics, versatility of primary and secondary fires for each gun, dual wielding(!!!), optional stealth, and talent trees that cater to your playstyle. The talent passive tree is an interesting subject I found to be good and bad. It's supposed to cater to your playstyle but if you're like me that wants to get the most/best, you will end up going out of your way to get various buffs. I've been told that this game is great from launch and time and time again from post-hype patches. Between getting blasted from a line of fire to heal another soldier in battle and getting spawnkilled from a sunderer to jump into battles, my poor experience from the game has yet to mature into something great.
I will admit, Planetside 2 has a lot of content to cover in the first couple of hours. There's just so much to learn on top of the fact that everyone seems to know what they're doing, but as for scrawny me, I didn't know about the training area until four hours in, and I clearly don't quite recall on the amount of depth the game had to offer between character, weapon, and vehicle customization from the trailers.
Not only do you as a character get to customize the kinds of weapons you would like in terms of a playstyle, but each of these loadouts contain a perk that you can choose to add-on, along with other smaller add-ons onto your vehicle. In addition, the weapons you equip and their inner machinations are something you can choose to change. These changes aren't for nought, of course. They do, in fact, change the game.
That said, if you're a player who wants to
Spawn times feel slow and deliberate, even if it is only 15 seconds. Instant Action consistently warps you into different locations, and don't even get me started ont travelling between each zone. When stalemates hit on a heavy day, these battles last longer than a typical infantry-only match in Battlefield 3.
As I mentioned earlier, I didn't play very well. I'm certain that is a primary result of it. If you want to play well in the game, there's certainly the whole "aimng and shooting" aspect of it, but there's a lot more than just that, and many of the players account for this whilst being in the battle.
All of that in mind, if you know you want to put a lot of time into not being productive, this is the game for you.

PROS:
- Rich storyline attempting to give a psychological depth to the characters
- Good graphics (not as good as you would expect from its system requirements, though). Also, this game is very well optimised. When I was buying this game, I was worried that I would be barely able to play this game on lowest settings. However, with the in-game compression enabled, I was able to get frame rate somewhere between 25 and 40 FPS on high settings, which is enough for me. (I have Geforce GT 650M 2 GB, i5 3210M @ 2,5 GHz, 6GB RAM, Windows 8.1, 1920x1080 Philips 234E external monitor connected through HDMI). I would have liked the graphics even more, if there were other colours, too, not just different shades of black, grey and white.
- Lot's of action, challenging enemies (they cover, duck, turn somersaults, call for reinforcements), environment that requires constant adaptation to new conditions - this game is not your standard straightforward shooter. There were times when this game reminded me FarCry 3 in terms of gameplay.
- Multiple ways of killing enemies (stealth attacks, grenades, machine guns, blitz attacks), although stealth, which is my favourite style, is not always possible; actually half the time it's impossible to perform stealth attacks for a prolonged period of time
- Decent amount of upgradable weapons (shotguns, assault rifles, pistols, knives, Tesla grenades, laser guns) - for many of those weapons there are two modes and you can even use two weapons of the same type simultaneously, if you wish - like  gunzerking in Borderlands 2)
- You get to shoot Nazis on the Moon!!! (How cool is that?)
- There are also collectibles, health upgrades and a skill-tree, but not that they actually matter
- Lots of blood and gore and even a couple of sex scenes (another way how this game reminds me of FarCry 3)
- The designers and artists have paid attention to each tiny detail
- No bugs/glitches - with all those half-baked indie games on the market, it's a big thing for me nowadays
Cons:
- Ridiculously mediocre soundtrack, athough I liked the German versions of some of the 60's hits
- You should be very careful about how you spend you ammo. There's a constant shortage of ammo in the game.
- Some plot holes: for example, J. Blaskowitz survives multiple punctured wounds, grenade explosions, plain crashes and even keeps all his combat reflexes after 14 years in a vegetative state due to shrapnel in his medulla oblongata. On the other hand, what I'm nagging about? Beating the entire Nazi empire solely on your own is not very likely in real life either
- No Nazi occultism in this part. Just hi-tech deathmachines. Although there's an episode of a Jewish secret society.
- The games is a bit short for 50 EUR. It took me 16 hrs to complete the game and cutscenes make for about 50% of the game. Luckily, I bought this game with 50% discount, so I don't feel that my money was wasted.
Overall, I think Wolfenstein: The New Order is one of the best games of 2014. It's always a challenge to make a good sequel to a great game. I think Bethesda managed that well.
My overall rating: 9/10.

Solid atmosphere, good shooting, and functional story are terminally crippled by a lack of conveyance, frustrating mechanics, and a shockingly poor final boss fight.
Tutorials are designed poorly, such as sliding under the panzerhund, which resulted in multiple deaths before I had a chance to read the on screen text.
The environment, while a gorgeously rendered, were a pain to navigate and find things in as everything drew from the same drab pallette.
The mechanics, such as the one and only time alt+down was needed in the entire game (and then forgotten), were more frustrating than interesting.
Deaths were often not a result of making a visibly poor choice, but something that required multiple attempts to understand and learn for the purpose of trying to create tension. Panzerhunds were the primary culprit of this frustration, and their chase scenes often did not make sense until corpse running through them three or four times to learn them.
Getting captured or incapacitated, or getting stabbed in various places lost any meaning after the first couple of times. Over the course of the game, Blazkowicz is concussed enough times to compete with Tintin.
On the other hand, the shooting is decidedly satisfying.
Stealth was my preference for the game.
Throwing knives were an absolute joy, being easily able to enter a room with several enemies and kill them all before they raised the alarm.
The silenced pistol was a close second, and was easily the goto when precision was needed.
The lasers however felt gimmicky and did not fit well with the rest of the weapons in the game, almost as if they were added as an afterthought.
All in all I can't recommend this game.
It had the potential to be my favourite shooter of 2014, but instead has ammounted to little more than a lot of frustration over the course of several days to completion.
If you are a diehard fan of the franchise this may be for you, but expect to spend a good portion of your play time swearing at the screen.

Wolfenstein has a large name to live up to, and Wolfenstein: The New Order breaks every expectation I had of it. Usually single player FPS campaigns are all the same, but the characters, environment, voice acting and cutscenes put this way above any other single player FPS I've played.
Do yourself a favor and check this out, I can't wait to get my hands on a sequel.

I've not played much of the previous Wolfenstein games, but I'm a huge fan of the FPS genre, so I had high hopes for The New Order. I'm pleased to say that it matched those expectations, and even surpassed them to the point where I was 5 minutes away from declaring this a contender for Game Of The Year.
Set in 1960, the Nazis have achieved world domination, having won WW2 after gaining access to some advanced technology. The player character, William "BJ" Blazkowicz, a veteran American soldier, joins an underground resistance movement to attempt to fight back.
The story is very well written, and completely embraces the alternate history and science fiction themes. Its absolutely ridiculous, but in a good, fun way. I mean, it starts with robot dogs and laser weapons and gets crazier from there. And it doesn't mess around with shades of grey. This is a celebration of heroes fighting the good fight against villains of pure evil.
Blazkowicz's character is outstanding. The writing and voice acting combine to give true depth to his personality in a way that is rare for a FPS protagonist. BJ is a tough soldier guy, but at the same time, his dreams, his fears and his pain felt real to me. The other resistance members are also very interesting, and help to remind us what we're fighting for.
Unfortunately the ending felt a little bit rushed to me. I wouldn't even call it a cliffhanger, it just felt incomplete. I was actually convinced there would be one more cutscene after the credits to tidy up a couple of unresolved plot threads, but sadly not.
Wolfenstein also fulfils most of my preferences for FPS mechanics. I prefer health packs over regenerating health. Wolfenstein has an acceptable hybrid system where health regenerates to the next multiple of 20. So for example if you take damage down to 33, you'll only regen to 40, and need to find health packs to get back to maximum. I prefer being able to carry all the weapons instead of being restricted to 2 or 3 at a time. Wolfenstein lets you carry everything.
There is a nice variety of weapons - knife, pistol, assault rifle, shotgun, sniper, laser rifle - and you can dual wield all of them which is really useful against heavily armoured enemies, and has the added bonus of just feeling awesome. You've also got grenades, and will occasionally find a heavy laser minigun. And there's a perk system that provides passive buffs as a reward for meeting challenges, such as get 100 kills to reload faster.
Level design is linear with side corridors and Deus Ex style air vents allowing for a small degree of stealth. Graphics are fantastic and I got a smooth framerate. The music fits the mood perfectly, especially during cutscenes. Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard. I finished the campaign in 10 hours and I didn't notice any bugs.
Wolfenstein The New Order is one of the outstanding games of 2014, and is an absolute MUST play for every FPS fan. I'd also recommend it as a good starting point for non-FPS fans, if you're curious about what makes the genre so amazing.

The key word for this game is
. Yet the game is missing some key elements to go from another Free2Play shooter to a wonderfull game you have to play.
I liked RTCW:ET very much and that is how I noticed Dirty Bomb early on. I've played this game since beta. In the meantime they got rid of most cheaters, very important for the skill based game it is. The rest is about skins, which I don't really care about.
The eSports element never really took flight, which might be one of the biggest problems of this game. It somewhat lacks the name or the fame to become big enough. Public games are therefore mostly skill-mixed and that might not be fun for everyone.
The Devs are really fun people and I've played with them on livestreams many times. However in the past it took too much time (for my personal liking) to fix basic problems in the gameplay. Most are fixed now.
The game is free, so I'd say if you are interested just give it a go. Play a couple of rounds and see if it fits your idea of a fun game. If it's not, just deinstall and go on. If it is, you can get a lot of hours of fun out of it.
Therefore I recommend this game.
Tip for new players: Play the tutorial and join max level 5 servers to avert being slaughtered by high skilled players in the first couple of rounds. Don't worry, you're level 6 soon enough.

All that aside, though, Max Payne 3 delivers an interesting storyline and setting with satisfying over-the-top, Hong Kong action cinema style gunplay.

I haven't had this much fun playing an FPS for a long time.
The decision to make it single player only was fantastic, each level was interesting and different with multiple routes to take and varying strategies to execute.
The graphics and audio are superb and the story was really deep and at times some one must have been cutting onions nearby because my eyes kept watering up.
I've seen a few people complain about the enemy A.I and all I can say about that is they must have been playing on an easy difficulty because the A.I was really challenging on Death Incarnate. When I went back and replayed on the easy mode to pick up the collectable items I previously missed, the A.I did seem pretty dumb but what else would you expect on a difficulty called   "Can i play daddy?".
The weapon selection is good, you don't have massive selection but each weapon has a role to play and I found myself using the best weapon for the situation more often that not, rather than just sticking with my favourite. Each one felt different and took a bit of experimenting to find it's strengths and weaknesses.
The replayabilty is good which is something often lacking in single player games these days. The two different time lines mean you'll want to play it at least twice and then you'll probably want to go back through again to pick up the collectables/ finish of the achievements. Also when you crack the enigma codes you unlock some bonus game modes which seem really fun and challenging, I'm taking a bit of a break before I take on the "Ironman" mode.
Overall this game has restored my faith in the FPS genre and given me hope that more developers will realise that there is a market for these types of shooters and not just the generic online shooters riddled with microtransactions.

Personally I do enjoy this game and while this game certainly does have its ups and downs, I am not here to praise or criticize this game. I am here to offer a phenomenal 4 Cheese Ravioli recipe!
Here are the ingredients you will need!
Ravioli Dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 pinch salt, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 2 eggs, 1 1/2 tablespoons water.
Ravioli Filling: 1 (8 ounce) container ricotta cheese, 1 (4 ounce) package cream cheese, softened, 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, 1/2 cup provolone cheese, shredded, 1 egg, 1 1/2 teaspoons dried parsley.
Pesto-Alfredo Cream Sauce: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 cloves garlic, crushed, 3 tablespoons prepared basil pesto sauce, 2 cups heavy cream, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 (24 ounce) jar marinara sauce.
1. Mound the flour and salt together on a work surface and form a well. Beat the teaspoon of olive oil, 2 eggs, and water in a bowl. Pour half the egg mixture into the well. Begin mixing the egg with the flour with one hand; use your other hand to keep the flour mound steady. Add the remaining egg mixture and knead to form a dough.
2. Knead the dough until smooth, 8 to 10 minutes; add more flour if the dough is too sticky. Form the dough into a ball and wrap tightly with plastic. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
3. While the dough is resting, prepare the ravioli filling. Combine the ricotta cheese, cream cheese, mozzarella cheese, provolone cheese, egg, and parsley and mix well. Set the filling aside.
4. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and pesto sauce and cook for one minute. Pour in the heavy cream, raise the heat to high, and bring the sauce to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the Parmesan cheese and stir until the cheese melts. Remove the pan from the heat and keep warm.
5. Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, warm the marinara sauce over medium-low heat.
6. Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Beat the egg with the tablespoon of water to make the egg wash.
7. Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets no thicker than a nickel. To assemble the ravioli, brush the egg wash over a sheet of pasta. Drop the filling mixture on the dough by teaspoonfuls about one inch apart. Cover the filling with the top sheet of pasta, pressing out the air from around each portion of filling. Press firmly around the filling to seal. Cut into individual ravioli with a knife or pizza cutter. Seal the edges.
8. Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the ravioli, and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the ravioli float to the top and the filling is hot, 4 to 8 minutes. Drain well.
9. Grease a baking sheet. Place the cooked ravioli on the sheet pan and bake in the preheated oven until brown, about 4 minutes.
10. To serve the ravioli, divide them among four warmed serving bowls. Drizzle the marinara sauce over the ravioli and then top with the cream sauce.

The biggest compliment I can give this game is it that even though there has been a lack content to make the game feel fresh I have never stopped coming back to play.
There has definitely been updates and support from the devs (such as the performance and map enhancements) however I personally feel the game has become stale. But, I have faith in the developers and know that content is coming and I can't wait to see what this game has on final release.

The movement is fast and fluid and feels great; it's a nice mid-way point between classic FPS and arena shooters. The game has a very complex level of tactical and teamwork requirements to be competitive. Additionally, this game allows the better players to shine, there isn't much balancing of ability in Dirty Bomb, it gives players the platform and let's your skills do the talking.
For a free game it's a must try, no question. Especially if your a fan of FPS. There are zero P2W elements in this game, do not believe otherwise! The game has it's issues for sure, the biggest one, for me personally, is very very unbalanced teams on occasion that really kills the fun. Like most videogame stories, this one doesn't entirely 'flow' from chapter to chapter - so when you get to the end of the game you may be left wondering how exactly you got from Point A to Point B and how that involved going to the moon at some point (not a spoiler, it's a selling point in the trailer).
This is definitely a game, and not a series of cutscenes padded with sprinkles of action/stealth.
But although you might wonder 'how' things click together, you won't really question 'why'. Every character has a motivation that makes sense in a world that doesn't, but the attention to detail on everything with a German flavour is immaculate.
My eyes lit up when playing a 'nightmare' Easter Egg within the game that will remain unspoiled, and the health/upgrades/perks system blends old school action with modern expecations. Even cliché moments have context and the story even has a few moments that switch from 'ridiculous over-the-topness' to some really impacting moments.
The main thing to know about this game is it exceeds expectations. Sure you don't need a reason to kill Nazis, they're Nazis - but this game gives you more than it had to, and deserves every bit of credit for it.

Begin mixing the egg with the flour with one hand; use your other hand to keep the flour mound steady. Add the remaining egg mixture and knead to form a dough.
2. Knead the dough until smooth, 8 to 10 minutes; add more flour if the dough is too sticky. Form the dough into a ball and wrap tightly with plastic. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
3. While the dough is resting, prepare the ravioli filling. Combine the ricotta cheese, cream cheese, mozzarella cheese, provolone cheese, egg, and parsley and mix well. Set the filling aside.
4. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and pesto sauce and cook for one minute. Pour in the heavy cream, raise the heat to high, and bring the sauce to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the Parmesan cheese and stir until the cheese melts. Remove the pan from the heat and keep warm.
5. Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, warm the marinara sauce over medium-low heat.
6. Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Beat the egg with the tablespoon of water to make the egg wash.
7. Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets no thicker than a nickel. To assemble the ravioli, brush the egg wash over a sheet of pasta. Drop the filling mixture on the dough by teaspoonfuls about one inch apart. Cover the filling with the top sheet of pasta, pressing out the air from around each portion of filling. Press firmly around the filling to seal. Cut into individual ravioli with a knife or pizza cutter. Seal the edges.
8. Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the ravioli, and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the ravioli float to the top and the filling is hot, 4 to 8 minutes. Drain well.
9. Grease a baking sheet. Place the cooked ravioli on the sheet pan and bake in the preheated oven until brown, about 4 minutes.
10. To serve the ravioli, divide them among four warmed serving bowls. Drizzle the marinara sauce over the ravioli and then top with the cream sauce.

The hard-boiled detective is back, but is this the same Max that we've seen in before?
A new Max Payne game! Set in Brazil!? I have to admit that I was perplexed, perhaps even turned off at this idea when I initially heard about it. After all, Max Payne had established itself as a melodramatic noir crime story set in New York City, the complete opposite of its new sunny, colorful, Brazilian setting. Along with the new setting there were also new developers, while previous titles were handled by Finnish studio Remedy Games, Max Payne 3 was being developed by an internal Rockstar studio in Vancouver. This definitely raised a few eyebrows, mine especially. How did it all turn out?
Wonderfully.
Max has never felt better. Controls are snappy. The animations are some of the best I've ever seen in gaming. The story is a little lacking, but all we really needed is Max with guns, truckloads of bad guys, and bullet time.
The dark and brooding atmosphere of the first two games is replaced by an aesthetic that closely resembles a Tony Scott film, particularly the film Man on Fire. There are a lot of filmic effects overlayed on the cutscenes that distort and blur the shots as they are framed off, highlighting key moments and important plot points. The combination of these effects gives the production it's own unique feel.
Overall a must play of ANY action game enthusiast.

Being a Max Payne fan from a very young age (totally shouldn't have been playing it then) I was very happy with this game. I could listen to Max's dreary narration forever, I swear.
A few things that are different about this game are the bullet time mechanic and the setting. For bullet time there is an overall slow time button and also a kind of slow mo lunge button. A little different but no biggy. Guess it offers more variety as to what you can do and you don't always have to ridiculously lunge through windows just to shoot someone. Combat was really fun. I enjoyed the bullet time but also just too breaks from it at times to play with the cover mechanic and just fight in real time. Gunplay feels good. Blood splatter indicates when you hit an enemy. Weapon pickup was a little weird and clunky. Dual wielding would often drop your main weapon, so there's a lot of weird selection, but whatever.
The game takes place primarily in Saou Paul Brazil which was a little different for me, and Max. I'd rather have stayed in the old setting of the previous games but the game backtracks a bit to memories, bringing you back to places like New York and New Jersey. I felt like this was some nice fan service and good storytelling. While I didn't enjoy the new setting much it was fun to see Max react to the situations he was forced into.
Character development was good to me. Max seems to have some ♥♥♥♥ed up priorities. He's a guy who just doesn't die. He's self destructive but he'll do anything for the damsel in distress.
Soundtrack was great, classic Max Payne stuff. I think the main theme song was redone and it just sounds better. Really enjoyed the music in the combat. Stood out a lot for me. I think I'll remember the final level track for a long time, it was badass.
Must play for a Max Payne fan I'd say!

Rewriting my review since the old one did not do it justice.
Max Payne 3, the sequel to the fantastic 2003 Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne, is an entertaining, thrilling, amazing experience from start to finish.
Set in São Paulo, the protagonist, Max Payne, is a retired ol' NYCPD cop. Max’s diet consists of liquor and painkillers to make him forget the sorrows of what had happened to him and his deceased family. Desperate to get out of his pitiful condition, he takes a job as a bodyguard for a rich Brazilian businessman named Fabricas Branco. But it turns out that it isn't an easy job after all, when Fabiana, Fabricas' wife, is kidnaped.
The plot is full of conspiracies and sick twists and huge amazing set pieces and in the end... it pays off; it is one of the best stories told in a video game.
Simple yet incredibly fun, with a huge array of weapons to choose from, you shoot, jump and make amazing "Matrix" style tricks that are not strange for Max Payne fans. The gunplay also received some polish as it is refined and perfected.
The game is beautiful from art direction to meshes and polygons. Animations are one of the best around. Surprisingly, the game is very well optimized and it utilizes many PC-specific features such as DirectX11. (which is weird for a Rockstar game)
Voice acting is top notch with James McCaffrey returning as Max Payne. The soundtrack is AWESOME, don’t believe me? Just check out "Tears by Health" on YouTube, you'll love it!
For the first time ever in a Max Payne game, a multiplayer mode is included. Many people were skeptical about it but it turned out that they were all wrong. This fun creative experience has all the single player abilities such as Bullet Time and Shootdodge in it which makes it stand out from the crowd. it is fast paced and (sometimes) chaotic and balanced.
Overall it was my personal 2012 GOTY and it still is.
