Ok first thing’s first, this is NOT a remake, it’s not even a reimagining, this game appears to happen roughly in the same universe as the original Woflenstine but it is it’s own game.
Visually it is a vast improvement over iD’s last title Rage though they appear to be using an updated version of the same engine.  You will see some Unreal engine style texture pop-ins, which is a shame in this day and age, however it runs very well and for what it is the game still looks good and has some very nice visuals.  Levels have some level of destruction; at least of cover so there is that upgrade, pillars, barriers, certain types of metal sheets can all be gradually broken and shot through different methods.  There is a minor cover system, akin to FarCry 3’s system where you can pop out or over something if you get into the correct position which helps during combat.  There are modeled and skinned in damage indicators for enemy troops, and given that this is a iD game expect some gibs, limbs, some pretty brutal cut scenes, and fair quick but significant take down animations some are quite visceral.
There is a stealth mechanic and depending on your play style you may simply favor running and gunning which, given the fact that you can dual wield almost every weapon in the game you have enough firepower in your hands.  However if you wish to avoid as much attention and fighting as possible, or you enjoy watching the stealth kill animations then you can, at times it’s more beneficial to do so as a fair amount of the enemies in W:NO pixel hunt or are just extremely accurate even while running or moving around.  However stealth wise they tend to be both blind or severely impaired, while at the same time incredibly hyper sensitive to anything and unfortunately the cause varies, the stealth over all can be very forgiving, which is good because there is NO QUICK SAVE!  That is unfortunately correct, there is no quick save in this PC game, I do not understand why this was not added in but the actual developers Machinehead Games really screwed up with this omission.  If you die part of the way through an engagement you will probably not be able to start where you’d like and sometimes you have to do entire sections over again, other times the auto save places a spot right after.  You will need to learn from your mistakes or trial and error it unfortunately; however there are only a few sections in the entire game where I can honestly say that I had trouble with.
There is a leveling up/skill tree system for this game and for the most part it flows quite well.  There are requirements that you have to meet in order to move onto the next branch or in order to meet a requirement for a skill that is not actually connected to a previous skill.  These vary from performing take downs, throwing back grenades, killing a certain amount of enemies while dual wielding weapons, silent kills with throwing knives, and so on.  Some of the requirements however are for the most part nothing but grinding and putting yourself into situation that you would normally not put yourself into AND the game very rarely actually uses this kind of attack which defeats the purpose of requiring it, so you will have to find work around for these unfortunately.  Luckily the forums on Steam are fairly helpful and I know of two skill points that I didn’t know if I would be able to do them that I was actually able to pull off fairly easily by cheating the system, but not actually cheating mind you, simply the description on many of them is vague and the requirements can be met in different ways then what is actually written in the game.
One other major fault is the totally not old school mechanic of having to manually pick up items one by one.  Picture this, you’ve expended your assault rifle ammo and you’re in a semi arena still rife with bad guys, well in W:NO you need to crack open boxes and constantly be looking at the floor for dead bodies so you can rapidly press your use key in order to pick things up.  I can not understand what they were trying to do with this; I can maybe understand it for the gold items, intel and other collectables but NOT armor, health and ammo.  This gets worse when you have to fight the last boss, since every enemy in the game has pin point accuracy you have to continually run and “dodge” in order to juke his shots and on top of that you need to scramble around looking for health, ammo and armor pick ups in boxes and frantically press your use key in order to pick them up.  I have to wonder if Bethesda had anything to do with this choise since, as I recall, you picked up items manually in many of their games; the difference being however that unlike say Oblivion you are not dodging bullets in frantic fights.
The story and characters are pretty well done and there is a single point where you make one decision that will alter what doors you can interact with and that is all, there are no alternative story arcs.  This is fine because the story is fairly good, at least when compared to past Woflenstine titles, the characters and B.J. are the main focus of most cutscenes as well as minor story additions when you are back at the main base.  B.J. is far more fleshed out in this version of him then in any of the past games, while he may seem to be just a muscle head they make him out to be fairly intelligent and kind.  Each side character has their own story line and you will get bits and pieces of it as the game progresses which is a welcome addition as it further fleshes out that person.  While nothing ground breaking happens during these lulls in the fighting it’s defiantly a welcome addition.
The weapons feel and sound quite good and the skill upgrades add some flavors to them that help in dealing with some of the more heavily armored enemies.  Though speaking of enemies some of the armored human units like the shotgunners are just damn annoying and practically a mini boss, their shotguns ricochet off surfaces and do insane amounts of damage in a short amount of time.  There is usually one extra attachment for each weapon, though one in particular has several through the entire game.  The real benefit to the skill columns is that you can gain all of them and go back and start a new game, getting the benefits which will enable you to play with a different playstyle then you would have before.
Both the sound effects and the music are very fitting for the game type, the weapon sounds are very good and have a plenty of oomph behind them, the shotgun being one of my favorites, it sounds like the part.  The music was actually better then I expected, and it changes from stealth to active engagement when stealth is broken.  Each level has its own music score and they all sound very different from each other, sort of giving them even more of their own personality.
Being a Wolfenstine game the developers saw fit to go back to the roots and added a fair amount of collectables, gold items, intel, music, letters and audio logs.  If you’re a completionist then you will get some extra hours trying to fine every single item, which for me added to about 36 hours total play time.  Granted this game is only single player thus some people may say it’s not nearly enough content given how large the game really is, 40 gigs is never something to sneeze at.  There is some talk about adding a few extra levels, maybe multiplayer or something; however it is all just hearsay.
For $60 full price I might be hard pressed to suggest a game like this, however given that it did give me 36 hours, it’s not a hard sell I would say however that if you are at all on the fence about the price versus the content then I would wait for a sale, after that it will be well worth it.  Either way I had fun with it and I hope they will continue in some way, this also gives me some hope as to what Doom could possibly be like.

Personally I do enjoy this game and while this game certainly does have its ups and downs, I am not here to praise or criticize this game. I am here to offer a phenomenal 4 Cheese Ravioli recipe!
Here are the ingredients you will need!
Ravioli Dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 pinch salt, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 2 eggs, 1 1/2 tablespoons water.
Ravioli Filling: 1 (8 ounce) container ricotta cheese, 1 (4 ounce) package cream cheese, softened, 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, 1/2 cup provolone cheese, shredded, 1 egg, 1 1/2 teaspoons dried parsley.
Pesto-Alfredo Cream Sauce: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 cloves garlic, crushed, 3 tablespoons prepared basil pesto sauce, 2 cups heavy cream, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 (24 ounce) jar marinara sauce.
1. Mound the flour and salt together on a work surface and form a well. Beat the teaspoon of olive oil, 2 eggs, and water in a bowl. Pour half the egg mixture into the well. Begin mixing the egg with the flour with one hand; use your other hand to keep the flour mound steady. Add the remaining egg mixture and knead to form a dough.
2. Knead the dough until smooth, 8 to 10 minutes; add more flour if the dough is too sticky. Form the dough into a ball and wrap tightly with plastic. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
3. While the dough is resting, prepare the ravioli filling. Combine the ricotta cheese, cream cheese, mozzarella cheese, provolone cheese, egg, and parsley and mix well. Set the filling aside.
4. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and pesto sauce and cook for one minute. Pour in the heavy cream, raise the heat to high, and bring the sauce to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the Parmesan cheese and stir until the cheese melts. Remove the pan from the heat and keep warm.
5. Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, warm the marinara sauce over medium-low heat.
6. Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Beat the egg with the tablespoon of water to make the egg wash.
7. Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets no thicker than a nickel. To assemble the ravioli, brush the egg wash over a sheet of pasta. Drop the filling mixture on the dough by teaspoonfuls about one inch apart. Cover the filling with the top sheet of pasta, pressing out the air from around each portion of filling. Press firmly around the filling to seal. Cut into individual ravioli with a knife or pizza cutter. Seal the edges.
8. Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the ravioli, and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the ravioli float to the top and the filling is hot, 4 to 8 minutes. Drain well.
9. Grease a baking sheet. Place the cooked ravioli on the sheet pan and bake in the preheated oven until brown, about 4 minutes.
10. To serve the ravioli, divide them among four warmed serving bowls. Drizzle the marinara sauce over the ravioli and then top with the cream sauce.

Planetside 2 overall is a great game with a very good concept behind it. This review is more of a tutorial to get new players from quitting because they are frustrated from the game which is a very common occurence.
It only becomes fun if you know what you are doing. From the start, you are given no tutorial, and you are launched into Koltyr, a continent that is supposed to train beginners but does nothing of the sort. When you spawn in, go to a terminal that has a globe projected on it and goe to either Hossin, Indar, Esamir, or Amerish. This is where the real battles are going to be. Never go back to Koltyr.
Let's take a step back. When you start the game, you will be asked to join a faction. Here is an overview of the factions:
Vanu Soveriegn - Higher accuracy guns, no bullet drop for guns where it doesn't matter. High tech, stuff looks cool.
New Conglomerate- Hard hitting weapons with a lower rate of fire.
Terran Republic- High fire rate weapons, low damage output. Prowler OP.
Once you are in the game, you will have to learn the classes, the guns, and how to use them. This is what I meant when I said it will only be fun if you know what you're doing. There are so many useless guns and terrible combinations that new players can get frustrated very quickly. I highly recommend watching Wrel's videos on youtube on what do do.
Finding a good battle is an essential skill to know so you don't become bored immediatly or get tired of being spawn camped. When you scroll over a hex, there will be statistics about it on the right side, inculding a pie graph and the amount of players. You want to find a hex with between 12-24 players and 48-96. Also, you want to make sure that the population is no more than 45%-55% for either side, otherwise it will be way to easy or way too hard. This does not change depending on your skill, if there is a severe population imbalance there is no way you can do anything about it.
Ok, so now you have spawned in a battle. What now? The default class (light assult) is a good class especially if you are playing New Conglomerate as it is equipped with one of the best default weapons in the game. Run out of you spawn and scount the battlefield. From what you see, and your playstyle, you should determine what class you would like to play. Here are the overviews of each class:
Infiltrator- Sniper*, can cloak to be invisible. Has a little less health than other classes (100 less shields). * Pro players use this class with SMG's, the other gun option available to them. Good for people who like long range combat.
Light Assault- Has a jetpack, medium to close range guns. Good for people who like high mobility.
Combat Medic- Can revive team mates, variety of guns. this is a great way to grind certs. Good for people that want to actually be useful.
Engineer- Can place turrets and repair veichles. Good for people who like to use veichles, but those are useless until you put tons of certs into them.
Heavy Assault- Has a shield that can absorb damage, generally has guns with large clips (LMG's). Also has a rocket launcher. Good for people who like tanking.
Once you have seen what the battle is like and chosen a preference, select that class at a weapon terminal.
Feel free to switch classes depending on the situation. DO NOT buy anything yet. Once you achieve battle rank 11 you should have 1000 certs available. (The game gives you 100 certs per battle rank until battle rank 15). Go to the warpgate and go to the terminal with the globe. Select the Virtual Training facility. Here you can see what weapons will be like for free. You can test out anyhting you want here. Choose a weapon that you would like for a class that you enjoyed the most playing. If you really like the default weapon as some are very good, you are free to spend the 1000 certs on suit upgrades and what you please. Also, make sure to see if it has a review online to see if it is good. Now buy your first gun! Get attatchments recommended by the review so you don't end up using the gun wrong.
Suit slot reviews
Nanoweave armour-gives you resistance to small arms fire, usful for loadouts where you don't think you will have the drop on you opponent and it boils down to who can deal the most amount of damage faster.
Grenade bandolier- gives you extra grenades. Useful for 2 situations: Advanced infiltrator gameplay where you have EMP grenades, and as medic when you have revive grenades equipped.
Advanced shield capacitor- when you know you can take out enemies without them killing you and you need to get into the fight faster, or when you control the situation (you can duck behind cover knowing you won't take damage for a few seconds) so that getting your shields back up will give you an advantage.
Anything else is not recommended.
Useful things to know:
There are good bases and bad bases, avoid poorly designed bases (e.g. Subterrainian Nanite Analysis).
Always play with a squad. Find a squad that talks a lot using voice chat and that coordinates thier actions. Playing by yourself can be discouraging.
If you are being farmed, leave immediatlely.
Knowing this, hopefully you will no how to start the game properly and will not be frustrated.
Here is a small list of pros and cons to wrap up the review if you are still debating to get this game:
Pros-
-Free, and microtransactions do not give you an advantage (NOT P2W, despite what noobs say)
-Tons of custimization to suit your playstyle
-Every fight is different
Cons-
-takes a while to get certs if you aren't good after battle rank 15
-Playing field is not really leveled, high ranked players are mixed with low ranked players and they will kill you a lot more often.
-terrible tutorials and introduction to game, you have to know what you are doing to play

Pros: Great graphics. Style evokes current action flicks, right down to the hand-held camera. Multiplayer has a lot of RPG elements without it being overwhelming, and a ton of guns. Solid acting. Interesting setting, taking you through the office buildings, night clubs and slums of Sao Paolo, Brazil. In spite of plenty of the game set during the humid sunny day, the bleak noir mood is ever-present. Challenging. Addictive, especially the MP.
Cons: Unresponsive controls. Poorly done basic-at-best cover system that adds nothing to the slo-mo-diving TPS game-play of Max Payne, which returns with no new additions. Thin story stretched beyond breaking point to prolong SP, which still barely breaks 7 hours. Max and Passos never shut up, repeat themselves constantly, in spite of having absolutely nothing to say. We're given every reason to hate almost all of the characters, then expected to care about them being in danger. The game takes over every couple of minutes, because each area that you linearly move through is tiny, before it has to load another - and the loading is always "covered" with a cutscene.
My recommendation: This is more for fans of Rockstar than fans of Max Payne.

It's Max Payne on roids, and it definitely has the CoD "must shoot everything hundreds of times" mentality. I got this game for cheap (under $10) so I can't really complain. It is a tough one to judge gameplay wise. As others have pointed out, the gunplay and shooting/graphics are quite nice. However, Max Payne in my opinion was always more about a dark film noiresque story than the action. The shooting and action always complimented the original story quite nicely. This doesn't quite capture that feeling. Lay off unless under $10 imo.

Pros-

Cons-

Dirty Bomb is a very fun fast paced(5-30 minute) gameplay experience with good graphics. The downplay of this is that the anti cheat system has no value whatsoever. Do I recommend Max Payne 3?
Well, on one hand, it's an easy question; on the other hand, it's quite hard to answer it.
Fans of MP2 (like myself) will surely miss the grittyness and surreal, almost insane setting. MP3 is more down to earth, more in your face. The cutscenes in which Max breaks down are a little naiive and may appeal to younger players. Adults surely won't buy the over-the-top alcoholism and pill consumption displayed in the (partially non-skippable - why, oh, why?) sequences.
On the other hand, as the storyline unfolds, the game starts rolling, pulling you in. It's fast paced and action packed, which does a good job at making you forget about MP2. MP3 needs some time to get you into the mood, but once you start roaming the favelas, you get this good old depressive Max Payne feeling.
The controls definitely need some getting used to, but after you manage that, the game really starts paying back.
A downside is that I almost never used the shootdodge technique, for which the Max Payne serier is so famous for. Too bad, it surely was a thing I was looking forward to.
One thing that positively surprised me is its length. Aproximately seven to eight hours to complete the main storyline is quite ok these days.
The learning curve is quite steep, so bear that in mind. It's by no means an easy game.
There are also some graphical and sound bugs, which can be managed using the methods mentioned on the internets. I encountered only some sound problems which I got rid of by setting my speakers from 5.1 to 2.1. It surely didn't mess up the gaming experience.
So, do I recommend Max Payne 3?
Yes, even though I definitely think it's inferior to Max Payne 2.

Dirty Bomb - Free to play. I can't say that I've put a lot of money into this one ($12 total through the humble bundle.) However, with over 300 hours on tap, I've unlocked all of the characters available. Cards, on the other hand, are where the choices are. Fragger or Thunder? Easy. Whether to go with the M4 or another gun relies on what cards you've either purchased or earned. They're bought with either real money or in-game credits, which don't drop at a substantially high rate, although fast enough to feel that you're always close to whatever card you need. Playing objectives helps, and daily quests (first win, first objective map finished, etc) are there to bump your credits as a faster rate. You'll always feel that the next card you buy will the one that makes you a better player.
And that's where things are rough with Dirty Bomb. There are a lot of new players. There are a lot of veterans in game. Matchmaking doesn't quite work properly (yet) to make learning an easy task. Veterans complain that you're not in position. New players think everyone is cheating. And because of the smallish player base, this is a frequent nuisance. Since the game is still 'beta', the matchmaking system is being overhauled for a new one, completely rewritten to take these things into account. In the meantime, it's either a runaway spawn camping fest with you on the offense, or on the defense...rarely is the game competitive.
Gunplay is okay. Characters used to be bullet sponges, which is ultimately made me stick around for so long. It didn't have that Call of Duty time-to-kill of less than a second. But as the game as progressed, it's become closer and closer to that. Shotguns kill faster than SMGs at medium range as well as short, and some of the assault rifles have such a random bullet pattern, they're objectively inferior to others.
Maps are the worst part. They've just updated the game with newer visuals, and performance tweaks. But overall, they're not balanced. There's no one 'best' map because they're all mediocre. Some have terrible choke points, some are too big. Some aren't played at all (here's looking at you Dome.) They haven't released a new map in ages and the ones already in play don't feel they're getting the attention that they deserve to make them better.
Give the game a shot. It'll take you a good 50 hours to really understand the maps and gun game and how things work. PLAY THE OBJECTIVE.

This is a really difficult one to judge. I like Max Payne, the story-telling, art direction, voice acting and style are toxic yet addictive, and this game has been a long time coming. I'm also a big fan of a number of games where cover-based shooting is a core-mechanic such as Red Dead Redemption, Deus Ex: HR and LA Noire.
But in general, I'm not a huge fan of cover-based shooting, and if you aren't either, steer well clear of this game. You can still leap around in bullet-time like previous entries and pull-off ridiculous John Woo-style bullet dodges, but it seems the years of alcohol abuse have made Max more vulnerable than ever.
Basically, this is move from area-to-area and shoot people from cover (occasionally slowing time to make it easier when they pop their heads out). Most of the time you are hoping you will spot the enemies first before they blow your brains out or that they don't surround you so that your cover is relevant (there are some annoying examples of ending up being a sitting duck through no fault of your own). The mechanics are sound, the AI is OK, the graphics are vibrant and the story "telling" is excellent.
But I just don't want to recommend this game because it's dull. The story is dull, the level design is dull (no matter how pretty they look) and the game is simply a by-the-numbers AAA shoot-people-from-cover game. A VERY stylish one and fun if that's your thing, but shortly before I finished the game I decided that it wasn't.

Both in gameplay and visuals, Rockstar Games have mixed their own brand formula of shooting action in Max Payne 3. Finnish game developer Remedy's magnum opus Max Payne and Max Payne 2: Fall of Max Payne gave character to a basic TPS formula by mixing in a bloody film noir story and beautifully crafted comic cutscenes.
Max Payne 3 opts to move the story onwards with lengthy cutscenes, sunny visuals and more focus on other mechanics (for instance a full on cover system is included) than its predecessors. Do mind that these cutscenes are essentially unskippable (hard coded STILL LOADING screen that actually doesn't load anything prevents you from bypassing them). Visually the game is VERY impressive. Cloth bends realistically, everything from the gun models themselves to individual shells are modeled carefully and the physics engine is very impressive. Technically the game is nicely optimized, with extra graphics options giving such things as full-blown HBAO and tesselation.
I really enjoyed the story, which has amazing setpieces and explosive action. Everything is crafted carefully and all the pieces of the puzzle fall into place - some Remedy-style boss battles also are snuck in, making the game even more fun. Gameplay wise the shooting is better than ever, I'd argue that some of the mechanics surpass even the originals in such areas as gunplay and level design.
The game itself might be jarring to an old Max Payne veteran, since it bears little of the mantle the old games held. It is an awesome game, a kind of Rockstar spinoff of the old formula. It's full of action, amazing sights and it has an awesome soundtrack by HEART.
Some minus points come from artificial difficulty during the latter sections of the game (fully bodyarmored enemies, far away checkpoints) and troubles with Social Club DRM. Otherwise my playthroughs were really enjoyable and I heartily recommend the game.
Get it, you won't regret it!

Nine years. That's long it took for Max Payne to get his♥♥♥♥♥♥together and return to the stage. Our beloved action hero might have aged, grew some white hair and wrinkles but his moves remained sharp and polished. He is still the killing machine who once extinguished half New-York's underworld for his loved ones.
This time around we find Max in the sunny Brazil instead of the snowy streets of the Big Apple. It's a nice, but sometimes strange change of scenery. He's working for the Bronco family as their bodyguard, but as usually things turn upside down pretty quickly around him. The narrative is a masterpiece. We jump in time back and forth as  the story unfolds, because hey, guess what even our hero doesn't know everything. A dark plot is growing around him and he has to act on his instincts to keep himself and the others alive while he slowly findis out his part in the grand scheme. It's a really well written story with major turns and very effective scenes and if there's one thing that topples that it's Max's script. James McCaffrey brings the best to make us feel that we are playing an interactive story. His lines are funny, witty and sad in the same time, but we don't have much time to stop and think about it because the next shootout will surely interrupt our thoughts.
Yes, the gunplay occupies the major part of the game. It's very cinematic. The master of the bullet time returns and he has some new tricks up in his sleeves. It's a superb mechanic that works very well in most cases. As for usual, our health doesn't regenerate so we have to pop up some painkiller bottles every now and then to ease the pain. What is a minor letdown that - and in this matter the game still resonates with its predecessors - there is really only one way how to handle things. Kill them, shoot them, burn them, explode them. You can't take any silent routes there as enemies will almost instantly see you if you get out of cover. As a matter of fact, the AI is so super aware that enemies will know where you are and how to flank you even if you switch cover and they weren't looking at the time. This is what makes the game very frustrating sometimes. It's simply too difficult even on normal settings and there's really no room for error or you're dead. Add that to the fact that it will take around 3-4 bullets to take you down and you've got a very tough game. The devs probably acknowledged this fact in the late stage of the production as it seems they tried to put some lifelines for the players. For starters there is a more than forgiving checkpoint system. After almost all of the rooms you've cleared you get a checkpoint. Also there is this lifeline when you fail a couple of times in the same place and the game gives you a pill, like saying "hey, we know it's difficult, try with this!"
The game looks absolutely astonishing. Emphasis was put on every detail, every little object. Most of the characters look real-like mostly Max Payne. Every wrinkle on his face has a story behind it. Every cut scene is in-game which makes the story even more believable. To be honest you'll see one in every five minutes or so. For some it could be too much, but it develops the story in a unique way.
Even tough the gameplay can get repetitive towards the end - after all what you only do in the 10-12 hours of the SP campaign is kill an army of enemies - this is one of the best third person shooters in recent years. Max moves and shoots like he did in his thirties and past events has only made him more badass. He's became hands down one of the greatest action heroes without super powers in gaming from the last decade. Well, he might have a super power after all; I guess his luck really never runs out.
Rating: 83/100; Replay Value: 2/5; To Beat: 10-12 hours; Played on: normal.

Where to begin...
It's a bit of a sad, sad little mock-up of other FPS games; The gunplay is a bit silly, the balances were, for quite a long time, more of a nerf cannon than actual tweaks, resulting in a lot of useless back and forth, and the community sometimes doesn't think about how a real war goes.
It's definitely a game where you practically have to make your own fun at times, but over the course of the past couple of years(don't believe my hours on Steam; I've actually got almost three weeks total on a main character. No lie, screencaps later,) I have seen it go from confusing, to fun, to no_fun, and it's come back around to fun and loads of fun. Ever since DBG took over, you'll notice that some of the chat filters profanity into Higby or other terms that Forumside players are familiar with, and DBG seems to be keen on attoning for the past that SOE had built and left them. Even now, they made it more interesting for me as a TR toadie.
With that said, however, in the absense of the original Planetside, this MMOFPS is pretty nice to waste my time with with my buddies, rolling around Auraxis in MBTs and Harassers, sending digital metal down-range, before winding up having to do the groundpounders' job for them to save a base.
The fights are a lot bigger, though perhaps not quite as detailed as games like say ARMA, even though the balance in PS2 is clearly geared towards trying to appease the COD and BF folks and their infantryside gameplay more than a genuine Combined Arms game, but there ain't nothing sweeter to my eyes than a QQ over someone getting headshotted out of a Valkyrie with an AP Prowler, crying hax when no, it was just a damn nice, lucky shot that I would give my favorite body part to be able to do consistently.
The game will bog down in big fights. That's no biggy, though. You'd kinda expect that when you have upwards of a hundred to three hundred people involved in a single base area, crawling all over each other to get the thing that does the thing and zomg we gotta get the thing because otherwise the thing won't do the thing like we want it to. Some particle effects will also screw with you, and it was why they had to remove flamethrowers--a sad day, IMO, as I love the BRRRT and the FOOSH and the CATHUNK a lot.
Still, if you want a game that you can unlock a lot of things without spending a dime, and know you have six to twelve good friends to make a squad with(more's always better, though,) and just want to try steamrolling or out-fighting the opposition, for hours on end, even days on end, then this game will satisfy that craving. It's no problem for me to spend upwards of five to ten hours when I have the free time, just sending red boolitz down range, even when I die to complete and utter stupidity like a Galaxy pilot cartwheeling the troop transport down a mountain on Amerish, spewing all of us all over the continent, or having a Death Race across Indar just because of the thrill of cheesing it like a car thief in Mogadishu.

In mid-2001 a game called
was released for Windows. It was a third person shooter with a gritty, film noir setting and graphic novel themes. But possibly most importantly, it had one revolutionary feature: “bullet time.” Although it wasn't a coined term at the time, the slowed down gunfight mechanics of this third person shooter proved so adrenaline-inducing and satisfying that a multitude of ports garnered enough success to inspire a sequel and, eventually,
.
If you're not familiar with the series, you're going to miss out on story seeing as how this is a sequel that takes place about eight years after the events of the other
s. The story is so well-told, however, that even if you're adamant on jumping into the series here, you can more or less pick up on the state of affairs in Max's life almost right off the bat.
The
series was always an insatiable combination of hard-hitting plot with movie-like cinematography, mixed in with the perfect amount of no-holds-barred, guns-blazing, ridiculous action. But
really sets the bar at an all-time high throughout the game. The pacing of the story and gameplay is wonderful. Intense actions sequences are interspersed with no-load cutscenes that keep the flow of the game very natural. Assuming you never die, the entire game can be played from start to finish without looking at a single load screen, because it does so during the cutscenes, which transition from level to level like a graphic novel.
Of course,
wouldn't be a
game without jumping, diving, dodging, and slow-mo. And rest assured, it has all those and more. The modern physics engines allowed for Max to actually dive, and more impressively, land realistically. Max will adjust his body as he flies through the air in slow-mo depending on which way he is heading, facing, and what is in his way (like a wall, or object). You will also take damage from any kind of high jump, and Max will stay prone after a dive until you tell him to get up. This leads to some downright epic firefights.
The series' motif is still clear and present in
: A graphic novel like film noir story with our antihero, Max, being thrown into a tangled web of mortal affairs against his will. Max, still voiced by the wonderful James McCaffrey, keeps his razor-sharp wit as he narrates not only the cutscenes, but also commenting on various elements of the levels as the player goes through the game. This is a welcome return and the script is as brilliant as ever; Max has a quip for everything.
The modern graphics do nothing but compliment the game. Crisp textures, gorgeous setting, and interesting level design make the game a pleasure to look at for all of its entirety. Despite taking place in sunny Brazil the game maintains the series' dark overtones by having you play through a dark nightclub, depressing ghettos, and dilapidated buildings. Max's flashbacks to his life in the States is as gritty and dark as ever.
Unlike some other shooters of the last generation,
's playability is far from over after you've beaten the storyline. A vast multitude of gameplay modes, some new and some returning, vie for your interest and hours. There are various offline arcade modes, focusing on things like scoring as many points as possible, or rushing through a level within a limited time. A brand new online component also begs for your attention.
The multiplayer in
doesn't exactly revolutionize any concepts that are already on the market, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. It employs various features like gathering experience for perks or new weapon loadouts, which may or may not please players depending on who they end up getting into a match with. But, as it wouldn't really be
without bullet time, it's the one essential thing that sets this game's multiplayer apart from the rest. You cannot employ it as liberally as you can in single player, which keeps the game fair for most players. It's actually incorporated into the multiplayer gameplay very smoothly and seamlessly.
Apart from that, though, you have basic multiplayer modes like deathmatch, team modes, and probably nothing you haven't seen before. Some modes are locked until you can gain more experience, which can sometimes prove difficult when you end up being matched with nothing but players who already vastly out-level you. The matches are typically hectic and chaotic, regardless of map size, and the multiplayer continues to enjoy a healthy population of players.
Overall,
does so many things right that it's actually hard for me to pick out things that it does wrong. It has incredibly enjoyable third person gameplay, an interesting and well conveyed plot, is wonderfully cinematic while still offering plenty of action, and has many ways to enjoy the game even after beating the story. It's the kind of game that, regardless of what genres you normally stick to, everyone should at least try.

I really wasn't expecting much from Max Payne; it was a series out of it's prime. Curiously, that became the central idea for the story of the game. Max is pushing 50 now. He's washed up, his alcholism consuming his life. Then he gets the chance to turn it around. Only Max doesn't have the best of luck.
The story is the real gem in this one, and it will keep you guessing for a lot of it. It's expertly delivered via voiceovers, continuing the brooding film-noir feeling the series is known for. Only just behind it is the graphics which genuinly suprised me. The animations in paticular are very lifelike and the gunbattles all turn extremely cinimatic, as though every bullet is planned. Control is smooth and responsive, and the bullet-time effect is still very satifying. Rockstar are well aware that they were the creators of this now ubiquitous gameplay mechanic, and they still do it best.
Adding "golden-gun" parts to each level encourages exploration; it was one of the games that after finishing, I went right back to playing it again, to see if I could find all the hidden items. It doesn't hurt that trying to get through each room more effeciently is part of the game's charm: there is nothing better than bursting through doors and laying waste to everyone without taking a scratch.
No real complaints; this was a sleeper of a game, I don't know why it didn't get more attention.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is one of the best shooters I've played in a long time, and a magnificent return to form for the series. It's apparent that Machine Games put a great amount of effort and care into the title, and the blend of old school and modern shooter elements was near perfect. The levels were large and explore-able, there were secrets and hidden treasures to find, you have a wide arsenal at your disposal (as opposed to the two weapon system of a lot of modern shooters), the setting was vast and imaginative, and so many other things that shooters today are not. Although there were a few things that made it apparent this was not entirely a throwback: the movement is clunky and awkwardly weighted, scripted events were present (although thankfully not numerous), shooting from the hip is basically useless unless you're dual wielding weapons (which you can do, by the way, so that's cool), and some areas tend to turn into corridor enemy spawners. But these are merely minor faults, at worst. On top of all that, the graphics are gorgeous (although the bugs/annoyances of previous ID Tech 5 games are still present), the cutscenes are well done, and the story/characters are interesting and creative. Not to mention the soundtrack is absolutely kick♥♥♥♥♥ I loved this game, and now I certainly can't wait for the upcoming Doom title.

This game makes me sad. Im sad everytime I see the game in my library. The game itself is awesome even in its current "we-are-in-beta-what-did-you-expect" state. Im sad because nearly everyone whom I have ever invited to play it or to whom I have ever recommended it was thinking about is as "some sort of crappy PTW FPS that was made intirely to make money on youngsters who like bikini styled kevlar vests and mostly beeing another copy of CS".
Well it is not.
It is not another warface or another point blank. It has nothing in common with palladins or overwatch. Actually the closest, that came in minds of those few who tried it with me is TF2 (after youve played some time youll see they are not that similar).

The thing that matters here is your aiming skill. Be sure for 100%. If you are not able to score headshots several times in a row (there are no (well, not much) oneshots here), then there is no way that you will win a duel with ANY of those perks.

first and foremost:
drop your K/D ratio expectations before installing this game.
numbah two:
look into all the available servers before choosing one. the highest populated servers aren't always the greatest, since during peak hours, there's always a queue in whichever one of the three battlefields (within each server) has an "alert" active, which is like "whoever has the most territory by the two hour mark wins"-objective.
if you're willing to pay, you can forward into the queue i think. double check that though.
i personally approach this game more casually and want to get into the phat enough battles without waiting in line, or paying, so i stick with the lower populated servers.
when you're in, it takes some time getting used to what the hell is happening everywhere with everything. but once ya get the hang of it, it's pretty fun. the very first thing i did was say in chat "what the f*ck do i do?" and someone quickly pm'd me willing to show me the ropes and give me like a two hour tour. and that person was happy to do so.
you guys might not be as lucky like that, but still, don't be afraid of being a noob -- that goes with any game. but then again, use google as much as possible and don't ask A LOT of dumb*ss questions (IN A ROW or within a short period of time).
and don't forget to say your "thank you's!!"
but then again, if you don't care about that♥♥♥♥♥♥ go ahead. it's not like you can't just make another character with a different name or go on a different server. personally, that's too much trouble for me, but hey, i'd rather people do what htey gotta do to learn.
anyways, test out the guns before buying them. find your playstyle, including for each class, situation. and again, don't give a sh*t about your K/D ratio.
i started having more fun when i threw that K/D expectation out the window. took some time, but glad i did. and funny enough (as usual), when i did, my K/D ratio started normalizing.
it's important to have a certain loadout for each class / vehicle / role so when you get bored with one, you can just switch to another that you're competent with or feel like improving on or just f*cking around with.
of course though, you're not gonna earn enough credits fast enough, so focus on hte ones you're good at / have an affinity for first.

Been looking for a decent shooter to play that wasn't Betafield or a CoD rehash. This game hit the spot. You build your own robot, wreck other people across a few different game modes, win loot, level up, and unlock higher CPU levels to build better robots. It's free to play so expect micro transactions but don't expect those transactions to give you an edge in combat.
Pros
-Not pay-to-win
-No public KDR record to promote elitism
-Nice personal feel to killing people
-Plenty of guns and transportation-oriented objects to build some cool bots
-Recycling system that allows you to farm items and cash them in to buy better items
Cons
-Wider variety of maps is needed
-Mobility blocks like tank tracks, skiis, and tires feel extremely weak and fragile for how vulnerable they are, ultimately leading to people building planes, helicopters, mechs, hovers, and tesla balls
-The matchmaking system needs reworked. A good many people like building robots under 500 CPU to get thrown into the lowest tier available because it's more fun and challenging. You can either make a power-house bot with weak defenses, a tank with low offensive ability, or attempt to balance the two. You're limited to a very low amount of CPU you can use and that makes building bots challenging. Unfortunately, there's a leveling system that seems pointless as it does not unlock any new items to purchase to build your bots- it simply raises your max CPU level for robots and seems to factor into the queue system. For example, if you're at average skill, level 100, and build a bot under 500 CPU, you may be thrown into matches with people who have bots with CPU levels of 500-1000 just because of your level. This makes no sense and puts YOU at a serious disadvantage since there are no advantages to leveling.
Conclusion
Solid game for not being finished. The game is fun and highly addicting- there were so many times I ended up wasting HOURS just building robots. Unfortunately, the matchmaking system is a deal-breaker for me. Getting matched up against robots with CPU levels around 800 when your bot is under 500 is about as effective as trying to sprint across an open field with a knife to stab a sniper. It's almost as if the game is forcing you to build higher-tier bots and, honestly, those matches are dull and boring. Some people might not mind it, but I do. Make the matchmaking system fair and this is easily one of my favourite games.

Wolfenstein: TNO is a meathead shooter straight out of the 90s with absolutely no new ideas.
I feel that everything you need to know about the game comes down to the selection of weapons it gives you. You have:
- Pistols (with a silencer)
- Assault rifles
- Shotguns
- Sniper rifles
- A laser
- Knives
And that's it. You couldn't have a more bog standard set of armaments in an FPS if you tried. There's no grenade launcher, there's no jetpack, there's no light saber, there's no psychic telekinesis... just a standard set of weapons to use against a standard set of enemies. You can't even do something as radical as hold a shotgun in one hand and an assault rifle in the other.
It's not aggressively bad, in spite of its stupid habit of taking away all your guns at arbitrary moments in the game, but there's just nothing here that I haven't seen before. Even the battle against the giant spider mech consists of tired 'shoot him in the eye and then hit the weakpoint' gameplay.
Maybe that's enough for some people. Maybe all you want to do is point your gun at someone speaking German and fire. I get it. But I think that in a post-Bioshock world, our shooters should have higher standards than that.
As for its story, I've seen it being lauded in a lot of different quarters. It's not terrible I guess, but I think that if you want to attempt to create serious alternate history fiction revolving around the Nazi regime then you probably should leave out the robot dogs.
Just sayin'

Maaaaan this game... I actually finished it, which was kind of a feat. I don't know if it was the health mechanic, my lack of talent, or simply the game, but this was a lengthy experience. It's kind of strange actually. I bought this thinking it'd be a quick grimy, shooty romp, especially given the focus on the games multiplayer, which I did not touch. But there is a full length third person shooter, with at least three different action movies worth of plot.
The games presentation is kind of ridiculous actually. From the VHS scan lines to the painstakingly animated exit wounds, this game wants you to take it seriously. And if it was around say half it's length and omitted the flashbacks, you might be able to. But nothing disconnects the tone and style of the story the game is trying to tell more than its gamplay. You're a rough, barely functing ex-cop on the edge, struggling through a haze of drug and pill addiction, trying to ride connections and past success into an easy retirement.The game works to convey this to you with every other line out of Max's mouth. And Max immediately proceeds to outshoot, outrun and generally outmurder a shadowy cabal of criminals, paramilitary, actual military, and like an army of italian gangsters, with no more than three guns at any one time. That said, if you edited the cutscenes and say, the last minute of combat from each level you'd have an overwrought, noir inspired B-movie starring the guy from Beaking Bad.
You will definitely get your moneys worth if you buy this, not including the mutiplayer. Just be aware there's some Rockstar account DRM nonsense you'll need to sign up for, even for the single player.

Finally, a game that truly feels oldschool. I love how much effort was put into the singleplayer because the devs concentrated solely on it, leaving out the multiplayer.
The story is pretty intriguing (if not too complex) and the length of it is also pretty damn high for a linear game. Took me about 25 hours to complete it on easy difficulty while taking my time to explore the enviroment (which is made up beautifully, every little sign or poster is worth reading).
The gameplay itself? True oldschool shooter with no regenerating health, armor, all kinds of dakka, most of which you can dual wield for even more carnage. Blowing limbs off is not uncommon and generally the whole game has that special feel that you rarely see these days if you do at all.
Of course, there is no oldschool FPS without hidden areas and items, right? That's right, the devs didn't forget about that either. Lots of stuff to discover and find, you can solve puzzles with the stuff gained from exploration (which I did not complete yet, so I can't have an opinion on it).
All in all, if you loved the FPS games of the past decade, you will really appreciate this one :)

Just a quick note:
I've played all the previous Wolfenstein games except the 2009 variant and have followed the game since it originally came out in the 90's.  Wolfenstein was awesome back then :)
Overall (more details below):
Wolfenstein doesn't break a lot of new ground, but what it does do it does pretty well.  I found it to be a fair amount of fun, with a good story, good level design, good graphics and good gameplay. It took me 12 hours to complete on Hard Mode, but I tonned it down for the end boss since I wanted to finish it up as it was getting late.
This is a FIRST PERSON SHOOTER.  This is not Dishonored, Call of Duty, Crysis or whatever.  It is Wolfenstein and the game tends to keep that original Wolfenstein feel for the most part.
Basically, if you like first person shooters, this is a MUST BUY game.
Period.
Note:
Realize a bunch of your weapons have Alternate Fire Modes.  Your pistol for example can go to SILENCED mode.
Graphics:
The graphics are pretty good.  Clearly not the best out there, but still really good.  It suffers from the same issues that the ID Tech 5 engine suffers from, so if you have played Rage, you know what I mean.  Still, the graphics fit the world pretty good and there are plenty of neat effects.  I would of prefered some higher resolution textures in certain areas, but whatever.
Story:
I had no idea what to expect from the story, and this one was actually decent this time around.  It is told with pretty good voice acting, cut scenes and a some audio logs and such within the game.  It isn't the most gripping story, but its good enough.  It didn't get into the stupid like the last game did with super natural.
Level Design:
Nothing too memorable here as far as Level Design is concerned, its mostly your standard Quake/Doom type shooter with corridors and some interesting areas (the bridge area, the starting castle area was cool).  Some areas are a bit open, allowing you to do whatever you want, others are more corridor.  The levels are good though, just don't expect anything here to stand out in your mind after you finish the game.  At least it didn't for me.
Perks:
There is a basic Perk System in the game that allows you to grow your character a bit.  I didn't really aim to grow it too much, but it does add a bit to the game as you can do certain things to give you extra perks, like more Knives, etc.
Gameplay:
The Stealth part of the game is actually pretty well done and I took advantage of it whenever I could.  If you break stealth though, you can't go back into it until the next area.  The idea of neautralizing the Captains/Officers to prevent re-inforcements is a neat gameplay element, and I usually tried to do that.  So you can stealth through until you kill a officer with a knife/silencer and then run and gun the rest of the area if you want.
There is a hub area you stop by a couple times, things to collect, some upgrades to get for your one weapon, etc.
The types of Monsters are challenging, with a few being a bit annoying.  A few areas I had to try 5 or 6 times to kill everybody before they got me, but it didn't get too hard on Hard.
Weapons:
I found the weapons to be ok.  Nothing over powered, and for the most part I used everything a lot.  In the later stages, you use your Welding/Lazer gun a lot.  You upgrade it, and depending on the monster, you can 1 shot kill a lot of the tougher things.
Bad Guys:
Lots of Nazi's, and you can shoot them in the head for quick kills.  The armored ones can be annoying (flak cannon guy sucks♥♥♥♥♥ but the rest are fun to kill and provide enough of a challenge.
Stealth:
As I said, the stealth part is ok done.  Use your Pistol (switch to Silencer Mode) or throwing Knifes.

I do recommend the game however I do
believe the game suffers a lot due to
the addition of new elements into the game.
The Following contains minor hints at the
game which some may consider spoilers, if you
do not wish these elements to be spoiled for
you here's the TL;DR:
-It's a good game however it does have
certain issues the first game did not have.
Pros:
-The new mechanics added into Portal 2
give a bit more flavor. You still use portals
in conjunction with the new puzzle mechanics like
the gels, which flow really well.
-The music is excellent, Highly recommend getting it.
-The added plant life and broken down interiors
to the test chambers are a great addition.
Cons:
-Test chambers now have A LOT more
black panels, making it really obvious where
you're supposed to place portals. This means
most puzzles are limited to one type of solution.
In the first game white panels were more common, which
actually made the puzzles a bit more challenging because
you needed to figure out where the portals had to
be placed yourself.
-Also, even when there are many white panels around,
the game gives you the portal placement on a
silver platter. Most white panels in the game
are either broken or covered in moss or rust....
Except for the one panel where you need to place
the portal, which is often completely clean and free of any
imperfection, and often has a different line pattern
to make it stand out from the other white panels.
This is taken to the point where puzzles are so
simplified you could argue (and I would) that they
are not really puzzles.
-Wheatly doesn't have any distortion in his
voice. Considering that he is a core, and every single
other core has a distorted voice, this is a bit off. Not saying
his line delivery is bad.
-The game more often than not tries it's hardest to be
funny, often stoppinjg the game and having you listen to a
"funny" line. Stuff like the Birds, the potatos, and GLaDOS
poking fun at Chell being adopted and fat. Same with Wheatly.
It feels as if Valve is trying to re-capture the level of viral humor
they got from Portal 1 with stuff like the Companion Cube.
-Cave Johnson's addition is a bit off. Again his lines often spout
out jokes or funny-sounding lines. I mean Aperture always had
really crazy scientists, but at this point the game just
spits out all sorts of crazy experiments. Like how apparently
there is or used to be a race of Mantis Men created by
Aperture Science in the Half-Life/Portal universe.
I do still think Portal 2 is a good game, and do recommend it.

Ok, while much of this review is subject to debate, it essentially biols down to the fact that I really enjoyed this game.
While previous entries to the Wolfenstein franchise have been infamously shallow, TNO actually attempted to aadd that extra dimension.
It must be said, there is still a little way to go, but I think it's fair to say no one buys a Wolfenstein game for the compelling storyline, although this one gives it a good effort.
The gunplay is genuinely satisfying, visceral and entertaining. Who knew blowing Nazi limbs off could be such a pleasure. However I would say that the variety in weapons leaves a little to be desired, as most are just full auto bullet sprayers it seems. Some interesting points like bouncing shotgun bullets and energy weapons go almost under the radar, when they could be really game changing.
Level design is good and there's enough variety in tactics to keep them interesting, although in some situations your hand is forced into certain attack patterns where it would be nice to have a choice.
Boss battles are a little easy, but herald back to the days of old in thier design and progression.
Then of course we come to the main character, who within the first mission is hit in the face by a flying plane. Twice. Then has a giant boulder dropped on his face. Later on he is stabbed in the face and repeatedly in his chest, yet he still keeps on going. In short, He's a ♥♥♥♥ING TANK.
So in conclusion, this game does have its little flaws here and there, but it is completely ridiculous and so is a really enjoyable and engaging experience. This game is definitely one of my favourite games so far this year and one of the most entertaining shooters I've played in a while. It's really nice to see a game that doesn't take itself too seriously nowadays :)

Don't be fooled by the first glance on the community! Dirty Bomb is a great FPS game which stands out from other games.
There are multiple characters to choose from(called Mercs). These Mercs have different abilities varying from Medpacks and ammo stations to lasers and landmines. All of these mercs have their "class". There are currently 5 main classes, which is Medic, Firesupport, Objective Specialists(aka Engineers), Recon and Combat.
- Medics are the backbone of any team, since they heal.. and do other magic tricks..
- Well, firesupporters give ammo and have fancy abilities like molotovs, airstrikes and lasers.
- Engineers are mercs who are able to do objectives much faster than other mercs(cus they have shiny smartphones), and they are very important if you wanna win a match.
- Recons are snipers and sneaky mercs. They mostly spot enemies so their team knows where to shoot.
- Combat mercs are those who kill alot of stuff. They often
a medic so they don't die so fast. These mercs have lots of HP
There are 3 gamemodes, Objective, Stopwatch and Execution. Objective is a standard gamemode where one team defends some objectives(Defenders) and one team blow stuff up(Attackers). This gamemode is time-limited and the time is based on the map.
Stopwatch is the same as Objective, but there are 2 rounds in a match. This is more of a competitive gamemode, I'll come with an example : One team(teamA) does 1/3 objectives using 10 minutes(so they lost the round). Then the teams swap and the other team(teamB) is gonna beat the time by, lets say using 5 minutes to complete 2/3 objectives.

And then we have the gamemode called Execution. This is pretty much just like CS:GO. Attacking team is gonna blow up something, and defending team has to stop them. There are around 14/12 rounds( i dont play it that much xP ). The teams switch mid-game and the team with the most round-wins, wins the whole match.
So it has a simple parkour system allowing you to do walljumps to either get around faster, or to trick your enemies at close quarters. There isn't so many good spots to use parkour, but it's useful on maps where the devs haven't put invisible walls everywhere. Also, try to be moving all the time!
The game is a TTK(Time To Kill) game, which means enemies have different health points! Some can be killed in a flash, others take more bullets to kill.
This is pretty much all the basics you should know about DB( this is more of a guide but ok xP ),  I hope it helps :)

This is probably the best puzzle game ever made. It is a puzzle game for everyone and an extremely fun game to play. It was not a difficult game to complete and the story was very satisfying. Portal 2 is absolutely worth the purchase even if you are terrible at puzzle games. Every puzzle was clever and engaging yet none of the puzzles were difficult enough to make my brain hurt.
In terms of difficulty, Portal 2 is a cakewalk to complete compared to games like The Witness, though I don't consider it a bad thing since I got too frustrated with that game to continue playing it. Being so well-balanced in its difficulty, Portal 2 is much more of a joy to play than all the other puzzle games combined. It is a puzzle game I was actually able to get through smoothly without having to look up hints/answers or trying to pull my hair out.
My only complaint is that the final chapter was way too easy. None of the final puzzles were challenging and the final boss battle was easily completed on my first try. The most difficult puzzles were in chapters six, seven, and eight, but there were only a few puzzles in the game that had me stumped for a while trying to figure out what to do.
Overall, this game is almost perfect in every way. The only other puzzle game I found to be anywhere near as engaging and interactive as this game is The Talos Principle, which is great in its own way but fails to match Portal 2 in terms of pacing, dialogue, and entertainment value. This game is truly something special and I recommend it to all gamers, regardless of their puzzle solving skills.

By and large a pretty good game, as shooters go.  Just a few major quibbles.
1) You're touched by the hand of God.  Therefore you're screwed.:  No matter how you play or what you do, there are certain junctions where a pre-programmed action WILL occur and that will deprive you of almost all of your health, or all of your weapons, or something.  Just because.  A guy is hiding.  You know he's there, so you toss in a grenade.  Turns out he's grenade-proof.  So he tortures you to within an inch of your life before you magically manage to fight back and barely save yourself.  Now nearly dead, you march on to face the boss, because for the first time anytime in the game, this particular lab has absolutely no health packs in it, and the door you came in has become magically sealed.  You know the drill.  The last refuge of the creatively bereft.
2) Magic weapons:  All through the game from the time you raid the London Lab, you have this laser cannon, which apparrently fits in your ear canal, because you can carry it with you everywhere and nobody notices.  However, toward the end, it's amazingly useful on robots.  In the third-to-last fight, though, suddenly it vanishes when you're fighting - you guessed it - a giant killer robot.  So you have to fight this robot with a dagger and whatever you can find on hand.  That's bad.  However, once you defeat the robot, the second-to-last boss - a mech - marches into the *SAME AREA* - you're still standing next to the giant killer robot - and suddenly your pocket-cannon is BACK!  It's about as contrived a hurdle as you can possibly get.  It's not as if they figured nobody would notice that it kind of threw the continuity out.  They just didn't care if there *WAS* continuity.  Platform gamers, I guess, are used to such idiocy.
3) The puzzles solved by death:  There are more than a couple of 'puzzles' in this game whose solution is simple but not immediately obvious that you have about 5 seconds to solve before you die.  Consequently, you die about fifteen times trying to figure out a way past it.  Once you know how to get past it, it's not a puzzle at all anymore - it's just a pre-destined path that you must learn.  Why it is that they don't bother to give you time to learn it without the constant reloading of the save point, I don't know.
4) Save points:  Yes, those again.  In their defense, they're reasonably well-placed for the most part.  To their disgrace, they still have a whole bunch of programmers - in the 21st century - who don't know what a disk drive is.  That was pathetic ten years ago.  It is not somehow becoming *less* pathetic as the years go on.
But, I'll still recommend it.  Aside from the blandly obvious in-your-face dumb stuff noted above, it's actually pretty good.  But here's a hint.  The 'nightmare' is kinda dumb.

One of my favorite shooters all year. If you liked Black, you'll love this. If you liked the recent Shadow Warrior reboot, you'll love this. If you liked Chronicles of Riddick: ESFF or AODA, you'll probably like this. Funny enough, if you're in love with Wolfenstein and only Wolfenstein, you may be on the fence. The game's design is not just informed by the evolution of this single franchise, but the genre as a whole. It introduces things some may not like. It does fall victim to some modern shooter tropes like scripted sequences and exposition vomit cutscenes. That being said, I'd say it does it better than anyone has in the past 5 years... Scripted sequences and cutscenes were genuinely well done. Voice acting is amazing, with every cast member's native language being that of their character's leading to some awesome (I can assume) improvised lines.
Solid shooter. Good characters. Well balanced puzzles. Good amount of hidden collectibles and areas. Gory as hell. Satisfying guns. You get bottlenecked a few times and there's moments of stupid difficulty spikes (I mean literally being thrust into an ambush of armored enemies with flak shotguns and you only 20 percent health and some pistols, the health being forced no matter how much you went in with), but it's worth it.
The ending is a bit obtuse, attempting to leave it open while tying the arc up in a nice bow. It doesn't really do this very well, but the journey was so damn fun to me it didn't matter.
Graphics are what you'd expect from an Idtech 5 game. Not ground breaking on any technical level, but obviously created with an artistic freedom that no other tool set can provide. Love went into the look of this game. So did Tor Frick. If you've never heard of this dude, look him up. He's a hard surface modeling god. Despite some visual glitches due to Idtech 5 being Idtech 5, the game is truly something to behold if you can appreciate some good design work over modern technical standards.
Solid 9.5 from me.

With Portal 2, Valve have succeeded in creating a brilliant full-length sequel for the original Portal. How they have done it is anyone's guess, but I managed to get about 13 hours out of this game compared to about 3 in the first game, enjoyed every minute, and somehow Portal 2 seemed just as tight, taut, and economical as Portal was. There's still no flab or unnecessary padding and the game, despite being puzzle after puzzle, never feels repetitive.
The main reason for this is the quality of the puzzles. They are absolutely ingenious. The solutions to all of them are deceptively simple yet it still feels like a major breakthrough when you solve them. The level design is such that in some of the bigger ones you might spend upwards of 20 minutes trying to find an answer, and when you eventually do it seems like the most obvious thing in the world. Often the simplest way is the best. As soon as you get an idea in your head, try it! Don't come back to the game another time as you may forget it.
Only a few of the walls/surfaces accept portals, but somehow the answers to the puzzles still never feel contrived or obviously placed. Still, when you see surfaces that can accept portals, you can be sure that this is a clue for how to crack the puzzle. Other than that, pay attention to the info boards at the beginning of each test - they show you what elements are needed, but otherwise it's all up to you on how to use them. There are plenty of new innovations in the sequel, like light bridges, tunnels of light that can transport you and any other physical objects over gaps, and new fluids or "gels" that manipulate physics in some way. I won't tell you what they do, as discovering that is part of the fun. It's not just a matter of pressing buttons but also you need to get the timing right in many puzzles as well. It's also worth noting that many of the chambers are huge - the sense of scale and the number of things you need to use can be daunting at first, which only makes the feeling of getting to the exit in the end sweeter.
Flaws are minor. I did have a couple of crashes, it's a bit odd that there's no fall damage (although the game would probably have been less fun if there was), the loading zones are small, and there is one gel puzzle two-thirds of the way through that relies on a little bit of luck as well as timing. But that's about it, I had more fun playing this game than anything since Half-Life 2, and I wasn't even a puzzle/platforming fan before playing Portal 2.

Rockstar's Max Payne 3  is surely one of my favorite games of all time, as the makers of the game worked hard to put a lot of detail into the environment throughout the game without sacrificing any game mechanics making each level unique and beautiful. Speaking of game mechanics, the combat system in the game is really the icing on the cake, the bullet time ability allows you to carefully place your shots as well as allowing you to move from cover to cover in an epic way. There are many weapons in the game that you can use, ranging from pistols/revolvers and sub machine guns to rifles and shotguns, all weapons you have equipped will appear on Max's body as well as appearing in cut scenes where in some situations you will have your weapons taken away from you. Movement is fluid which gives the game a realistic effect to it. Max Payne 3 is easy to pick up which welcomes any new comers to the Max Payne series. All together the cut scenes of the game, voice actors and Max's narrative really brings the characters to life. Though unlike Max Payne 1 & 2, Max Payne 3's story isn't all that dark but still depressing. After playing Max Payne 3 I can't wait to see GTA V on PC as it includes a character named Micheal De Santa(Micheal Townley) who is similar to Max Payne having the ability to slow down time during combat and being miserable. :D
TLDR:
+ Detailed environments
+ Excellent voice acting
+ Bullet time ability
+ Simply HUD
+ Realistic movement
+ An Arsenal of weapons
+ Action based plot
+ Easy to pick up
+ Fun and challenging
- A few bugs here and there
- Max may make you feel depressed

This review is for the single-player portion. I did not play the multiplayer.
Wolfenstein: The New Order isn't a 10/10 game. It's really not an 8/10 either. That said, it is so vastly better than most any shooter that has come out in god knows how long and its old-school level design and difficulty is something to be commended.
Starting the game I was worried: Getting bombared by objectives and cinematic sequences isn't exactly promising for gameplay in this day and age. But, low and behold, after the first 5 or so minutes I was shooting nazi's with a variety of weapons and having no tutorials shoved into my throat. It gave me free reign to experiment with whatever I saw fit. On top of that, instead of incorporating a leaning to two buttons (left and right, respectively), it incorporates a more interesting system. Holding alt activates lean, which you can then lean in any direction you see fit. It works wonderfully and added a layer of depth to combat. The enemy AI was nice too, ducking behind corners and running when you shoot them. It's not something revolutionary, but a nice touch that is a must for a game centered around gunplay. Additional weapon types and ammo are a plus, as is an old-school multi-gun arsenal, no two weapon limit in sight. Almost every level introduces something new which is wonderful, not enough games do this anymore. Boss fights are probably the only thing I'd criticize, as they're not very inventive. Just shoot until it dies.
The story isn't half-bad either. Though it suffers from manly gravel voiceovers, it's nice to see characters that aren't paperthin like most shooters. Each person has a small backstory that usually explains how they are today. The game also has a lovely change in scenery every few levels, going from the civillian sections to a labor camp and eventually to the moon. It sets a nice background for killing nazis to. Though I view the ending as fairly dumb and rushed, if you're gonna allude to such a large climax, you better show it.
The latest Wolfenstein will last you about 10 or so hours on the single player campaign and the difficulty levels are definitely varied enough to give you a reason to replay. It's definitely worth $30 or so.
Note: There are noteworthy graphical issues with this game. I spent around 2 hours trying to get it running smoothly on an intel/nvidia rig. It requires more than just a workaround or executable before you launch the game. Texture pop-in, as always with ID Tech 5, is horrendous and the game can stutter here and there. Aside from this, it was running fairly smoothly the whole way through.

Just know that this game just barely qualifies as an "HD" version. You won't really notice the difference while you're playing. But then, graphics are doing their job if you don't notice them.
Aside from that, a solid classic. Worth any RTS fan's time.

Ah yisss. It's been a long time since I've enjoyed a single player story driven FPS this much. Wolfenstein: The New Order (W:TNO) is somewhat of a return to roots for the venerable franchise. As most people know, the first game, Wolfenstein 3D is the FPS PC game that popularized the genre and is responsible for its continued success today. After a few sequels, an amazing multiplayer game, and a supposedly disappointing reboot in 2009, W:TNO has a lot to prove. Thankfully, W:TNO exceeds expectations and more.
We return to protagonist B.J. Blazkowicz, the seemingly most generic of all generic McWhite guys who gets knocked out in a late WW2 operation to take down series antagonist uber Nazi, Deathshead. He wakes up 14 years later, but the world has changed. The Nazis won. The Beatles are singing in german. Manhattan is a nuclear wasteland. Swastika flags are flown across the world. Instead of a U.S. army, there is nothing but a small insurgency against the world's new masters. This change in narrative is well executed and shows a hopeless group of rebels fighting for little more than a dream of a world that no longer exists. I was genuinely surprised by how seriously this game took itself, but instead of being soapy and melodramatic, it hit some legitimately painful emotional notes. The storyline is dark and dreary, strange in a game that allows you to dual wield automatic shotguns and blast entire rooms of nazis to bits.
It’s strangely refreshing to see a return to the design of older FPSes. W: TNO is released on today’s market full of killstreaks and regenerating health, where an FPS with no multiplayer component is akin to financial suicide. It’s released in a market full of games with moral ambiguity as well as unrestrained jingoism. However, the bad guys in W: TNO have no moral ambiguity. They’re just evil, dastardly Nazis, who have now taken over the world and are spreading their evil deeds like wildfire. Which makes killing them very cathartic. And oh boy, is the gunplay in this game fantastic. You can dual wield most weapons and each gun is “punchy” and full of character. Eventually you’ll get alternate firing modes that adds to the strategy, as you can have a gun in your right hand using one mode and the gun in the other using another. If I have a complaint about the gunplay is that dual wielding is pretty OP. I understand that this game is all about mowing down Nazis without discrimination, but there’s literally no reason to NOT dual wield. Honestly, you don’t really suffer an aiming penalty at all for holding two giant assault rifles, you can still hit a penny from hundreds of yards away. Regardless, busting into a room, strafing the entire area with a hailstorm of bullets, churning up papers, woodwork and blasting into groups of Nazis, throwing blood splatter and body parts everywhere in a violent cacophony is really something quite special. The stealth system works well too, it’s much like Far Cry 3’s sneaky beaky stuff with throwing knives and silenced pistols.
The developers were right in stating that the lack of multiplayer really allowed them to focus on bringing an amazing world to life. This is one of those games where there’s almost  too much detail. You can read tons of newspapers clippings hung up the wall, each explaining a snippet of just how the Nazis won the war. They didn't have to model the thompson submachine gun just for the first mission of the game (never seen for the rest of the game), but they did anyway in order to avoid being anachronistic. Every part of the world is meticulously crafted, from the books lined on a Nazis commander’s room to subtle graffiti dotting the Berlin sewers. It’s all extremely pretty and immersive, and it shows by the insanely large install size (~50gb). I had to leave my computer for almost half a week for it to finish. Regardless, this game is a labor of love, and an incredible showcase of how much detail a development team can cram into the environment.
$60 bucks is asking a bit much for a single player experience that lasts about 15 hours, but multiple playthroughs and collectible items are reasons to come back for more. The core shooting and stealth mechanics are enjoyable and never get old. I’d say wait for it to be about 50% off to pick it up, but if you’re an FPS shooter fan, especially if you’re a fan of older FPSes, this is a must have!
