Overall, this game is great!
BUT
there are some major flaws that need to be (and surely already have been) addressed
1st: immediately, one may not help but notice how similar in visual and literary style (style of what little spoken diaglogue there is) it is to Team Fortress 2. Some may view this as a good, bad, or irrelevant thing, but it's almost uncanny to me.
2nd: the parkour elements (the ability to wall jump on and off of nearly every surface) are reminescent of Mirror's Edge, but are no where near as useful or dynamic. It's easy to suggest a complete overhaul is needed on these mechanics before being useful (if not bearable).
3rd: the progression system is SOOOOOO pay-2-win, especially after level 6; it would take about a month or two of grinding to progress past the aforementioned level.
4th: customization of weapons seems absent, but perhaps for good reason, perhaps for stylistic and/or gameplay reasons... Either that, or I just don't know how to, which brings me to my next point...
5th: the user interface may seem nice and clean, and it is, but it's unorganized as well, which probably explains why I can never seem to find the store or class sections. (and/or Black Ops 2 has spoiled me)
Now, here are the pros:
1st: the gameplay is very tactical, if you're into that kinda stuff, and the maps almost force you to do so; there is no deathmatch in this game; all modes are goal or objective-oriented, which is a fresh step in the right direction.
2nd: the characters are unique and fun to play and experiment with; eahc with their own witty banter and stylistic features; some lines tend to be cringe-worthy after a while though.
3rd: the game has this cool system where, instead of choosing one loadout per round, you're only able to use 3 different mercs, each with their own strengths, weaknesses, and special abilities.
4th: the maps are amazing for the game's mechanics, with lots of tight corners and ledges to jump around and be agile about. They're not too big and not too small, and quite easy to mentally visualize, making them easy to traverse.
5th: along with the Team Fortress 2-esque style comes the speed of the player/character, which is faster than normal, kinda like Doom's multiplayer, but much better. speed is noticeably increase when your secondary firearm is equipped, even more so with your melee weapon.
6th: it's just really fun to play, with a light-hearted feel to it, it feels like a game instead of a grim war story like Call of Duty, Halo, or even Doom.
So, in short, Dirty Bomb is a great game that could use a little more work and a lot less pay walls.

Max Payne 3 is a fantastic game.
It's an action oriented third person shooter, basically. Where this game shines is in the details and the impressive challenge it can present to you. While the story is...alright, this game is amazing in how Max narrates the story and the events around him. There is a definite homage to film noir, and Max's chilling narrations are both incredibly well written and hauntingly appropriate.
Max moves in a very realistic way, turning his body and rolling and falling in a way that's very believable, despite some moments in the game where you sorta...jump the shark in terms of action. There's an IMMENSE focus on headshots and precision, and you will most certainly have a hard time beating this game if you are not a good shot. There are multiple difficulty settings, but even Normal can present a good challenge at times.
The use of bullet time is central to the game's mechanics, but Max Payne 3 uses it well, sometimes scripted in it's use, but also allowing you to use the limited function to engage large groups of enemies for Die Hard-esque cinematic style asskickery.
The game also looks fantastic, and the game runs smoothly. I haven't experienced any bugs or glitches in it. Rockstar did a great job making a PC version of this game. Aiming is responsive and won't hold you back or hinder you. It's just you, your gun, and your aim.
I definitely recommend if you enjoy shooters that take skill, are full of action, and basically just trying to get as many people as possible to stop your bullets with the bridge of their noses.

This review is for the single-player portion. I did not play the multiplayer.
Wolfenstein: The New Order isn't a 10/10 game. It's really not an 8/10 either. That said, it is so vastly better than most any shooter that has come out in god knows how long and its old-school level design and difficulty is something to be commended.
Starting the game I was worried: Getting bombared by objectives and cinematic sequences isn't exactly promising for gameplay in this day and age. But, low and behold, after the first 5 or so minutes I was shooting nazi's with a variety of weapons and having no tutorials shoved into my throat. It gave me free reign to experiment with whatever I saw fit. On top of that, instead of incorporating a leaning to two buttons (left and right, respectively), it incorporates a more interesting system. Holding alt activates lean, which you can then lean in any direction you see fit. It works wonderfully and added a layer of depth to combat. The enemy AI was nice too, ducking behind corners and running when you shoot them. It's not something revolutionary, but a nice touch that is a must for a game centered around gunplay. Additional weapon types and ammo are a plus, as is an old-school multi-gun arsenal, no two weapon limit in sight. Almost every level introduces something new which is wonderful, not enough games do this anymore. Boss fights are probably the only thing I'd criticize, as they're not very inventive. Just shoot until it dies.
The story isn't half-bad either. Though it suffers from manly gravel voiceovers, it's nice to see characters that aren't paperthin like most shooters. Each person has a small backstory that usually explains how they are today. The game also has a lovely change in scenery every few levels, going from the civillian sections to a labor camp and eventually to the moon. It sets a nice background for killing nazis to. Though I view the ending as fairly dumb and rushed, if you're gonna allude to such a large climax, you better show it.
The latest Wolfenstein will last you about 10 or so hours on the single player campaign and the difficulty levels are definitely varied enough to give you a reason to replay. It's definitely worth $30 or so.
Note: There are noteworthy graphical issues with this game. I spent around 2 hours trying to get it running smoothly on an intel/nvidia rig. It requires more than just a workaround or executable before you launch the game. Texture pop-in, as always with ID Tech 5, is horrendous and the game can stutter here and there. Aside from this, it was running fairly smoothly the whole way through.

I'm a newcomer to the genre of killing Nazis, but Wolfenstein: New Order has made me a fan. I now dream about Nazis, and in my dreams I come ever so close to ending old Adolf before he can end himself. But we'll save those juicy tidbits for my psychiatrist.
The game is based on a premise that has been done ad naseum in alternate history stories, but it works in establishing your moral incentive for mindlessly slaughtering every Nazi in your path. In sum, Nazis now rule the world. 'Murica's great cities of New York and Boston have been reduced to atomic ashes. The beginning of the game has you thrust in the middle of the action, years before the Nazi takeover, a last ditch attempt by the allied coalition to stop the Nazi war machine. Early on you have to make a difficult choice that would break the most feeble-minded of men, but not BJ, Blazko or Blazkowicz, the series' hero. Right from the beginning the game plunges the player into the throes of a pivotal moment in this game world, with no moment to breathe or relax. This makes for a truly gripping experience.
From a gameplay standpoint, the game is a pretty standard FPS shooter. You can take cover and lean from the walls and take potshots, but nothing too fancy. You can dual wield pretty much every weapon available. Forget the plausibility of doing so and remember that you're a Nazi killing machine. There are three gameplay trees that allow for upgraded abilities and enhancements: stealth, assault and demolition, if I recall correctly. My preference is the knife, so many of my kills on unsuspecting Nazis were stealthy knife kills. Kudos to the developers for the gruesome takedowns. In one memorable moment, BJ can kill a Nazi commander as he sleeps. BJ thrusts his knife from under the bunk bed and into the back of the poor sap. Satisfying. Anyway, by killing many Nazis with my knife, I unlocked perks that increased my ability to carry knives and unlocked the ability to throw them for ranged stealth kills. Throwing knives do have an arc when thrown, so tossing them a bit upward should allow you to target Nazis from a distance. Every kill, from jamming your knife into a pesky guard dog to blasting Nazis to bits, has a satisfying feel to it. As BJ, you feel like a master craftsman, your craft the art of killing. And he does it well, much to the dismay of his enemies.
BJ has lots of guns to choose from in his quest to rid the world of Nazi scum, ranging from rifles to shotguns and unlockable weapon upgrades. I found myself relying on dual rifles for the most part. The ammo's pretty plentiful and you'll be plowing through most grunts with ease. You will have to select different weapons to effectively deal with the armored super soldiers. For these enemy types, laser based weapons may be more suitable than standard solid projectile based weapons. Or just blast them to bits with your rocket launching rifle upgrade. Yes, your rifle can later fire rockets. Variety is the spice of the Nazi killing life, indeed.
In a gaming era in which modern stealth-based games have raised the standard for enemy AI, the AI in Wolfenstein is a step down to a time where guards exclaimed “I feel asleep!” Nazi commanders can be dispatched to prevent them from calling reinforcements, which is neat for the stealth-minded player, but they are often standing still, facing some pointless direction or strolling around. Other guards move in predictable patterns. Move left. Stop. Move back. Stop. If they do spot you, and you're quick enough to move behind a corner, they’ll say, “huh” and go back to walking in the same pattern as if nothing happened. For the most part, you can easily stroll up to most enemies without them reacting. If they do catch you in the act, a few clicks during a brief struggle is all it takes to finish him. And mind you this is on hard mode, or "I am death incarnate" mode.
Fortunately, during firefights, enemies will take cover and attempt to flank you. I remember going down one hall to take down some Nazi scum from behind, only to find another Nazi right behind me. Firefights can be pretty intense as a hail of bullets come down on you from all directions. I do think that the availability of health kits, ammo and armor did make the game an easier experience. Veteran FPS fans may claim that the game is more casual friendly because of this. I tend to agree on this aspect, but there were a few moments when I felt like I was screwed. Even then, you can exploit the AI and run back in some areas. The enemies often stop chasing, giving you time to recover (if you've lost almost all of your health, at most you can regenerate up to 20 health out of, say, 100) and launch a counteroffensive.
The game does an excellent job of preventing stagnation, masking the fact that you're just killing waves of Nazis, by dropping you in diverse battle environments. At one point, you’re no longer killing Nazis on Earth, but, in the words of the great Blazko, the mother-♥♥♥♥ing moon. The game’s a rollercoaster of near non-stop Nazi killing action with a few opportunities for character development in the form interactions with your fellow resistance members, unique characters who, in a short time, you might grow to like. Here I'll commend the developers for taking the time to add depth to the nightmarish world that BJ now inhabits. Scattered throughout the game world are newspaper clippings that add context to this alternate timeline. The narrative and characters are compelling enough for us to care, a nice touch for what could have otherwise been a pretty generic FPS experience.
That said, the game begins to become a little stale by the end, which isn't too bad considering the strong beginning and middle arcs. By the final level, the freshness of the earlier levels was gone and all I was left with the reality that all I was doing was killing waves of the same Nazi types – unarmored, armored, biomechanical dogs, super soldiers, robots -- over and over again. Anticipating enemies became predictable. First, a few waves of grunts, which are easily dispatched, then move forward and a few hulking supersoldier Nazis come down raining laser minigun hell. At this point, you've unlocked the perks and acquired the weapons necessary for dispatching these Nazi fools without breaking a sweat. It's still fun, of that there's no doubt, but it feels a like a bit of a lazy way to end a great game.
Still, I recommend this game. It’s rare nowadays that I’ll run through a game in a day without stopping. If anything, the game succeeds in making the player feel badass by fixing a world gone wrong, one dead Nazi at a time.

Dirty Bomb - это командный мультиплеерный шутер, действие которого происходит в Лондоне 2020х годов, опустевшем после загадочной техногенной катастрофы. В игре присутствует две конкурирующие частные военные компании, взявшие на себя обязанность контролировать ценности, еще оставшиеся в городе. Как не трудно догадаться, вы и будете воевать за одну из группировок.
Сражаться надо в кампании наемников ради контроля над ключевыми зонами с жизненно важными ресурсами. Происходить это будет в закоулках Лондона, его подземных научных комплексах, открытых площадках, мостах через Темзу и многих других локациях. Графическое окружение в игре аккуратное и имеет красочную эстетику, где то между ультра-глянцем и футуристической мультяшностью. Физическая среда хорошо продумана и разнообразна, геймплей в Dirty Bomb то несется как на американских горках, то застревает в узких средневековых улочках.
В настоящее время игра предлагает два полноценных игровых режима, плюс третий, экспериментальный режим. Цель все режимов проста: одна команда атакует, другая защищается, одна команда сопровождает автомобиль, другая пытается его уничтожить. Играть придется на время, к тому же еще выполняя дополнительные задания, которые дают очень полезные бонусы. Например, во время боя вы сможете отремонтировать воздушный насос, с помощью которого откачаете ядовитый газ из пещеры. Открывшийся проход подарит вам выход прямо на фланг команды противника.
Классовые сословия в Dirty Bomb разнообразны и умеют образовывать суб-классы. Есть несколько вариаций на медика, солдата, инженера, артиллериста - и каждый из них можно немного изменить. Персонаж может сосредоточиться на всех аспектах боя или двигаться в одном направлении: получать технологичные обвесы на оружие, индивидуальную защиту и т.д. Но всё же, в Dirty Bomb огромное значение имеет командная игра. Боеприпасы и аптечки не безграничны, ими надо делиться. Кроме того, если не играть в тандеме и не смешивать навыки персонажей, то даже не смотря на мощное оружие и доминирование в атаке, можно получить сокрушительный удар в спину, особенно если не уделять внимание навыкам обороны.
После удачных сражений вы будете получать командные очки опыт, и игровую валюту, которую можно тратить на оружие, аптечки, боекомплект и улучшения. За дополнительную плату вы сможете полностью перекроить своего персонажа, правда один раз. За реальные деньги можно делать вообще все, что душе угодно. И делать это можно достаточно комфортно, игра хорошо оптимизирована и часто обновляется.
Хороший баланс, поножовщина и перестрелки, большое разнообразие классов, приятный визуальный стиль и интересный геймплей - игроки даже называют Dirty Bomb панацеей для уставших от Team Fortress 2.

This review comes from someone who has never really been that into FPS games in general, with the rare exception.
I did get really into the original planetside way back when (up until they put in giant mecha robots?), and I played PS2 when it was in open beta quite a bit, and loved it. Now I've rediscovered it for free on steam and am loving it just as much.
Planetside is not a shooter in the classical sense of the word. The maps are not little battle maps, they are continents broken up into grid with bases to capture. This is one massive war with hundreds of people involved. You will die. When you are new you will die a lot. This is not because of your equipment, but just getting used to how the environment works, how bases are set up, how steep of a slope you can climb, etc.
Your starting weapons are plenty to go face to face with vets. I've read negative reviews that say they aren't but to them I say "git gud". find the gun you can do it with, maybe you are more of a shotgun kind of guy, maybe you prefer to snipe like a little ♥♥♥♥♥ up in the mountains, or maybe you enjoy a nice medium range assault rifle. Get used to the fact that if populations are high there will always be someone up on that hill or up on that roof, or around the next bend. The scale of this war always amazes me. By the time you get good with a few of the starting weapons you will have plenty of points to unlock something else. What that is is entirely personal preference.
When you die, the game breaks down how good of a life you had. You are going to die. Die with glory, die with flair. Dont be afraid to run into that doorway that everyone is standing outside shooting in, shotgun blazing.
Most of the complaints about this game can be broken down into one category: want something? do it yourself. Not enough medics? so suit up, doc.  No leadership guiding the masses? take the reins. No air support? Learn to fly. Be as worthless or useful as you make yourself. Even if you suck at normal FPS you can contribute solidly as an engineer, a medic, or sneaking in and capturing bases when nobody is looking.

A pleasant surprise. After the RAGE incident, my faith in id Software wasn't the same as before. But this game, even though it's using the as beautiful as broken engine id Tech 5, which leads to tons of hardware incompatibilities, glitches and artifacts (like texture pop in), is a jewel. Easily beats the rest of the shooters released in the last few months, and maybe years.
The story is divided in two timelines based on a choice you make in the first episode. Each timeline features different routes to finish the game, different dialogs, cinematics, and character development.
The gameplay goes back to the roots of FPS games, it really feels like a 90s game. The difficulty is hard even in normal so it's a bit of a challenge. It has collectibles, secrets and everything an id Software game needs to triumph.
It mixes technology with myth and gives kind of a steampunk feeling to its atmosphere, and it suits it really nice. It's a very mature and adult story, definitely not PG-13, so for those who miss the feeling of playing an adult game here's your chance.
However, due to its engine, I need to say that you shouldn't buy this if you don't have one of the latest Nvidia cards, and an Intel processor. This engine is not compatible with most AMD rigs (I even had to change my vcard before being able to play it).
I hope this and DOOM 4 is the last we see of this broken engine. In the meantime, those who can, enjoy this piece of art.

Overall, the game doesn't really stand out when you're only playing single player.  It really shines when you get three of your friends to join you.
The four heroes finally reach the final battle.  A man standing three times your height is your opponent, along with half a dozen minions.  They are the only things standing between your team and the princess you must save.  The second you are let off of your leash, you attack.  Chaos ensues. You quickly lose track of your character, only to realize you were cornered and killed.  One of your friends stops what they're doing and begins reviving  you, while the others defend him.  You're then thrown right back into the chaos, pummeling enemies left and right.  One of your friends consumes a peanut butter and jelly sandwich that turns them into the hulk.  You perform CPR on someone as he kills enemies using the mighty power of his fists.  Finally, the battle is over.  Now all that's left is to claim the princess' heart.  But what's this?  Only one knight can have the princess?  Allies quickly turn on each other.  All friendships are forgotten as you murder the very people you fought alongside twenty seconds ago.  Finally, only two remain.  You are one of them.  The other has been your best friend since the second grade.  But that no longer matters.  You duel for two seconds.  Five seconds.  Ten seconds.  You are both covered in sweat by the time it's finally over.  You stand over the corpse that was once your friend.  Strangely, you do not feel guilty.  You feel prideful.  The princess is yours.  You walk over to her, preparing for the kiss that you have dreamt of for the past two minutes.  Unfortunately, you make the fatal mistake of taunting your friend.  He then stands up from his computer and punches you in the jaw.  You are taken to the hospital, and are released the next day.  Sadly, you learn that your friends continued without you.  They celebrate their victory of completing the game, while you celebrate the fact that you have a fractured jaw.
10/10 would murder my friends for a virtual princess again.

***LONG REVIEW WARNING***
I’m not sure how many times I actually asked myself “Why?” as I played Max Payne 3. “Why is he doing this?” “Why did they make this design decision?” “Why am I supposed to care?” It would go from the typical reflexive inquiries, to the borderline obsessive ones. I would continue after every stumble, extending a hand to the game, picking it up and giving it another chance to attempt walking. Eventually, I just decided to drag it until we reached the end of the road and left it there.
There is not much that makes Max Payne 3 a bad game, but rather, there is plenty that makes it a bad sequel. I’ve seen and participated in various discussions on the subject, seeing many dodgy arguments as to why people liked or hated the game. There’s a clear discontent among a certain number of people, as though something was missing in the title. Possibly the most common claim being “it’s not noir”.
And that is a claim that is as hard to support as it is to debunk. Men smarter and more qualified than either you or I have spent decades tackling this subject alone. Whether noir is an aesthetic or genre, or whether it even exists to begin with. Even among people who agree that noir exists, the criteria varies, and any “List of film noir titles” on Wikipedia or in any book wouldn’t be accurate. However, the golden age of noir died when the genre became self-aware, so now it would be more accurate to call anything written in a noir “style” neo-noir.
Claiming that either the setting or the daylight denies Max Payne 3’s right to carry the banner is dodgy at best. Many noteworthy noir titles, like White Heat, were set during the day without it being detrimental to the atmosphere. There are many other reasons to say the game lost its noir charm, but such a discussion would last for an eternity with no side being able to win. Something that can be agreed upon, though, is that if Max Payne 3 is indeed neo-noir, it is of a different ilk compared to the previous two games. Quite reasonable if you consider that movies like Sin City and American Beauty both count as neo-noir while being vastly different.
The first two games were a fusion of extreme noir melodrama and John Woo-style gunplay. It reached absurd levels story-wise, often mocking itself, but also placed a character who had rational reactions to the grimdark world around him. It’s why when you completely immerse yourself in the game, you never question Max’s actions. It never tears you away from the screen. But when you walk away and think about it, you realize just how unreasonable and silly the entire plot is.
The third game makes the mistake of toning down the setting into a more realistic one. Nothing is over the top, and there’s more emphasis on realism (as far as a third person shooter can allow). All of a sudden, we are asking questions we otherwise wouldn’t have. Our immersion breaks with every conflict between what the cutscenes imply and what the gameplay implies. Not only that, but all of a sudden, Max Payne stops being about Max and focuses on the events around him. This distinction is clear when you take into account that neither the first, nor the second game offers any sort of epilogue. It starts and ends with Max. On the other hand, Max Payne 3 offers a proper “this is what happened after Max put the gun down” scene.
This difference in atmosphere doesn’t stem only from the narrative, but also from the gameplay. Whether it was due to technical limitations, or just a savvy decision, Remedy used a minimal amount of in-game cutscenes. If Max sees an object he wants to comment on, the player needs to actually approach it by moving Max. Rockstar’s approach was to force the player’s movement, whether by cutscene or just slowing Max down due to injuries or the environment. The latter isn’t even much of an issue and is a better alternative to cutscenes, but coupled with them, it sets a much slower pace. Even trivial design decisions, like taking away the player’s control when watching TV, damages the experience.
The combat also follows this change of pace. Max Payne 3’s combat does revolve around cover, which is true to the predecessors save for the addition of a “stick to the wall” button. But it quickly becomes binary. You either have bullet-time, or you don’t. You are either at full health, or nearly dead. With infinite bullet-time jumps and only putting a cap on regular slow-mo movement, the pace changes drastically. Before, Max could jump into the action guns blazing. Now? Every single enemy is a threat, putting more emphasis on the previously mentioned increase in realism.
And then, of course, there is the actual character of Max Payne, probably the biggest problem with the latest game. Someone once told me that Max is very good at lying to himself. That’s quite an accurate statement. After all, at the end of the first game, he thought blood revenge would give him peace of mind, but as the second game showed us, it didn’t quite work out that way. However, at the end of Max Payne 2, regardless of which ending you got, Max was at peace with himself. It wasn’t something questionable like “this person is dead, everything is fine now”, but merely the culmination of all events just pushing him to a realization.
And obviously, he lied to himself again, according to Max Payne 3. This leaves a branching path, where one says that Rockstar wasn’t true to the character, while the other says they were. With the latter, one has to wonder why we should even care for the character now. There is a difference between falling on tough times and picking yourself up, and actually having two opportunities to take your life back and get at least a bittersweet ending. Payne stops being a powerful determinator and turns into this Guy With the Gun bum. A person one would find hard to care for. It would be easier for those who entered the series with this newest installment, as the predecessors become one big blur called “the dark past”, but as someone who played through both events, I find it quite difficult to ignore this kind of character development.
This is not the only issue when speaking of Max, though. His mannerisms are also drastically different. Despite the tone and rating of all games, Max rarely, if ever, swore in the first two games. I was halfway through the second game recently and I’m not quite sure if I even heard a “damn” from him. He had a sort of cold composure, dealing with his issues within himself, rather than swearing, raging and generally being openly upset about the situation. The trademark noir metaphors are also close to nonexistent now. Most of Max’s statements have become plain observations, rather than actually processing the information as he did before. No melodramatic thoughts on life beyond the occasional pearl in an ocean of dry writing.

As Payne himself says in the second game: “If you had done something differently, it wouldn’t be you, it would be someone else looking back, asking a different set of questions.” And that is what the core issue with Max Payne 3 is, in the end. It’s not about Max Payne. It’s about someone else with the same problems, dealing with them in their own way. There are many other issues we haven’t mentioned, like the highly out of place shock about the organ black market, or the redundant “Do you kill him or let him live?” prompt at the end of the game. Max Payne 3 suffers from Fallout 3 syndrome. Just how Fallout 3 was a good game, but awful Fallout, so is Max Payne 3 a good game on its own, but an abysmal addition to the series.
One only has to wonder where Remedy would have taken Max Payne 3 had they been the developers. “Max Payne’s journey through the night will continue,” say the credits of the second game. Sadly, most of the levels of Max Payne 3 were in broad daylight.

Damn fine AAA FPS shooter - that's the bottom line.
It's looks, sounds and plays great - great fps mechanics, nice story, cool characters, flawless voice acting, and a badass soundtrack. Not for the faint hearted though - some of those cutscenes were pretty darn cruel and vivid.
But when a game overall is so great, it's easier to spot the flaws, and here they are as I saw 'em:
- No SLI support - wtf? I had to put the game away until I upgraded my card, as it ran too poorly on my old dual gpu GTX 590. Make sure you have a fairly decent single gpu card.
- Stupidly small obstacles are often unclimbable.
- Enemies walking through walls
- Maybe I'm just thick, but it was unclear to me when my weapon was actually doing damage, or if I was wasting bullets on an inpenetrable armor.
- A few really low res textures despite highest setting
- Having to press a button to pick up ammo/armor is stupid
- Giving you the option to pick up a "special" weapon that has no ammo is stupid
- Quite heavy reuse of large geometry sections
- If you go to a recharge station and you're not being shot at - you should automatically recharge both battery powered weapons
- Sorta anti climatic end game boss fight

I'd like to be short but useful, with my personal review.
Max Payne 3 is a very good game, and i talk from an old episodes fan's point of view.
When i purchased it, i was a bit skeptical...all that brasil stuff...I thought i was going to have a terrible "MACHO" product in my hands.
Well, i was wrong.
Ok, i'm forced to admit that part of the old Max Payne games has been lost, and the story is nowhere close to the old "New York  Noir" goodness, but that doesn't mean it's dull.
If the old story was better, in this game we have a much deeper analysis of the character to balance the whole thing.
Max's personality is so well made and intruguing in this game, that, even in those sunny favelas, you can feel the emptiness and darkness inside his heart, with a nice touch of sarchasm.
We constantly listen to max's thoughts and during the game he reveals to us some intriguing metaphors (some are so good they deserve to be noted and used again while conversating :P).
Here comes the good part.
Nothing to say about the gameplay....SIMPLY FLAWLESS!
Max Payne 3 is insanely fun to play! Su much fun that i completed it 5 times and i'm still not bored.
The scripted events are great, enemy disposition brillant, level design SUPERLATIVE...nothing else to say...JUST BRILLIANT...much more fun to play than the old episodes (Gameplay wise).
I'll be very short with the tecnical part...THE GRAPHICS ARE GORGEOUS! Specially here, on the PC.
Simple as that....GORGEOUS (and i have to notice this is the first VERY WELL MADE Rockstar game PC port).
To conclude everything i have to say that Max Payne has only one problem...that is called MAX PAYNE.
The game is so different, in a matter of atmosphere and location, that will always be compared to the old epsiodes...no matter why...it's just like "Alien" and "Aliens", two very good movies, but the second one was, and will be, constantly compared to the first, because of its different direction.

I've enjoyed all three Max Payne games, all for different reasons. Max Payne 3 catches a lot of flack, mostly for switching out the comicbook style cutscenes for the more standard CGI cutscences, and for interrupting the action more than we've seen in the past. I've always been a big fan of the old style of Max Payne story telling but I didn't miss it here, I thought this had a lot to offer in it's own way. The whole thing felt very fresh and that's something I feel is important for a series I've spent a whole lot of time with. Even more importantly (to me) is the gameplay/combat which in my opinion has never stopped moving forward, the action is even more cinematic than ever before and in my opinion the cover system adds considerable depth to the combat. For a challenging and stylish third person shooter with a story worth paying attention to, look no further than Max Payne 3.

F2P isn't all bad and Dirty Bomb is a good example. Firstly, some reviewers have mentioned P2W elements. Compared to say  the late Ghost Recon Phantoms, this is a laughable statement. Everything is unlockable through the credits earned in game, and while the credits per match are pretty low (no matter how awesome you are), new 'missions' appear every two hours with a max payout of 1000credits and there are three of them, so on average you can get ~2000credits or more just by playing a session. With mercs being unlockable at a max price of 50k credits (less for other classes or when they are on sale) that isn't too bad. Cards for your loadouts are probably the biggest gripe, but personally I don't see them having too much of an impact. Random drops of cases mean you get random cards which can be used in the upgrade process.
Negatives? Well there are some. Mainly the slow introduction of new maps or content in general. There have been more hackers of late (edit: I personally haven't seen anyone obviously hacking in the last few months), but the reporting process is straightforward and there are always other games that you can join to avoid them.
Final verdict - it is free, why not give it a shot?

As a fan of the previous games, I have been very attached to the story of Max Payne and his downfall after losing his family, continuing with life and trying to find meaning to it all. In this game, there is little to nothing about it. The story instead focuses on the resurrection with Max Payne running away from his problems to San Paulo, where as always, trouble seems to find him at every corner. It's good that you do stop caring as slow-mo-ing your way around levels shooting people in the face is a significantly better reason to play the game and the story won't destract you from it.
I clocked in more than 30+ hours with no Multiplayer (which by the way is filled with disapointments for me, but I suppose it is playable in the same way the first three Star Wars episodes are watchable) going around each of the levels again and again, diving and creating hell for anyone who stands in my way. The game might seem arcaic by todays standards, but there is simply nothing quite like it. The mechanics and controls of the game are tight enough to allow you to do pretty much anything within reason. I'd recommend the game on those basis alone.

Time to add my two cents in this pot for this game.
Max Payne 3 is supposed to be based on the same premise from the last game. The game's plot is that Max is at an extremely low point in his life, where he is suffering still from the murder of his family, The Valkyr Case, and even the Cleaner case and Mona (play MP1 and 2 to find out) but also the other pains in his life that have not been resolved.
He is hired by a man by the name of Rodrigo Branco to protect him and his family, but of course, everything goes completely array and Max stumbles upon something darker than the previous games...
The story is very good. But not as good as compared to the other games. What makes this story good is the fact that Max is a more relateable character when it comes down to his emotional turmoil. His side kick (Raul Passos) I think I like a lot too. This game  is also a satire and very thematic with the talks of things like Good and Evil (Personal opinion: I believe it is a Fantasy/Illusion people hide behind to show they are morally better), The Past vs the Future, Acceptance, Modern Society etc.
I did have some gripes that some of the characters (The good ones like Rodrigo's Wife's Sister, Or one of the Antagonists) weren't expanded upon.
This game also has that level of nostalgia to Max Payne 1 and 2. If you played both, like myself, you will love the tiny references put in.
When it comes down to gameplay, this game still has the original Shootdodge and BulletTime but the game then has a cover system... This is where I personally do not like the game but I love it at the same time. The game is too cover based both online and Singleplayer.
Now as for the online... It's average, but my gripes is the usage of Explosive weaponry. Grenade launchers are okay as long as they are downgraded, but this game just makes it a stun gun. My real gripe as well is the realism factor. I will also mention that the dual wielding is also kinda frustrating. A lot of people do it.
The original Paynes weren't as realistic, and more Hyper Realistic, whihc I loved. The Realism puts me off at times. Especially Online, which makes me sometimes feel frustrated.
If you are an Original Max Payne 1/2 guy, don't buy this unless you are just wanting the single player. THe Realism factor also may put you off, and the over usage of the cover system as well. If you are new, I would recommend playing this and then playing the first and second to get the full angle on the story. Then you can make up your mind.

Max is back, with Maximum Payne.
I'm a little late to review this, but better late then never.
So, as many of you know, Max Payne 3 is a third person shooter. The main twist to the whole series is it's bullet time feature. Which is amazing. It feels fantastic to kill five+ guys in one bullet time, all head shots. You feel better about yourself. But, let's get down to the review.
STORY
Max Payne 3 takes place 9 years after the events of Max Payne 2. In the third game, Max is still heavily traumatized by his painful past. Currently, Max is heavily drinking and on excessive painkillers. He feels sorry for himself.
To get his mind off of all that, Max get's a job as a bodyguard for a rich family. However, gangs in Sao Paolo target this family, and Max must protect them. Two daughters of the father, Rodrigo Branco, is kidnapped and Max must find them and rescue them.
Now, we're done with the description. Let's get to the ratings. I'd say that the story is great and the writing is brilliant, however I PERSONALLY didn't feel the characters were fantastic. Even Max himself. I feel Max is the same character through out, drunk, depressed, and sometimes happy. I love seeing characters change through out a story, which I didn't see here.
I never really got too engaged with Passos. I just saw him as a guy who helps me with missions. Sad, I know... but that's how I felt.
GRAPHICS
This game looks beautiful. It's not the textures, shadow quality, or DX11 that impresses me. It's the greatly colored environments and facial animations that really grab me about the graphics.
So far, I have not noticed any pop-in textures at all. They all appear perfectly when you suddenly turn around. Basically, the opposite of RAGE... my lord.
GAMEPLAY
The gameplay in this game is perfect, seriously. As I said before, bullet time feels amazing. The guns feel great. The shotguns feel like shotguns, pistols feel like pistols, etc.
I'd say my only complaint about the gameplay is the bullet time "recovery time" as I call it. When you go into bullet time and, let's say, run into a wall, you fall over and it takes a few precious seconds to get back up. I have died COUNTLESS times from that. But it's seriously only a minor complaint.
I never got bored with the combat, and I feel like I won't for a while.
ARCADE
A new feature in Max Payne 3 that weren't in the other games is it's ARCADE mode. Basically, it takes snip-its from the story mode and the challenge is to complete these snip-its in either a required amount of time, or you need to gather as much score points as you can depending on what mode you choose.
One complaint about it, though. I feel like the Arcade levels are super unbalanced. I had super difficulty with the stadium level whatever it's called, but in the next one in the bar, I did it in one shot. So my only thing about that is it's unbalanced nature at times.
MULTIPLAYER
Yet again a new feature of Max Payne 3 that weren't in the other games, is multiplayer. No shock here, just about any game now-a-days has multiplayer. Even though I haven't been deeply affected by the multiplayer, I've had some good fun with it.
There are some very mundane modes. Deathmatch, Team deathmatch, those sorts of game types. But then there is a mode like Gang Wars, which is where you go through a "story" of sorts, going through 5 stages of a match. These 5 stages contain different objectives. Like planting/defusing a bomb, killing everyone, good stuff.
FINAL THOUGHTS
So my verdict is I'd say, a 9/10. I think this game is awesome despite some minor flaws, and it's well worth $60. I look forward to playing the single player of this game a few times over and over.
If you have not picked up Max Payne 3, I highly suggest you do.

PlanetSide 2 is a game that you can take a break from, come back, and still feel the initial excitement of your first three-platoon Galaxy drop, MAX crash on a heavily contested Tech Plant.
Squad or Platoon up and pick the role you are in the mood for that supports the tactical objectives: ground pounder, tanker, ESF jock. If you stay with the action, be prepared for intense combat where balanced team consistency, agile and tactical gameplay, augmented with solid strategic decisions significantly increase the level of success (and enjoyment) you and your team achieve. This is something that PlanetSide 2 does better than any other FPS where many games encourage (by virtue of the mechanics) lone wolf antics.
Since Daybreak purchased SOE, there have been a lot of enhancements suggested (some implemented already) and I look forward to what they can deliver to make this game even better.
PlanetSide 2 is the bar for MMOFPS. When walking away from a 2-hour gaming session, you feel not only the glow of a battle well-fought, but also mental fatigue of immersion in intense combat.
This will continue to be the staple game in my library that I know I can always come back to and enjoy a few hours of intense combined arms combat.

Hey there Steam community,
this is my first review... EVER... so please forgive me for any errors in reviewing. First of all I'd like to start by saying that well.... I ABSOLUTELY LOVED THE GAME! For me it was really amazing, this is the first game of the Wolfenstein series that I've tried and I love it love it love it (might try the old 2D one just for fun xD). Before I begin I'd like to apologise for its length, its kinda long but please bear with me.
What I loved the most about the game was its concept, set in World War 2 and well, the Nazi's won and now they rule the world. That itself made it interesting enough to try. I liked the ideas that the producers thought of (the enemies and their uniforms) because they brought a nice combination of the retro Nazi soldier uniform (probably from the helmet) with well.... the "modern" soldier, its interesting to see it (at least for me). Especially with all the crazy technological advancements the Nazi's made in the game and of course.... throw at you... and believe me they got all sorts of crazy sh.. stuff. The game lets players use well... enough weapons, though i would say that a little bit more weapon types would be nice, to make the game more enjoyable.
Mild spoiler... The producers present 2 different storylines that each present slight differences in gameplay and what you can earn, I won't elaborate too much on this as I don't wanna be stoned as a spoiler. The best part is that completing one of the storylines allows the player to try the second, while keeping ALL of the achievements that he earned from the last play through (so the second playthrough should be more kick♥♥♥♥♥, this also adds a little bit of value for your money spent on buying the game since honestly, it gets boring to complete a game over and over and over with only one storyline.
As for the gameplay, it follows the typical COD, or any action FPS genre (aim and shoot), though one thing that makes it stand out is that it gives players the options to Rambo their way through the level or to go Sam Fisher and sneak. But, the game adds these officers that will call for backup if alerted, the player's reaction would most likely be to target these officers, but they are usually in secure locations (and run away from the player if alerted) that are hard to reach if the tactic is a head on assault. Those who try to go Rambo run the risk of being overwhelmed (running out of ammo for me) should they forget/are unable to kill the officers as they can call in unlimited reinforcements (I haven't seen the officers run out of back-up before). Therefore the game promotes strategic thinking because players must learn to conserve ammo as the game is pretty cheap on ammo drops from dead enemies and take down officers quickly using tactics such as flanking, etc.
I must say that the sneaking option in Wolfenstein is generally limited, at least in my opinion, because the sneak paths are usually pre-determined (take left lane for assault and right lane for stealth) and well honestly pretty stagnant. Though I do appreciate the producer's attempt at presenting more options for players. One thing I did not like about sneaking was that enemies that saw dead bodies were not alerted, (I mean I'd be pretty worried if I found someone who was standing at that one place ALIVE a few seconds ago dead when I turn my head) but I guess if the AI was that intelligent, the game would be extremely harder to beat using stealth as you must take out all enemies before something wrong is noticed (maybe introduce it as a hardcore add-on or something). I would ask for a body dragging/moving feature to make up for that. My favorite part of sneaking was finding hidden weapons/add ons that could improve the players fighting abilities, its okay to not find them, the game is still do-able... but it makes life easier.
The game features collectibles and a perk system to add a little bit of that 'oomph'. Collectibles make the game more interesting as you need to keep your eyes open and explore a little bit while blasting Nazi's away and gives more purpose for those 'die-hard' must finish 100% game guys... Moving on to the perk system, I loved this feature because it boosted abilities based on the players play style, there are perks that help in sneaking and those that help war junkies achieve mass destruction... This way the game actively promotes all styles of play, not just one and once again this helps present more options and gives incentive to try alternate styles of play (true for me).

Overall, I really really do recommend this game cause it was just so much damned fun for me, I played all night cause I couldn't stop (don't follow in my footsteps as that is not healthy @__@). The only thing I didn't like about this game is its massive computer spec requirements, it was kinda laggy for me and of course that ruined my gaming experience, and its pretty damned big on your hard drive, 56 gigabytes for me (much larger than any game I ever had before).
So I guess this is it for now, so long, I hope this review helps those still wondering whether or not to buy the game, hopefully to buy it.
P.S do NOT buy this game before you are absolutely sure you can at least run it on minimal, buying a game you can not play is a waste of money and I hate for anyone to experience that
Cheers, HipsterKiller

Dirty Bomb is F2P game developed by Splash Damage, the studio behind Enemy Territory, and is published by Nexon America. The game itself is full of action and is set at an incredibly fast pace. It pits 2 teams of 6-8 players against one another, one attacking and the other defending and each player must use a Merc who has varying weapons, skills and augments.
Sounds like Team Fortress 2 almost doesn't it? Well it's not,because we don't have a million weapons and hats ruining our steam inventory and meta game balancing. As good as the F2P market is locked down by TF2 and DOTA, Dirty Bomb IMO is a good competitor as it has the action, the easy to grasp controls, its quick and easy to get into the game, easy to learn hard master, as is the motif with character skill based games. But i can also understand why it's not as popular as it could be, mostly with balancing issues, an illusion of P2W and sometimes really bad matchmaking.
Gameplay
Like I have said before, the gameplay is set at a very fast paced, but it's balanced in a way that can make it slow. It's normal to see people jumping off and over walls to get to better positions, or to increase their speed to get objectives faster. But as often you see that, you will see long corridors of death that defenders are trying to hold for the win, bringing the game down to a slow crawl until you overcome it. It all depends on one team's skill to quickly get into the perfect positions faster than the other team can take advantage of.
When it comes down to pure player skill, it's another thing. You can take things slow, but you will have to learn to pick up the pace, getting into ideal position is important, especially when it comes to setting positions to take on the other team's position. Gunfights at range are very fickle things because of this, grinding through a defenders well fortified position is tough unless the attacker are well skilled, prepared and fast. Fighting them at range is the most promising, but many of the weapons have little damage at range, especially with the damage fall off and aiming down sight doesn't help much against small targets because of the recoil. In fact most the time firing from the hip is your best option. Tracking player movement with your weapons learning their recoil and weapon spread can help, get those headshot right.
Mercenaries
there are close to 20 different mercenaries to choose from, who are split into different categories which are slayer, support, engineer and medic. Each type obviously has different roles to play, slayers only job is to be on the front lines killing everything in their path, engineers go in behind them and complete the game's objectives. Some characters can fill a second role quite easily, Fletcher is an engineer but with his weapons and skills, he quite a capable slayer character too. The characters themselves look incredibly well designed, heavy hitting mercs are usually large, carrying immense amount of armour and equipment on their backs or body's, smaller mercs are light carrying very little and will zip around the level.
I would be lying when they saying how good many of the mercs, obviously there will be the absolutely best top tier characters who shine anywhere, then there would be the ones who are good at times, then the very situational ones. A top tier example is Fragger, he is a combat power house, 150 health armed with two of the strongest assault rifles in the game and he chucks a very powerful grenade to kill multiple mercs instantly. He just shines no matter what player has him, or what situation, he will will get the job done.
You won't be able to change much about a merc, except maybe their loadout card. This card will have different weapons and augments which can slightly change the style of play the merc can do. There are 9 of them in total, none of them are really OP, there is one that obviously the perfect embodiment of their playstyle, where others tend to make the more aggressive and some just so situational and useless. Obviously the augments are the cause of the change of style, and they are regarded by the community as useless, what actually makes the character good is their skills and the weapons you are most proficient in.
Mercs however are locked, and you must have enough in game credits to unlock them. This is where people become idiots and fail to seek out information which they can get by playing. Credit generation most of the time is slow, I will admit that, you will get at most 150 to 200 per 15 min game, double that on stopwatch, and even more on ranked. Mercs however cost 30k-50k credits, so you can see why people get a bit mad. But Splash does do many things that help settle these woes. Every two weeks they offer 3 mercs on rotation to try for free, they added the ability to earn credits by accomplishing missions, which you get by normal play or by doing specific things, and these refill every few hours and can reward 500-1000 credits per mission. Finally once a day you can claim the first match of the day and first win of the for each of the games which give you 500 credits each.
Game modes
There are 3 Game Modes, objective, stopwatch and execution. There is also the ranked mode but that only has stopwatch games for the moment, and it is unclear if the other modes will be added for future seasons. Objective mode is simple, complete your objective first. Attackers have a multi stage set of objectives which they must complete under a time limit, these being destroy, escort and repair. On the other side, defenders have to stop the attackers accomplishing their objective until the timer runs out.
Stopwatch is the exact same as objective mode with one twist, the attacks have 15min to complete all of their objectives. After which the teams will swap and the once defender now have to beat the attacking team's time, or get further than them if they failed to complete all of the objectives, You can also draw if both teams fail at the same point progress. Execution is the search and destroy of Dirty Bomb, nothing new except for the games mechanics allowing people to be rived and use character and what not.
The maps that you play each have their own charm, as well as their own grind of death point. For some maps this can be the start like in bridge’s funneled corridors in order to get to the ev, or Dome’s pit of death delivery point. Other times it's halfway through the map like church's long street or even train’s blocker carriage. Regardless of attitude you will come across certain of objectives on each map that are just a pain to do. The EV escorts are most hated, largely because their ease of being destroyed by almost everyone with an explosives weapon, which is the vast amount of merc on the roster btw. Still I suppose it's a skill in itself to quickly repair it with an engineer, but it's annoying for the defenders to get a cheap win because they can stack explosive skilled characters.
Conclusion
So what do we have? A well made F2P game, that is still currently in its beta phase, so it's continually adding more mercs and maps, balancing and improving them. It has albeit small but a very dedicated community, its own competitive mode and ranks and the game is very easy to get into and enjoy. But yet we do have a potentially rage inducing game because it doesn't follow the current motif of many shooter games on the market, as well many of the issues i have already stated. In the end its a free game, you lose nothing but time and potentially happiness or boredom by playing, and you could always remove it if you really hate it.

There once was a time when this game was simple, had a simple matchmaking system, and a simple ship building concept. It was a game where you battled to get more stuff for your ship, used the stuff to battle and get more stuff, and eventually unlock cool items to put on your ship. Players were sorted into "tiers", which were general leagues of power for a ship. You simply could not place powerful items on your ship and expect to keep facing noob players. The tier concept allowed good players to maximize ships for specific laugues of players, and for less skilled players to know that, once they place enough items on their ship to go into a new tier, they will be at a slight dissadvantage unless they prepare right.
It made the concept of unbalanced gameplay less unbalanced. Now, unfortunately, you know absolutely nothing about your opponents, or whether specific items will be overspending for your level and land you in a new group of opponents, or if your weapons aren't quite powerful enough to face off with the people at your level. You go in blind, and can't even leave the damn match with any means other than the task manager when you screw up your build. This could mean a solid ten minutes of gameplay in which you are simply wasting your time.
If it's really a concern about unbalanced teams after someone leaves, then just throw in one of those pre-made ships piloted by an AI or something. Or better yet, don't make it a damn trial and error session just to make a ship for a specific group. I couldn't even make a ship with nothing but cubes and a few smg's without getting blasted apart by people outside my preparation.
Seriously, I don't know what to use and what not to use. Do I grab some shielding, or does it raise my ranking a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton so I don't know? What guns are people using at my level? Are cubes good armor, or do they even HAVE armor in this game?
This game was once simple, and it was good. Maybe people like what they have now, but I wouldn't know since I have no F-ing clue what they'd be talking about.

Forget this game. I'm done. Rockstar ruined Max Payne.

All and all I give this game a 4/10

I was anticipating this game for a few years, and have loved all of the previous games (even though the sequels were generally panned by most people). I expected a lot from this game, and did a lot of reading up on it to see what sort of things that MachineGames wanted to implement. It all sounded great, but sadly there has been a lot of hype surrounding pre-releases with very little in the way of substance upon release.
So when this game was released, and I got to try out the first mission (after hours of downloading, keep the size of the game in mind), I was happy with what I saw, but not ecstatic.
I soon found that the game continues to get better and better throughout the length of the game, building up to something huge, largely in line with the story.
The story is extremely well written, and while it is not particuarly extravagent, it tells the story perfectly. The characters and voice acting are among the best I've ever seen, you really get attached to them. BJ (the protagonist) comes across much better that n in previous titles, where MachineGames explores a deeper side to him without making him seem too... Emo I guess is the best word for it. He feels no remorse in killing the Nazis, but they clearly get across that he does not enjoy what he does, and he does it so that the world is a better place.
The combat is great, nothing too new, but at the same time it does what it does perfectly. There are numerous options to take when going into a fight without really forcing you to play a particular way. There is cover for instance, in fact two different mechanisms for using it, but at no point are you required to use it. The perks add subtle increases to the effectiveness of BJ as you progress, and rather nicely, these upgrades apply even when going to do previous missions.
The weapons all feel good, though I do feel that a little more in terms of futuristic weaponary could have been provided. I really miss the Tesla Coil...
The alternate story line is a great idea and provides minor differences in the length of the game, however I feel that a lot more could ahve been done with it.
Overall this is a brilliant game, well worth a look from Old school shooters and new comers alike, with mechanics that cater nicely to all generations. There is plenty more that could be said about this game, but it is best to find out further for yourself.
(I did not experience technical difficulties myself upon release, but I ahve heard plenty of issues that seem to have been resolved)

This is an FPS shooter worth every cent. Striking graphics, smooth gameplay, intense storyline and well tuned gunplay. From start to finish Wolfenstein: The New Order will keep you immersed into the life of William B.J. Blaskowitz and his fight against the Nazi empire in this timeline branch like story where the Nazi war-machine continued a successful domination of the world, during which, Blaskowitz is in a vegatative state over a fourteen year period. The world has changed and the war is now over, only relics of the world he once knew have been crushed beneath the heel of the Nazi Empire which now rules the world.
A well balanced array of enemies are encountered throughout the game, giving challenges to gunplay and keeping you, the player, on your toes during tough firefights. Through much of the game however, you're given the option to stealthly advance through many levels and avoid major complications. Through these missions you will have to find bits of armor and health pickups with only minor intervals of health regeneration; another more rewarding gimmick though, being able to find secret or alternate paths to find in-game extras or earning perks effecting gunplay.
On a more personal note, I felt reminiscent of the Half-Life series. Good well placed maps and enemies with modest AI, rewarding secrets such as health, armor and ammo and the flow of events. All good things which help make up a fantastic FPS worthy of many playthroughs.
Despite the sometimes sluggish AI, the occasional stupid AI are made up for in a good balance between when the AI knows it needs to duck for cover, not hide in the open or shoot at regular intervals. Though there are times when sneaking, the AI doesn't seem to recognize you or even see your there, despite being right in front of them on.
Did I forget to mention that you're an unstoppable Nazi killing machine?

A genre-defining must-play classic of RTS remastered in HD. The original based-on-a-true story epic. This game has a ridiculous amount of content. TWENTY fully scripted and voice-acted campaigns (and still counting) @5+ hours each. Worth its price several times over, especially on sale.
Then theres multiplayer! 29 semi-unique civilizations with historically accurate, albeit imbalanced, strengths and weaknesses. Graphics and AI are hugely improved over the original game. Great mods. Didn't honestly think I'd come back to this game again given what else is on the market (unplayed in my library), yet here we are. 11/10 currently playing again.

Age of Empires II, known in the professional world as Human Resource Management Simulator 99’, is the premier HR Management Simulator. After 16 years, it still stands in a league of its own. Simple to use, this software is utilized by the likes of Fortune 500 companies and top tier business schools for training and retaining skills. Furthermore, it doubles as an entertaining and interactive platform for learning about the Middle Ages.
HRM Simulator 99’ takes place in a historical period running from the fall of the Western Roman Empire to the dawn of the Colonial Age. You will be placed in the role of a medieval leader seeking to build your kingdom and defeat your opponents. In order to win, however, you will need to micromanage your human resources with the utmost efficiency and effectiveness.
Central to your efforts is the villager. Villagers are the ideal worker. They can work for indefinite periods of time while earning nothing and aptly work several different jobs throughout your kingdom. They can handle everything from construction to fishing to sapping enemy buildings. Your villagers are also loyal to you beyond question; they will even gather berries while wolves are mauling them to death.
Once you have established a perfectly efficient economy using the principles of operations management, you will have to shift your attention to raising an army and defeating your enemies. As a human resources manager at Proctor & Gamble put it, “HRM Simulator 99’s army management is good preparation for some of the most daunting tasks that a new manager may face in the real world”. While managing your army in battle, you will also still need to pay attention to your economy, keeping your villagers on task and away from becoming useless, idle drones.
If you successfully complete these campaigns with flying colors and prevail over your colleagues in online skirmishes, you will be ripe to become the CEO of one of the largest corporations in the world!
Preferred by all large-cap corporations listed on the S&P 500. In other words, buy this game if you want to invest in the American economy!

First things first, This is what i would call a niche game. At first it may just seem like another FPS but oooh no... it's an actuall MMOFPS. So i need to explain why this game is not for everyone. This game is so massive you could be in battles of litterally hundrends of players all at the same time. And that is on a contenant with potentally thousands of people fighting all over the map. What that means is... YOU WILL DIE... A LOT. Doesn't matter how good you are at COD or Battlefield, so if you can't stand dieing over and over, then this game isn't for you.
That said, let's take a look at some of the pros and cons of this game:
PROs:
x. Multipule classes to fit yer playstyle and battle situation
x. Absolutely massive battles
x. Vehicle warfare (Land and Air)
x. Inspires Teamwork (playing a support class you still feel like you are helping, even if yer not on the front lines)
x. Totally not pay to win (All weapons are side grades, there is no "win all" weapons. you pick weapons according to yer playstyle)
x. In game voice comms for squads and platoons
Cons:
x. Overwhelming at first (since there is no other game on this scale)
x. Pretty demanding on yer PC
x. Gameplay can sometimes feel repetitive due to capture mechanics being the same
x. Sometimes glitchy
Overall i'd give it a 9/10. Granted that's because i love teamwork games and the massive scale of this game. If you are not into those kinds of mechanics this game may cause too much fustration for you and feel more like a 6/10. You have been warned.

EDIT: Construction update is out now, if you've ever wanted to try this game out for the first time, or ever thought about trying it out again after burning out, NOW IS THE TIME TO PICK IT UP. Granted, It's a brand new system so it's a bit janky, but there's already been a huge influx of people so the fights have been amazing. I would put more into this review here, but
. TL:DR is this: If you've ever wanted to try out the game, now is the time.
Recently got back into playing this game, and have been having a blast. Here's some things I've noticed:
* The new tutorial continent is exactly what they needed for the game, it's a small scale version of the actual continents that mostly keeps the newer players "safe" from veterans, excluding Smurfs, since you must be under BR15 to be able to spawn there. It's still not a full tutorial, but at least it's a controlled environment to learn the ropes.
* The cert grind is also much easier than before, with ribbon bonuses (first 5 of which are doubled), weapon medals, directives etc.
* Alerts are no longer the deciding factor for locking a continent with the new Victory Point system. Never did like basically getting the boot every time an alert ended, whether you won or not.
When it comes to FPS, nothing comes even close to what this game comes to offer when it comes to the sheer scale of battles, and the only other thing that I can think of that comes close to the sense of scale that Planetside 2 offers would be Guild Wars 2's World V World. It's free to try out, so the only thing you lose is time.
Some tips for new players:
* Stick to the beginner continent until you hit BR15. You can always leave and come back before then if you want to test the deeper waters, but once you're past that you cannot go back. Take advantage of the smaller scale zones to familiarize yourself with the mechanics before diving headfirst into the zergs.
* Try out *everything* before you buy it. There are two ways of doing this, VR training and Trials. VR training lets you use any combination of gear and attachments for no cost, but only in VR training (unless you unlock the stuff with certs/DBC while in there) They have target ranges for vehicles, infantry, air, complete with range markings for infantry. Take advantage of this. See how each gun works, how it kicks from recoil, cone of fire, and try out how each attachment effects how it fires. Only problem with VR training is that none of the targets move, they're just static and don't truly show how they work in a real fight. That's why Trials exist, so you can use a weapon, albiet just base without attachments, in a real fight for a few hours before spending those hard earned certs on them.
* Lastly, Planetside 2 is a game about numbers more than it is a shooter, so go in with friends and find a good outfit. Best way to find an outfit is to join an alert platoon, usually run by an outfit, and essentially trial running them. Most outfits recruit this way, so don't be afraid to ask about them while running with them. You'll find the game much more enjoyable while in an outfit, if only to have people to talk to while running with randoms or while participating in organized operations.
Hope this helps at least some people with starting out.

To those looking to get this game, you are going to get a lot of time out of it with a roughly 20 hour campaign and then potentialy another 20 if you do a second playthrough to get a slightly different storyline (or to get any collectables you missed out on or what not). I highly recomend this game, even I (the uncontested cheapest person I know when it comes to video games) thought it was easily worth the $30 price tag (I bought it on sale) so to a normal persons standards, it's totally worth the price. Age of Empires II, known in the professional world as Human Resource Management Simulator 99’, is the premier HR Management Simulator. After 16 years, it still stands in a league of its own. Simple to use, this software is utilized by the likes of Fortune 500 companies and top tier business schools for training and retaining skills. Furthermore, it doubles as an entertaining and interactive platform for learning about the Middle Ages.
HRM Simulator 99’ takes place in a historical period running from the fall of the Western Roman Empire to the dawn of the Colonial Age. You will be placed in the role of a medieval leader seeking to build your kingdom and defeat your opponents. In order to win, however, you will need to micromanage your human resources with the utmost efficiency and effectiveness.
Central to your efforts is the villager. Villagers are the ideal worker. They can work for indefinite periods of time while earning nothing and aptly work several different jobs throughout your kingdom. They can handle everything from construction to fishing to sapping enemy buildings. Your villagers are also loyal to you beyond question; they will even gather berries while wolves are mauling them to death.
Once you have established a perfectly efficient economy using the principles of operations management, you will have to shift your attention to raising an army and defeating your enemies. As a human resources manager at Proctor & Gamble put it, “HRM Simulator 99’s army management is good preparation for some of the most daunting tasks that a new manager may face in the real world”. While managing your army in battle, you will also still need to pay attention to your economy, keeping your villagers on task and away from becoming useless, idle drones.
If you successfully complete these campaigns with flying colors and prevail over your colleagues in online skirmishes, you will be ripe to become the CEO of one of the largest corporations in the world!
Preferred by all large-cap corporations listed on the S&P 500. In other words, buy this game if you want to invest in the American economy!

This game is one of many reasons why piracy should be legalized.
I actually don't think it's a game, but merely a technological demonstration.
It sucks in many ways. First and the most important of them all is gameplay. I understand video games have to follow these weird trends nowadays that are dictated out of someone's♥♥♥♥♥(or perhaps that's the sad necessity that reduces the likeliness of bug occurence - too lazy to fix the bugs nowadays?), or speaking more literaly, nowhere. I understand every shooter has to have checkpoints instead of the capability of saving the game (seriously, that's one of the dumbest inventions I've ever seen, it literally kills the joy from playing a game, because you can't go back before the checkpoint and make the other "checkpoint" [being more specific, a save game] different than the previous same spot you made, so you can take a different approach in which you can actually win the game or have some fun with varying situations at the same spot).
Either you successfully comply, or die and start over again.
If you die, you are forced to start over from the same scripted situation. No variability, no different outcomes. Same formation of enemies, a little bit more ammo (since R* wanted to dumb this game down for some reason), a pack or two of painkillers that Max probably took out from his♥♥♥♥♥(I think I didn't have them the last time I was alive), trial and error (meaning there's no fun, you are literally forcing yourself to play this game, and you're getting♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off), NO VARIABILITY. And VARIABILITY of situations made previous installements of Max Payne so fun to play. Every time I played, I would actually reload the save, even after I successfully killed all the enemies to see if I can finish them off in different, perhaps more fun, perhaps more efficient ways. Now there's no point of doing that in MP3, since everything starts at fixed parameters and you also get some extra ammo and painkillers out of nowhere. MP3 isn't the only game to follow that nonsense trend that kills fun. Most modern shooters do that. But is that an excuse?
The general feel of the game is also different from the previous ones. Is it worse? IMO it is, but that's obviously arguable. While Max is still cynical, dark, unstoppable and badass (arguable as well), he is no longer poetic. The game's feel isn't dark and gloomy anymore. It is moldy and sultry instead. The first half of the game seemed like following yet another trend, which is being critical about consumptive lifestyle, disgustingly greedy people and nowadays trends (oh the irony) just for the sake of it, without giving it some constructive insight (for a moment I felt like I was playing GTA IV instead of MP3). Seriously Rockstar, Max is deeper than that. He has better things to speak about. At least he's still a vigilante, doing things his own way. For that I am grateful to you guys.
----------
[some spoilers might appear here]
I also lost track of what the hell was actually happening in the game's plot at about the beginning of the third chapter. Seriously, I had no bloody idea why Max was still fighting these guys, why was he chasing the guy who betrayed his employer (don't want to spoil too much, but if you know the plot, then do know that simply "because he betrayed my employer' doesn't sound very convincing to me) and why couldn't he simply leave before he became a fugitive.
[spoilers end here]
----------
The game was fun to play, or being more accurate, watch. Once. I'm not sure if I'll play it through the second time. The whole checkpoint system is just annoying, it forces the player to repeat the same scripted moment several times and memorize it before, through trial and error, they get it right. That just is not right. If the game allowed the player to save its' progress at any time, it would have been much more fun. I also hate the "cutscenes". Cutscenes, like the name suggests, are supposed to be short, to cut the gameplay to some smaller parts. But this game is so unique and non-conforming! Edgy! Hipster-y! Cutscene-to-gameplay ratio is 1:1! They wouldn't even be half as bad if they actually contained some sort of plot or even a decent choreography (spectacular stunts like in previous games). But no, there has to be a cutscene from 16 different angles and 24 slowed down repeats of Max going through the door. Just casually walking through the doorframe! Even the omnipotent, omniscient God couldn't predict such thing would happen and he just can't believe what the hell is going on here.
As for multiplayer - I'm still working on it. Perhaps it will be much more fun than single player. It seems like it, but I haven't tested it yet, so I'm not reviewing it yet.
All in all - MP3 is a decent game (interactive movie?) that measures up to other third person shooters that are being made these days and it sure is fun to play once, but being an old fan of Max Payne, I am very disappointed in this game. "Disappointed" is actually mild - I am heartbroken. I thought it'd be better than it was. Well, shame on me for expecting so much, I guess.

This iteration of Wolfenstein also added some interesting new mechanics and approaches the perk system many games incorporate in a more personal way.  Instead of leveling up and spending points on skill unlocks, Wolfenstein let's you play it your way, and specific benefits unlock as you perform certain challenges.  This way you're never pigeonholed into singular play style.  There are four style trees to shape the play that suits you best:  Stealth, Tactical, Assault, and Explosive.   You'll be doing a little of each style so it's recommended to complete as many challenges as possible to get the benefits.
The one thing that took me by surprise the most was the story.  There was actually a well written, and voice acted story behind this shooter.  It was effective in boiling my hatred for the cruel and merciless enemies, that I felt sweet revenge when piling up the Nazi body count.
This was pure old school shooter fun with modern improvements, and I'm going on record to predict a FPS Game of the Year award.
