First the good: The character animations and voicing are outstanding and the map designers and texture artists are very good. I’ve never seen a game’s cut-scenes (rendered in-game) look so good and feel so realistic. But unfortunately these high-points don’t make Wolfenstein worth playing.
The actual game-play is completely lacklustre: The gun-play is weak and unfulfilling, the story is pretty stupid and unbelievable and there are no memorable moments. The whole game is run-of-the-mill, nothing special, been there, done that, got the T-shirt boring.
For whatever reason, this game lacks the magic X factor that makes a game greater than the sum of its parts. Boss battles are tiresome (and I kept having to look up what I needed to do to progress), there were no hooks to make me want to keep playing to see what would happen next, picking up ammo is a key-mashing experience to ensure you pick everything up and guns are rubbish (even if they do have two different firing modes, oh wow amazing).
The only unique thing in this game that made me smile was the laser cutter. It was pretty nice to be able to cut through some sheet metal to get to some place, but when that’s the only new experience a game has to offer, you have to ask yourself if it’s worth playing.
My answer is no. This game is a solid 7/10 – it does nothing wrong but it’s nothing special and in a year’s time you won’t remember any of it. And you won’t care that you don’t remember.

If you're buying this for the multiplayer then you might as well buy the console version. On PC the multiplayer is riddled with cheaters. There is apparently no anti-cheat software in place on this game, looking up rockstar support as to what to do with such things is basically "Drop an e-mail at this address with this info and hard evidence." which somehow just won't cut it. There is NO server browser. Meaning you're getting connected to whoever is hosting a game on whichever corner of the world meaning you'll need some luck to get connected to someome close enough for you to have a low ping, which you can't check. Unlocking guns as you level up is nothing strange to most players, but you have to buy them with in game currency, mostly that you earn by looting corpses OR if you're lucky to survive long enough, getting kill streaks. And even then the amount of money you get is very little.
The singleplayer experience, while differing from the previous titles is actually pretty good, however. Other than the title screen when you start the game, you'll get no loading screens. They've actually been replaced by cutscenes to give a more dramatic feel to the plot. However, there is no way to skip those cutscenes. The story is interesting, it explains how things went from bad to worse, also explaining how Max ended up in Brazil. After playing for a while you might be able to actually figure out what is happening before getting to the end of the game, minus some rather interesting details that contribute to plot, but just sort of don't tie in with the main storyline.
If you DO manage to actually install this game, the DRM is a VERY big letdown and a big obstacle to playing the game. Not only you'll need to be signed on rockstar's social club, but rockstar's social club seems to be there to prevent you from playing the game. Issues with not being able to connect with to the service, not being able to activate the game and so forth. You may need to look for workarounds for some of the issues, such as the "Failed to contact key server" issue.
Overall, the game delivers a good singleplayer experience if you're into an action filled game, altough it is rather difficult at some points. The multiplayer experience is quite frustrating due to the issues with it (no server browser, lots of cheaters, no anti-cheat). I'd say this game can rate a 7 out of 10, maybe 8 if you can get it to work withouth needing to use workarounds for all its bugs, crashes and DRM related issues.

First and foremost, I have to confess that, sadly, I'm really useless when it comes to play these kind of games; I'm awful. However, Age of Empires II has become a chapter in my life, and it's really worth the money.
I've had long and endless hours of joy and laughters thanks to the mythic "wololo" and to the hordes of elephants that made great effort to catch that sneaky villager that was hiding behind the trees. Moreover, it has significantly improved my knowledge and my interest into Europe's medieval history (no joking).
Despite being a stone in the way for my allies, and despite knowing nothing about war games, I've had really good moments with my friends playing this. I totally recommend it.
Besides, the most important thing is that, with this version, you can play now through Steam, which really helps with online issues and make playing with friends much easier. The "HD" they announce is quite disappointing, but that isn't important at all since it doesn't really change the price. It does not change my opinion on this PC legend.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Antes de empezar, he de confesar muy a mi pesar que soy un pedazo de inútil y un completo estorbo en este tipo de juegos. Ahora bien, Age of Empires II es un capítulo en mi vida y una compra que verdaderamente ha merecido la pena. No solo me he reído incontables horas con el clásico "wololo" y las armadas de elefantes y catapultas que se cebaban con mi pobre aldeano escondido tras el bosque; también me he sumergido más en la historia de Europa (lo digo totalmente en serio) y me he divertido muchísimo con mis amigos a pesar de ser un aliado totalmente inerte.
Además, crear casitas y hacer mi ciudad bonita es algo muy atractivo. Lo recomiendo muchísimo. Su antigüedad no es para nada un inconveniente.
Por otro lado, la versión "HD" no es nada del otro mundo. El hecho de que esté en Steam facilita muchísimo el juego online, eso sí; y es un dinero que merece la pena pagar. Pero vamos, la "alta calidad gráfica" es un engañabobos.
Pero nada de esto es algo que afecte a mi opinión de este clásico de los juegos de PC.

First Person Shooters has been around since decades, it is one of oldest gaming genres that hasn't much evolved since it first came out.  The foundation of it was so solid that despite with relatively minor tweaks here and there, the genre still sells millions and millions of copies annually with likes of Call of Duty and it provided one of the key platforms for competitive gaming through the likes of Counter Strike for example.
Leading up to the release, I thought it was going to be just another shooter trying to market itself using the franchise's legacy. For the case of Wolfenstein, the legacy of being the first one there - thats right, the original Wolfenstein from id software is pretty much the first game that let you see through the eyes of the protagonist as you go from room to room, clearing enemies while wielding a gun on the bottom of the screen. Yep, it was the very 1st FPS in history.
The story takes place during the high point of World War 2 in Europe, you crash land into a Nazi occupied castle, accompanied by a small group of soldiers scattered from various regiments, you have a clear task of cutting the head of the snake and end this war. The game captures the agony of defeat at your most vulnerable time -  just when you thought you had it won. It carries a very powerful and emotional punch to the gut itself, but what transpires during those darkest hours will haunt you throughout the rest of the game. It further connects you to the game on a very personal level. The characters that you meet to help you fight against the Nazis aren't just there to move the story forward, they aren't your typical forgettable characters you find in most shooters, oh no, they feel like real people going through real hell thanks to the New World Order of the Nazis. Everyone here lost something dear and precious in the 'Old World' to the Nazis and hence have very personal vendetta against them. While on the other side of the fence the cruel and horror nature of the Nazi is brought to life through very well written, well designed and I can confidently say, well hated antagonists in the game. You just don't want to save the people around you, but you also really want to hurt the Nazis and give them no mercy of a quick death.
First impressions are always going to be the visuals, and this game looks good, very good. Not just id tech 5 looks amazing here, from ultra crisp textures, great attention to detail in every corner to bring the world to life. What really caught my attention was the cinematography and the art style of the game: The game uses colors and their contrast to great effect, combined with the sheer attention to detail I mentioned before, it creates a visually ♥♥♥♥♥♥ic experience! The environments are very distinct and crafted with a lot of care and thought just like the rest of the game, no two places ever feels the same. Another thing to note, not only the game takes you to a wide variety of places across the world, but across the time as well. The art style, the condition of the world and it's inhabitants reflect this brilliantly.
The level design also gives the player a lot of options in dealing with situations and change tactics on the fly, which the game actually forces you to do so when playing in harder difficulty modes, which I suggest. The weapons are mostly standard you would expect from a sci-fi shooter with some cooling alternate firing modes and there is something incredibly satisfying when you can dual wield weapons like assault rifles, shotgun and even...rocket launchers..thats right..dual wield rocket launchers.
What really stood out for me is also the main reason I will continue to come back to this game long after I finished it is how precise and satisfying the shooting mechanics felt. It is just pure joy to point your gun and just shoot. Further, the weapons feel solid, distinct and carry satisfying feedback all of which combine to make one of the best shooting experience possible . It is the most basic mechanic for a shooter, but you would be surprised that most fail to deliver here. Modern shooters have made great strides in graphics and other enhancements through this medium, but it also came at a price of deteriorating the key functionalities which made this genre timeless. A lot of the essence of the genre is getting lost with modern 'refinements' being made into the genre. It is very pleasant to discover that Wolfenstein have gone back to basics with their approach to shooting. I found the firefights challenging without being frustrating most the time on the 2nd highest difficulty mode I played. The AI was definitely smart to box me in, flank and even find higher ground to get a upper hand during combat situations.Oh yeah one more thing, the game doesn't even have regenerating health, Win!
There really isn't much negative I can think off to be honest, I guess I have to really nitpick and can I fine just one - some of the textures are oddly of low resolution which really catches the eye because they are at times placed right next to the usual high resolution textures of the game, making it a bit distracting. Also I am not sure why, but the game doesn't have proper anti-aliasing support on the PC, kinda shocking really as it is a standard feature of PC Gaming. Not that the aliasing is too distracting or anything, but it is always nice to clean those jaggies when you have the power at your disposal.
Wolfenstein is very likely not just my game of the year, but it is one of the most important games to come around in my opinion with a clear message: sometimes you have to embrace the past to guide you a better future.
Editor's note: Since Bethesda also acquired the rights to another legendary shooter, DOOM. If they give that game the same level of treatment they gave to Wolfenstein, we can safely anticipate for another solid good comeback!

One of the best games this year, and one of the best AAA titles in a long time.
Gory as hell, with a story you can follow and characters that, shockingly, you can invest in, The New Order plays well and looks great. The gunplay mechanics are tight and very fun, with great diversity in the play styles and a skill-tree system that is as flexible as you are, and one that really compliments your preferred play style (if you don't just choose them all). Machine Games have really pushed idTech 5 far beyond the capabilities shown in RAGE, making this game a sight to behold. The textures and models are highly detailed without dragging down your framerate - I can play it on nearly full specs with a 4 year old Nvidia card, and the atmosphere of the game is thick and immersive as they have used that capabilities of the engine to compliment the game in all the right ways.
The game does toe the line of modern shooters in some ways that border on negative - specifically, the opening scene is great to play the first time, and then a drag upon replay as you go through the motions, but this is the only criticism that I really hold, and it's a minor one at that.
Highly recommended to any FPS fan.

First and foremost, I have to confess that, sadly, I'm really useless when it comes to play these kind of games; I'm awful. However, Age of Empires II has become a chapter in my life, and it's really worth the money.
I've had long and endless hours of joy and laughters thanks to the mythic "wololo" and to the hordes of elephants that made great effort to catch that sneaky villager that was hiding behind the trees. Moreover, it has significantly improved my knowledge and my interest into Europe's medieval history (no joking).
Despite being a stone in the way for my allies, and despite knowing nothing about war games, I've had really good moments with my friends playing this. I totally recommend it.
Besides, the most important thing is that, with this version, you can play now through Steam, which really helps with online issues and make playing with friends much easier. The "HD" they announce is quite disappointing, but that isn't important at all since it doesn't really change the price. It does not change my opinion on this PC legend.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Antes de empezar, he de confesar muy a mi pesar que soy un pedazo de inútil y un completo estorbo en este tipo de juegos. Ahora bien, Age of Empires II es un capítulo en mi vida y una compra que verdaderamente ha merecido la pena. No solo me he reído incontables horas con el clásico "wololo" y las armadas de elefantes y catapultas que se cebaban con mi pobre aldeano escondido tras el bosque; también me he sumergido más en la historia de Europa (lo digo totalmente en serio) y me he divertido muchísimo con mis amigos a pesar de ser un aliado totalmente inerte.
Además, crear casitas y hacer mi ciudad bonita es algo muy atractivo. Lo recomiendo muchísimo. Su antigüedad no es para nada un inconveniente.
Por otro lado, la versión "HD" no es nada del otro mundo. El hecho de que esté en Steam facilita muchísimo el juego online, eso sí; y es un dinero que merece la pena pagar. Pero vamos, la "alta calidad gráfica" es un engañabobos.
Pero nada de esto es algo que afecte a mi opinión de este clásico de los juegos de PC.

So this is a game that I used to playbefore they added in aerofoils, and it was great back then. When BA first came out it was still great. However the recent additions and revisions have completely destroyed it's gameplay value. They started adding in massivly over-powered weapons and modules (can anyone say Shredder/Blink Module?) They did away with the Teired armour and much of the old Teired system. But then we come to the issues they have constantly ignored. Want a high-speed car? Good luck with that, as every time you try to turn eve at half speed, you spin out and have to spend a good 15 seconds re-alining yourself only to spin out into a wall again. And probably one of the worst parts about this game is how if you find yourself constantly spawn =-killed in BA with the only deterent to save your life is an invinciblity sheild that lasts for a measly 3 seconds before that before-mentioned Shredder tears you a new one. Oh and let's not forget that they completely removed the old currency system where for each match you played, depending on how well you played, you were rewarded with RP, which you could use to buy new parts for your robot. They replaced it with a new RNG system in which you have to be excedingly lucky in order to get ANYTHING you may have wanted to get. Want that shiny new Ion Distorter/Disruptor? Good luck getting the 15k to 150k to buy it or even getting it in a Protonium Crate (the hiest tier of crate you can get.) I will however say that it is still a good game early on, just don't expect to progress fast in late game. I will also say that you should look on the Robocraft forums and at the other reveiws for this gameas the shortcomings that I have listed here are most certanly not the only ones. They are just some that I belive to be the most impacting on the game. I may change my reveiw in the future as features are added and removed (hopefully for the better) but until that time comes it will remain this way.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a follow up to the mediocre Wolfenstein game from 2009, which didn't really stand out against other WWII games and just generally failed to innovate. Coming from the team responsible for games like The Darkness and The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay, I had very high hopes for a polished shooter with a riveting story. I can happily say I was not disappointed; from start to finish, Wolfenstein: The New Order is expertly crafted and memorable in every way.
You are BJ Blaskowics, US soldier and steadfast killing machine, tasked with the elimination of General Deathshead. Standing out from previous game, BJ's character is extremely well characterised and likeable, supported by strong voice work and character movement/modelling. All of the characters in this game have excellent voice acting, and this really supports the role of the villains in the game; characters such as Frau Engel and Deathshead were memorable because of the terrifying non-combat encounters reminiscent of scenes from Inglourious Basterds.
Gameplay generally borrows from thw work of Quentin Tarantino, with plenty of gory explosions and dismemberment. The shooting mechanics are tight and refined, including a wide range of weapons which can all be dual wielded for maximum carnage. This works fairly well and allows the player to mix up the gameplay whenever it is desired. You can also take cover and peer over obstacles. You also have a mostly non-regenerating health bar, and there is more empasis on old school mechanics like health-kits and armour pickups. The refinement of somewhat simple mechanics means that this game is a successful blend of old and new age shooters, meaning the game never grows boring and even breathes fresh life into the genre. The levels are less restricted than other games of the genre, and you are actively encouraged to explore in order to find new weapons and unlocks. New features of the game such as perks (new upgrades unlocked by performing specific tasks) are not necessary to the game, but provide an interesting addition for completionists.
The visuals are also quite polished, and the game is often stunning to observe. However, there are occassionally texture pop-ins and slow loading textures, which can get distracting over the course of the game. Despite this, most of the game retains decent visual quality.
Overall, Wolfenstein: The New Order is an entertaining, over-the-top shooter that surprises you with a quality story and characters you'll really invest in. The high quality of the game ensures a definite return for the series, and has given me high hopes for both this franchise as well as DOOM; Machine Games has lived up to their reputation and delivered a fantastic game not unlike The Darkness and Riddick. Excellent and surprising. 10 / 10.

Game i was really looking forward to. Unfortunately this was not what i expected it to be.
Wolfenstein The New Order is all about story and moving forward in a totally linear fashioned enviroment. It does let you branch out from the mainpath and explore some corners every now and then, but that is not much to offer really. I thought that this game was going back more towards to that non-linear leveldesign of older shooters, but how wrong was i.. Don't get me wrong though, there is freedom in that regard, that you are not being killed if you try to explore. This game does not have that idiotic "Return To Combatzone" from Call of Duty. No, there is none of that crap, thank gosh.. But these levels are still very much like in Call of Duty. You move forward and never have to visit a area where you have been to already.
It's unfortunate that you always have to move in some scripted direction. Forexample, there are some places which have only one way out, a vent or you have to pull a switch or something (aka do what the game tells you to do or you're not moving forward). Another thing is that you are actually not being allowed to figure out anything on your own. You may play the game on Über difficulty and disable hints and tutorials and you will still always have this objectmarker on your screen (blue/yellow). So if there is a "puzzle", you know it's not hard because the objectmarker clearly shows you where the switch is. Same with being in a location and there is a clear objectmarker everytime on where that vent or hatch is. You are not allowed to figure anything on your own. All must be handheld. Another thing which don't disappear regardless of what setting you play on, are the blinking objects..
Gunplay is the most strongest part of this game. I really like how the guns feel very awesome for mostly. When you fire even that single Assualt Rifle, it feels very good. Not even mentioning dual weilded Shotguns.. :D There is neither any weaponlimit that Modern fps is used to have. So you may actually carry all the guns you see in the game, there is no swapping inorder to have that specific gun. Although.. regardless that the game has many guns, they all seem to be somewhat similar. There is no huge differences. And what i dislike about, is that the Railgun is actually significantly different and it's not really allowed to surface too much, since it goes on this "rechargeable ammunition". You cannot find ammo for the Railgun in this game because you can only recharge your Railgun from these electro stations. That is kinda a bad choice imo, because you cannot just manually manage the Railgun ammo by either finding secrets or just by exploring the enviroment, because you have to return to these electro stations if you want to have your Railgun at max ammo capacity.
This game neither has the typical modern full health regeneration. This game uses a hybrid of healthpacks and health regeneration. If you are at 5hp, you will regenerate all the way to 20hp but to further heal, you must find a healthpack. It's nice that a triple A title has taken the non-autoheal approach. I personally find health regeneration appropriate only in very few games. This game also has a modern sprint mechanic so if you want to run at max speed and do kills, it's not gonna happen. This game holsters your weapon when you sprint so it doesn't work like older fps such as DOOM. Jumping is also pratically useless in this game since kneehigh jumping will get you nowhere. There are some smaller boxes to which you can jump onto, but that is it.
This game also has another different feature to typical modern fps. Regardless of Wolfenstein The New Order having aimdownsights/ironsights, the good thing about it is that you are not being forced to use aimdownsights. Bethesda clearly demonstrated how you can very much pull a headshots by hipfiring from even a great distance. This feature i really like that i don't have to ever touch ADS in this game if i don't want to. I personally don't find ADS appropriate in an Arcade fps (aka run&gun game) because ADS is about being cautiuos and precise with your shots. Wolfenstein isn't exactly the kinda franchise where you want to stop and aimdownsights, because if you do that, you get shot to death. This is why MachineGames made ADS in this game totally optional. You hit 100% accurately from hip also, so ADS is totally up to the player if he wants to use it or not. More modern games need to take this approach. Give player the option to either look down the sights or not use them at all, because i know that there are many players like me who grew up with older fps and don't want to stop and aimdownsights inroder to be accurate with their shots.
New Order is plagued with this "cinematic" thing. New Order does very much shove cutscenes straight in your face. This a very bad thing. We bought a FirstPersonShooter (and especially a WOLFENSTEIN game), so we expect to be shooting stuff and not listening to some cutscene. Cutscenes are totally fine if used appropriately, but unfortunately in this game cutscenes go way overboard. There is pretty much all the time some sort of cutscene or a scripted event where you just watch stuff happen instead of YOU THE PLAYER doing the stuff.
This game does switch the pace somewhat though. Occasionally you get to swim and dive around and it's a nice little change for more diversified gameplay experience. Then there are also moments where you just run around without any gun. I find these non-shooting moments to be very out of place. Wolfenstein is a franchise about shooting, because if you don't know what Wolfesntein 3D is, then i very highly suggest you do some research about it. Wolfenstein 3D in 1992 created the whole fps genre and already back then, was all  about killing the nazis. In New Order there is way too much of "not shooting". In Wolf 3D you never had to wait for anything, you just explored and tried to survive.
There is one major design flaw with this game. You encounter nazis with totally black suits in a dark enviroment so you cannot see where you are being shot at. There are also nazis with white suits and usually you encounter them in a totally bright place. So i'm not sure if this is just an intentional troll by MachinGames? But be it troll or not, it's a very bad choice to make the enemy completey blend in to the background in an Run&Gun game. Due to this flaw, this game pretty much has to be played as an covershooter. Since if you go run out there, you are being shot by what looks like to be an wall eventhough it's actually a small nazi that completely just blends in the background.
PC-side of things.. It's a consolegame through thoroughly because the game enviroment is totally static outside of few walls that break. Forexample there was a PC showing Wolf 3D in a space level, and i just wanted to destroy the thing just for the fun of it and the game said no. Even 1997 released Shadow Warrior allowed me to break statues, plants and pretty much anything i wanted to. In this this consolegame that PC was invincible (probably because of console limitations).
Graphical options are ridiciolously small, so there isn't much stuff to tweak to get some good performance while maintaining nice visual effects. Nope, forget about that. This game is no Serious Sam 3 where you can finetune all the settings to get the desired perfomance. Oh and before we wrap this up.. Game has a 60 framespersecond framerate cap.
Pros
+ You don't have to use aimdownsights
+ No weaponlimit+dual weilding is awesome
+ Healthpack-based gameplay
+ Gore of the game (you can blow up enemies to a pile of blood)
+ Nazis outfits look cool
+ Guns feel good
+ Gibraltar bridge level
Cons
- Cutscenes/scripted events being overused
- Nazis blending in to the background
- Modern gameplay mechanics getting in the way
- Linear levels with diminished exploring
- Bulletspongy enemies with no effects
- Consolegame

Possibly the best F2P FPS out there right now.
+ Objective based team shooter: Much deeper, tactical and competitive than the average CoD-style run-and-gun shooter.
+ Skill based: The best loadout in the game won't help much if you can't aim.
+ Freedom of movement: Fast paced movement, master difficult wall jumps to get to strategic places, evade enemy fire.
+ Nice loadout system: Acquire entire sets of mixed equipment and perks instead of individual items. Can't build the "best loadout ever" and run with it every match.
+ Fair business model: Mostly pay-to-skip, can't buy advantages that non-paying players can't get for free (gotta farm them quests though).
+ Solid AAA shooter gameplay.
- Not many maps. You'll get used to the ones in place very quickly.
- Characters can take a while to unlock, even if you're focusing on quests and getting the daily wins/plays.
- Really slow development: One of those games that's been in Beta since ever.
- The occasional cheater (at the time of review, possibly fixed later)
In conclusion, Dirty Bomb is a very good skill-based, team-focused, objective-centric shooter that beats most of the F2P games on Steam. AAA gameplay, not pay-to-win, very original ideas, rewards practice and strategy...What else could you want from a shooter?

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a follow up to the mediocre Wolfenstein game from 2009, which didn't really stand out against other WWII games and just generally failed to innovate. Coming from the team responsible for games like The Darkness and The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay, I had very high hopes for a polished shooter with a riveting story. I can happily say I was not disappointed; from start to finish, Wolfenstein: The New Order is expertly crafted and memorable in every way.
You are BJ Blaskowics, US soldier and steadfast killing machine, tasked with the elimination of General Deathshead. Standing out from previous game, BJ's character is extremely well characterised and likeable, supported by strong voice work and character movement/modelling. All of the characters in this game have excellent voice acting, and this really supports the role of the villains in the game; characters such as Frau Engel and Deathshead were memorable because of the terrifying non-combat encounters reminiscent of scenes from Inglourious Basterds.
Gameplay generally borrows from thw work of Quentin Tarantino, with plenty of gory explosions and dismemberment. The shooting mechanics are tight and refined, including a wide range of weapons which can all be dual wielded for maximum carnage. This works fairly well and allows the player to mix up the gameplay whenever it is desired. You can also take cover and peer over obstacles. You also have a mostly non-regenerating health bar, and there is more empasis on old school mechanics like health-kits and armour pickups. The refinement of somewhat simple mechanics means that this game is a successful blend of old and new age shooters, meaning the game never grows boring and even breathes fresh life into the genre. The levels are less restricted than other games of the genre, and you are actively encouraged to explore in order to find new weapons and unlocks. New features of the game such as perks (new upgrades unlocked by performing specific tasks) are not necessary to the game, but provide an interesting addition for completionists.
The visuals are also quite polished, and the game is often stunning to observe. However, there are occassionally texture pop-ins and slow loading textures, which can get distracting over the course of the game. Despite this, most of the game retains decent visual quality.
Overall, Wolfenstein: The New Order is an entertaining, over-the-top shooter that surprises you with a quality story and characters you'll really invest in. The high quality of the game ensures a definite return for the series, and has given me high hopes for both this franchise as well as DOOM; Machine Games has lived up to their reputation and delivered a fantastic game not unlike The Darkness and Riddick. Excellent and surprising. 10 / 10.

Game i was really looking forward to. Unfortunately this was not what i expected it to be.
Wolfenstein The New Order is all about story and moving forward in a totally linear fashioned enviroment. It does let you branch out from the mainpath and explore some corners every now and then, but that is not much to offer really. I thought that this game was going back more towards to that non-linear leveldesign of older shooters, but how wrong was i.. Don't get me wrong though, there is freedom in that regard, that you are not being killed if you try to explore. This game does not have that idiotic "Return To Combatzone" from Call of Duty. No, there is none of that crap, thank gosh.. But these levels are still very much like in Call of Duty. You move forward and never have to visit a area where you have been to already.
It's unfortunate that you always have to move in some scripted direction. Forexample, there are some places which have only one way out, a vent or you have to pull a switch or something (aka do what the game tells you to do or you're not moving forward). Another thing is that you are actually not being allowed to figure out anything on your own. You may play the game on Über difficulty and disable hints and tutorials and you will still always have this objectmarker on your screen (blue/yellow). So if there is a "puzzle", you know it's not hard because the objectmarker clearly shows you where the switch is. Same with being in a location and there is a clear objectmarker everytime on where that vent or hatch is. You are not allowed to figure anything on your own. All must be handheld. Another thing which don't disappear regardless of what setting you play on, are the blinking objects..
Gunplay is the most strongest part of this game. I really like how the guns feel very awesome for mostly. When you fire even that single Assualt Rifle, it feels very good. Not even mentioning dual weilded Shotguns.. :D There is neither any weaponlimit that Modern fps is used to have. So you may actually carry all the guns you see in the game, there is no swapping inorder to have that specific gun. Although.. regardless that the game has many guns, they all seem to be somewhat similar. There is no huge differences. And what i dislike about, is that the Railgun is actually significantly different and it's not really allowed to surface too much, since it goes on this "rechargeable ammunition". You cannot find ammo for the Railgun in this game because you can only recharge your Railgun from these electro stations. That is kinda a bad choice imo, because you cannot just manually manage the Railgun ammo by either finding secrets or just by exploring the enviroment, because you have to return to these electro stations if you want to have your Railgun at max ammo capacity.
This game neither has the typical modern full health regeneration. This game uses a hybrid of healthpacks and health regeneration. If you are at 5hp, you will regenerate all the way to 20hp but to further heal, you must find a healthpack. It's nice that a triple A title has taken the non-autoheal approach. I personally find health regeneration appropriate only in very few games. This game also has a modern sprint mechanic so if you want to run at max speed and do kills, it's not gonna happen. This game holsters your weapon when you sprint so it doesn't work like older fps such as DOOM. Jumping is also pratically useless in this game since kneehigh jumping will get you nowhere. There are some smaller boxes to which you can jump onto, but that is it.
This game also has another different feature to typical modern fps. Regardless of Wolfenstein The New Order having aimdownsights/ironsights, the good thing about it is that you are not being forced to use aimdownsights. Bethesda clearly demonstrated how you can very much pull a headshots by hipfiring from even a great distance. This feature i really like that i don't have to ever touch ADS in this game if i don't want to. I personally don't find ADS appropriate in an Arcade fps (aka run&gun game) because ADS is about being cautiuos and precise with your shots. Wolfenstein isn't exactly the kinda franchise where you want to stop and aimdownsights, because if you do that, you get shot to death. This is why MachineGames made ADS in this game totally optional. You hit 100% accurately from hip also, so ADS is totally up to the player if he wants to use it or not. More modern games need to take this approach. Give player the option to either look down the sights or not use them at all, because i know that there are many players like me who grew up with older fps and don't want to stop and aimdownsights inroder to be accurate with their shots.
New Order is plagued with this "cinematic" thing. New Order does very much shove cutscenes straight in your face. This a very bad thing. We bought a FirstPersonShooter (and especially a WOLFENSTEIN game), so we expect to be shooting stuff and not listening to some cutscene. Cutscenes are totally fine if used appropriately, but unfortunately in this game cutscenes go way overboard. There is pretty much all the time some sort of cutscene or a scripted event where you just watch stuff happen instead of YOU THE PLAYER doing the stuff.
This game does switch the pace somewhat though. Occasionally you get to swim and dive around and it's a nice little change for more diversified gameplay experience. Then there are also moments where you just run around without any gun. I find these non-shooting moments to be very out of place. Wolfenstein is a franchise about shooting, because if you don't know what Wolfesntein 3D is, then i very highly suggest you do some research about it. Wolfenstein 3D in 1992 created the whole fps genre and already back then, was all  about killing the nazis. In New Order there is way too much of "not shooting". In Wolf 3D you never had to wait for anything, you just explored and tried to survive.
There is one major design flaw with this game. You encounter nazis with totally black suits in a dark enviroment so you cannot see where you are being shot at. There are also nazis with white suits and usually you encounter them in a totally bright place. So i'm not sure if this is just an intentional troll by MachinGames? But be it troll or not, it's a very bad choice to make the enemy completey blend in to the background in an Run&Gun game. Due to this flaw, this game pretty much has to be played as an covershooter. Since if you go run out there, you are being shot by what looks like to be an wall eventhough it's actually a small nazi that completely just blends in the background.
PC-side of things.. It's a consolegame through thoroughly because the game enviroment is totally static outside of few walls that break. Forexample there was a PC showing Wolf 3D in a space level, and i just wanted to destroy the thing just for the fun of it and the game said no. Even 1997 released Shadow Warrior allowed me to break statues, plants and pretty much anything i wanted to. In this this consolegame that PC was invincible (probably because of console limitations).
Graphical options are ridiciolously small, so there isn't much stuff to tweak to get some good performance while maintaining nice visual effects. Nope, forget about that. This game is no Serious Sam 3 where you can finetune all the settings to get the desired perfomance. Oh and before we wrap this up.. Game has a 60 framespersecond framerate cap.
Pros
+ You don't have to use aimdownsights
+ No weaponlimit+dual weilding is awesome
+ Healthpack-based gameplay
+ Gore of the game (you can blow up enemies to a pile of blood)
+ Nazis outfits look cool
+ Guns feel good
+ Gibraltar bridge level
Cons
- Cutscenes/scripted events being overused
- Nazis blending in to the background
- Modern gameplay mechanics getting in the way
- Linear levels with diminished exploring
- Bulletspongy enemies with no effects
- Consolegame

In my opinion, PlanetSide 2 has been a major success with all aspects that they were going for. The MMOFPS has definitley lived up to its name in my eyes given its massive servers (Both in land size and how many players can fit into one server).
Now, I could ramble on and on about how this game provides a stunning new look to the concept of MMO games, but at the same time the cons must also be examined.
The biggest con is sensitivity that must be tuned precisely by the player. For example, an infiltrator with too high of a mouse sensitivity would have difficulty aiming at a target. At the same time, too low of a sensitivity would inhibit the infiltrator from pulling off his shots on moving targets. Now, the reason it is a biggest con is that the sensitivity must be finely tuned. If off by even a small margin, your entire gameplay could be affected and could mean the difference between getting a kill or being killed.
Larger battles are also something to be reckoned with. This is both a pro and con for the game. No other game I have seen can create a fight such as those with more than 180 people fighting it out for a peice of territory. However, you must watch yourself. Enemies will pop out of anywhere and everywhere, and friendly fire can be rampant when in a fight since everyone is concentrated in such a small area.
Tactics can also mean the difference between victory and defeat. Again, another pro and con at the same time. A battle cannot always be won by sheer brute force, which is where a good tactic can some in. There are numerous ways for squad, platoon, and outfit leaders to formulate and enact strategies with those who have joined.  But, some people are independent. You should not think that because you lead a squad that they will follow you. Not to mention that some of the larger battles seem to be nothing more than a battle of brute strength, with those who have the highest numbers to be the victor and no tactics whatsoever incorporated.
Still. It is an overall enjoyable experience. The large size of the maps allow you to play the game however you wish. Even when there is a large fight going on, there are still locations for which a player to travel to for a smaller form of combat. There is plenty of opportunity for all six classes to run into combat and use each of their individual skills to the fullest. Squads, platoons, and outfits are also a major opporunity for players to communicate, strategize, and gain more XP. PlanetSide 2 really shows what it means to be an MMO game.

When you think about it.  The series is really depressing but also heartwarming.  GLaDOS was Caroline.  Cave Johnson and the lab boys forced her to become GLaDOS.  To take away her freedom and move her into a computer.  No one would ever know it was her.  She flooded the Enrichment Center with neurotoxin to kill the people who did it to her out of rage.  Later, she felt bad about it but what was done was done.  So she developed a mindset that, like the people who basically killed Caroline.  Everyone was horrible.  She eventually distanced herself from the nice, cheerful woman who Caroline was because she wasn't Caroline.  She was a murderer.  She awoke Chell, and very quickly begins to show distaste for humans.  Throughout Portal 2, she insults you on weight, lack of parents, and personality.  Just because she doesn't have that.  And she killed hundreds of people, and took it out on you.  At the end when she says "You were my best friend."  She means that as in, you're her only friend.  You're the only person who ever 1, wasn't using her for some higher goal or 2, forced around like some maid.  Although you killed her, disobeyed her, and tried to leave her.  In reality, you're one of the nicest people GLaDOS ever met.  But she wasn't programed for socializing.  She was programed for testing.  She can't keep you around.  You are a distraction to her.  And she gave you the best thing she could before she sent you off.  A memento.  Like when a best friend moves away in school, they give you a card, a bracelet, a gift, she gave you that too.  GLaDOS is one of the loneliest creatures on Earth but she found it in her heart to give you a gift, her one, true friend.﻿

I wrote a review for this some time ago but after a while I decided to redo the whole thing.
Be warned: This review is long and in depth!
Positive:
- 4 huge continent's to play on.
- Apparently up to 2000 players per continent (so says Wiki)
- Over 100 people can be fighting in one battle (I've been in a battle with over 150 people before).
- 3 Factions to choose from.
- Large assortment of weapons.
- 6 Playable classes.
- Many vehicles included.
Negative.
- The 3 factions are severely unbalanced (more on that below).
- The weapons are locked and you need to buy them or trade in game points for them which will be a very long time.
- The faction specific vehicles are severely unbalanced (again more on that below).
- Players... rude, moronic, can not play so love team killing instead and also cheaters.
- Lot's of cheating.
Each faction moans how over powered the other faction is, I've played all 3 so know what I'm talking about.
Ok for the factions you have:
Terran Republic (TR) - (Red) - (Normal Mode) - This team is more like the imperial army from Star Wars, they are a large government that has military might and forces law and order on anyone.
New Conglomerate (NC) - (Blue) - (Hard Mode) - This team is more like the rebels from Star Wars, they are a band of freedom fighters who oppose the stranglehold of the TR.
Vanu Sovereignty (VS) - (Purple) - (Easy Mode) - Umm... they wear purple spandex! :/ They basically believe that using alien technology is the only way humanity can evolve.
Why are the VS Easy Mode? Well they have energy based weapons so they have no bullet drop, their faction specific aircraft is very agile and accurate. Also their faction specific Tank hovers so can move very easily and is also accurate.
Why are the TR Normal Mode? Well their weapons are very accurate but do suffer bullet drop. They are also extremely rapid with little recoil. Their faction specific tank has 2 turrets which can be fired single barrel or both together, it's also very tough. The latest release of the vehicle mounted weapon - The Gatekeeper - can fire with high accuracy, fast firing, no bullet drop, high ammo count... not nice for anyone on the receiving end of this.
Why are the NC Hard Mode? Their weapons are slow firing, lack of range or accuracy. Their faction specific tank is slow moving, single shot... in fact nothing special about it at all. The NC are apparently the "Shotgun" group operating better with close range weapons but even their close range weapons are absolutely useless compared to the TR or even the VS! Because there is nothing good about the NC I feel that the developers hate them and just can't be bothered with them.
Now the players... what lovely people they are. If you kill someone then you get a message from them saying how crap you are, how you are a cheat or how good your sister was last night! If someone on your team is s**t and constantly getting killed, they'll kill you just to feel better even though they get no points or bonuses. Some are just pathetic f**k heads and have no I have no idea why they go around killing all their team mates.
Other players can not play at all so they do the next best thing... cheat! Yes they cheat a lot in this game, from aimbots, shooting through walls to warping about all over the place. Thing is if more than 3 (I think) people report the same person then they will get banned.
Now there are a lot of negatives here but I continue to play (at least until I reach level 100) and have given this game a Thumbs Up. The reason is is that I've never played a game of this scale before. Over 100 people in one battle! Intense!

Wolfenstein is a good, solid, shooter that was fun and enjoyable to play. It is set mainly in the 1960s where WWII was won by Nazi Germany. You play as a soldier who was badly injured during an assault and has spent the past few years in a vegetable state in a hospital. The game seems to borrow from other games as at times it will feel very familar. In ways it is similar to the early Medal of Honor or the first Call of Duty games where you encounter enemies at a middle distance and they dive and shoot from behind cover. Other times it seems to have been influenced by Dishonored with the stealth sections and animated backstabs. It doesn't quite match those games in terms of execution of the mechanics but they are decent.
Wolfenstein's employs a standard mission and base system where you complete a few missions and head back to your base for a breather. It uses the base as a way of expanding on some of the characters and fill in the back story. There are some interesting, memorable characters in Wolfenstein but unfortunately that makes some of the others seem one dimensional. I feel that maybe with a bit more time, focus and care this game could have been truly great. The story is at times over the top which lends well to the gameplay, however around the midway point there is one to two chapters which are just plain dumb. It stupidly tosses in a "secret Jewish organisation" into the mix which, gladly, is only touched on for one chapter. Aside from that there are nice touches which help shape the story; such as the main character muttering about distant memories throughout the game.
The level design is very good generally with expansive indoor maps that allow you to do a bit of exploring. As a homge to the early Wolfenstein games there are gold objects and other hidden goodies littered throughout the game. Letters and newspapers are hidden to provide background and as in early 90s shooters enemies drop armour and ammo. The game strangely gets you to press E to collect these pickups which seems a bit odd. Simply running over them would have been a better choose. I actually liked the perk systems in this game as it is not intrusive. You gain perks by just repeating actions such as killing enemies with throwing knives or headshotting guards. There are four bands of perks which cover stealth play, assault play, tactical and demolition. You can purposely pursue them but I found they populated as I played.
It was nice for me to play a game where the movement is fairly quick, guns are snappy, and pack a punch. Dual-weilding chunky shotguns was a good throw back. There is a peek-from-cover move which I rarely used as you can just blast away. Wolf contains a laser cutting weapon which was versitile and upgradable. Again, if more time had been spend on it I feel it could have been as good as the Gravity Gun in HL2. There just aren't too many levels that explore its features fully. It also highlights a few inconsistences with the levels and "world". An example would be how certain metal sheets and surfaces are destructable yet some wooden panels or metal boxes aren't. I think it is more a restriction employed for consoles that hindered the game a bit. Its the same with the textures which can be low-res in some places. The game does run very smooth and I experienced no slow down.
The AI of the enemies is a lot better when they are fighting as it quickly becomes apparant that their stealth AI is sloppy. I've had guards look straight at me or see their colleague get shot just to turn and walk away. The first stealthy mission is the best as it has multiple routes the others are very hit and miss. Firefights however are very satisfying and can be challenging when you encounter the different types of soldiers. The game has a decent difficulty level which can cause you to die a few times when you get overwhelmed. Overall Wolfenstein is worth it as it is a fun experience. The majority of the levels are diverse in theme and design. It is not run and gun shooter of old but more of a blend of modern and old. There is no magic directional arrow showing you the way so sometimes you can get lost. I will be replaying this game again to see what I missed. It just misses out on being an 8 out of 10 game.

So initially, my rating was negative because the most important part of an FPS - the guns - feel like crap in this game. The gunplay is below average in my opinion, and it's not my cup of tea. BUT, I change my rating now to a recommend, because while the gunplay is a bit meh, the teamplay and the team dynamic of the game is very well done. The game rewards players quite a bit for playing their class effectively, and often times I find myself enjoying the game quite a bit because of the well-done class dynamic. It also helps that the game is incredibly rewarding for good teamwork, and when every class is doing their role in sync with one another it's very satisfying.
Pros:
- Great team-oriented objective gameplay
- Good class dynamic
- Unique classes, each merc feels different and feels like they have a legitimate role on the team
- Games are really satisfying when the classes are played to their strengths. A good medic can carry by healing/rezzing, a good demolitionist can make objective escort absolute hell for the enemy team, a good engineer can secure objectives quickly, etc. it's really nice to see a class dynamic done so well.
Cons:
- Gunplay is meh (in my opinion) the guns sound like plastic, and there isn't much visual response to give the gunplay the good kick that other games do
- Loadout cards are terrible RNG. That being said, the loadouts don't matter that much and performance-wise a good player can overcome any disadvantages that come with a weaker loadout. Plus it's mostly skins-related for the higher tiers.
- Mercs take quite a bit to unlock
- Match balancing is iffy

Max Payne 3, a game that even as I understand it, was some time in the making. As a newcomer to the series, I mostly bought it as a, Hey, I may as well give it a shot. And I don't regret this at all. Max Payne 3 has distinctly proven to me, how much fun a cover based shooter can be.
Gunfights are fluid, and fast paced. And there are few difficulty settings where you can viably tank bullets. The violence itself is pulled off well, the shooting controls are standard, though there is a definite lack of weight to the guns. At the same time, oddly, it's not because they lack impact. They certainly have impact in abundance. You'll typically get a close up slow motion kill on the last enemy in the area, which will tend to be rather bloody. While I wouldn't call it excessively bloody, it's certainly not toned down either.
My main gripe with the game, has to do with the protagonist. While I do understand the tortured ex-cop archetype, Max himself takes this to such an extreme, he comes off as supremely unlikeable. While most action heroes in games and film have a snappy one liner, Max himself replaces these with his depressed musings. And while I wouldn't of wanted to see him cracking jokes, his emotional state would've been more relatable if it ever showed him having a moment where he wasn't convinced he'd be better off shooting himself, than going through the story.
The story itself is relatively standard, though I can't think of many games to use it. It makes use of cutscenes, however, the cutscenes can be of such length that they become obscenely irritating. While at first I thought it was to conceal loading, I later managed to jump right into a level through the mission select, without an absurd load time. While you'll certainly come to hear the story, in later playthroughs, you may just want to sit back and put more focus on the amazing shooting mechanics, in which case, the cutscenes will break your pace.
To sum it up, this is still a fantastic game. It's incredibly well optimised for the PC, and doesn't feel like a port at all. The optimisation surprised me, after Rockstar's release of the PC GTA IV, and the general lack of other Rockstar games that are put on PC. I'm looking at you, Red Dead Redemption.
This game has it's flaws, but none of them are gamebreaking. It's definitely a must own, unless you dislike killing. In which case, I think you may have chosen the wrong hobby.

If you are a fan of Max Payne and Max Payne 2 by Remedy Entertainment, then I would suggest you replay one or both of those games instead of venturing into Max Payne 3 with its sloppy Rockstar Games version of the character and world. (This has nothing to do with the new setting or the presence of daylight in the game. It has more to do with a completely different approach to the character as well as storytelling in general. Think about getting a Twin Peaks movie written and directed by Michael Mann... it won't be the worst movie in the world, but it will inspire plenty of headaches.)
Even the mechanics of Max Payne 2 are superior to what you'll get in Max Payne 3. You will be relying on hiding behind cover and exploiting sloppy shooting mechanics throughout Max Payne 3. In a third person shooter, the player can put the crosshair on an enemy while the player's model is still behind a corner, resulting in bullets hitting a wall instead of the enemy in the crosshairs... or at least that's what happens in Max Payne 2. In Max Payne 3, if your crosshair is on an enemy and turns red, then the bullet will land... Max's actual position in 3D-space be damned...
That being said, it's not a terrible game. On its own, under a different/new IP, this would have been a good, maybe great, game. But they called it Max Payne 3, and as such it fails to hit the mark on many levels.

One of the best shooters I've played in a long, long time.  They could have gone the typical FPS route and created a game with little to no story, but they've managed to create a compelling story (while still fun and campy) that actually makes you care about the characters and what happens to them.  To add to the fantastic story, they've also created a game that is a hell of a lot of fun to play.  The game mechanics work well, the guns are fun to shoot and have a weight to them, and there's a satisfaction in seeing a Nazi get his head or other body parts blown off with a shotgun.  I've already played it to completion twice and am on my third playthrough and can see myself playing through it a couple more times.  When's the last time an FPS made you want to do that?
One of the best parts of the game (besides the story and combat) is the ability to play it stealthy or loud.  You won't be able to stealth the entire game like you would a Splinter Cell game, but for a good amount of most levels, you can go stealthy, or go flat out loud if you so desire.  One of the fun parts of going loud is that you can dual-wield almost every weapon you get.  Want to dual wield pistols? Think bigger! Dual wield shotguns, submachine guns, assault rifles and have fun blowing your enemies away!
I only played a brief amount of Return to Castle Wolfenstein before playing this, and that was my only previous knowledge of the series, and I loved this game, so don't feel that you need to play the previous entries in the series before playing this game.  Just play it!  You won't regret it!

Over and done in 14 hours. But I did run in super-easy mode because I really just wanted the movie. Movie's pretty damn good. Had I done a harder level no doubt I would have needed to plot and skulk much more and that would have added time. On the other hand, I could have played it faster but I was admiring the stunning work done by the art crews. The lighting, the detail. Really worth getting a walkthrough at one level just to see that work. Nice one.
I did have a lot of trouble with the core sensibilities. I found myself thinking "This is irresponsible of them to make this." while admiring the brilliant alternate sci-fi history on which the plot is based. I'm not a squemish person, but I cringed in places. Yet I played on. Wanted to play on.
I found myself wondering how they could possibly generalize this to a class of peoples so obviously incorrectly as these types of events tend to be small groups of individuals. I started defending the German  people in my mind with rationalized arguments and social rhetoric. As I continued to flash back on how this game never should have been made I started musing on how this compared with the original that I played so long ago. It never bothered me back-in-the-day. Why now? Is it the addition of such a strong plot element only?
Today's graphics and story-telling power are light-years from the old 8-bit days. They can say a lot more and a lot more powerfully. With top presentation skills, that can be the thing that makes all the difference. When you do it well enough, it can become art - like great cinema does. Art makes you think. Exposes controversy. Upsets or delights or pick-a-verb, it affects you. Really great artistic piece, under it all, asks one simple question. And presents all the myriad parts to help you contemplate an answer, without judging or guiding.
I have my answer, and I'm glad the question was asked.

Short version: This game is worth playing.
Long version: Although the game is short (I spent about 8-10 hours on my first playthrough) it's got a very well-executed story and a solid grasp of enjoyable shooter gameplay. Neither story nor gameplay are revolutionary, but the QUALITY level of both and the way everything seamlessly fits together is what sets Wolfenstein: TNO above the bar.
As far as the story goes, it had a lot of typical "war is hell" commentary from BJ and the obligatory WWII battle opening scene, but it never got boring and it actually surprised me sometimes. Considering how short a time you spend playing the game, the characters are pretty well developed (the villains in particular). Seeing as it revolves around a world where the Nazis rule the planet, I guess I shouldn't have been surprised that the game doesn't take the "safe, politically-correct" route with all its storytelling. I'll give Machine credit for making most of the plot and features in the game actually make logical sense. However, the "deus ex machina" that the characters discover later in the game to help them win seemed a little too convenient and out of place.
As far as the gameplay is concerned, I feel like it struck a nice balance. There's static health & med kits, but you also regenerate health to some degree. The perks system isn't too intrusive on your ability to enjoy the game (unlike most  acheivement hunting) and usually you end up unlocking the perks that actually benefit the way you've been playing. Plus, the addition of the dual-wield weapon system was great and real fun (nothing like obliterating a corridor full of Nazis with a pair of shotguns firing ricocheting shrapnel rounds). Finally, I was glad they included stealth even though it was a bit shallow it still got the job done (though I refuse to believe throwing a knife at someone's ankle will 1-hit K.O. them :)
Since it's a story-heavy game, I probably won't play it more than one more time, just to challenge myself with the highest difficulty and getting as many perks as possible. Regardless, this is a gaming experience you shouldn't miss. Go get it and start KILLIN' NAZIS.

Note: This review has been updated.
The best in depth RTS ever made. No game can every come close to the replayability of this game. With the release on steam we get to see an all time favorite get new development and features. Two official expansions have been added since AoC was released in the year 2000.
A notable feature that the HD edition brings is an integrated lobby system. Users with any combination of the standard HD edition or expansions/DLC can play with each other and see each others lobbies. As a former player of Age of Empires 3 I hated seeing the community spit up into vanilla, The War Chiefs, and the Asian Dynasties.
I've put 1000 hours into the game so far and still enjoy it. The multiplayer experience is the heart of the replayability. You will experience more lag than older versions of the game due to the visual engine being updated with directx 9.0c. It was originally made with version 5 & 6. The minus is the peer to peer connections vs a client server model. The plus is there is no cost to maintain it and you'll see more dollars free for development rather than paying for servers. I've found that playing with players from a region close to you makes for a pretty nice running match.
Players from Europe with good connections+good PC's can also be played with a tolerable amount of delay. Cross continent play with poor connections or older PC's makes the game hard to play. Find games with 200 or less ping and you'll be sweet!
Single player runs very good with unlocked FPS and is very responsive. It makes campaigns very enjoyable, especially when you start with limited armies and need to spend more time microing your units. The classic age of kings and conquers campaigns are always great, forgotten empires campaigns lack a little bit of the classic feel. They don't' have voice acting and play very modular like. The feel is you are playing a well crafted scenario vs a retail campaign. The newest expansion African Kingdoms brings back some of the old magic with voice acting and fluid campaigns. I highly recommend it. I have completed all the campaigns so that's my experience with them.
I give the game overall 8/10 with 10/10 a possibility. It would need to make better gains in multiplayer to earn that perfect rating. If you consider $/hour played, this game is the best value you can find even at full price.

Its been awhile since a Wolfenstein game has been relevent, but The New Order was very enjoyable.  Not only did it manage a campaign alternating between smooth gunplay and satisfying (if simple) stealth, but all parts of the game seemed more polished than I was expecting.
The levels were well designed, interesting, and varied.  The characters were some of the best animated I've seen (I assume mo-capped).  The writing (though I don't think anyone was really expecting much) was quite good and filled with the fun and spirit that many modern games miss.  I enjoyed that while the game was about epic events, its one of the few games that didn't revolve around America and its fate (America is already lost before the game begins).  The cutscenes seemed to have been authentically well directed (exhibiting cinematography I'm not used to in modern shooters) and the sound/music design was quite moving.
From a technical perspective, the game ran very well for me, and since the release of Rage, its obvious that the IdTech engine has seen some polish.  The New Order was the best use of that engine I've seen (less texture popping than Rage).  The campaign stayed fresh and didn't overstay its welcome (some might be disappointed in its length, but I appreciate a game that knows when to quit).
Bottom line: its a genuinely fun game with sharp writing that manages to avoid the ludonarrative dissonance that most modern FPS games get mired in.  I think this game will interest both people looking for a shooter with a story as well as those looking to just shoot nazis while dual weilding automatic laser sniper rifles.

Now, it's been 9 months after that review, and I must say, DB is becoming what the community wants it to be. It's shining.

The gunplay is astonishing thanks to the satifying ding sounds for hitreg, the very down to earth feeling of using a damn gun, and straying away from games that emphasize on aiming down sights(ADS), it encourages you to shoot on the move. ADSing is usually for long range or last ditch efforts. Hence, because everyone wants to hit someone and also dodge bullets, they'll be running around gunning enemies. Hence, the game has a very fast pace, which would take some time to get used to due to how it differs from CS.
Unlike typical FPS games like CS, this game takes the movement system from Brink. Including wall jumping, long jumping, and using trick jumps to reach places for an advantage and to shave time. By practising you can probably get a tiny head start from your allies and reach the battlefield faster when you long jump to get more speed.
TTK(Time To Kill) is very high due to everyone being able to take a few hits before going down, and hence when you're in a firefight, you're going to be expected to track the enemy better to make him die faster.
There are these loadout cards that can be acquired in equipment cases(Which are dropped in regular matches and require NO PAYMENT NEEDED to unlock it). Each card can have a combination of augments, boosting your combat effectiveness and giving a single merc different weapons and combos of augments for alternating playstyles.
Again, this game rewards skill more than luck. There are no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t random crits, nothing is there to help you but you and your own teammates. Work together, or die.
There is a lot of people calling this game P2W for it's card system.
Let me make it clear. It is not.
Stock(Default) cards have no augments. I will disregard the weapons and focus on the rarity and augments.
Lead has an augment.
Iron has 2.
Bronze has 3.
Silver has 3.
Gold has 3.
Cobalt has 3.
Anything outside here is still 3 augments.
See the pattern? Everything above bronze will have nothing more than 3 augments.
Which makes the rarity of these loadout cards not important at all, since at this point they're just a reskin of the same bronze card, but rarer.
Not to mention that the game will send a lot of cards towards you if you play regularly, getting credits per day and cases per match to earn a steady income of cards and credits. Equipment cases can be bought in the store for 1000 credits, and each tri-hourly mission cycle has a credit yield of 1500-3000 depending on what you can do.
It's very easy to get yourself a bronze card and be competitive. You can still kick♥♥♥♥♥in a default card but of course the lack of 3 augments to help will give you a slight disadvantage.

I say it's better than the first Portal because all-round it is. There's more story to it, way more actual content, more characters/character development, co-op and custom puzzles/maps. Over and done in 14 hours. But I did run in super-easy mode because I really just wanted the movie. Movie's pretty damn good. Had I done a harder level no doubt I would have needed to plot and skulk much more and that would have added time. On the other hand, I could have played it faster but I was admiring the stunning work done by the art crews. The lighting, the detail. Really worth getting a walkthrough at one level just to see that work. Nice one.
I did have a lot of trouble with the core sensibilities. I found myself thinking "This is irresponsible of them to make this." while admiring the brilliant alternate sci-fi history on which the plot is based. I'm not a squemish person, but I cringed in places. Yet I played on. Wanted to play on.
I found myself wondering how they could possibly generalize this to a class of peoples so obviously incorrectly as these types of events tend to be small groups of individuals. I started defending the German  people in my mind with rationalized arguments and social rhetoric. As I continued to flash back on how this game never should have been made I started musing on how this compared with the original that I played so long ago. It never bothered me back-in-the-day. Why now? Is it the addition of such a strong plot element only?
Today's graphics and story-telling power are light-years from the old 8-bit days. They can say a lot more and a lot more powerfully. With top presentation skills, that can be the thing that makes all the difference. When you do it well enough, it can become art - like great cinema does. Art makes you think. Exposes controversy. Upsets or delights or pick-a-verb, it affects you. Really great artistic piece, under it all, asks one simple question. And presents all the myriad parts to help you contemplate an answer, without judging or guiding.
I have my answer, and I'm glad the question was asked.

Short version: This game is worth playing.
Long version: Although the game is short (I spent about 8-10 hours on my first playthrough) it's got a very well-executed story and a solid grasp of enjoyable shooter gameplay. Neither story nor gameplay are revolutionary, but the QUALITY level of both and the way everything seamlessly fits together is what sets Wolfenstein: TNO above the bar.
As far as the story goes, it had a lot of typical "war is hell" commentary from BJ and the obligatory WWII battle opening scene, but it never got boring and it actually surprised me sometimes. Considering how short a time you spend playing the game, the characters are pretty well developed (the villains in particular). Seeing as it revolves around a world where the Nazis rule the planet, I guess I shouldn't have been surprised that the game doesn't take the "safe, politically-correct" route with all its storytelling. I'll give Machine credit for making most of the plot and features in the game actually make logical sense. However, the "deus ex machina" that the characters discover later in the game to help them win seemed a little too convenient and out of place.
As far as the gameplay is concerned, I feel like it struck a nice balance. There's static health & med kits, but you also regenerate health to some degree. The perks system isn't too intrusive on your ability to enjoy the game (unlike most  acheivement hunting) and usually you end up unlocking the perks that actually benefit the way you've been playing. Plus, the addition of the dual-wield weapon system was great and real fun (nothing like obliterating a corridor full of Nazis with a pair of shotguns firing ricocheting shrapnel rounds). Finally, I was glad they included stealth even though it was a bit shallow it still got the job done (though I refuse to believe throwing a knife at someone's ankle will 1-hit K.O. them :)
Since it's a story-heavy game, I probably won't play it more than one more time, just to challenge myself with the highest difficulty and getting as many perks as possible. Regardless, this is a gaming experience you shouldn't miss. Go get it and start KILLIN' NAZIS.

There is no multiplayer in Wolfenstein TNO:
"If we could take every bit of energy and sweat the studio has and pour all that into the single-player campaign, it gives us the resources to make something very, very cool, compared to if we would also have to divert some of our resources to making multiplayer."
And I have to say, the dev was selling it short calling the campaign 'very, very cool'. It's absolutely amazing. This is the most fun I've had with a shooter since Bulletstorm.
I didn't expect the story to be interesting, but it is, mostly because the characters are well developed. You get a better feel for the resistance in the interludes, where you explore the underground base. These serve as a welcome break from the action, but also give more exposure to the characters.
This is no regular corridor shooter. Most levels have secret routes and sometimes there are multiple paths to take. The game offers a chance to approach a situation with stealth or guns blazing, but why not use both? For instance it's great fun to take out the commanders silently first (who can call for backup), then finish up with mayhem from your dual shotguns.
The arsenal isn't too big, but that's a good thing. Every weapon is fun to use (silenced pistol headshots hnnghh), with dual wielding and secondary fire modes adding variety to the combat. Some enemies are a bit too bullet-spongey when you use regular weapons, but that's a minor complaint. When you make full use of your arsenal, the encounters feel very satisfying.
If Wolfenstein: The New Order is what we get when developers ditch mp in favor of the campaign, I'm all for it. The focus shows, and I'm actually itching to go back in and replay the game. Machinegames have really delivered something special here.

Mixed Recommendation.
Would recommend this only in it is on sale under $5.  I overpaid at $8.
First the install and setup:  I had over 20 minutes in game before I could even play it.  Creating and linking the Rockstar social club account did not go smoothly.  This is  perhaps a year after the game was released, so no excuse there.  I don't really like the fact that I need another account, but it seems to be common practice now for the major studios.
Once that was set up and I could start the game,  I couldn't adjust any settings (sound, graphics settings) except for screen brightness until after the game had started and gone through minutes of cutscenes.
Every time you start the game it also has to reconnect to your linked rockstar account, which adds to initial loading time; it is unnecessary for single player play, but I suppose they want to track your playtime and achievements just like Uplay or Games for windows.  An annoying, but standard practice.  Still, just because everyone is doing it doesn't make it acceptable and it adds negative points to the review.
Worst of all, there are very long unskippable cutscenes.  The story is nice once, and I am enjoying that part, but once is enough and I don't care after that.  Completely unacceptable.
Other than that, graphics are not that great, but the environments and scenery are filled out nicely.  The non-structural elements are also destructible, which adds to the atmosphere.
Game play is standard Max Payne.
To play it at the harder difficulties, you have to unlock them by beating Hard mode.  I tried to replay an early chapter to unlock some skipped secrets.  It felt like punishment having to re-watch all of those unskippable cutscenes.  I'm just going to finish my one playthrough and then uninstall.  It isn't worth the frustration to sit through the cutscenes again.  I guess that is also standard Max Payne, but in the past it was just that one long dream level that you didn't want to have to suffer through a second time.  In MP3, it is 3-10 minutes per chapter of cutscenes.  At least they don't pause when you use shift-tab, and you can peruse web on Steam's crappy browser until they are over.
tldr:
5 out of 10:
-0.5: due to outdated (for the time of its release) graphics,
-1 poor install experience (especially given time since release),
-1 always-on internet requirement, and most egregious of all,
-2.5 the long unskippable cutscenes that suck the fun out of any single-player replay experience.
