While I wouldn't call this the definitive wallpaper customization tool (I think DisplayFusion does better if you're looking for a good multi-monitor desktop tool), I think that this is easily the most unique application I've seen. With how technology has improved over the years, it is a surprise to me that something like moving and interactive desktops hasn't been done in the way that Wallpaper Engine does (as far as I'm aware; their could easily be other applications like this that I've not heard of).
The tool is in Early Access right now, so limitations and bugs are to be expected. However, there are a plentiful amount of options to choose from. You can create wallpapers out of video files, html web files, displaying 3D models made in Blender, or even make interactive wallpapers through Unity. Of course, it does take some learning to make some of the latter wallpaper types, but if you know how to work Blender and Unity, this will be up your street. You can even submit your custom wallpaper to the Workshop for others to use, or if you have original wallpaper designs, submit them to be sold through Steam curation.
The developer has been pretty active with this so far. Since the release, he's shipped at least 3 updates that fix bugs and add requested options and features to the UI, such as automatic previews when choosing a wallpaper to display. He is also very quick with responding to bug reports or general discussions. I posted twice about certain issues in the forums, and he responded to me within 24 hours, and even fixed one of the issues I had in the following patch. It's active developers like these that better encourage me to support these applications.

Just a heads up for those who haven't bought this, and may think of buying it.
First you have to create an account on Social Club in order to activate the game and then it HAS to be permanently linked to your Steam account. Then if you want to change your privacy settings to private for instance on the Social Club account you have to Link it permanently to Facebook or Twitter account, before it will ever let you access the Social Club account.
This should be stated on the game store page IMO. For those of you who don't mind having everything public and all these accounts linked then it's not an issue. However I like privacy and don't have a social media account. The loss of privacy now adays just to play a game is ridiculous! Again there should be a notice to gamers considering the purchase about these things! If I had known I would NOT have bought the game.
This to me is nothing more than a sleezy data collection scheme.  AND YOU are paying them so they can USE you and your accounts for free promotion of their game at the expense of your privacy.
Which boils down to....Let me know these hidden requirements before I buy something because I don't want to buy something if these are things I'm forced to agree to. I'm old school, pay money for license and play game! I do not want to pay money in order to be forced into this social media crap!
EDIT (since some people were missing this in comments)
When I first registered this game and discovered the hidden account stuff, I sent a searing email to customer support at Rockstar Games about the account linking with Facebook and Twitter in order to change privacy settings. I also included this review to make them aware of what I posted publicly about their game policy. I gave them the choice of giving my money back, or changing my privacy. Whether it forced a policy change, it has since let me change my privacy settings without linking to a social media account.
*These additional account creation in order to play, and things like linking to social media ALL need to be optional.  Optional so that people like me can opt out of them completely, and those who like them can take part in them.

For example, when creating a waterflow wallpaper the only hint at what is required to make the water flow is "The red channel defines horizontal water flow, the green channel controls vertical water flow" and there is an image with red arrows and green areas on it. I haven’t a clue how it works :( (but I will ask the question in the discussion group)
But as I said this is still early access, I am sure either a guide or documentation will follow when the application is ready for full release.
The supplied wallpaper is very good, as is a lot of the available wallpaper on the workshop. The application encourages you to upload your creations to the workshop so if you can’t find anything that suits your tastes at the moment I am sure it won’t be long until you do.
One foible for myself though, I have a 21:9 monitor and rarely have apps in full screen (unless gaming), an animated wallpaper can get quite distracting and a lot of what is available is quite bright with high levels of contrast by default.
The overhead seems quite minimal, mostly CPU runs at 1% or less for the exe and GPU utilisation (GTX 1070) was up to 40% utilisation for some of the 3D wallpaper, 15% for 2D and 6% or less for everything else. As promised the wallpaper does pause when full screen is activated for an app/game.
The creation of web, flag and video wallpaper is a breeze and to be honest I was stunned with the ease of the creation and presentation of a video wallpaper. You can create some in-game footage using Shadowplay then immediately create a video wallpaper using that footage and have it looping on your desktop, flawlessly using less than 2% GPU on my rig!
If you are experienced in 3D modelling or (semi) advanced graphics I am sure you will have a ball creating wallpaper with this software. A quick look at the workshop demonstrates what is possible even at this stage of release. I only hope that some good guidance becomes available so that I can join in, I am sure it will.
Whatever your level of expertise Wallpaper Engine will have something that you can use and will like. At its current price it is a steal and it can only improve.

Wolfenstein delivers exactly what I expected, over-the-top nonstop Nazi killing fun. Not only does it successfully revive the father of all shooter video games, it stands its own as an excellent modern day shooter. You can peak from cover freely just by holding the cover button and leaning in any direction you desire, making it easy to quickly duck down behind cover and shoot around corners. You can also dual wield anything! Dual wield assault rifles, dual wield shotguns, dual wield freakin sniper rifles that transform into automatic lazer guns! This game is just nonstop, consistent fun.
The story offered in "The New Order" is fantastic. There's great voice over work to be found by all the characters, and the actual plot was the most creative thing I've had the pleasure of experiencing in years. I don't want to spoil too much, because I went into this game knowing absolutely nothing about the story, and loved it even more. The characters themselves are all interesting and having the short Headquarters missions where you have to help them out before your next mission really helped you feel like you were a part of the story itself. All of the action leads up to a fantastic finale that I was more than satisfied with.
Now let's talk about the tech behind the game. Here's where we run into a few major issues. This game is optimized terribly. And I say terribly, because my framerates struggled in many areas despite the graphics not even looking that great. The explosions look like something you would see in a PS2 game. Just bland yellow puffs of smoke that are only recognizable as explosions because of the sound effect. This is unacceptable, especially for a game being sold on "next gen" hardware. In addition to some poor effects work, there's many areas in the game where the textures look so bad that I was wondering if that game was supposed to have a cell-shaded look to it. But none of these graphical issues were as bad as the screen tearing. Despite offering a vertical sync option in the settings, this game screen-tears like nothing I've ever seen. It's very disorienting trying to search for ammo when the top half of your screen is looking the other way. I'm not quite sure what is causing this issue, and I'm sure if you used a 3rd party program to enable vertical sync, it may fix the problem, but hopefully this issue is officially fixed for the game given some time.
Now let's talk about the gameplay. Make no mistake, just like it's predecessor, this is a LINEAR shooter. However, the developers managed to slip in some creative approaches to areas. I enjoyed having the option to find a secret metal grate that I could use my welding torch on so I could sneak into an area high above the enemies, and steathily take them out one by one to prevent reinforcements from arriving. There are several different paths in and around areas which makes for some great strategic planning and offers some replay value. Not only that, but the game is completely flooded with collectables hidden everywhere. And these aren't your simple types of modern day secret areas.. these are oldschool secret stashes that only the most seasoned oldschool shooter fan will know how to find.
So despite it's few technical issues like screen-tear and poor graphic quality, wolfenstein holds its own in a world diluted with first person shooters due to its fantastic gameplay mechanics and surprisingly creative story. Don't miss out on this one, this is your only chance to kill plenty of dem nazis.

Wolfenstein's fallen from grace in recent years, and that's a shame for a franchise that practically launched the First Person Shooter that is so mainstream today. The 2009 title did nothing to fill in the gap between the legendary Return to Castle Wolfenstein and Enemy Territory titles, which were multiplayer juggernauts back in their day. Wolfenstein seemed doomed to fail and interest could never be lower, but perhaps that's what made The New Order one of the best shooters I've played in recent memory.
The New Order does so many things so very, very right, ranging from the tight, punchy feel of the combat to the stellar writing of its relatable and sympathetic characters, to the incredible art design of a Steampunk Nazi-controlled world, an intuitive and simple challenge-based leveling system, lifelike animations, cinematography that rivals many films of today, a lavish level design, collectables that are worth giving a damn about, and even an interesting early moral choice in the game makes it worth replaying. This game is tuned so tight in its' combat which alone makes it worth the price of entry. Weapons are punchy, sending enemies flying or satisfying limb dismemberment with a thunderous "thud" with a sound design that rivals that of Killing Floor or Battlefield 4, and the aiming is quick and snappy, making the gunplay not only a ton of fun but a pure, childish delight to blowing Nazi scumbags away.
Perhaps the most surprising element of this new Wolfenstein is all in the story. The main story is nothing new, but its' the context and the characters involved that will stay with you long after the game is turned off. The acting and writing goes above and beyond the quality a shooter should have any right to have. The actors and actresses commit to their lines and roles with the emotion and gravitas worthy of an Oscar-nominated film, and the script they read from is so natural and full of sharp and thoughtful dialogue that it's hard not to want to stop and listen to what everyone in this world has to say, and that is a tremendous accomplishment for a shooter, let alone a Wolfenstein game.
But alas, The New Order isn't without flaws. Issue number one lies in the metastory. While the characters and dialogue are what makes Wolfenstein a cut above a lot of story-driven games, the main plot itself is rather unoriginal and unfortunately overused. The plot focuses on a resistance against an oppressing force, in this case being the Nazis, trying to topple their government and win freedom for all. Apart from a few key moments in the story, there are few to no surprises and that's just as disappointing as the rather abrupt ending.
One of the main guns encouraged to be used and upgraded throughout the game is a laser gun that requires stopping at recharging stations in order to re-use, which breaks the steady pace and flow the game tries to hard to maintain so frequently. What's even more unfortunate is that this isn't the only weapon to use this energy system in the game. There is also a unique mechanic introduced half-way into the game that lets you cut through fences which is novel, at first, but it quickly wears out its' welcome due to lack of further development of said mechanic. Another issue is that even though the game encourages you to play however you want to play with its' intuitive level-up system, trying to play a straight up run-and-gun action player isn't a very viable option due to the questionable choice of a classic health and armor system that makes it counter-intuitive to eat a lot of lead while killing a lot of Nazis. Finally, another unfortunate element that breaks up the pace of the game is the absurd amount of pick-ups of health and ammo you don't automatically pick up. This is 2014, we don't need to manually pick up ammo anymore, especially in a game that's supposed to offer the ability to run-and-gun through it.
However, these last two paragraphs shouldn't stop you from experiencing Wolfenstein: The New Order, because despite the nitpicky flaws, it's an absolutely stellar shooter. It won't blow your hair back with originality or innovation to the industry, but it does its' genre so well that it's an effort that deserves to be commended and played. If you want an extremely well-polished and satisfying shooter which lets you kill Nazis, tug at your heartstrings, and give you more choice and flexibility than the leading FPS games in the industry, then this is a title you deserve not to miss.

If you pick up this game and fall in love with it, learn its depths, and attempt to attain some mastery, you, like me, will be routinely and repeatedly punished because of your efforts. I have even sunk lifetime premium into the game.  An admitted mistake.  In order to prevent others like me from making the same mistake, I ask that you not play the game.  I ask that you spread the message, and help to prevent the asinine tendencies of Freejam from deeply insulting every sensibility you've ever owned.  They have behaved dishonorably, and must be punished with a second bankruptcy, as the first one didn't seem to hurt them badly enough for Freejam to actually open their ears. Wolfenstein hasn’t been a strong franchise since Wolfenstein 3D. I’ve had a reasonably good time with all the later titles. But I wouldn’t hold up any of them as particularly strong shooters. I went into The New Order with cautiously optimistic expectations. I’m glad to say it exceeded them.
The mood of the game feels almost ethereal. It reminds me a lot of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay. Which maybe shouldn’t be a surprise since it’s by the same people. The New Order goes for the “play the way you want” school of FPS design. Combat arenas are open with plenty of alternative routes, and the AI is designed to allow for both stealthy and gung ho play styles. And it works! It doesn’t have sophisticated stealth mechanics, but they do the job. And what I mentioned earlier about the mood is conveyed in large part by the music. It hits just the right note for this type of game. It doesn’t stress you in any way. The voice over and dialogue is similarly subdued to not make you feel stressed. All this made it feel nice to be in the game world.
Despite this the game has a slew of problems, like the combat. In other FPSes like Serious Sam or Shadow Warrior you learn instinctively how to react to certain enemies. Like how you’re supposed to move in order to avoid their attacks. In Wolfenstein I never had a solid idea of how enemies really behaved. I’m scratching my head just thinking of how I’d describe the optimal strategy to taking out normal soldiers, or shotgun dudes, or the tough armored soldiers. It doesn’t feel like they’re designed to have an optimal strategy you can learn. Just shoot them all in the head and hope for the best. The design just isn’t good enough for a game of this length. It’s the same with the health system. It doesn’t have regenerating health, but I wish it did, because this wasn’t designed well enough to work without it. Sometimes there’s not enough health packs, and sometimes there’s way too many. It was rarely “just right”. It’s not a complete disaster, but far from ideal.
It has other minor annoyances like how it randomly chooses which weapons you have at the start of each level. Sometimes you get to keep your sniper rifle between maps. Sometimes you don’t. At one point it disappeared for several hours, only to reappear in my inventory for no reason, with all my other guns removed. There was no satisfactory in-game excuse for this, so it seemed like the game was screwing me over for no reason. Let me keep my guns you♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
The story also had obvious problems. There’s subplots that don’t go anywhere, and the drama curve is off. Meaning that when you reach the finale there’s no sense of occasion. The game hasn’t built up to that moment properly, so there’s no feeling of anticipation or excitement. Instead it just sort of happens. Overall I liked the story. It tried to make the main and supporting characters into actual characters, and it kind of worked. I’ve seen some describe it as laughably bad, and I don’t agree with that. This is head and shoulders above the current FPS average. It needed more time in editing though. The issues are glaring.
Despite all the problems I really liked the game. The stuff that sucked didn’t ruin the game for me. It still had elements strong enough that the problems didn’t matter. It would’ve been nice had the combat and story been better. But even with those issues it managed get enough things lined up right that it clicked. I wanted to see what was around the corner. I was never bored. That’s why I hope this team gets to do another singleplayer FPS. They’ve got a good thing going here. Try again, and maybe you’ll make a classic.

Wolfenstein hasn’t been a strong franchise since Wolfenstein 3D. I’ve had a reasonably good time with all the later titles. But I wouldn’t hold up any of them as particularly strong shooters. I went into The New Order with cautiously optimistic expectations. I’m glad to say it exceeded them.
The mood of the game feels almost ethereal. It reminds me a lot of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay. Which maybe shouldn’t be a surprise since it’s by the same people. The New Order goes for the “play the way you want” school of FPS design. Combat arenas are open with plenty of alternative routes, and the AI is designed to allow for both stealthy and gung ho play styles. And it works! It doesn’t have sophisticated stealth mechanics, but they do the job. And what I mentioned earlier about the mood is conveyed in large part by the music. It hits just the right note for this type of game. It doesn’t stress you in any way. The voice over and dialogue is similarly subdued to not make you feel stressed. All this made it feel nice to be in the game world.
Despite this the game has a slew of problems, like the combat. In other FPSes like Serious Sam or Shadow Warrior you learn instinctively how to react to certain enemies. Like how you’re supposed to move in order to avoid their attacks. In Wolfenstein I never had a solid idea of how enemies really behaved. I’m scratching my head just thinking of how I’d describe the optimal strategy to taking out normal soldiers, or shotgun dudes, or the tough armored soldiers. It doesn’t feel like they’re designed to have an optimal strategy you can learn. Just shoot them all in the head and hope for the best. The design just isn’t good enough for a game of this length. It’s the same with the health system. It doesn’t have regenerating health, but I wish it did, because this wasn’t designed well enough to work without it. Sometimes there’s not enough health packs, and sometimes there’s way too many. It was rarely “just right”. It’s not a complete disaster, but far from ideal.
It has other minor annoyances like how it randomly chooses which weapons you have at the start of each level. Sometimes you get to keep your sniper rifle between maps. Sometimes you don’t. At one point it disappeared for several hours, only to reappear in my inventory for no reason, with all my other guns removed. There was no satisfactory in-game excuse for this, so it seemed like the game was screwing me over for no reason. Let me keep my guns you♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
The story also had obvious problems. There’s subplots that don’t go anywhere, and the drama curve is off. Meaning that when you reach the finale there’s no sense of occasion. The game hasn’t built up to that moment properly, so there’s no feeling of anticipation or excitement. Instead it just sort of happens. Overall I liked the story. It tried to make the main and supporting characters into actual characters, and it kind of worked. I’ve seen some describe it as laughably bad, and I don’t agree with that. This is head and shoulders above the current FPS average. It needed more time in editing though. The issues are glaring.
Despite all the problems I really liked the game. The stuff that sucked didn’t ruin the game for me. It still had elements strong enough that the problems didn’t matter. It would’ve been nice had the combat and story been better. But even with those issues it managed get enough things lined up right that it clicked. I wanted to see what was around the corner. I was never bored. That’s why I hope this team gets to do another singleplayer FPS. They’ve got a good thing going here. Try again, and maybe you’ll make a classic.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

Let me start off by saying that i never write reviews so i'm probably not really good at it.
I found Robocraft about 10 months ago while browsing the Steam Store for F2P games, i was looking for something new, something fresh since i grew bored of playing the same popular F2P games over and over.
"Build your own robot and the use it to fight other robots? This must be great!" i thought while downloading it.
From what i remember i really like playing 1-2 hours each day thinking about the best robot designs, driving my trusty mechs to battle and triumphing with them.
But, as with many other F2P games i played, Robocraft quickly became stale and i stopped playing it.
Now, 10 months later, i opened it again out of couriosity and oh boy has it changed.
The global chat is all about spam, factory advertising (the factory is basically the auction house of the robots) or players insulting eachother.
The grind for good robot parts is atrocious, the only way to acquire parts is by receiving loot crates at the end of the match. These crates have different tiers based on your performance and each contain 8 random gear pieces (4 items locked, 4 free).
The "Recycling" system allows you to recycle unused robot parts into robits that later can be used to craft the desired gear, problem is that recycling gives you a minimal amount of the robits value of the recycled part (1/5 for commons, 1/4 for rares, 2/5 for epics) and since you are probably recycling low value gear while trying to craft those top tier weapons it takes an eternity to get to the good stuff, not counting that you will need most of the gear you aquire through the loot crates in order to improve your robot CPU.
The robot CPU indicates how much "advanced" is your robot: if you put a low tier gun on your robot then your CPU will increase by a little, if you put an higher tier gun it will increase by a lot. The higher your CPU the better the gear you find in your crates. Problem is that to increase your CPU you need to find better weapons in the first place and to consistently find those you need an high CPU. If you fill your robot with a lot of crappy parts just to increase your CPU you will be matched with high CPU robots and since your weapon quality is lower you will get low scores, low scores means worse loot crates.
Now it's time to talk about the battles: you just finished building your awesome robot, gave it a cool name and colored it nicely. You hit the play button, you queue for a match. Battle starts, you sprint to the middle of the map to join the frey. Finally you face your first enemy! But wait... that dude has the legendary minigun mounted on his robot! He also has 8 laser guns, 4 rail guns and even 1 medic gun installed! How is it possible that your basic robot with just 6 basic laser guns installed got matched against him? The answer is that matchmaking in this game is broken. How am i sure about it? yesterday i tried to create a robot with only 1 specific gun mounted on it (let's call it A), i was around 200 CPU. I got matched against another robot with a total of 4 A guns with also shields. Now that's what i call fair game. Let's return to your game: you start shooting at the robot, you try to aim at the minigun to destroy it but wait! your robot is bugged! If you leave the Robocraft client open for too long the game bugs out and when you shoot the rounds will not come out of the gun! The other robot easily destroys yours, you wait and respawn at base. Just as you respawn you hear "Your plutonium reactor is under attack!" (that thingy is your base and if it is destroyed you lose) You quickly check the reactor to see where the attack comes from but all you can see are the cristals of your reactor exploding without an apparent reason. Because apparently there's an exploit that makes you invisible/invulnerable to the enemies that makes you cheese the game. And you stand there watching your base gettin destroyed, unable to react because there's no kick vote system in the game.
And now the last thing that gave the final blow to Robocraft for me: Premium. When 3 days ago i started playing again the game automatically gave me 3 days of Premium. I have no problems with Premium being in the game, if you support the game you get bonuses, i'm ok with that. Premium players receive double EXP, cool colors unlocked, get to have a custom avatar in game, cool stuff. Now that my Premium is over i find out that you must be premium to get the full Loot Crates at the end of the matches or else you only get half items from those. This added to the awful recycling system really♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off and i told myself "Ok, this is it. I'm out of here. If i want to play grindy games i will just go back to Warframe."
Now i uninstalled Robocraft and my only regret was wasting 60 hours in this poor excuse for a game.

I was incredibly surprised by this game. I expected mindless 90s style FPS, but got the best of early 2000s FPS with the addition of the good elements of newer games.
PROS:
+ Story is intriguing. (So far!)
+ A lot of areas where you can approach enemies as you'd like. (Stealth, Head-on, etc.)
+ Scavenging for those that want to; semi-regenerating health for those who don't care.
+ Many levels of difficullity.
+ Humor.
+ Graphics in cut scenes are breathtaking. It's rendered in-engine, but it doesn't look like it.
+ Nice to be able to shoot people without any moral qualms. The nazis here are complete monsters!
+ Interesting and scary antagonists.
+ No QTEs!
+ No Multiplayer! No launch-day DLCs! No "AAA publisherisms" AFAICT!!!
CONS:
- Still just an FPS, if you don't like those
- A lot of collectibles. People with OCD tendencies will want to find them all.
- Gun play isn't very diverse right now.
- Still pretty linnear, in order to advance a story.
OBSERVATIONS:
o This feels a lot like Bioshock: Infinite, but without the magic. The run-and-gun has a very similar feeling and the alternate history is also a theme that is common to them.
o You can carry a lot of weapons, as in classical FPSes. You can also dual-wield weapons if you so wish.
o It's a bit like a WW2-shooter, but in the 1960s.
o This game feels pretty grown-up; e.g. "mature" in the original sense. I guess they see their target audience as grown-ups and not the audience of CoD and BF, which is mainly younger. Smart move! That audience wouldn't care less for "Wolfenstein" ("what's that, lol?") as they already have a game(s) to play. Find your own audience and pander to them!
o The protagonist looks like the original sprite for Wolfenstein 3D.
Buy it if you like the classical FPSes!

game is insanely fun if you like doing the large scale battles with tanks, airplanes, airdropping onto enemy territory, and sniping unaware enemies who are busy trying to mess up your teammates, i have always loved playing games like battlefield and battlefront so this game, after you know what your doing is almost a now brainer

though i will mention that they do have a program that you can download to create your own armor and camo and helmets and whatnot, which most of the ones you see are all custom made which look sick, BUT in order for you to do such a thing you have to have a decent knowledge on 3d artwork and making 3d models, cause if you dont know this then good luck trying to make your own anything for this game, there is almost no customization if you dont want to drop money

What's worse is that that the NEXT time I bumble into sight with the SAME guy, same freakin' deal:  the Nazi accepts that his mind regularly plays tricks on him and until something overt happens he's alright with his pathing... which never changes.
And if said Nazi runs into the corpses of his comrades and their cybernetic doggy, he takes it just as stoicly.  The entire thing takes me out of what might otherwise be a decent experience.
If/when the game gets a major AI patch it might be worth looking into during a sale.

Very tentative recommendation, only if it's on sale, and only if you don't mind a metric♥♥♥♥♥ton of cinematics. Max Payne 3 is a game that really just should have shut its mouth ninety-percent of the time and let the excellent gunplay take over.
In the moment, the mechanics are smooth, responsive, and ridiculously cool in the most fluid and explosive way you've ever seen in any shooter, but the issue is that MP3 constantly takes you out of the moment, nonstop chatter, nonstop unskippable cutscenes that just aren't that well written with a droll story that doesn't really go anywhere. When that doesn't get in the way, the level design can be too narrow and prevents full use of the game's coolest features, like shootdodge or bullettime, it's hard to do those things and feel cool when the level is a tiny office or corridor that's going to have you hitting your head on a desk chair that inevitably results in your premature death.
When it's good, it's really, really, ♥♥♥♥ing good, so get it for that, but beware of Max Payne 3's propensity to be a total wind-bag.

I was incredibly surprised by this game. I expected mindless 90s style FPS, but got the best of early 2000s FPS with the addition of the good elements of newer games.
PROS:
+ Story is intriguing. (So far!)
+ A lot of areas where you can approach enemies as you'd like. (Stealth, Head-on, etc.)
+ Scavenging for those that want to; semi-regenerating health for those who don't care.

+ Humor.
+ Graphics in cut scenes are breathtaking. It's rendered in-engine, but it doesn't look like it.
+ Nice to be able to shoot people without any moral qualms. The nazis here are complete monsters!
+ Interesting and scary antagonists.
+ No QTEs!
+ No Multiplayer! No launch-day DLCs! No "AAA publisherisms" AFAICT!!!
CONS:
- Still just an FPS, if you don't like those
- A lot of collectibles. People with OCD tendencies will want to find them all.
- Gun play isn't very diverse right now.
- Still pretty linnear, in order to advance a story.
OBSERVATIONS:
o This feels a lot like Bioshock: Infinite, but without the magic. The run-and-gun has a very similar feeling and the alternate history is also a theme that is common to them.
o You can carry a lot of weapons, as in classical FPSes. You can also dual-wield weapons if you so wish.
o It's a bit like a WW2-shooter, but in the 1960s.
o This game feels pretty grown-up; e.g. "mature" in the original sense. I guess they see their target audience as grown-ups and not the audience of CoD and BF, which is mainly younger. Smart move! That audience wouldn't care less for "Wolfenstein" ("what's that, lol?") as they already have a game(s) to play. Find your own audience and pander to them!
o The protagonist looks like the original sprite for Wolfenstein 3D.
Buy it if you like the classical FPSes!

I have only played the single player of this game, therefore I cannot judge the multiplayer aspect.
The gameplay is acceptable in it's core, but boy did they mess up with some aspects.
After every cutscene (which is every second door you go through) you are usually put in a bad position in the middle of the room facing around 7 enemies, equipped with 1 pistol in your hand. Regardless of what you had equipped before said cutscene.
Further ruining this is the weapon switching mechanic. There is no more nice layout showing you all the weapons you collected. You have a stupid circle split into 4 which constantly bugs if you use the scroll wheel (keeps switching between only 2 options) and the default keybindings to said circle are horrible.
There are hidden things in most areas. Newspapers, television clips, clues about the story and parts of golden weapons that you can collect.
Which is a nice feature, I like exploring and finding out more about the story.
But! Max or whoever is on your side is constantly nagging you every 3 seconds to move forward, that you don't have time to look around.
Which pretty much makes you choose between getting more insight into the story while constantly being harassed or rushing through the game because the story tells you to, ruining any immersion.
Every time your life depletes and you still have some painkillers you go into slomo facing the person that shot you giving you a chance to kill him and use a painkiller.
Not a bad idea, if it wasn't ruined by what happens next.
After you kill the guy, you fall on the ground forcing you to get up again.
You can't get into cover instantly from the ground. If you press Q (default key to get into cover) while behind some cover you first stand up and THEN go into cover thus getting shot multiple times again (usually forced into the whole slomo shootoff again on higher difficulties).
Why didn't they bother working out the cover mechanics? They just slapped some half a$$ed attempt into the game.
One thing that I found pretty good was the ability to switch the camera angle so that your character was either left or right of the reticle.
BUT! As expected, there is also a flaw with this.
The bullets hit the target of the reticle regardless of what is between the gun and the reticle.
So most of the time I was hitting an enemy behind a wall even though Max himself was completely behind that wall.
The only reason I kept playing until the end was my hope of there being just a little bit of the old Max Payne in there.
But I found the story to be a boring, cheesy joke. I could not feel anything for the characters at any point in the game, they were all just dull and uninteresting. Everything about it felt forced and mindless.
I actually replayed the first Max Payne about a year ago. I loved every second of it! Everything about that game sucks you in. The way the story is presented, the story itself, the gameplay, the atmosphere, the freedom to save whenever you want.
Even today it's still a refreshing game!
Rockstar couldn't have done much worse with this attempt at Max Payne. They had a solid foundation with the story and gameplay from the first ones. They decided to take Max Payne a completely different route and completely failed to deliver.
If I had to rate it as a Max Payne game I would give it no more than a 3/10. Not even worth buying during a steam sale.
If, however, they made this as an original story I would give it close to a 6/10 probably.
The game has lots of flaws and the story really lacks, but it is an acceptable action game.
I played it on hard difficulty and the challenge was decent.
You can probably have a bit of fun in the multiplayer and it would be worth a couple of bucks if you're looking for an action game to kill some time with.

You play as BJ "Big Testicled" Blazkowicz and your mission is to kill as many Nazis as you can using a arsenal of deadly weapons including knifes, shotguns, assault rifles, sniper rifles, and lasers. Along the way, you'll be pulling out several knifes, eating several rockets to the face, and being shot to Hell and back all before dawn. Along the way, you'll find true love (<3 Fergus), tragedy, and most importantly, mountains of dead Nazis.
So, let's get to the basics. Wolfenstein: The New Order is a shooter set in a alternate history where Nazis won World War II and have taken control of the world in the near future of 1960. In this advanced era, Nazis have developed atomic weaponry, giant robots, and spaceships (but not color TV, evidently). So yeah, the premise is a bit silly, but it's a nice change of pace from a war torn unnamed  Middle Eastern country.
So how does Wolfenstein differentiate itself from the pack? Well, for starters, there's no multiplayer of any sort. No Nazi Zombies, no Nuketown, no de_dust, no nothing. The real meat is the single player campaign (along with various collectibles and extra modes). So, on that note, this game holds up as a single player experience, albeit without some flaws.
Gameplay doesn't try to do anything too different than most shooters. It's your standard run and gun shooter (more in the vein of titles like Shadow Warrior and Rise of the Triad rather than Battlefield or Call of Duty) in that you use impractically large weapons to pulverize the entrails of dozens of Nazi soldiers. For the most part, combat is satisfying. The assault rifle is quite fun to use, the shotgun liquefies enemies, the sniper rifle turns enemies heads into broken watermelons, and so on. The gore definitely helps with the brutality of the combat, which adds to the frenetic nature of combat. Being able to dual wield pretty much and weapons helps quite a bit too. However, outside of dual-wielding, laser cutting (which tends to be finicky and frustrating), a unique health system (you have 100 health, and you can regenerate up to a multiple of 20 - so 40,60,80,100,etc. and any health pickups past your maximum health will grant you an "overcharge" that acts as a quickly fading buffer zone for you main health).
What elevates Wolfenstein from being an "average" game into a "good" game lies outside of the traditional shooter gameplay. Namely, this game stands up because of its tight pacing, great attention to detail, and engaging world.
Regarding the pacing, Wolfenstein understands the importance of downtime, which many shooters often seem to forget. While you might blow up a Nazi fortress in one chapter, the other chapter will have you run various errands like finding toys for Max (an infantile giant, similar to Lenny from "Of Mice and Men" except more intentionally violent) or scraping mold off of concrete for analysis. During this downtime, you'll have a chance to learn about each character's unique personality and the world of Wolfenstein as a whole from various newspaper clippings.
For the most part, the game manages to avoid the pitfalls of ludo-narrative dissonance (for example, you can kill dozens of Tribalmen in Far Cry 3, but you can't stomach skinning wild animals) despite the rather ludicrous setting since the game recognizes that you're a badass Nazi killing machine. It goes a long way into making you feel more immersed in the experience.
On that note, Wolfenstein has so much love put into it, that it's hard not to notice. You can perform mundane tasks like flushing a toilet or examining mold repellent. Nazis speak in authentic German and not some horribly accented English (for the most part, at least). There are little scattered gold treasures around every level, and so much more.
Now that most of the pros are out of the way, let's talk about some of the issues. While the port of the game is solid for the most part (FOV slider, 60 FPS, QHD support, rebindable keys), it can be a fairly ugly game and some of the texturing looks atrocious. It's not enough to ruin your immersion, but it's definitely a blemish on the experience as a whole.
I also wish there was some more variety in your weapons and enemies. While shotguns, rocket launchers, and pistols are nice, I wish there were some more ludicrous and exotic options for the player (like the Excalibat from Rise of the Triad, or the Painkiller from Painkiller). Enemy variation typically boils down to "dog, Nazi, bigger Nazi, even bigger Nazi, robot, drones". While there's enough variety of enemies to keep the experience from being stale, there really aren't all that many memorable enemies in the game.
Also, without spoiling anything, the ending is a letdown compared to the rest of the game. While it fits thematically, it goes against all that you've done as the giant pair of testicles up to that point and doesn't really resolve too much. If anything, it seems rushed.
So yeah, I liked Wolfenstein a lot despite its issues. I hope that any sequels or new entries into the series will build upon the strengths of The New Order and fix its issues. But, considering that Wolfenstein is Machine Games' first released product, it's hard not to be impressed by its debut effort.

and possibilities.
+ The current resource system lets you pull the most expensive vehicles with a maximum waiting time of 9 minutes,
the cheaper vehicles can be pulled almost infinitely if you don't get blown up repeatedly right after spawning.
+ The various weapons you can buy with ingame currency or real money are mostly sidegrades, specializing in different
fields (long range, mid range, CQC), while the starting weapons for each class are good allrounders.

Like all games, it also has some flaws:
- Stock vehicles aren't really competitive, it takes time to unlock the more crucial defensive / utility slots.
- Since the continents are huge and there's no player limit like on common server matches (e.g. 6v6, 12v12)
battles can be very one-sided, with one platoon of 48 people stomping small bases defended by 10 people.
- At the time i'm writing this review there's no real metagame in place. People just fight for bases, over and over again.
To keep it interesting you'll have to set your own goals in the ongoing battles.
I'd definitely recommend checking this game out. There's so many options to wreak havoc among your enemies in hilarious ways.

"Duke Nukem: Forever done right" pretty much sums it up.
There's an interesting balance of older shooter qualities and modern ideas in Wolfenstein: The New Order. What didn't work in older incarnations was removed and replaced, what does work from modern shooters was integrated in, and the resulting game comes off as being smarter than the average gritty shooter tends to be. Levels are linear but contain multiple pathways; health regenerates, but only up to a point; cover is present, but can be created by the player via the blowtorch turn laser gun. Weapons are pretty standard: pistol, machine gun, shotgun, rifle, throwing knives, ect. but each one can be dual-weilded, which makes for three distinct playstyles; stealthy stab-'em-up, not so stealthy shoot-'em-up, and extremely unstealthy liquidize-'em-up. Which one you have to use at any given time is up to the player, as the game rarely forces you into stealth or cover.
The main story and main character are both kind of bland, but it seems that most of Bethesda's work went into the framework instead. Rather than the storyline that the player is actively participating in, the more interesting bits come from the period when Blazkowicz is a vegetable, between 1946 and 1960. The alternate history of that time is told on faded newpaper clips and audio logs, which is strangely effective in making the over-arching story more engaging. Same goes for characters; the protagonist isn't all that interesting, with a cyllinder for a head and speaking only in irritating gravely whispers, but the other characters seem much more human. None of them act overly patriotic or uncomfortably psychotic, but much more level-headed and believable.
Overall, Wolfenstein: The New Order provides much more than you would expect from AAA shooters these days.

Ok, so I finally get to see the game which consist mostly of Max Payne talking while you watch these "seamless, highly detailed, cinematic experiences" the game brags about. This game is good...Probably one of my favorite games of all time.  But rereleasing a 15+ year old game and selling it for $20 is ridiculous.  On top of that they are trying to charge $10 for a mod that has been out nearly as long that was once free.  They plan on releasing a new "expansion" soon that focuses on African civilizations....this will probably also be $10-$20.  If these 2 expansions were included in the original rerelease for $20 it might have been a somewhat fair deal.  The main issue with the game though is that it brings nothing new to the table and actually runs worse!  How does a 15 year old game run even worse on a computer that is more than 100x more powerful?!  Some of the issues have been fixed since release, but it is still MORE unstable than the original release was when I was running it on a 56k modem 300mhz machine.  The lag is mind boggling....I seriously had less lag running the old version of this game on a 28kbps connection when compared to running it on 1gig ethernet now.  They might have fixed this since rerelease...I wouldnt know though I tried some other multiplayer matches recently, but everytime I would get an error before the game even started.
Even if a  lot of the issues are fixed, which I doubt they are, this release for this price is still unacceptable and you should not purchase it.  They also used false advertising....they say its an HD rerelease, but it is not!  SERIOUSLY?!  The amount that they are charging for this game they couldnt update the textures just slightly?  What is really sad is that the modding community released HD textures within a week of this games release!  I mean how much did Microsoft spend on the rerelease of this game?!  Obviously nearly nothing if modders can visual upgrade this game within days and a full development team cant do jack squat with months of paid development time.  It is almost as Microsoft is RELYING on the modding community to fix and improve this game.
For the amount of glitches, the uncomprehensible downgrade from the original, and the reliance on modders to essentially make the ACTUAL game....This game should have been free!  Or they should have allowed us to put previous versions of this game into our steam account.  The only thing this game has going for it is its new multiplayer interface, which still sucks, but will offer you more than the original if you can get it to work.
Actual game = 10/10
Rerelease compared to actual game = 2/10 (+1 for multiplayer, +1 for modding support, -8 for performance issues, bugs, and nothing new)

Merciless but satisfying gun battles with the usual hardboiled narration that makes Max Payne a rich character, even if the plot was a bit plodding in terms of narrative development.  I played on the default (medium) difficulty setting, and it was one of the most difficult and occasionally frustrating games I've played without having to change difficulty settings.  On the down side, the fights were so hard as to disrupt the overall narrative flow of the game (as Payne might say, "I'd been killed so many times over, I didn't even know why I'd started fighting in the first place").  The reticle is simply a white dot that only appears when you're aiming, and often it blips in and out of view; it's a bit glitchy, so tense gun fights against multiple opponents have a brutal learning curve.  On the upside, there's bullet-time dodge shooting, so killing every last one of those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s is not an impossibility and leads to some very satisfyingly bloody resolutions.  Shooting from moving vehicles is occasional and a nice change-up in the game.  Overall, totally worth playing even if half the game time was spent dying. Max Payne 3 brings back the dark and gloomy mood from the previous games. The story is very good and this combined with the Brazil scenery makes for an enjoyable game. The story mode took me about 12 hrs to complete on Hard so it's relatively short. On the other hand, near the end of the game it becomes a repetitive chore: dozens and dozens of enemies which pop up from all possible angles, killing you so you have to replay those parts again and again and again. Especially the battle with Becker was more of a nuisance than fun. So all in all those 12 hrs were long enough for me.
The gameplay itself is quite nice, the Bullet time being an interesting feature in the series. The killcam is nice but sometimes it pulls you out of the action. The reaction shot (when you're about to get killed you can make a last ditch effort to kill the enemy who would kill you) is again a nuisance. More often than not your character isn't facing the enemy's direction so needs to turn, or is out of ammo, or has his view blocked by obstacles or .... which causes you to passively stare at the screen until the slow motion is over so you can restart that scene.
Overall I had a good time except for the repetitive parts at the end. It's good for a playthrough but doesn't have much replay value, even not for the 'golden gun' unlocks. Since multiplayer has nothing to do with the story I haven't touched that part.

This game is good...Probably one of my favorite games of all time.  But rereleasing a 15+ year old game and selling it for $20 is ridiculous.  On top of that they are trying to charge $10 for a mod that has been out nearly as long that was once free.  They plan on releasing a new "expansion" soon that focuses on African civilizations....this will probably also be $10-$20.  If these 2 expansions were included in the original rerelease for $20 it might have been a somewhat fair deal.  The main issue with the game though is that it brings nothing new to the table and actually runs worse!  How does a 15 year old game run even worse on a computer that is more than 100x more powerful?!  Some of the issues have been fixed since release, but it is still MORE unstable than the original release was when I was running it on a 56k modem 300mhz machine.  The lag is mind boggling....I seriously had less lag running the old version of this game on a 28kbps connection when compared to running it on 1gig ethernet now.  They might have fixed this since rerelease...I wouldnt know though I tried some other multiplayer matches recently, but everytime I would get an error before the game even started.
Even if a  lot of the issues are fixed, which I doubt they are, this release for this price is still unacceptable and you should not purchase it.  They also used false advertising....they say its an HD rerelease, but it is not!  SERIOUSLY?!  The amount that they are charging for this game they couldnt update the textures just slightly?  What is really sad is that the modding community released HD textures within a week of this games release!  I mean how much did Microsoft spend on the rerelease of this game?!  Obviously nearly nothing if modders can visual upgrade this game within days and a full development team cant do jack squat with months of paid development time.  It is almost as Microsoft is RELYING on the modding community to fix and improve this game.
For the amount of glitches, the uncomprehensible downgrade from the original, and the reliance on modders to essentially make the ACTUAL game....This game should have been free!  Or they should have allowed us to put previous versions of this game into our steam account.  The only thing this game has going for it is its new multiplayer interface, which still sucks, but will offer you more than the original if you can get it to work.
Actual game = 10/10
Rerelease compared to actual game = 2/10 (+1 for multiplayer, +1 for modding support, -8 for performance issues, bugs, and nothing new)

After playing some more I have to change my review. I have found out, that when I just started, I was simply very very unlucky, with bad player, low pop and some issues. Then I had a whole new experience. It seems I started playing in the middle of some patching and maintenance.
I joined the server. There was a full scale battle with all three factions fighting. I joined a squad, which I didnt even need to, due to the massive action, but I did it, to feel as part of something. Very cool experience. There was teamwork to some degree, and our medic was very awake and useful, even though he was very low level like me (by this I mean, I think he hadn't played for long). There were ally squads everywhere, and it reminded me about the long intro in Saving Private Ryan. The enemy attacked with tanks in the distance, while infantry units tried to move in on us. Apparently, and to my favor, it was us defending a huge base. Seemed like a key point to control. I don't know.
I started out by Infiltrator. What fun gameplay I had. I died a lot, yes, but I am aware this is a game pretty close to the real thing. I was suprised over how well I did. I managed to find very good sniper-spots, and remember this is in the middle of a full scale battle, and i man FULL SCALE battle. Bombs, explosions, bullets and flying light infantry everywhere. I think I was lucky, and the enemy was focused elsewhere, but I managed to use the surroundings, instead of my cloak. I got a lot of kill there. 13 or or, which is pretty much for me. I then went into our base, and found what previously looked, and seemed, like poor building design, suddenly showed huge sniping potential, and great structual design, with a lot of planning behind it. I felt like a coward, just sitting in here, in safety. I shifted to infrantry. Oh boy do they have it hard.
It is very hard being infrantry, and being so new that you do not know the surroundings that well yet. Yet I stuck to my group, got split up, united again and fought our way over a bridge. I died a lot, but a well praised medic, kept us alive. This was war. This was awesome. The Light Infrantry clearly is better, the more you know how to control the class, and know the enviroment. It is hard, and unforgiving at first, but you then get to know how to utilize the jetpack, and mobility to evade death. You/I most absolutely have to train a bit, but then you should be fine. I got some kills, around 5. Notice that I almost never kill an enemy alone. It is all about teamwork. This can be frustating, but if you like teamwork, it is no problem. Yet I was lucky to be the one dealing the final bullet a lot.
I felt the other Light Infrantry in our squad did a much better job than I. Both at killing and surviving. This might be due to them being higher lvl. This has nothing to do with the lvl, just that they have played longer and knows the game better than me, therefore I felt I didn't do much. So I changed class to be of better use. I mean we already had well trained light infrantry. I chosed medic. Our medic had dissappeared, so why not.
It is few games where support roles are fun, and even tactical to play, but damn medic in this game is cool as hell. You don't just throw health-packs and sit back in safety. NO you have to go with them straight into battle and grow some soldier balls. We ended up on a stone kind of pillar. We had a bit of shielding from ground infrantry. Yet snipers, and units had a good shot, if we did not crouch. We also took some bad aimed tank shots. I was glued to the ground, crouching and dodging to stay alive. My squad was shooting Rambo-style and doing one hell of a job, also when close-encounter ambushed jump down onto our stone-pillar. Everytime they died, and they died a lot, I would revive them, and try to keep them constantly healed. It worked and I am pretty sure that we were able to hold that piece of the base secure, for at least a little while :) It felt as we did something for the Colony, even though we payed with our lives.
I noticed that high ranking players takes no♥♥♥♥♥♥at all. I was, in panic, shooting unscoped at a infiltrator trying to melee an ally high rank. I managed to kill the INF, but was executed by my ally high rank, as I had also hit him. I would personally not act like this. It is a bit Eric Cartman-style. Other than that 1 incident, I actually didn't get teamkilled at all. This is wierd since it was all out total chaos. I want to thanks the players online for that. Good Game.
I did not play the other classes, as I still think I need to get to know the game more. Therefore I will focus on 2 classes, maybe 3 with the medic.
I had a very fun time, and will join the game again later. I just kept thinking about, with this little urge to just give it one more try. It worked, and I am beginning to like this game a lot. It really gives some unique and incredible huge battles, that you can safely call wars. You really feel like a little♥♥♥♥♥♥amongst the total amount♥♥♥♥♥♥in the world. You are nothing, but as soon as you team up, you are able to at least do a difference. It will never be your name on the front pages, but it could be your faction's name.
The game can surely throw some players off at first. It is rude and harsh. You have to first get to know the game, enviroment and to control correctly before you are even ready to kill effectively. This can scare off a lot of people. I am still not totally fine the movement in the game. I feel a bit slow, cuffed.. I don't know, it just feels a bit wierd. It is something I have to learn, but it does not annoy me anymore.
You can be unlucky and join at a bad time, THIS IS IF YOU PLAY ON EU, where there are not that many online. This seems to cause a bit of bad behavior, and team killing seems more likely here. You will have trouble finding action, and what you find might be unbalanced as hell. I don't know how often this happens, but it does not seem to happen that much. I don't feel like weapons are unbalanced. They are more there for a prefered playstyle. An example would be that a sniper can have a high dmg weapon, but very slow firerate/reload. The other sniper has a quick shooting, but low damage sniper rifle. It forces two very different playstyles. So it is clearly not pay2win. I never even accused it of that, but I saw someone complaining about it. It is not.
I am not a fan of the classes easily outmatching other classes, but then I remembered this is not the purpose. You are never ment to go into a base as Light Infrantry and be the hero. This is teamwork. You have to be unfair, and burst in with more men, and smack the ones already laying down. That is just war.
My biggest issue now is the movement, which is something I just have to learn. Like everything in the world, when you first learned it, it becomes an easy task. I believe that good players have the movement under control a lot, which helps a lot to survive.
I had to change my opinion, this game is really good. If you have friends, and are able to teampeak, then this game would be amazing.

You are put into the shoes of a WWII captain (B.J. Blazkowicz) who has lived the horrors of war, you fight for the U S of A.  tearing through Nazi establishments blasting Nazi scum.  You undergo severe head-trauma after an explosion and wake up 14 years later to a world overrun by the Nazi Regime. This game has got to be one of my favorite titles so far in the 2014 Gaming Year.  It has some very memorable moments and characters.
Gameplay 8/10
The gunplay is extremely fun as you are able to dual-wield damn near every gun, albeit the detachable turrets and laser-cutter.  There is a perk system is in place so you can upgrade B.J. Blazkowicz in a variety of ways.  Personally, I liked wht the stealth tree had to offer and found it very satisfying as you can play a good majority of mission stealthily.  Guns are also upgradeable through pick-ups you find throughout missions.  There are little files known as "Enigma Codes" found throughout the campaign which aid you in ways I have not yet discovered; but from what I have heard, they grant you access to some system of collectibles.  In the first level lalone, I found a system of three levers on the wall.  I became confused because I could have sworn I hit-up every possible combination! I turned around shortly after and found words written in German and instantly knew I had to translate them and pull the levers in whatever order.  A secret door opened and I found a supressor attachment for the pistol and an Enigma Code.  Personally, this was one of the coolest moments for me in my time playing it.
Story 9/10
The story is a great leap in in the Wolfenstein franchise as it provides choices that impact Blazkowicz's friends.  For instace, (
) Early on in the campaign you are faced with the decision to kill either a long time friend of yours or the rookie of your squad.  You end up rescuing the one that didn't die later on in the campaign.  Even though it seems YOU made the right decision, your pal will blame himself for this death and said the other soldier deserved to live.  This will affect his behavior as this NPC is still a bit tonal with me (
).  These decisions don't add the most drastic effects as they just seem to add to the immersion.
Graphics 8/10
Certainly the textures aren't the best or most boisterous as Crysis 3, but I find it pretty nice.  One of my favorite FX from the game is the Depth of Field when you are in a room in your hideout and staring into the other room.  The Depth of Field really shines in that moment as it blurs out the room you are staring at.  (Certainly you have the option to scale this DoF to your liking).  The Cinematics are truly gorgeous! All of it was motion captured meaning they had people move around to capture each and every move and facial detail.
Multiplayer 0/0
Unlike the previous installments of Wolfenstein such as Return to Castle Wolfenstein and Wolfenstein (2009), The New Order lacks a multiplayer but really shines in the singleplayer.
Overall, an amazing title and the most fun I've had in a singleplayer title since Bioshock Infinite! Well worth the $59.99 pricetag albeit I picked it up for $29.99 at the most recent Steam Sale.  - Happy Nazi-Stabbing

Five years after the crapfest that was Wolfenstein (2009), we finally have a new Wolfenstein.
Wolfenstein uses IDTech5, which is the same engine used in Rage. As you'd expect, the world is designed in a very similar fashion, putting lots of little details all over the place. I think visually the game looks pretty great, even better than Rage. The level design, both in layout and visual style is top-notch.... easily the best part of the game. There are often multiple ways to enter a room, usually through vents or a side hallway, that add a bit of extra strategy; it feels really open because of this. My only gripe would be that there are a hell of a lot of vents you travel through... that you're FORCED to travel through. It's supposed to make you feel stealthy I guess, but constantly having to crouch walk through them is slow and boring. There's a huge amount of variety in the game, everything looks great, and nothing seemed repetitive.
The texture quality isn't that great despite taking up over 40GB of HD space. When you get close to textures, they're too blurry for a modern AAA game. Small text on posters, newspaper clippings, etc can't really be read. Everything still looks really good from a medium distance, though. Water effects are absolute garbage, especially considering some sections utilize water for the gameplay.
The engine seems a bit more optimized than it was in Rage, but some of the same problems still exist... I still get major pop-in when looking around, even if I look at an object, turn away, then look back at it. It's really distracting, and can be lessened via tweaks but that shouldn't be necessary.
Gameplay-wise Wolfenstein is in a weird spot, I think. The weapons look awesome and are pretty fun, but the actual combat leaves a lot to be desired. Despite the weapon designs being cool, the upgrades you can acquire for them, and the ability to dual-wield the majority of them, the game still tends to focus on one energy weapon later in the game. It's almost pointless to use any other weapon, kind of like Half-Life 2 with the gravity gun. There's just so much focus on it getting so many fancy upgrades, always having somewhere to recharge it, and the fact that it's so strong. Other weapons are still useful, I just didn't want to use them as much because they were less effective. Aiming also feels floaty, and enemies are pretty much bullet sponges; especially the later enemies. Looking down the sights of a gun doesn't feel like it allows me to aim any better except for when you get a scope on a couple of the weapons.
The cut-scenes in the game are really well done and feel epic, but then you get back to gameplay and it's so lackluster that it creates a disconnect. The AI is particularly bad. In early sections of the game I'd stealth around and try to take people out one at a time. Whenever I got noticed all the enemies would group up and spam infinite grenades and shoot me whenever I try to pop out of cover. I would tend to come out ahead when I'd just run at a group of enemies with my guns a-blazing... it just makes no sense. Later in the game you can't just run out in the open... you have to generally single out enemies one at a time. The peek system is just cumbersome to use and shouldn't exist in the first place, or should be more automatic (such as you peek over cover when going to aim.)
The other big problem with gameplay feeling so lackluster is the stealth. The stealth implementation is fake and lame... enemies have specific patrol patterns and they tend to end up stopping at the end of their path while facing a wall, so you can sneak up and stab them. They're looking at a wall so they have no chance of setting you. Absolutely no skill, and no real chance to fail. You perform a takedown by pressing a button and it instakills them. There's no real point to having it in the game other to conserve your ammo for the bullet-sponges. The death animations are cool, however.
Control-wise it could be better. Playing with a X360 controller has some glaring issues. To throw a grenade you tap Right-Bumper. To switch weapons you have to hold it down. It ends up feeling cumbersome, and I wasted a ton of grenades and throwing knives because of this system. Strafing was also an issue as you push in the left stick while running forward. If the stick isn't perfectly pushed forward, the strafing stops. A lot of times I'd run from cover to cover and the strafing would screw up or fidget on/off repeatedly and get me killed.
The first half of the game was well paced and I just wanted to keep seeing more. Eventually it turns into a slaughter-fest and too much action ends up leading to fatigue. The enemy variety doesn't really change throughout the game that much, and that just adds to it. The "challenging" portions of the game generally revolves around just having to fight more of the bigger dudes.
There's a ton of other stuff that I haven't even mentioned, and a lot of specifics I didn't go into. Having said all that, this game was a pretty good experience. Really good story, great characters, excellent cinematics... There's always something cool happening while playing. The game seems to be polished well, and I never had any real issues that affected my play. I got about 10 hours out of the game, and recommend getting it when it goes on sale.
tl;dr: A really good game that could have been excellent if they spent more time on the combat and AI, which are the weakest parts of the game. Still, a huge improvement over the previous installment of Wolfenstein.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a easily one of the best FPSes of the year.
The shooting itself is so satisfying that it easily stays fresh for at least two playthroughs. Add some nice level design, multitude of weapons, a lot of gore and a lengthy campaign, and you have an awesome game that is very easy to recommend for fans of the genre.
A good comparison to make here is with the new Shadow Warrior: it takes the gameplay to new directions while it does not forget it roots. For this reason, I wouldn't call the New Order an old-school FPS but thankfully, it is FAR away from the typical, dumbed-down modern shooter.
I have only three gripes with the game:
- I hope it won't come in a DLC or something but when you establish a really twisted boss throughout the game (and I'm not talking about Totenkopf), it is downright painful to see that character (though not unscratched) get away .
- While the levels are varied enough, there were some opportunities that the developers missed out on especially if we look at how over-the-top the game is. For example, if you put us on the Moon, have some nice fights on the surface with low gravity or something! (Instead of just shooting down three drones over the course of 2 minutes...)
- The game presents two timelines that are essentially two playthroughs, however the differences are just too small to bother. Sure, it is worth is because of the gunplay, but it would have been nice if at least some of the scenes are different. (Apart from meeting another side-character and getting another type of collectible, it is pretty much the same. Wyatt and Fergus even say some of the same lines, like how both are mad at you for making the wrong choice.)
But these are just very small concerns for an otherwise fantastic game.
While I am a bit hesitant recommending it at €50, I got it during the Steam Sale for half its price, and I must say it was very, very worth it.
P.S.: I can't stress enough how satisfying the shooting is. Seriously, dual-wielding shotguns (one that shoots the regular pellets, the other shooting ricocheting pellets) and mowing down a bunch of enemies is majestic.

Wolfenstein: The New Order
I'll cut through the chase and say that it is a very good game. For its type, I would say it easily rates a strong 5/6 rating, where six out of six are Half-Life(1-2) and Modern Warfare(1)
Strengths:
+ The gameplay rewards exploration in an organic, almost old school manner.
+ Controls for weapons and movement are tight and very responsive.
+ You get to kill nazis, by the dousins.
Weaknesses:
- Graphics
- Internal consistency
This is where it gets interesting. In my mind there are really two flaws that prevent top score. And while it may seem odd and out of character coming from me, my first comments concern graphics, the second comprises the authenticity, or internal consistency, of the story being told.
Graphics. While the character models, and indeed motivations, are wonderfully rendered-- panoramic views, or really any of the wide-angle shots, leave much to be desired. Particularly when compared to other idtech games like Rage and Quake4, which have both delivered jawdropping panoramic visuals.
From personal preference, I would say that the aesthetic design of the Nazi warmachinery, ranging from combat drones to larger war machinery, also leaves me cold and uninspired. This may be a leftover homage from the previous games of the series, neither of which I am particularly familiar with, but from a personal point of view, the concept art could be much streamlined-- which leads us to my other concern.
Internal consistency. It may seem odd to criticize the internal consistency of an over-the-top action shooter, but my point is not that the game fails to  replicate Arma, it is that the game plays sloppily with the 'setting realism,' and therefore authenticity of story it presents. Certain plot elements seem improvised, the plot characters response to wounds are inconsistent, and the handling of plot elements (read high-tech military vehicles/weapons) seems ad-hoc and poorly thought out.
Contrast this to the games that earn top score. Modern Warfare, while hardly a realism game, applies its concepts consistently. Half-Life, presents a set of concepts, AND STICKS WITH THEM. In essence, these game feel authentic, even if they are not realistic, in a pedantic sense of the word. Now vehicles moving at 'the speed of plot,' are hardly new to the genre, I just prefer consistency to wishy-washy-handwaveium.
Conclusion:
Neither of my points of criticism are dealbreakers. Wolfenstein: The New Order, is a good game in all the ways that matter.  Its a good game, but not a great one. MachineGames is a studio to be watched in the future.
