Five years after the crapfest that was Wolfenstein (2009), we finally have a new Wolfenstein.
Wolfenstein uses IDTech5, which is the same engine used in Rage. As you'd expect, the world is designed in a very similar fashion, putting lots of little details all over the place. I think visually the game looks pretty great, even better than Rage. The level design, both in layout and visual style is top-notch.... easily the best part of the game. There are often multiple ways to enter a room, usually through vents or a side hallway, that add a bit of extra strategy; it feels really open because of this. My only gripe would be that there are a hell of a lot of vents you travel through... that you're FORCED to travel through. It's supposed to make you feel stealthy I guess, but constantly having to crouch walk through them is slow and boring. There's a huge amount of variety in the game, everything looks great, and nothing seemed repetitive.
The texture quality isn't that great despite taking up over 40GB of HD space. When you get close to textures, they're too blurry for a modern AAA game. Small text on posters, newspaper clippings, etc can't really be read. Everything still looks really good from a medium distance, though. Water effects are absolute garbage, especially considering some sections utilize water for the gameplay.
The engine seems a bit more optimized than it was in Rage, but some of the same problems still exist... I still get major pop-in when looking around, even if I look at an object, turn away, then look back at it. It's really distracting, and can be lessened via tweaks but that shouldn't be necessary.
Gameplay-wise Wolfenstein is in a weird spot, I think. The weapons look awesome and are pretty fun, but the actual combat leaves a lot to be desired. Despite the weapon designs being cool, the upgrades you can acquire for them, and the ability to dual-wield the majority of them, the game still tends to focus on one energy weapon later in the game. It's almost pointless to use any other weapon, kind of like Half-Life 2 with the gravity gun. There's just so much focus on it getting so many fancy upgrades, always having somewhere to recharge it, and the fact that it's so strong. Other weapons are still useful, I just didn't want to use them as much because they were less effective. Aiming also feels floaty, and enemies are pretty much bullet sponges; especially the later enemies. Looking down the sights of a gun doesn't feel like it allows me to aim any better except for when you get a scope on a couple of the weapons.
The cut-scenes in the game are really well done and feel epic, but then you get back to gameplay and it's so lackluster that it creates a disconnect. The AI is particularly bad. In early sections of the game I'd stealth around and try to take people out one at a time. Whenever I got noticed all the enemies would group up and spam infinite grenades and shoot me whenever I try to pop out of cover. I would tend to come out ahead when I'd just run at a group of enemies with my guns a-blazing... it just makes no sense. Later in the game you can't just run out in the open... you have to generally single out enemies one at a time. The peek system is just cumbersome to use and shouldn't exist in the first place, or should be more automatic (such as you peek over cover when going to aim.)
The other big problem with gameplay feeling so lackluster is the stealth. The stealth implementation is fake and lame... enemies have specific patrol patterns and they tend to end up stopping at the end of their path while facing a wall, so you can sneak up and stab them. They're looking at a wall so they have no chance of setting you. Absolutely no skill, and no real chance to fail. You perform a takedown by pressing a button and it instakills them. There's no real point to having it in the game other to conserve your ammo for the bullet-sponges. The death animations are cool, however.
Control-wise it could be better. Playing with a X360 controller has some glaring issues. To throw a grenade you tap Right-Bumper. To switch weapons you have to hold it down. It ends up feeling cumbersome, and I wasted a ton of grenades and throwing knives because of this system. Strafing was also an issue as you push in the left stick while running forward. If the stick isn't perfectly pushed forward, the strafing stops. A lot of times I'd run from cover to cover and the strafing would screw up or fidget on/off repeatedly and get me killed.
The first half of the game was well paced and I just wanted to keep seeing more. Eventually it turns into a slaughter-fest and too much action ends up leading to fatigue. The enemy variety doesn't really change throughout the game that much, and that just adds to it. The "challenging" portions of the game generally revolves around just having to fight more of the bigger dudes.
There's a ton of other stuff that I haven't even mentioned, and a lot of specifics I didn't go into. Having said all that, this game was a pretty good experience. Really good story, great characters, excellent cinematics... There's always something cool happening while playing. The game seems to be polished well, and I never had any real issues that affected my play. I got about 10 hours out of the game, and recommend getting it when it goes on sale.
tl;dr: A really good game that could have been excellent if they spent more time on the combat and AI, which are the weakest parts of the game. Still, a huge improvement over the previous installment of Wolfenstein.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a easily one of the best FPSes of the year.
The shooting itself is so satisfying that it easily stays fresh for at least two playthroughs. Add some nice level design, multitude of weapons, a lot of gore and a lengthy campaign, and you have an awesome game that is very easy to recommend for fans of the genre.
A good comparison to make here is with the new Shadow Warrior: it takes the gameplay to new directions while it does not forget it roots. For this reason, I wouldn't call the New Order an old-school FPS but thankfully, it is FAR away from the typical, dumbed-down modern shooter.
I have only three gripes with the game:
- I hope it won't come in a DLC or something but when you establish a really twisted boss throughout the game (and I'm not talking about Totenkopf), it is downright painful to see that character (though not unscratched) get away .
- While the levels are varied enough, there were some opportunities that the developers missed out on especially if we look at how over-the-top the game is. For example, if you put us on the Moon, have some nice fights on the surface with low gravity or something! (Instead of just shooting down three drones over the course of 2 minutes...)
- The game presents two timelines that are essentially two playthroughs, however the differences are just too small to bother. Sure, it is worth is because of the gunplay, but it would have been nice if at least some of the scenes are different. (Apart from meeting another side-character and getting another type of collectible, it is pretty much the same. Wyatt and Fergus even say some of the same lines, like how both are mad at you for making the wrong choice.)
But these are just very small concerns for an otherwise fantastic game.
While I am a bit hesitant recommending it at €50, I got it during the Steam Sale for half its price, and I must say it was very, very worth it.
P.S.: I can't stress enough how satisfying the shooting is. Seriously, dual-wielding shotguns (one that shoots the regular pellets, the other shooting ricocheting pellets) and mowing down a bunch of enemies is majestic.

Wolfenstein: The New Order
I'll cut through the chase and say that it is a very good game. For its type, I would say it easily rates a strong 5/6 rating, where six out of six are Half-Life(1-2) and Modern Warfare(1)
Strengths:
+ The gameplay rewards exploration in an organic, almost old school manner.
+ Controls for weapons and movement are tight and very responsive.
+ You get to kill nazis, by the dousins.
Weaknesses:
- Graphics
- Internal consistency
This is where it gets interesting. In my mind there are really two flaws that prevent top score. And while it may seem odd and out of character coming from me, my first comments concern graphics, the second comprises the authenticity, or internal consistency, of the story being told.
Graphics. While the character models, and indeed motivations, are wonderfully rendered-- panoramic views, or really any of the wide-angle shots, leave much to be desired. Particularly when compared to other idtech games like Rage and Quake4, which have both delivered jawdropping panoramic visuals.
From personal preference, I would say that the aesthetic design of the Nazi warmachinery, ranging from combat drones to larger war machinery, also leaves me cold and uninspired. This may be a leftover homage from the previous games of the series, neither of which I am particularly familiar with, but from a personal point of view, the concept art could be much streamlined-- which leads us to my other concern.
Internal consistency. It may seem odd to criticize the internal consistency of an over-the-top action shooter, but my point is not that the game fails to  replicate Arma, it is that the game plays sloppily with the 'setting realism,' and therefore authenticity of story it presents. Certain plot elements seem improvised, the plot characters response to wounds are inconsistent, and the handling of plot elements (read high-tech military vehicles/weapons) seems ad-hoc and poorly thought out.
Contrast this to the games that earn top score. Modern Warfare, while hardly a realism game, applies its concepts consistently. Half-Life, presents a set of concepts, AND STICKS WITH THEM. In essence, these game feel authentic, even if they are not realistic, in a pedantic sense of the word. Now vehicles moving at 'the speed of plot,' are hardly new to the genre, I just prefer consistency to wishy-washy-handwaveium.
Conclusion:
Neither of my points of criticism are dealbreakers. Wolfenstein: The New Order, is a good game in all the ways that matter.  Its a good game, but not a great one. MachineGames is a studio to be watched in the future.

Let me preface this by saying that this is not a good game. You need a high-end gaming PC to even run it, the hit detection is sketchy at best, the learning curve is astronomical, and the unlock system is abysmal.
Having said that, let me put forward why I'm still reccomending this game. Of all the first-person shooters I've played, this is the first to make me feel like an actual soldier.
Here's the average experience that someone new to Planetside will... experience.
You'll start by choosing a faction, based on color, uniform, core philosophy, consulting goat entrails, or what have you. You'll speed through character customization, which is token at best, but since your face is covered by a helmet 90% of the time,it doesn't really matter. After a short tutorial, which will tell you that bullets go away from you, bad guys come towards you, and the idea is to make the two intersect, you'll be given the option to be dropped into whatever battle happens to be going on at the time.
At which point you'll get airdropped in, take a moment to get your bearings, and die.
Typically, the first emotion you'll feel is confusion. "Did I really just die?" You'll ask yourself, "But that's not possible, I couldn't possibly die that easily, I've got a shield!"
You'll respawn, certain that some cheeky sniper just got off a lucky headshot, and, this time, knowing what you're heading into, you'll dash immediately for cover.
At which point you'll die again.
Now, you're getting angry. "Is this all the game is?" You'll ask. "Spawning, dying, and spawning again? What's the point of it all?!"
Here's the point where most people quit. Here's the point where all the little niggles that are the game's technical aspects finally get to them, and they stop playing. But some people, like me, will stay, despite all the game's flaws.
I can't speak for them, but I stayed because this game provides a war experience unlike any other.
You aren't some almighty space marine, gunning down legions of enemies with an assault rifle in your left hand and a supermodel in your right.
You're just another footsolder. Cannon fodder. Expendable.
And once you realize that, the game starts to really shine.
It may not have been intended that way, but that's what it's become.
And I like it.
TL:DR: It's a crap game, but I had fun with it. Check it out maybe.

This game is great, however, the ending seemed rushed, compared to the rest of the game. Other than the unfulfilled feeling you get when there is a gaping hole in the story, the gameplay and story was decent. It makes sense to have the hole in the ending though, since they said they were going to make a sequel. As for gameplay, the stealth mechanic is really broken, but great, due to the fact that you can play on the hardest setting and just headshot people with a silenced pistol right in front of other enemies, and nobody notices. Otherwise, you have to go guns blazing in, and usually end up worse for wear. The armour and health system in the game is nice as well, resulting in armour and health placed at the right times in the map to be picked up. The damage system was well written, damaging you and your armour at the same time, and as your armour wears down, you take more damage. The Perks in the game are nice, where they don't give you an unfair advantage, but make the game easier and more enjoyable to play, resulting in far less grindy gameplay. I can't really say much about the actual story without spoiling it, but the beginning seemed well written and thought out, while the end seemed to be rushed together.

If you are a fan of the Max Payne franchise, do not but this game.  Everything about it just feels off, from the combat to the story.  Rockstar chose to drop the old comic book and noir story telling in favour of a more cinematic approach, and in doing so took away much of the charm that made Max Payne what it was.  On the topic of combat, the game tries to automate many features (like painkillers and save points) rather than letting that player regulate these things by themselves (yes there is a mode which does not auto-utilise painkillers, but it should not require that the combat be at an incredibly difficult level as well).  Furthermore, the level design emphasises a basic cover-bases system (insert generic 3rd person shooter here) rather than fully utilising the bullet-time elements the series has become famous for.  Overall, as a fan of the series, I was quite disappointed with this entry but have hopes that a good developer like Rockstar can raise the bar for the next instalment.
On an unrelated note, I did experience a number of technical bugs in my play through with an Nvidia 500 series card.
Took me less than 19 hours to clear the game on uber difficulty (which wasnt very challenging.) I was really pleased otherwise.

Planetside 2, is a solid choice for your FPS pleasures.
Skirmishes can be from a lowly 1v1, to well over 200+ versus.
While the combat seems generic at times, the massive size of maps and bases add room for the thinking person to make a difference with superior logistical and tactical decisions.
Teamwork is unstoppable here.
Everything save some cosmetics and other non gameplay items can be unlocked with the almighty grind, time or money.
The biggest negative is that when starting out the amount of information to assimilate can be overwhelming to even the most seasoned FPS player,  the tutorial is fine, and does a great job of explaining combat, bases, vehicles, and getting around, however it quickly becomes insufficient once you get out into the game world.
If you are new to Planetside 2, and want to give it a go, I recommend quickly finding yourself a friend or a small group who is willing to show you the ropes, stay away from large groups and platoons as you will be thrown into a sink or swim situation and will be easily overwhelmed by the speed at which things can happen.
Considering the price, one should not avoid this game, also if you are a FPS addict, you owe it to yourself to experience a 200 versus battle with infantry, ground and air vehicles, at least once.

The game, while fun and at times challenging has probably the worst match making system in gaming history. Till about level 6 you have servers/rooms with a level cieling. An arguement can be made about learning and improving one's skill but this is a moot point when the enemy can snipe (1 shot) you for merely moving. On the plus side, the game does offer some unique characters, each with something a little different to choose from. Sadly the weapon choice are limited to the Loadout cards, the only time this does not apply is when you have a weapon crate which allows you to craft a card with your weapon of choice. To start: I used to add a header at the top of these reviews describing my rating ethos, but it made the reviews too long to submit on more than one occasion, so I left it on my Backloggery page.
Gameplay: Well, it's better than that godawful reboot a few years back; that's for sure. This game has been described as a fusion of old and new, and that's not a half bad description. It has regenerating health (to an extent; it regenerates to the nearest increment of 20), but it doesn't hold your hand much. There's quite the variety of weapons that you can use, but cover-based fighting is still often the way to go. It presents a challenge along the lines of the classic Wolfenstein 3D, but it still remains fair and hardly ever makes use of cheap enemies or traps. The game has faith in your abilities as a gamer, and to be honest, that's all I've wanted to see out of newer games. We can do challenging things in video games; it's the designer's job to make us want to do them.
One of the things that I've read people complaining about is the mandatory stealth sections. It's almost a breath of fresh air to be complaining about stealth sections. Hell, I remember when the big complaint from mainstream gaming was too many WWII games. To be honest, though; I didn't mind the stealth sections so much; even if the AI isn't always the greatest on those stages. You don't have to be perfect, though; there's always an out if you mess up. That's part of why I didn't mind these stages so much. Being forced to do stealth perfectly is annoying. You can mess up here; you just gotta be quick with the takedowns so that nobody is alerted.
Apart from some derpiness with the AI during stealth sections, the AI during combat is quite good. Heavies will run toward you because they can take your fire; Commanders hang back so that they can call in reinforcements; Grunts seem to have pretty good group dynamics. It's not gonna blow you away, but they do at least present a semblance of knowing what they're doing. Bosses are actually bosses, as opposed to the stronger than normal enemy that passes for a boss fight nowadays, and they're certainly the highlights of this game, even if they are few and far between. The final boss is definitely the best of the bunch - as it should be - despite the relative lack of any cover whatsoever.
All in all, this is definitely a solid FPS that won't disappoint. It's not Game of the Year material or anything, but I'm not sorry I bought it, especially considering the price I got it for from the Steam Summer Sale. 8/10.
Story: Surprisingly well directed. There's some very cool cinematography stuff in there that film students will surely appreciate. The writing isn't half bad, either. Admittedly, it does kinda jump the shark a little bit toward the end, but it's not too big of a deal. Plus, it can be rather easily justified by the fact that the Nazis have ruled the world. All of the characters have a surprising amount of believability to them, and it's all generally quite good. One thing that was disappointing, however, is the lack of any real resolution. It's not one of those cases where it's all about the character's journey, either. It just kinda... ends. There's no post-credits scene, either. Disappointing, considering how the rest of the story and writing were. 8/10.
Graphics: This is the part where I talk about why the game is so fezzing big! It turns out that this game uses something called Megatextures, or very large textures that are streamed from the storage device for the game to memory. This helps with performance, as there aren't just a bunch of textures laying around unseen in memory; as well, it makes the game generally look better, as higher resolution textures can be applied to their respective polygons. It's not a case like Titanfall where there's just uncompressed data; quite the opposite. These textures really are that HUEG. So, now's the time for the question: is it worth it? To be honest with you, I think it is. It really does lend a higher degree of realism to the environments. Admittedly, we're not supposed to be looking at the textures all the time, but it really does help each area look just that little bit better.
Now, regarding performance. This game is optimized quite well; at least for NVIDIA cards (I can't say for ATI cards since I don't own one). You don't need an i7. I'm pretty dang sure this game doesn't use hyperthreading. Nevertheless, the game ran at a very consistant 60FPS at max settings, 1080p resolution on my GTX 760, reaching a peak temp of about 70degC. Antialiasing isn't available on the menu, oddly enough; you've gotta turn it on through the console. It's easy enough to do, though. I was able to stay at 60FPS at 8X MSAA, but bringing it up to 16x was a bit much. The art style is fantastic, as well. The architecture has a really grandiose feeling to it, fitting in with the Nazi motif. Enemy designs are certainly unique, and the boss designs are just plain cool. For a game that looks as great as this game does to be running so well on a $260 graphics card that's a year or so old, that's fantastic. 5/5.
Sound: A bit of a head-scratcher, this category. What music is there is quite good and all. However, there's a lot of places where music would really help out a lot. Boss fights don't have any music. Even the giant robot boss that a Strider from HL2 would cower in fear at had no music. I really don't get why there's so little music here. The voice acting is pretty good, though. Blaskowitz has the outward appearance vocally of a tough guy, but there's also an air of exhaustion and just wanting to be out of the hell he's been in for the past 14 years. All of the baddies are just evil enough to make you wanna beat their faces in, but not so evil that you just end up laughing at them. For pretty good presentation on the audio front, with a disappointing lack of music in general, especially for the boss fights, I'll give this game a 4/5 for the audio.
Overall scores are: 8/8/5/4; cumulative score of 8.3/10. It's a really solid FPS that I certainly won't mind playing again in the future on higher difficulties. It's brought some glory back to the Wolfenstein series at least.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a fantastic action game. Not only because you can go every bit as crazy as in previous installments, if not even more, but because it reaches beyond the conventional boundaries.
The narrative and especially the characters have been given a lot more attention. While it is perhaps not as moving as games like The Walking Dead, it certainly shines as being a lot more faceted and polished than most other high-octane shooters.
The environments are varied and levels layered, offering depth and tactic. There's even a branch in the storyline as early as the end of the first mission. This means that some characters you will encounter and places you can go in levels change. It doesn't affect the gameplay dramatically, but it makes for at least some variation, warranting another playthrough.
If you're looking to dual-wield shotguns in a game world that's not just decorative but also brings an interesting take on an alternate history, you've come to the right place. This is an action game developed with passion and I can't wait for what MachineGames makes next.

This is a 12-hour long cutscene with occasional third-person shooter segments and grind-fest multiplayer. It has almost none of what made the first two Max Payne games so great: the phenomenal storytelling, gripping plots, noir styling. The one thing it *does* have that the original two did is solid third-person shooter gameplay with cool bullet time mechanics. Only problem is that out of the 12 hours the story goes, maybe 45 minutes to an hour and a half of it is actual gameplay. The style in this game isn't noir. It's like the movie "Man on Fire," which on its own is actually a really good movie, but here it comes across as a bad crossover fanfiction. Replacing the noir style with Hollywood action/thriller was a terrible idea. It constantly feels like the game's trying to trigger epileptic episodes by having bright colors and distortions as well as random text from the dialogue (much of which is completely pointless to emphasize so why they bother with it is beyond me) flash all over the screen. The plot itself is rather stupid and has basically nothing to do with Max Payne; frankly they should've just made the protagonist someone else. Ultimately it insults me as a Max Payne fan that they didn't care at all about what made Max Payne 1 & 2 so special, and even outright spit in my face with segments like the graveyard sequence. It also insults me as a reasonably intelligent person because the plot is so incredibly thin and predictable, yet the game keeps acting like it's some masterful example of the art form. When there actually *is* gameplay, it's pretty decent, though you'll find the camera often spazzes out due to the cover in the environment, causing you to die because you can't get an angle on anything (which is especially annoying during the "last stand" thing the game does). Multiplayer's tolerable once you get to rank 4 and can create your own classes, but it's punishingly unfair to new players and there's barely anyone playing it so I advise not even bothering.
In summary, a badly-presented 12-hour cutscene with occasional third-person shooter segments that are decent, multiplayer that's a total grindfest and is completely unfair to new players, and a litany of technical issues. It's insulting to me as a gamer, as a Max Payne fan, and as a person with even reasonable intelligence. Don't bother.

I really enjoyed the story in this game. The alternative history is well explained for what the game needs it to be.  If you're looking for a more detailed timeline, pay attention to the various newspaper clippings and concept art.  Anything more, and you're probably asking for a proper novel.
Controls are tight and the quality is definitely AAA.  I'm not a stickler for graphic fidelity, but it looked good enough for me.  Facial expressions on the primary characters were definitely a plus and made the experience more immersive.  The weapons were pretty standard fare.  Nothing really exciting on the boom boom, bang bang front.
The game does have its faults, though.  The alternative storylines aren't really alternative.  You're going to play the same game, regardless of the supporting character you wish to save.  The changes are so minor, I'm not even sure it was worth it to go through and play again.  It's worth exactly ONE replay in that regard.
The Steam achievements are stupid easy to get. I don't feel like they are real achievements.  You're rewarded more for just shooting Nazis than doing something "interesting". My decision not to 100% the achievements likely came from burnout on the game.
Also, I can't help but get annoyed at the random 2-spawned NPCs to keep the action "going".  Clearing a hall of Assault Rifle Nazis ends up feeling like fillers in an otherwise rich environment.  Failure to clear set pieces will cause an endless wave of magically appearing enemies that get free headshots.  Often times, I would suddenly find that I'm low on health because a once clear hallway now has 2 guys getting free, cheap shots on me.
It was worth the $30 I paid for it during the Summer Sale.  Heck, $40 isn't a bad price either.  It definitely deserves some DLC as the ending leaves room for more gameplay.  And although the story is somewhat fulfilling, I wouldn't mind more large set-piece boss battles like the London Monitor fight.

Max Payne 3 is a very enjoyable 3rd person shooter. The game mechanics are good as the game returns with it's core bullet-time mechanic and adds a modern snap-to-cover mechanic. The art style is enjoyable with the game leaving the New Jersey / New York area for sunny Brazil and it gives the developers a chance to show plenty of daytime areas. It borrows a lot of visual style from Tony Scott's 2004 Man on Fire film but luckily that's toned down during the last 3rd of the game. The story is great. It's pure noir with double-crosses, plenty of bad guys, and a protagonist that is flawed and broken. James McCaffrey might not be the original voice actor for Max Payne but he gives the right performance as I constantly enjoyed his dark humor. The story isn't realistic, obviously, but it's different than Max Payne 1 or 2 as there is no longer any reference to the Valkyr drug that was so prominent in the first game. There are very few callbacks to the earlier games.
As for problems, I had no technical problems running the game. It does require Rockstar Social Club activation in order to run it so that was disappointing. There were also a couple of levels where despite it being a linear shooter, I had difficulties finding the the route in the environment to the next area. I wished there had been a better indicator where to go.
Definitely worth a play especially since it is often deeply discounted during Steam sales. Max Payne was a transformational 3rd person shooter during the early 2000's and its great to see it still getting quality sequels.

For a shooter and the fact that this game has been taken by Rockstar, Max Payne 3 is a vast improvement when compared to Max Payne (let's say MP) 1 and 2. This game is definitely enjoyable, the shooting cinematics are amazing and very fun to watch, as well as your ability to control certain elements (whether you keep shooting during cinematic, whether it goes into slow mothion, etc.) On top of this, the best aspect about this game is the utilisation of the Euphoria engine. This engine allows "ragdolls" to react much better to its nearby environment as well as impacts, giving AI a very life-like reaction to being shot in certain places, falling off ledges, grabbing nearby items etc. Some of Euphoria also works on Max Payne and you'll notice this when you shoot-dodge into a wall. The game however, is very linear, like previous titles and whilst it improves a lot when compared to its previous titles, I find it hard to look at the cutscenes over and over when playing through the game again on a higher difficulty. The option to skip a cutscene does present itself, but not before a good 1-2 minutes of the scenes actually playing out, leaving you with a bit of agony before you get into the real juicy action. Also, this game features frontal nudity of topless women. Yay!
The story itself is believable and the way it is presented gives you a sense of the cunning behind the writers of the game. Usually games develop your main character as you progress, and then gives you a bit of "You killed this person, and now I'm here for revenge!" type deals. However, Max Payne adopts the flashback method of viewing your history between characters. So now, it's "...I'm here for revenge!" *Flashback* And you play out the scenario that occur, as opposed to watching a five minute cinematic. The story... It's debatable whether it's actually good or not. It might appeal to some, and not appeal to others. In short, it's a very straight forward; protect this family, find this person, save that person. But there's a very nice twist to the overall story arc, and you find yourself not only biting off more than you could chew (well, it seemed that way) but rather you solved more problems than you had originally planned to solve. How's that for a spoiler free summary of the game? Also, the game handles story telling through length cutscenes and that sort of kills its replay value.
Combat in this game is truly fun. Rockstar promised to deliver a very reactive and precise shooting game, and they have delivered. The only quirk I can complain about is the strangely odd difficulty on Normal, where you actually do die if you don't prepare yourself a bit; and the fact that this game is a console port so some of the default control schemes are a bit odd. Sprinting also... doesn't seem like sprinting... In single player you never see grenades (that you use) and the camera angles can be a bit awkward at times (Pressing H swaps from left to right shoulder, something that happens by itself depending on what side of cover you're shooting from and how you've just stood up after a shoot-dodge).  The game also adopts the, "bullets come out from your crosshair" mechanic as opposed to the "bullet comes out from your character model's weapon" which serves to work better for accuracy (as opposed to say, Fallout 3) but can be exploited for shooting around corners without exposing yourself (which is something I assume occurs frequently in Multiplayer, as it's the same mechanic as the popular game, APB Reloaded).
The multiplayer aspect of this game was pretty hyped, and it seemed like a really cool concept sort of thing, though unfortunately in Australia, there's barely anyone playing the game online and it's just a dead community over all. It might be fun to grab a few friends and have a shoot out, but there's something sweeter about versing complete strangers over the internet.
Collectibles in this game are done properly; they actually are hidden and requires a little bit more effort to look around and find. Pressing ESC allows you to view the amount of collectibles left in a certain part of the game, which serves as a nice little check-list for achievement hunters out there. Some of them also add to the overall story and they aren't tedious to read through, as Max narrates the entire thing for you so you can continue on your journey whilst listening to his relatively entrancing voice. The only problem is when two dialogues cut eachother out (ie. activating a collectible whilst Max is speaking a story-related line.)
Overall, I enjoyed this game and it's worth its value in singleplayer. Two playthroughs may be enough, any more and you'll start to feel the tediousness of watching each cutscene play out over and over.

Quite simply one of the most enjoyable FPS I've played.
Pros:
* Solid gunplay that succesfully mixes both old school fps design and newer fps.
Prefer to hug cover and pepper the enemies from afar? You can do that, but beware cover erodes and you aren't invulnerable behind your chest high walls.
Prefer the stealthy approach, knifing enemies from behind or taking them out with a well aimed suppressed pistol? That works too.
Or do you want to go in guns blazing, laughing as you mow down your enemies while dual wielding automatic shotguns, turning nazi stormtroopers into a cloud of red and exploding guts? You can do that too.
* Great level design. Many modern FPS suffer from really linear level designs with little room for changes in tactics or flanking. Although the game is linear it isn't a corridor shooter like many other modern fps. Replaying old sections are still enjoyable and I find no matter how many times I die on the same section I never get mad at the game.
It is simply a joy to play.
Add to that all of the awesome Nazi architecture. It might not be a place you'd want to live but the monolithic architecture make for good setpieces.
* Good pacing between frenetic action and more atmospheric sections.
* Fun and varied enemies that require changes in tactics and different approaches.
* Well written story that somehow manages to mesh both the wackier fantastic science nazis with the real horrors of nazi doctrine without cheapening either. In a way it reminds me of how Quentin Tarantino mixes both horror and dark comedy.
It doesn't merely lazily throw nazis and tell you 'these are bad because nazis.'
The game actually shows their poisonous ideology for what it is.
Characters are well written and surprisingly the game actually manages to make you care about them.
*Nazi moonbase
Cons:
* Sometimes levels get overly grey.
It is duly compensated for by good level design and locations. Besides this is the third reich we are talking about, they aren't known for their love of colors and diversity.
* Uses checkpoints, no manual saves. An irritation with modern shooters, checkpoints are usually plentiful enough though and I never found myself in an unwinnable battle.
* That one underwater level. Although atmospheric replaying it wasn't very satisfying.
Why are underwater levels always a bore?
* Cheap explanation for the whole nazi superscience. Probably the only weakpoint of the games writing. It isn't enough to ruin the experience though or overly effect it.
All in all none of this is enough to ruin my enjoyment of the game.
tl;dr:
This is some of the most fun I've had with a shooter in ages.
That it reminds me of Half Life 2 is definitely not a bad thing!

The first thing worth mentioning about Max Payne 3 is the amount of detail in the environments. I say this because so many have complained about the graphics in Max Payne 3. Yet every single location you play through looks so believable, no environment looks vacant of life or detail. Just as impressive is how varied these environments are. You will play through apartment buildings, a cemetery, a prison, and so on. Sure these kinds of environments are almost common place in most action games, but in Max Payne 3 they have a level of detail that is so impressive you can't help but appreciate them more.
Gameplay wise, Max Payne 3 does not stray too far from the first two games in the series. As you take out enemies your bullet time meter fills up, once you have the amount you need you can trigger it to slow down time. Enemies, bullets, grenades, and other hazards are easier to avoid in bullet time, not to mention how impressive the feature still looks. Shoot dodge also returns, letting you dodge in any direction (left, right, forward, or backwards) in slow motion. This time around you do not even need to have any bullet time in your bullet time meter to use shoot dodge (although some will be consumed if you do use shoot dodge while having bullet time left).
Max Payne 3 really is a great action game and a great game period. It is not perfect, but the good aspects without question outweigh the bad ones. Whether or not your a fan of the first two installments in the series, Max Payne 3 is definitely worth playing.

Not just a 'dumb shooter' with ideas above its station at all. Most areas give the player freedom to mix stealth and shooting as they please, making both approaches meaningful and satisfying. All weapons are a joy to use and have a real sense of weight and significance. I loved Wolfenstein's lazer cutter and how it upgraded during the game to become a strong weapon as well as a useful tool. It's not dynamic in the sense that Half Life 2's gravity gun was, but there's plenty of times it's used to hide alternate routes and collectibles and it's always fun to use. Level design is great with alternate paths and well hidden secrets with some occasional mild environmental puzzle solving thrown in. I found every place the game dropped me into was rich and engaging; a joy to explore.
Yes, it's a linear adventure. It's not open world. But if it's a big corridor, then it's a wide one, that lets players experiment and breathe. It's not narrow and prescriptive like Call of Duty. None of this 'this is a stealth bit, here's a sniper rifle' rubbish: in Wolfenstein you get to decide when to be sneaky.
Graphically I was very impressed. Depth of field is used to good effect, and id Tech's mega texture technology (or whatever it's called) makes for visuals that don't look like copy-paste jobs, though it does mean a massive download size. Every new area feels unique. There's plenty of detail and I often found myself standing still to take in the view or just have a thorough look at everything. Music was also impressive, especially the rousing stuff toward the end - it really stirred me onward.
What I wasn't expecting, especially after reading some reviews, is the emotional impact of some scene and how the game made me think. Characters are likeable and developed. I cared about them. The writing was very good and I enjoyed downtime at the hideout, getting to know resistance members. Again, this is not a dumb shooter that's simply trying to be more. I found myself being reminded of Half Life 2 rather than, say, Serious Sam or Duke Nukem, which I'd expected having got that impression from some reviews. This is a solid campaign that tells a good story and takes you on a memorable journey that you'll be sad is over when the credits rolls (as they did for me 20 minutes ago).
As a side note, I'm not sure why some reviewers here have mentioned that the game is not suitable for kids because of gore and sexual content. The game is clearly rated 18. Enough said.
I applaud Machine Games for focussing on a high quality and lengthy single player game. Not sure why anyone here is moaning about the lack of multiplayer. Since when did every release have to have multiplayer and how many first person online multiplayer games do you need anyway? So glad you didn't spread yourselves thin and make two games that were half as good, and it's great that a dev has the bottle to make a good game rather than just tick the usual boxes.
Machine Games, if you're reading, please know that the people who actually buy games love this. Reviews may call it old school in a slightly derogatory way or say you can't have a sensitive story and a hero who can take a daft amount of bullets - I say otherwise. Gordon Freeman soaked up his fair amount of lead too and nobody thinks the story his second game told was less impactful and, at times, moving and thought-provoking.
There is a massive market for high quality, lengthy single player games like this, just as there was when Return to Castle Wolfenstein came out, just as there was when Half Life 2 came out etc. Not everything has to be another bloody online multiplayer or an open world or a survival zombie game. More like this please! I think - if you hadn't worked it out yet - Wolfenstein New Order is fantastic.

This was a tough call to make. I wanted to like Max Payne 3, but it just really did not want to be liked. The good news is, at the core, the gameplay is actually pretty good... when you get to play it, but more on that in a bit.  The combat is true to the John Woo style of the series.  The game is also considerably more difficult than Max Payne 2, but not as much as Max Payne 1, which is a happy medium.  It's a bit heavily cover-based, but you do have the shootdodge at your disposal to mix things up.
Unfortunately, you will spend the majority of your gaming hours locked in sequence after sequence of unskippable AND unquittable cutscenes which smugly display the text "still loading" when you try to skip them, despite the fact that it has clearly been 5 minutes or more. If you try to press escape, the cutscene will just pause.  Once the gameplay actually begins and you start to have fun, the instant the last guy is killed you are forced to watch a 30 second cutscene of Max opening a door or vaulting a ledge, or something else you could have easily done yourself.  It often doesn't even allow you time to search the room for guns, painkillers, or collectibles. When you do get the opportunity to scavenge the room after a battle, you cannot backtrack to the previous room (which is always inexplicably locked behind you) and you are CONSTANTLY nagged every five seconds to proceed forward, either by one of Max's allies or Max himself.  He'll say to himself, "I had no time to admire the scenery, I had to move forward," as if he's in a rush to finish his own story. I suppose he needs to make time for more compelling details in his storytelling such as "there was a security door across the hall" or some contextual remark on every bottle of pills that he finds.
The general flow of the game, as you may have guessed, between all the cutscenes is just shooting gallery after shooting gallery.  In many a cutscene you have the dubious privilege of watching Max bumble his way into a room, alerting the entire mob, and spoiling what would have been a perfectly good sneak attack.  And after the game spends most of its time yanking you forward against your will, in other chapters you will be forced to slowly walk or stagger drunk or wounded through the level for ten minutes, unable to actually do anything useful. It absolutely refuses to let you play at your own pace.
But that's just the story mode -- if you want to just shoot stuff in combat scenarios without all the talky talk then surely Arcade mode is where it's at... right?  Ehhh, no.  The only difference Arcade mode has is that it removes the *skippable* cutscenes from the game, which there weren't that many of to begin with. Wonderful. And it gives you a score at the end of the chapter, with none of the instant gratification the game so callously denies you.

Robocraft is slowly dying, just look at the steam charts. It is definatly not as popular as it used to be.  However it can be revived, and with this new news of the return of megabots and the community vote it can just as easily come back. I will always be a robocrafter as I have been for almost 3 years at this point. here is what I think about this game after 380 hours.
Pro's about Robocraft:
Lots of creativity, you can build with no limits except for your CPU
You can easily play with your friends
It isn't pay to win; now many people may disagree with this as you can pay to progress much faster with 2xp with premium or the crates you can buy however if you pay money you dont immeadiatly win it takes skill too.
great physics and use of mass and carry weight in the weapons.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cons about Robocraft:
No clear progression path; once the greats were introduced the game is solely based on chance of what you get out of the crates, A long time ago teirs in the game existed and you could see how to progress and build better bots, eventually leading up to the end game of building a megabot. sadly I was level 97 when megabots were removed on april 4th 2016.
With megabots dissapearing came tier flattening, and dissapearing of progression.
No longer a huge con, but RNG only; the only way to get cash was to rely on the luck of what you would randomly get out of your crates, now that Robits are in crates its a little better but you can still do amazin in a match and get garbage parts v.s. doing terrible and then getting lucky with an amazing part.
players are not like they used to be; In the old days of robocraft people didn't usually build bots for 100% practicality and efficiency they built average bots they though would be fun for a match or two then made a new one. I may not be speaking for everyone but this is just what I saw from my own experience. Nowdays though, people will build Smg drones or Ion pihranhas (forgive spelling)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Final Thoughts: Robocraft is a great game and these problems are rooted deep in the game and would require alot of it to be overhauled to make it better however this would cause so many more problems and the decision on how the game is to be made is ultimatly up to the devs because they made it. However it is also the communities game, and to say one thing I am very glad that these problems are obviously clear to the devs now. For example I said a con was the drones in the game. Mark Simons had tweeted that they want to make aerofoils so good that drone fliers become airplane fliers again. Also with the new custom game updates and the announcements of the different marks as well as the return of megabots. Freejam Clearly recognizes the issues, and wants them fixed, and hopefully the rest of the community sees what they are doing as a step in the right direction as well.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

***Just a quick note, while this game is longer than most Single Player games out there it is not as long as some are claiming it to be. I played through and finished Wolfenstein: The New Order on the 'I am Death Incarnate' difficulty in under 8 hours while trying my hardest to explore every nook and cranny. I also approached the game stealthily (In many circumstances this is impossible with enemies instantly knowing where you are as you walk into a room) which in some cases can get you through some sections of the game faster, but more times then not, takes longer.***
I personally loved Wolfenstein: The New Order from Start to Finish with only a few minor things taking away from the experience ever so slightly. Having played through the original games (Including the dreadful 2009 game) I came into this game not expecting much more than a Run and Gun Style Shooter. But I was blown away with the amount of Depth that they had put into a seemingly linear game. With newly added Cover system, Perks, Stealth and, of course, Dual-Wielding any two weapons in the game, Yes, even knives truly gives the Wolfenstein franchise a whole new flavour. The game also splits itself from the modern 'Copy and Paste' shooter we see to much of nowadays. This Wolfenstein brings back the days of the Original Doom and Wolfenstein by having no (well, slightly) regenerating health and the ability to pick up armour. But, as I progressed through the game I noticed a few small issues that can take away from the experience slightly. Having to constantly run from cover to cover only to get Destroyed by bouncing shotgun pellets that leap over and around cover and continously respawn with 20HP and no armour (Making me a one hit kill for just about every weapon in the game) does get extremely frustrating. Sure, you could blame this on my lack of skill or the High difficulty level but when you finally clear an area of enemies only to run around the next corner and be faced by 2-3 Heavily armoured Gatling/Bouncing Pellet Super Soldiers and get repeatedly killed, only to respawn with 20HP does indeed take its toll. The enemy Ai also leaves something to be desired, but only rarely will it be completely brain-dead, such as taking cover on the wrong side of a wall and so forth. Let me be clear, I'm not saying Wolfenstein: The New Order is a bad game by any means it just needs a little patching of buggy Ai and maybe respawing with slightly more health and Armour. The Story of Wolfenstein: The New Order is quite simply fantastic. While not a complicated plot, it is paced so well and truly makes you hate the Nazi War Machine you are fighting. The game also has some amazing set peices. From entire Air Fleets to even *Slight Spoiler* Moon bases! Yes, Nazi Moon Bases! Who would of thought huh? While the story is quite simple it is truly a gritty and mature game that some people may find to much. Torture Scenes, Sex Scenes and Human Experimenting (Not of the Good kind) may push some people away. But for a game about 'Killin' Nazis 'Merican Style' It does a great job at keeping the story at a good pace. Guns feel and sound great and the sound design is some of the best I've seen in a while. The Graphics of Wolfenstein also can be truly breath-taking. I didn't notice much texture pop in and only occassional screen tearing (I do play with V-Sync on). While maybe not as Next-Gen as they claim to be, The graphics certainly stand out from other recent titles. Also, the amount of exploration and 'Side-Stories' available such as newspaper clipping which develop the games lore deeply and multiple collectibles like Nazi Gold give players a reason to explore the beatiful levels of Wolfenstein.
All in all, I believe Wolfenstein: The New Order is worth every cent you pay and I hope to see more games like this from Machine Games in the future. I would suggest starting off on the Bring 'em On difficulty and then turn the difficulty up if you are finding it to be to easy.
I give Wolfenstein: The New Order a very well deserved:
9/10
*Side Note*
I'm now on my second playthrough on Bring 'Em On Difficulty level and am enjoying the game Much more this time. Also, near the beginning of the game you will be faced with a Choice (You will know it when you come by it, trust me) make sure to choose wisely as I've found out, different choices alter the games levels and people you meet through out the entirity of the game.

Everybody should try this if they haven't. As Rockstar had taken over development of Max Payne 3 there were going to be some changes...
A big change is the multiplayer which not nearly enough people play. The main problem with the multiplayer is it tends to be a bit unbalenced at times as higher level weapons can give you quite an edge. Apart from this there are no big issues with the multiplayer. On the subject of multiplayer, they released a DLC that added co-op. Barely anybody plays this mode but it is awesome. The main issue with that being there are only two maps to play on but still worth it really.
The single-player is simply awesome and has a really good length plus extra modes like New York Minute and Score Attack to keep you playing as you try to score highly in the leaderboards.
Actual detail to the game is amazing as more linear levels make room to add such detail. They also really went for it with the animations of the characters, especially the player's. The way your character interacts with the environment as it bumps into things if you do a shootdodge looks so good. Making it all the more entertaining when you mess up and hit your head or fall down a flight of stairs.
Overall it is a really good game with few glaring issues (if any) and definitely worth anybody's time. Something I did start to notice is the game is easier in some ways in comparison to the previous games. This could be because you can take cover now but I'm not sure. I always play on harder difficulties anyway.

Spoiler: The Nazis won the war and rule the world. Time jump to 1960: BJ is determined to liberate it by killing everyone wearing a swastika.
The combat mechanics are pretty good, basic FPS stuff with no forced cover but lots of peeking out from behind crates and corners. Plenty of stealth options, but you can always run and gun if you prefer. The guns are a lot of fun, the selection is rather limited but there are enough alt-fire options to play with and they are all useful throughout the game. Most of the maps are linear but allow for some exploration to find secrets and nazi gold. No multiplayer or randomization, so limited replay value. There are some codes for extras, Google it. First playthrough (normal difficulty, exploring without going for 100% completion) took me ca 14 hours.
What makes this game well worth it is the setting and the story: Nazi Europe looks great, very evocative. 1960s Nazis are still the perfect bad guys, and as they are nastier here than in any game I've played before the catharsis of murdering them by the hundreds is greater than ever. The setting and the NPCs are well presented through dialogue, cutscenes and low-violence episodes, and throughout the game there are a lot of minor details (newspaper clippings, letters, music) that rewards exploration and brings the world to life.
In sum: Decent shooter, excellent setting and story, very highly recommended if you don't mind cutscenes. Murdering Nazis never gets old.

◇ 𝐖𝐇𝐀𝐓 𝐈𝐒 𝐃𝐈𝐑𝐓𝐘 𝐁𝐎𝐌𝐁? ◇
                        ▣ Dirty Bomb is a great fast paced FPS game which is objective driven, It has tons of different classes (mercenaries) to play to fit your playstyle whether it be Medic, Assault, Recon, Fire Support and Engineer with each of them varying from health pool, movement speed, abilities and weapons. There are currently 20 playable mercenaries and they are divided into 5
1.) 𝐌𝐄𝐃𝐈𝐂 = Can revive people instantly using their defibs wherein other classes can pick up downed teammates for 10 seconds.
2.) 𝐄𝐍𝐆𝐈𝐍𝐄𝐄𝐑 = Can Plant, Repair and Defuse objectives two times faster than non-engineer classes
3.) 𝐑𝐄𝐂𝐎𝐍 = Can reveal the enemies position by using their abilities.
4.) 𝐀𝐒𝐒𝐀𝐔𝐋𝐓 = Can help you push the objective with their High damage and Health pool.
5.) 𝐅𝐈𝐑𝐄 𝐒𝐔𝐏𝐏𝐎𝐑𝐓 = Can provide you ammo and Area damage using their abilities.
                        ▣ Dirty Bomb has a high skill ceiling wherein you can't just win by using your abilities because you can outgun the abilities of the mercenaries if done correctly, gunplay still takes skill even if the recoil is small considering that the game has a very fast paced movement system with its wall and long jumps for you to access different places you wouldn’t access with merely just walking. With this you can access flank routes that can help you achieve the objective easily.
◇ 𝐃𝐈𝐑𝐓𝐘 𝐁𝐎𝐌𝐁 𝐆𝐀𝐌𝐄𝐏𝐋𝐀𝐘 𝐕𝐈𝐃𝐄𝐎𝐒 ◇

                        ▣ The things you could do with real money in this game is to buy credit booster, crafting kits, exclusive trinkets (Trinkets are nothing but decoration to your primary weapon) and Expert & Elite Cases these are cases that gives you higher chances of getting higher tier cards than a normal case. Spoiler: The Nazis won the war and rule the world. Time jump to 1960: BJ is determined to liberate it by killing everyone wearing a swastika.
The combat mechanics are pretty good, basic FPS stuff with no forced cover but lots of peeking out from behind crates and corners. Plenty of stealth options, but you can always run and gun if you prefer. The guns are a lot of fun, the selection is rather limited but there are enough alt-fire options to play with and they are all useful throughout the game. Most of the maps are linear but allow for some exploration to find secrets and nazi gold. No multiplayer or randomization, so limited replay value. There are some codes for extras, Google it. First playthrough (normal difficulty, exploring without going for 100% completion) took me ca 14 hours.
What makes this game well worth it is the setting and the story: Nazi Europe looks great, very evocative. 1960s Nazis are still the perfect bad guys, and as they are nastier here than in any game I've played before the catharsis of murdering them by the hundreds is greater than ever. The setting and the NPCs are well presented through dialogue, cutscenes and low-violence episodes, and throughout the game there are a lot of minor details (newspaper clippings, letters, music) that rewards exploration and brings the world to life.
In sum: Decent shooter, excellent setting and story, very highly recommended if you don't mind cutscenes. Murdering Nazis never gets old.

There was one day when it wouldn't let me log in, thus preventing me from playing.
Aside from that, the graphics are very realistic with plenty of detail to go around.  Max is definitely a bullet sponge and it shows, during gameplay and cutscenes.  95% of the game is intense action, from start to finish.  I especially enjoyed the flashback levels, though I think having armies of goons during every episode was a bit too much.
In the end though, it was heart pounding, agonizing, enjoyable, and satisfying to complete.  There is apparently another difficulty that I unlocked- I think I'll stay away from that one for now!

Max Payne was one of my childhood games (along with Unreal Tournament 2004, Devil May Cry 3, GTA Vice City and TES III Morrowind). Up to now, I still can't forget the cop with monkey face (due to old graphic technology) a.k.a highest NY mobs bodycount mungo with sick humour who only has one thing to do: blast a hole in bad guys' faces in slooooooooooow motion, oh yeah and drug too, that Valkyr drug created nightmares inside Max's mind became one of the first horror segments in video games that I've ever experienced. And then Max Payne 2 came to my life, the awesomeness continued with a love story, Captain Baseball Bat and moar sloooooooooow motion. With me, Max Payne 1 and 2 redefined third-person shooter genre and they remained my favourite games of all time.
When Rockstar Games first announced Max Payne 3, I honestly thought the game would failed because it no longer took place at NY and it didn't have classic noir them anymore. Well, I was wrong...
Let's kick off with the reason why we all play Max Payne for: presentation and story (I won't tell anything related to the story because I want to avoid spoilers). The game is heavily filled with rendered cutscenes instead of comic style cutscene, which will make many Max Payne fans dissappointed. But let me tell you one good thing: these cutscenes are all well-made, I had a great time watching them and I didn't even bother to press "skip" at 2nd playthrough. Max continued to narrate in the game and with the I-don't-even-know-how-to-describe-them effects, the cutscenes in the game are very unique and cinematic.
Max Payne is no longer obsessed with his wife and daughter's death, he still has his sarcastic humour and "One vice at a time", he is addicted to painkiller (which is not surprise), no more nightmares, no more depression. This is a new Max Payne with brighter tone and less dark atmosphere. Although I still miss the classic noir them, I have to admit that Rockstar Games did an amazing job in changing the original style of the franchise.
If you asked me what I liked most about Max Payne games, I would say BULLET TIME, YAY !!!!. But sad news guys, you can't dodge bullets by moving fast in slow motion anymore and you can only bring 2 guns at one time, but the good news is: now you can shoot GRENADES, yes I'm talking about flying GRENADES in the air that will blow your face anytime. Max is also able to make a last stand kill in case his health bar goes down to zero if he has a spare painkiller in his pocket. Anytime the cinematic killcam appears, you can see the bullet flying to enemy and blood spills out of his face. Shootdodge is still one of my favourite features in the game, Shooting 6 or 7 guys by 7 bullets while flying from the balcony to the ground like a real badass, hell, who doesn't want to do that ?
If you're a fan of the previous Max Payne games like me, you can find some easter eggs related to them, like Vincent Gogniti and Nicole Horne's graves in chapter 8: "Ain't No Reprievement Gonna Be Found Otherwise". You can also watch the Captain Baseball Bat on a TV when you're escorting Fabiana to the bus (it reminded me of Vincent, that poor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥).
I haven't tried multiplayer yet because I bought Max Payne 3 in order to play as Max Payne, not some nameless dude running around with an AK-47 who have no idea how they have Max's ability to slow down time.
After I had finished the game, I watched the credit in sadness because I realized that I won't have a chance to see Max anymore. Suddenly I remembered Max's line in MP2: "When you're looking down the barrel of a gun, time slows down. Your whole life flashes by, heartbreaks and scars. Stay with it, and you can live a lifetime in that split second". It has been 7 years since the first time I played Max Payne 1. After all, every adventure must have an end, right ?

Wolfenstein: The New Order surprised me.  It surprised me with its high production values, interesting storyline (!), wonderfully realized characters, and excellent voice acting. There are enough references to events in "Return to Castle Wolfestein" to support this game being a "proper sequel", but it stands alone if you haven't played the previous title. It also gives many nods to the original "Wolfenstein 3D".  The alternate history 1960's where Nazi Germany won WWII is very interesting, very dark, very sci-fi/high tech. It's over the top, but it holds up. There were many, many really thoughtful design decisions in the look and feel of the environments, the weapons and vehicles, etc.  The developers obviously took the time to ask what a Nazi dominated world post-WWII would look like, and the results are excellent...and often disturbing.  Again: it holds up. For all that, though, the crowning achievement in W:TNO is the story and the characters. Invest some time in this game.  You won't be disappointed.

Rockstar finally got around to creating advanced PC graphics for one of their games. It looks like they learned something after GTA 4 after all.
This time we get DX 11 tesselation, ambient occlusion (advanced sun rays), FXAA, MSAA, Anisotropic filtering as well as texture, shader, shadow, reflection and water quality tweaks. Needless to say this game has some heavy PC requirements. I was able to get 30 FPS with my powerful rig, but as soon as I turned down the multisampling anti-aliasing from 8x to 4x I got around 50-60 FPS throughout the rest of the game. Some jumpy shadows and halo around certain objects were also fixed. There are much more sharp edges and corners to be seen now. There will be certain areas in the game where you will see objects just appearing out of thing air.
Here are some other things that I have noticed. When you die at a checkpoint and you start over, you get to play with your full health even though you're supposed to be wounded. No more manual saves for us PC gamers. So you can thank Rockstar for when you get stuck in am awful area where you die over and over again. I also haven't noticed the first time around that you can actually go prone in this game. Sometimes its helpful but it takes you a long time to lie down and get up, so you will feel pretty exposed.
Remedy sold its soul and now its turning in its grave. Oh wait, they are still around! I wonder how they feel after letting Take-Two/Rockstar make the third installment. I mean what were they thinking? ok so Max crosses some people back home (finally); then get recruited by an old police academy buddy to go work in Brazil. How exciting. I also like how you protect the girl because Max Payne doesn't like seeing girls get hit; moments later you can actually shoot the girl with no consequences. This thing has GTA written all over it.
I really wonder whose bright idea at Rockstar it was to make Max Payne bald and place him in Brazil. When I first saw the screenshots back a couple of years ago I actually, in all honesty, thought it was a joke. I thought that Rockstar was just fooling around with some pre-production ideas.
Let's start off with a little history lesson.
The first game introduced the bullet time feature. This feature revolutionized third person shooters. Since then, many games copied the mechanics. Dead to Rights, F.E.A.R., Call of Juarez, Strangehold, Red Dead Redemption, Sniper Elite, Vanquish, Wanted. What started off as a style mechanic slowly evolved into assist mechanic, aim assist that is. The first and second games did not rely on protracted gun fights with cover; it was mostly about short encounters with a handful of enemies, so the gun fights were all about your reflexes. (more on that later).
Imagine a heavily scripted and narrative-driven GTA 4 plus a little bit of Red Dead Redemption touch. Congrats, you have just imagined Max Payne 3 (minus car theft). Same engine was used in GTA 4 and RDR.
Gone is the dark NY noire. Gone are the days when Max Payne 1,2 came out on PC FIRST and was rated higher than the console counter-parts. Gone are the characters from the first two games. Gone is the isolation that you felt in the first two games (now you will have back up nearby quite often). Gone are the derelict New York city alleys, gone is the comic-book narrative. In fact, the feeling you got from playing the first two games was that there WAS no world outside of New York at all. Here you get about 40 minutes of gameplay in New Jersey with the old Payne Jacket, the snow falling and the mobsters shooting you, (flashback to the good old days), but that's as close to NY as you will get in the game. I mean why couldn't they continue with the NY/NJ timeline? The mafia boss could be the villain and Max could easily continue running around NY and NJ. Ironically, the two flashbacks were the best parts of the game for me.
Now it is time to make way for the dance clubs, mini-skirts, Hawaiian shirts, the ability to kill friendly NPCs with no consequences, the annoying unremarkable uninteresting characters (Rockstar has a hard-on for those); make way for the side kicks, crazy blinding lights (people with epilepsy, BEWARE), the rural slums, sunny outdoors, frequent cut scenes that can't be skipped because the game is loading the new level (there are no loading screens here btw), Portuguese speaking enemies (no English subtitles by the way), the lack of suspense, and don't forget the multiplayer....yeah, the Max Payne franchise desperately needed that one.
And don't even get me started on the cut scenes, there are so many of them. The interrupt the fire fight continuity and decrease the urge to replay the game with guns blazing. The cut scenes also place you in scripted locations even though you were taking cover a second ago. At times, there is a cut scene every 1.5 minutes. Half the time you cannot skip them because that is when the game is apparently still loading. Every, and I repeat, EVERY cut scene is messed up. What I mean by that is that every cut scene has "effects" added to it. These include: blurry/static screen, double vision, various color and hue variations, sepia hue, frequent change of camera angle, blinding flashes, etc. It's frigging nauseating! Rockstar thought that adding too much "style" to these cut scenes would make them look more "cool" I guess. It sucks bad though, your screen can't ever focus on a single thing because everything goes haywire every two seconds. This "style" is even sometimes oozing out in real gameplay, no kidding. I also like how random dialogue words just pop up on the screen during cut scenes. Useless.
I also like how as you progress through the game you get these achievements, like "250 enemies killed" or "you shot 50 enemies in their hands" or "100 enemies killed with pistols", etc. WTF! When did Max Payne turn into a arcade shoot filled with rewards? Seriously, you can't even turn that infantile thing off!
So Rockstar decided to go with cover, since they are using their RAGE engine again, okay. What sucks though is that you cannot move when shooting while in cover. It's weird because you could do that in RDR.
The firefights are good, there is sufficient destruction and satisfaction of each kill.
Also when you run, you have the ability to roll and pick up ammo, like in Uncharted. However running itself is sluggish and imprecise, just like in any console third person shooter.
As you progress through the game you get too look at "clues" that describe your situation. You can also look for weapons parts to be used in multiplayer I guess. Take that for what its worth.
The campaign is pretty long (by today's standards anyway) but it is only so because 40% of the time you watch cut scenes, like in the last Metal Gear game.
As far as the story goes, well, nothing will ever beat the first game in that department. In the first Max Payne it was you against the world: the cops were after you, so was the mafia and the pharmaceutical corporation during the worst storm in history. The third game is a train wreck where you have to save a rich girl... who cares seriously? Moments ago Max was talking about how much he despised the vanity filled rich people. Yet he jumps into the pool with both feet (literally) instantly and keeps risking his own life for them. Then you turn into Sam Fisher/Arnold Schwarzenegger/One-Man Army kind of guy and do some spec ops missions, then you turn into a fearless unstoppable killing machine just looking for trouble. It just doesn't feel like a Max Payne game at least half of the time (boat chase sequence with infinite ammo anyone?) Certain areas the game plays like Kane & Lynch, no kidding. I still say that the franchise spiritually ended back in 2003.

Wolfenstein: The New Order surprised me.  It surprised me with its high production values, interesting storyline (!), wonderfully realized characters, and excellent voice acting. There are enough references to events in "Return to Castle Wolfestein" to support this game being a "proper sequel", but it stands alone if you haven't played the previous title. It also gives many nods to the original "Wolfenstein 3D".  The alternate history 1960's where Nazi Germany won WWII is very interesting, very dark, very sci-fi/high tech. It's over the top, but it holds up. There were many, many really thoughtful design decisions in the look and feel of the environments, the weapons and vehicles, etc.  The developers obviously took the time to ask what a Nazi dominated world post-WWII would look like, and the results are excellent...and often disturbing.  Again: it holds up. For all that, though, the crowning achievement in W:TNO is the story and the characters. Invest some time in this game.  You won't be disappointed.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Max Payne 3 has been developed and published by Rockstar. Many of you know about them, and in my opinion they are one of most known companies out there. They are publishers of Grand Theft Auto series, Max Payne series, Midnight club and many more.
Max Payne 3... Is amazing. In this game, you are a guy named Max Payne. The game is happening couple of years ago after Max Payne 2. Max was invited to a party where he needed to make sure that one family will stay safe. Of course, if everything went according to plan, the game would be boring. Max Payne is one of those typical "shoot first, ask questions later" games. All you do through the whole game is kill people. But you kill them with style. You can jump over the tables, chairs, from wall to wall, over obstacles and so on and on. And while you're jumping like that you enter a slow motion. That makes the game much more fun, and enemies much easier to kill.
Though, don't get me wrong here! Max Payne 3 is one of hardest single player games I've played in a long, long time. It takes you two to three bullets to die, while it takes quite a number of bullets to kill your opponents, since they have body armor. That makes the game very challenging to play, but also, sometimes, extremely frustrating. I remember trying to beat the beginning of last level like seven or eight times how hard it was. I just couldn't do it.
Max Payne 3 is also the first Max Payne game that allows you to play multiplayer. You can chose between three game types - team deathmatch, deathmatch and gang wars. In deathmatch everyone is against everyone. In Team Deathmatch you randomly get into a team of players and your objective is to kill the other people. Gang wars are almost the same as the other two, except here you have an objective. For example, capture and hold a bag. Or protect a building from the enemy forces who are trying to take it over. Though, no matter which game type you chose, you are always in one of five gangs. Those are like sides.
You can even customize your own character! You can pick from various faces, chest, tattoos, hairs, pants and shoes. Each gang has it's own clothing which makes them unique. The only drawback on multiplayer is leveling up. In multiplayer you need to level up to open up more looks for your characters, more weapons, perks and so on and on. Bad thing about it is that it takes forever. Leveling up is so slow already from early levels, that it seems impossible. And with most of the people being level 50 and having overpowered skills and guns, leveling gets even harder.
Graphic and audio of this game are extremely good. Even though this game is not openworld sandbox game, they made sure that the background of the game looks as realistic as it possibly could. And songs in the game are extremely catchy to listen! They do get repeatable at some point, but they are so fun and catchy that I didn't mind them at all.
