Pros:
-High octane action reminiscent of the shootouts in John-Woo's films (Hard Boiled, The Killer) with Max Payne's signature Bullet Time sequences which are very rewarding when taking down enemies with the good ol' kill cam.
-Graphics are stunning with high-detailed textures and post processing effects for the player models and the environment. Same goes for the decals ( especially the bulletwounds), which emphasise the impact of every shot. (You would not want to be caught in Max's crosshairs!)
-Improved gaming mechanics add a new experience and adds flair to the shootout sequences of the game (Fluid body movements makes Max look so life-like).
-Story is innovative in terms of how it is carried out (dialogues, interesting monologues from the titular character himself!)
-Destructive environments intensifies the action sequences (flying debris, exploding cars, broken glasspanes)
-The soundtrack from HEALTH is effective in capturing Max's grim journey throughout his "vacation" in Sao Paulo. Check out the song 'Tears', which plays in the finale of the game.
Cons:
-Cutscenes are frequent to a point where it can break immersion of the game. Despite this they are insightful
-Linearity of the game does not justify its highly demanding hard disk space (35GB!?).
-Game environments are not as interactive as its predecessors (does not really help with the 35gb install size).
______________________________________________________________________
Overall, this game is a must play!! Although it feels different to its previous two games which carry the neo-noir night dark aesthetics, the experience is paid off with improved and innovative gaming mechanics (fluid movement) which intensify the action sequences which stays true to the previous two games. While its a shame Sam Lake, the original writer of the other two games, was not involved with this game, the Houser brothers once again do a terrific job with writing the story, which is different yet stays true to the trilogy.

I am a huge fan of the Max Payne series - the first two are one of my favorite games of all time.  The writing, the atmosphere, and the gameplay are top-notch.  As a self-described Max Payne fan, Max Payne 3 continues the trajectory of Max as he has gotten older but not any wiser.  He's still a sucker for a woman in danger, and he's always finding himsef coming up short.  The gameplay of MP3 has evolved to take into account more recent FPS mechanics like cover and weapons inventory (you can't carry every weapon like in the first game).  The writing of this third entry, particularly Max's voice and view, are spot-on.
Overall replay value is there, as you can explore different styles of play, and you can sharpen your skills in the arcade modes of new york minute (speed) and score attack (points/damage).  The one drawback is that there are a few unskippable cutscenes that are quite lengthy.  The writing and voice-acting are great, though, so it's not unbearable.  The cutscenes all take place before a save point, so you don't have to worry about repeating it if you immediately die.
Multiplayer adds several new game modes, from straight deathmatch, to teams, capture territories, and so on.  I highly recommend this game for both fans of the Max Payne series as well as those who like strong story and voice talent.

(If you don't like to read, just scroll down to
the ---Conclusion--- section)
You'll play as William Blazkowicz, a special forces operative
captain, sent out on a massive air raid to take out the evil
Nazi General Deathshead. The beginning of the game
takes place in 1946, and after a failed mission William Blazkowicz
ends up in a vegetable state. You'll wake up from this vegetable
state some years later, in 1960, and you'll learn that Nazi Germany
won the war, and the world is now under Nazi regime.
The game uses the Id Tech 5 engine, a pretty new engine
previously seen in the game RAGE.
This engine has both bad and good sides going for it.
This engine utilizes mega textures, meaning instead of
having several small textures re-used several places in
the game, mega textures is one huge texture spanning
over the entire game.
This is both good and bad. On the downside the textures are
so huge, they need to be seriously compressed,
compressed down to "only" 33GB. Yes, this game
has 33GB of textures. The compression brings with
it downgraded texture resolutions. The textures at
times looks awful, muddy and blurry, to the point
where it burns my eyes.
On the up side of these mega textures, is that the
textures are unique through out the game, no re-used
materials, so the game has a superb texture variety
which brings some realistic feeling to this world the
game brings you to.
The graphics also lacks AA, so get ready to see the
pixel outlines of objects. (can be forced on through the consol)
Buuuut, even due to all these downsides of the graphics,
the characters and facial animations looks stunning.
This game has really nice facial animations which brings
a believable characters to the game, and the game
has some stunning art design. Some of the Nazi technology
looks so cool and original, the world looks stunning and
is full of details, they've really created a great world for this game.
The game has some good soundtracks, playing correctly
to place suspense during the correct moments,
a mix between orchestra and rock.
But the weapons lacks in the sound department, they
kinda has the "pew pew" weapon sounds, which
takes away the feeling of wielding something powerfull.
The voice acting in this game is generally good, and
the nazi soldiers walks around peaking german.
Most of the voice acting are good, and the characters
are ok, the game tries to create some emotional bonding
with the characters, and they mostly, fail at that,
the fault lies in that you're on your own for the majority
of the game, and the few parts where you get too mingle
with the other characters are too short and contains
little content, so you'll know about them but you'll
not get sad if they die.
There's sure some likable characters, and a couple
who you'll don't care about, but the best character
in the game, eventho he is the evil villain,
is Deathshead. The voice acting of this character was
outstanding, it was brilliant, he felt so real, and you
really started to hate him because he was so evil.
Only sad thing is that you'll only encounter him
twice in the game.
What you do encounter, are a lot of nazi soldiers.
And here's the part where the game shines.
The combat is splendid, there's a good varaity of
weapons to use, and you can dual wield most of them,
something which is incredible badass and fun.
The shooting is precise and tense, the game throws
in some new enemies to keep it fresh, and a couple
of bosses. You'll have a simple cover machanics
similar to Medal Of Honor: Airborne, which kinda
works, and they finally removed the damn
auto generative health... Kinda, it'll only regenerate
some, 10-20% of your remaining HP, but to fully
get it up you'll need to pick up health packs.
I found the game too easy at times, I started
off my first playthrough at "I AM DEATH INCARNATE!",
and I mostly cleared the game without much
difficulty. The game do have some collectible
items, some of them are Enigma Codes, which
you get to crack to unlock new and harder
game modes.
The game gives you the choice of either going
guns blasting into an situation, or go stealth.
You can take out every enemy in a level without
being seen by going stealth. It's also fun, they
did a good job on the stealth mechanics, tho
it's somewhat "too" easy going stealth. Often
if you pop up from cover and some nazi soldier sees
you, he'll go "huh, what was that", but he will never
bother investigating it, he'll just continue his normal
walking round. They will also not react if a fellow
nazi brother next to them get's assassinated in the head
by your silenced pistol. It's just too easy at times.
Stealth machanics are good, shooting mechanics are awesome.
Something which also is just good, is the story.
It's interesting enough to keep you going, and
you'll meet some new characters and see new places,
and with these new characters you'll set up a plan to
bring down Deathshead. The game's story is mostly
driven and told through narration and cut-scenes,
and kept interesting with some damn good characters,
mainly Frau Engel and Deatshead.
You'll also be able to read small articles from news papers
to read up about what has happened in the game world.
I like the twist where Nazi Germany won the war, and
seeing how the world is under the Nazi Regime.
I was kinda dissapointed in the story part, because early
on in the game during Chapter 1, you'll be given a pretty
difficult task, picking whom of your two team members
will be tortured and used as an speciment in Deathshead's
experiments, and I thought this game would give me
more difficult choices and there would be a story branching
based on your choiced through out the game with
different endings... The story will slightly change
because you'll be playing with either one or the other
of them, but it'll have the same ending regardless of
whom you chose.
The game is somewhat expensive for what you get.
I spent around 11-12 hours completing it on my first
try at the second hardest difficulty level (not counting
the unlockable modes), and I was looking around trying
to find all the collectibles and reading nearly all the
news articles I could find, and it does not really give
you a reason to play it over again, I guess you could
collect ALL the collectibles and try the Hardcore difficulty
level, but there's story wise no reason to play it again,
it has only one ending, no branching story, no New Game+,
so despite how awesome those 12 hours were, this game
does not give you much value for 50€.
This game does a lot correctly, the shooting is superb
and fun, it's pure awesome to play this game shooting
down evil people, eventho going Stealth is kinda too easy,
the graphics lacks at some areas but the art design is stunning,
some failed tries to get you emotionally bonded with the
characters, but it has somewhat interesting story,
and Deathshead is maybe the best villain character ever.
All in all, despite it's few faults, this is some of the
most fun and awesome games I've played in some time,
even if the game doesn't give you much value for your
50€, I would still warmly recommend this game. It's
a pure, clean and awesome shooter game with minimal
gimmick ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t and a lot of focus and love for the shooting
part of this game.

Title: Max Payne 3
Genre: Action
Developer: Rockstar Studios
Publisher: Rockstar Games
Release Date: 1 Jun 2012
Story : 9
Max Payne,the main protagonist,has suffered beyond the limits.9 years have passed since the last game in the series,yet the Max is still traumatised by the death of his beloved wife and child.Apart from that,Max has been betrayed many times before.His only company are pills[Painkillers]and of course,Alcohol.
Max,leaves New york,and goes to Sao Paulo,Brazil.His close friend,Raul Passos,offers him a job as a private security for a rich businessman Rodrigo Brango.However,things don't work as expected.Rodrigo's wife,Fabiana,is kidnapped during Max's watch,which will later set in motion a chain of events that draws Max into a bigger,extremely interesting story.
Throughout the game,you will never be sure if Max wants to live,save another man's wife,or he just wants to put an end to his life while he is on a suicide mission.
G-G-G-Gameplay : 8
The gameplay is simple.The game contains [for some people] -some-more-than-usual- cutscenes,but if you want to get deeper into the story,i believe it wont annoy you.There are many weapons in the game,BUT you can only carry two one-handed [pistols/smg] and one two-handed [ak-47,shotgun etc. etc.].If you choose to play dual-wield,you will have to throw the two-handed weapon.your playstyle will probably be Slow-Mo[you can trigger slow-motion either by holding shift when its available,OR you can just press space to dive which will also affect to slow motion.]/Bullet-Time/Dodge.
To regain health,all you have to do,is use your pills[Painkillers].if you lose all your hp but you have at least one painkiller left,slow-motion will get triggered,and if you shoot the enemy who gave you the last hit,you will get back to life and it will count like you used your painkiller to regain health.
During each chapter[level],you will find some gold parts for your weapons.There are three gold parts for each weapon.For example,if you find the three parts for the shotgun,it wont just give you the visuals of a golden weapon which will make you look badass,it will also give your weapon an extra +10% more damage,and,some an increased ammo capacity per magazine.
Apart from the gold parts,during each chapter.you will find some clues.those clues are items and other things scattered throughout the game. Collecting them all will lead to the An Echo of the Past Achievement / Trophy.
The main story lasts 12-14 hours.
Graphics : 9
Beautiful Game Graphics.Environments are impressively detailed and performances sensitively captured.you can see all the violence and blood R* put on this game.specially on slowmotion,where you can see the bullets you shoot the bullets the enemies shot.
Multiplayer : 9
Multiplayer was a total surprise.You will play four rounds,with different objectives that alter depending on what happens in each of them:from claiming territory to assasinate a random selected leader of the opposite gang to defuse bombs.The final round is an all-out death match.
Bursts, which function like perks, are central to this mode, and confer advantages to the members of your crew, from raising the calibre of your weapons to inducing paranoia in the opposing team, making friendlies appear as enemies.
CONCLUSION :8.5

I expected a brainless shooter but I got way more than that. Wolfenstein has a really well written story that takes you through some unexpected locations (for a linear shooter, anyway).
The mechanics are very solid and except for the weapon selection wheel there's usually nothing distracting you from action. You can actually opt to play most missions in a stealth manner as well.
The whole story is, of course, a 'little' far fetched, but the way the environments, story, characters and their relationships are presented actually draws you into the story and makes you feel for them. There's a lot of side info that you can choose to read or listen to, which helps as well.
The characters are well put together. Anya, a character that you meet in one of the chapters may remind some of Alyx Vance from Half Life 2.
You run across collectibles throughout the game that actually unlock optional challenges. The collectibles are very well placed and don't distract you from the main story line if you choose to go for them.

A must play for any Max Payne fan, the third installment of the game series takes some uncertain steps while out of the hands of its original developers, but Rockstar does the gritty noir shooter justice.
The single player is where the majority of the fun is to be found. A highly polished and artistic story of redemption ties together the game's fantastic gunfights, which are more destructive and elegant than the previous two games. There is also an increase in tactics, although a skilled player can still run and gun through the levels with ease. After playing through the story, the game also features an arcade mode, and competing to unlock high scores gives the game a great replayability.
The less said about the multiplayer, the better. It's a joke, a stain on the game, sparsly populated, awkward, confusing, and it does not do the game's mechanics justice, as those mechanics are best used for mowing down enemies en-masse, not for player-to-player combat.
The good news though, is that you will easily get your money's worth with the single player alone. If you're on the fence, allow me to push you off; buy this game. Now.

There's a lot of internet backlash for what I have to say is a brilliant game. I've known about the Wolfenstein series for years but  aside from a very brief playthrough of Return to Castle Wolfenstein, Wolfenstein: The New Order was the first time I payed serious attention to playing. And despite all the dissapointment from others, I say this is a great game almost undeserved of the complaining.
The levels are massive, on several maps I dropped my jaw at the scenery. Id software have gone to great lengths to make awe-inspiring scenes and even arenas for fighting. The AI itself is not stupid (mostly), i've been flanked by the rank-and-file and on higher difficulty levels I've been killed by being outsmarted by the AI (although on the opposite end I have seen soldiers stand in the middle of the floor to shoot me). This game is a love-letter not just to old-school shooters, but veterens of the Wolfenstein series as this game's story continues on from general Wolfenstein canon.
I have not finished the story yet but so far it has kept me hooked. I feel for the resistance leaders, i feel for the poor people being oppressed. There are newspaper cuttings that detail events during the Nazi regime which move me to tears. Machine Games did a good job showing how grim this world is as at one point reading these cuttings I even wondered if this Nazi-ruled world was even worth saving.
With a low-end processor (Intel i3) I can't play with the shiniest graphics. I have seen several patches of low-res texturing but  after a while it didn't bother me, the game as great and the scenery was impressive nonetheless. The cutscenes are gorgeous and the animation is of very good quality. I'd say what Machine Games have done is actually fairly clever as despite my low-end processor as I could still witness moments of some very detailed modeling. While walking around, the PC performs idle animations even if he is just a pair of arms for the most part; checking ammo, priming the weapon and adjusting the sights or playing with his knife. I did have problems getting the game to work as I needed the very latest driver for my AMD graphics card and it took me some time to find the right 64x Catalyst Control Centre for WIndows 7.
Overall I say we got what many old-school veterens want from the FPS genre: An affectionate throwback to the stuff we lost in the advancement of the shooter genre. But this game also includes modern concepts. I'm hunting for ammo, health packs and collectables while watching my ammo supply (old-school) while also shooting from cover down an iron sight (new-school).

One of the most anticipated sequels back then in 2011! It comes with the same simple but efective portal mechanic from its prequel with very nice tweaks and additions like the introduction of gels. Thankfully the single campaign has more content in comparison of the 1-hour long prequel, taking more of 12 hours long! So the game is even worth buy it at full price!
The dialogs & the posters are very hilarious and clever dialogs during the course of all the game (enough proof that during the first day I had almost 20 screenshots in my computer that gave me little lazyness to upload all of them to my Steam profile). More importantly they add crucial clues about the laboratory's background and about the personnel back then (there is a comic named "Lab Rat" included in the game, I recommend you to read after playing the prequel).
The best thing of the game for me is without doubt the co-op courses, unlike the single mode puzzles, they are hard and gives an awesome satisfaction completing them (even my brother and me end hugging like the bots after completing the levels). Storywise the co-op mode is after the events of the single mode but is nothing related so you can freely first start the co-op without get spoiled!  Also the online connection between both players is AWESOME! Unlike most of the online game, here there is not a single lag moment during the levels (there sometime little slowdown during the load times but you know, is better that than DURING your game solving).
Last but no least, there is the community maps so with enough storage there is enough content to keep playing!
Can be a little laggy for older systems but infinite fun.

You can play it stealthily, sneaking around sniping enemies with throwing knifes, tactically clearing the room, or going in guns blazing old school style.... the point I'm trying to make here is that it does all three of these REALLY well. You can play the game however you want! Another thing done well is the enemies are varied nicely and boss fights are super satisfying. One thing I might add to that is that I found the combat to be so satisfying I would always be bummed that the levels were over. Overall I found the game to do a whole lot of things great- if it ever goes on sale, do yourself a favor and kill some nazi scum!

Before the release, there has been a lot of controversy regarding the new setting of the game. While the predecessors have been placed in New Noir York City, a large part of Max Payne 3 is set in São Paulo, Brazil. Indeed, the grim, dark streets filled with Russian mobsters and Valkyr junkies are no longer here, instead they have been replaced with nightclubs, favelas and luxurious cruise ships. After the events of Max Payne 2, our antihero returns to his home in New Jersey, where he lives the life of self-pity. That is until he meets Raul Passos, a former colleague from the police academy, who is doing a private security job for the Branco family. Max and his friend engage themselves in a conflict with the mob, and soon Max is forced to move out to Brazil as well. As you might suspect, things don’t work out well for him. Seriously, has things ever worked out for him?
The old comic-panel storytelling device is gone, but the flashy cutscenes definitely make up for it. Their visual aspect, heavily inspired by IO Interactive’s Kane & Lynch 2: Dog Days, actually plays a large role in storytelling as well. It represents Max’s constant hangover and tipsiness, with cut-up, multi-framed, noisy scenes, flashing lights and weird camera angles reminding me on my own drunken ventures and the morning afters, but let’s not get into that. Overall, Max’s story is an engrossing, brilliant experience, and what’s even more important, it keeps in touch with the noir aspect of Max Payne 1 and 2.
Max Payne 3’s gameplay is the old-school fun you remember from the previous games. There is a massive arsenal of weapons to choose from, ranging from revolvers, through micro SMGs and ending with a sniper rifle and a grenade launcher. However, you can only wield two one-handed weapons and one two-handed weapon at a time. If you choose to dual-wield, you drop the larger weapon. The cool thing about it is, all weapons are shown on Max’s body throughout cutscenes as well, and the way he reloads his pistol while holding a shotgun in another hand at the same time is one of the finest animations in gaming to date.
Here comes the first complaint though, after each cutscene, and there are a LOT of them, Max defaults to his one-handed weapon, which might sound like a minor thing, but is actually quite annoying and breaks the immersion slightly. It is something that should definitely be fixed in a future patch. The old gameplay mechanics are still here- both bullet time and shootdodge make a return, and you absolutely need to use them if you want to stay alive. You might think that the game has been dumbed down because of the newly introduced cover system, but you couldn’t be further from the truth. Not only does the health not regenerate even on the lowest difficulty setting (painkillers make a return as well, so you can’t make Max suck a thumb for a few seconds to recover), but the cover is also fully destructible. And so are the enemies.
Max Payne 3 is mercilessly brutal. The developers take pride in that it seems, since there is a button that allows you to slow down time to see your bullets shot at the last enemy in the area. And then allows you to shoot him some more. With 50 bullets more. To the chest. By the time the guy is down, his body has more lead in it than blood, and each of the wounds gushes blood and leaves bloodstains on clothes as well. The game utilizes the Euphoria physics engine known from GTA IV, and although some hilarious glitches might occur, you can feel the impact of the bullet with every shot, and seeing an enemy stumbling over a set of stairs never gets old. The game is a majestic theatre, a wet dream of John Woo and Chow Yun-fat, and a glorious sight to any gamer. The environments intensify the firefights even more- from shattered glass, through empty shells bashing the floor with every shot, to massive splinters falling off of wooden surfaces; the game is a truly thrilling ride throughout all 14 chapters, lasting about 9-12 hours.

Max Payne 3 is very fun when it comes to shooting, but, unfortunately, that is really all it has to offer. I could not finish it, simply because I didn't care about what would happen next. The problem with writing a story about a bunch of drunk middle-aged jerks, is that people neither like nor care about them. The game tries very hard to get you to sympathize with Max, but then it makes it nearly impossible because they try to maintain "hardened super Tom Cruise man" and "drunk man wallowing in his sorrows" at the same time. It doesn't even come close to working.
The gameplay is, despite the shortcomings I just addressed, very good. It is quite fun to dual-wield weapons, jump off buildings, take out a ton of enemies in bullet-time, etc. This will likely grow old on you in a few hours, however. Sadly, Max Payne simply doesn't offer anything new throughout the game to keep things interesting (it tries to drive you forward with the story, which, as I previously stated, is not very good).
I know this isn't very much related to the game at all, but I absolutely adore the menus in this game. I mean honestly, instead of advertising the actual game, they should just give you a three minute clip of navigating the menus. They are literally the most amazing menus I think I've ever seen. This is, perhaps, the reason I didn't enjoy the story very much. I just couldn't stop thinking about how awesome the menus were. Not only does it give you more options than anything I've ever seen (except for Gravity Bone or anything else based off Quake), it also tells you how much video memory you have available. This way, you can get the perfect settings for whatever system you have.
Overall, unless you really like menus and/or mindless fun, I don't recommend that you buy Max Payne 3.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a lovingly crafted game made with a ton of heart and charm that I feel will have legs as more and more people try it out. It’s not radically innovative or revolutionary, but it does so many things to stand out in the current landscape that it doesn’t have to be. A brutal and charming adventure that doesn’t pull any punches but knows when to be light-hearted. The combat design and shooting mechanics (no restricted 2-weapon system, no need to aim-down-sights, multiple ways to approach enemy encounters, glorious hit feedback and gibs) are liberating while being supported by tough AI and fantastic weapons to shoot at them with, in more expansive levels that encourage exploration. Meanwhile, excellent storytelling through fantastic characters and the environment is happening all around you, rather than at you. Also, has one of the best soundtracks in a game with some of the most hard-hitting rock and metal with touches of industrial music that gets your blood pumping to fight for the resistance.
It brings the best of the old and the new. It’s exactly what people who complain about modern shooters should play, to see it’s not all doom-and-gloom. Personally, it has set a new standard in shooters. It’s one of the best shooters I’ve played.

"Wake up.  You're dead."  Wolfenstein: The New Order is what a great single player FPS should be.  It's got a beefy campaign, reasons for replayability, great gun play, great stealth play, and very nice pacing throughout.  At every point where you are getting worn out by action, the game will introduce some sort of non-combat gameplay element, such as a hub where you talk to NPCs.  Take all of that plus tons of secrets, interesting weapons and tactics, and great attention to little details such as the quote above taken from the player as you stealth kill a sleeping Nazi.
This is certainly the best single player FPS I've played since Bioshock Infinite, therefore I have to really recommend it.

Planetside 2 is my absolute FAVORITE game to play.
In FPS games like COD or CS:GO, the game is all about the actions of the individual (actions of the group require a command structure, which these games lack), and victory relies solely on the twitch-response skill level of a player. In RTS games like CIV or C&C, the game is all about the actions of the group as a whole (actions of the individual require each soldier to be independently controlled, but these games' soldiers are all automated and alike), and victory relies solely on the tactical abilities of a single player.
Planetside 2 is a perfect mix of the two methods. Each and every soldier is controlled by its own player, thus they are independent. The comperable command system was specifically designed to have an orderly way of organizing players. Victory cannot be obtained without the command system, as players would wander from battle to battle with little or no progress and no fun. Victory cannot be obtained if there is a well-designed command system, but only AIs were controlled, as skill and improvisation would become meaningless.
Victory is obtained only because FPS gamers - skilled at shooting to kill and having individuality - fight under the organized banner of RTS gamers - skilled at battle tactics and ordering force deployments.
This is no generalization of RTS and FPS gamers (as many can competantly play both roles), but skill sets are skill sets, and Planetside 2's skill set is BEING AWESOME.

Less Hide and Seek missions (boring)

More environment weapons (exploding barrels, flame pipes and cutting chains to drop objects on enemies)
Less ammo (even in normal felt too much, every room just about had a recharge station for battery weapons)
More puzzles (not hide and seek crap)
Less cutscenes and more play scenes (you have free looking or can move while the scene plays out)
More "memorable" boss fights

This game should not be as good as it is. The traditional story of a Wolfenstein game is:
"There are Nazis. They are bad. Kill them all."
And at its most base level, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a faithful rendition of the Wolfenstein formula. There are Nazis (beautifully rendered, gorgeously designed diesel-punk Nazis). They are bad (the game makes this clear through some surprisingly effective and affecting story beats). And you will kill them all (The weapons are what you'd expect, but very well realized. The stealth system, as you might not expect, is both effective and fun.).
However, Wolfenstein: The New Order goes beyond the basic formula by giving you environments that reward exploration and that you actually want to explore. It also introduces actual characters, including making that grimacing head at the bottom of the screen in the original Wolfenstein into a somewhat interesting protagonist. While the character interaction is kept pretty much to bare minimum, the game does effectively establish several relationships between characters, to the point that I found myself actually caring about what happened in what is, at its base, a dumb game about killing Nazis.
This game is probably not worth the full $60 price tag. I finished (not 100%) the game on normal in around 12 hours. If you are a completionist, that number will probably double. If you're actually good at FPS games, it will be less. However, this is probably the most interesting FPS game to come out since Bioshock: Infinite and is well worth playing if you have even a passing interest in shooters. Pick it up at the next Steam sale and you won't regret it.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing

SUGGESTIONS FOR DEVS:
- New maps should play with the Y (or whatever axis is up/down in Unreal Engine) more. Perhaps a construction site for a map? It is London after all, there's always construction cranes in London!
- A new objective, something like King of the Hill, where the defenders have to guard a destructible objective (perhaps a high-health barrier that blocks access to a low-health computer terminal?). This would be like a C4 objective, however you end up C4ing a gate that protects the computer terminal, the gate can be destroyed with C4 but the computer terminal must be destroyed manually, the gate can be repaired at any time.
- Like Dome starts to do, the maps should have places where you can only get by chaining different jumps - perhaps some secondary objectives that block you from doing these chained jumps around the corner, if a door/gate is closed, you'll fall down!
Reasons to try Dirty Bomb:
- 100% free
- 0% Pay-to-Win
- Pretty well balanced classes - more balanced than Overwatch
- Fun gun-play that rewards skill with kills
- Team-based game where good team-work and use of each merc's individual abilities can turn the tide of any battle
- ... Its free? Why not try it?
- A very comprehensive tutorial that covers absolutely everything you need to know to play well, with a little obstacle course to learn how to do more advanced moves.
- In-game cash unlocks new mercs, giving a good sense of progression. The starter mercs are actually really powerful
- Dedicated servers ensure no one slows down the game, unlike peer-to-peer lobbies.
- Server browser nullifies the need to sit in matchmaking queues that take ten minutes to put you in one of the 50 games you can easily be put into
- Servers cover EU, NA East & West, Russia, Aussie-land, Asia and South America.
- Objective-based, with CTF/Reverse CTF/Escort/Repair/Plant-C4 objectives with 'secondary objectives' like generators which controls doors available to control movement around the map
- 'Max level' servers so all new players can join servers where only up to level 10s can join, letting them learn the game without getting thoroughly stomped each time they play
- No DLC beyond paying for stuff that you can get with in-game currency over 2-3 days
- Small but good collection of balanced maps
- 'Execution' game-mode, one life with a C4 objective, similar to Counter Strike
Reasons to not try:
- Matchmaking times are high
- The dedicated server host isn't... perfect, but 95% of the time everything is pretty good
- The occassional hacker. You get about one hacker in every hundred match, fortunately they get kicked half of the time
- Map development is slow. Its slow with most games, although the maps do get improvements
- Every so often with new mercs, they are usually slightly over-powered or under-powered (Phantom BANEBLADE!!!)
- Matchmaking still isn't perfect. You either get stomped or you stomp. Rarely an in-between.

This game should not be as good as it is. The traditional story of a Wolfenstein game is:
"There are Nazis. They are bad. Kill them all."
And at its most base level, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a faithful rendition of the Wolfenstein formula. There are Nazis (beautifully rendered, gorgeously designed diesel-punk Nazis). They are bad (the game makes this clear through some surprisingly effective and affecting story beats). And you will kill them all (The weapons are what you'd expect, but very well realized. The stealth system, as you might not expect, is both effective and fun.).
However, Wolfenstein: The New Order goes beyond the basic formula by giving you environments that reward exploration and that you actually want to explore. It also introduces actual characters, including making that grimacing head at the bottom of the screen in the original Wolfenstein into a somewhat interesting protagonist. While the character interaction is kept pretty much to bare minimum, the game does effectively establish several relationships between characters, to the point that I found myself actually caring about what happened in what is, at its base, a dumb game about killing Nazis.
This game is probably not worth the full $60 price tag. I finished (not 100%) the game on normal in around 12 hours. If you are a completionist, that number will probably double. If you're actually good at FPS games, it will be less. However, this is probably the most interesting FPS game to come out since Bioshock: Infinite and is well worth playing if you have even a passing interest in shooters. Pick it up at the next Steam sale and you won't regret it.

Review changed based on issues fixed. Rubber banding for this game only hasn't been fixed, but its play-able now!
SUGGESTIONS FOR DEVS:
- New maps should play with the Y (or whatever axis is up/down in Unreal Engine) more. Perhaps a construction site for a map? It is London after all, there's always construction cranes in London!
- A new objective, something like King of the Hill, where the defenders have to guard a destructible objective (perhaps a high-health barrier that blocks access to a low-health computer terminal?). This would be like a C4 objective, however you end up C4ing a gate that protects the computer terminal, the gate can be destroyed with C4 but the computer terminal must be destroyed manually, the gate can be repaired at any time.
- Like Dome starts to do, the maps should have places where you can only get by chaining different jumps - perhaps some secondary objectives that block you from doing these chained jumps around the corner, if a door/gate is closed, you'll fall down!
Reasons to try Dirty Bomb:
- 100% free
- 0% Pay-to-Win
- Pretty well balanced classes - more balanced than Overwatch
- Fun gun-play that rewards skill with kills
- Team-based game where good team-work and use of each merc's individual abilities can turn the tide of any battle
- ... Its free? Why not try it?
- A very comprehensive tutorial that covers absolutely everything you need to know to play well, with a little obstacle course to learn how to do more advanced moves.
- In-game cash unlocks new mercs, giving a good sense of progression. The starter mercs are actually really powerful
- Dedicated servers ensure no one slows down the game, unlike peer-to-peer lobbies.
- Server browser nullifies the need to sit in matchmaking queues that take ten minutes to put you in one of the 50 games you can easily be put into
- Servers cover EU, NA East & West, Russia, Aussie-land, Asia and South America.
- Objective-based, with CTF/Reverse CTF/Escort/Repair/Plant-C4 objectives with 'secondary objectives' like generators which controls doors available to control movement around the map
- 'Max level' servers so all new players can join servers where only up to level 10s can join, letting them learn the game without getting thoroughly stomped each time they play
- No DLC beyond paying for stuff that you can get with in-game currency over 2-3 days
- Small but good collection of balanced maps
- 'Execution' game-mode, one life with a C4 objective, similar to Counter Strike
Reasons to not try:
- Matchmaking times are high
- The dedicated server host isn't... perfect, but 95% of the time everything is pretty good
- The occassional hacker. You get about one hacker in every hundred match, fortunately they get kicked half of the time
- Map development is slow. Its slow with most games, although the maps do get improvements
- Every so often with new mercs, they are usually slightly over-powered or under-powered (Phantom BANEBLADE!!!)
- Matchmaking still isn't perfect. You either get stomped or you stomp. Rarely an in-between.

Where to start... There is a LOT to be said about this game. Mostly good things, don't worry.
About the game and story:
Wow... I loved the game. The story is very strong, and I love how the game combines action, humor and romance. It's also a perfectly challenging game that really puts all of B.J's skills to the test.
I almost couldn't stop playing once I started, and within two days I had finished the game (and I don't usually like to finish the games that quickly).
The strong story really made me feel like "Okay, this is what I'm fighting for, Ima put my life on the line and I love it" and that got me really motivated to slay all those nazis and get past the obstacles. And it's not only endless fighting, there are also fun and joyful moments, which kept me going.
Also I'm very picky when it comes to games, but this definitely makes my list of top 5 best games ever!
About the marketing of the game:
I truly got my eyes opened to this game after the actual release. But I emidiately thought this is a game I could possibly like. As I watched more trailers and also videos of some gameplay, I knew I would love to try it out!
The only hesitation I had was the fact that "minimun requirements" were set really high, requiring a PC with with Intel Core i7 and a fairly new graphics card.. My PC was built in 2011, and I don't get that many FPS in most games, so the high requirements were a huge turn-off for me, not knowing if it would be a waste of money if I shouldn't be able to even run the game.
Finally I decided to buy the game anyway since it was on sale.
And to my suprise I've been able to run the game fine from the very beginning, not lowering settings. Never had troubes launching or lag, it just runs very smoothly.
I'm on a PC with Intel core i5-2500 @ 3.30 GHz (4 cores) and a pretty old graphics card; AMD Radeon HD 5670.
So I really had my doubts, but it ran fine! Okay, I'm definitely not close to this games ideal 60 FPS (rather half of that), but I think at least the "minimum requirements" should be changed to "recommended specs", since minimum sounds as if it's not possible to run the game if you dont meet these requirements, which clearly it is.
About the ending of the game (*SPOILERS* DON'T CONTINUE READING IF YOU DIDN'T FINISH THE GAME):
I don't fancy games that leaves you wondering "what happened?" and where you have to imagine the actual outcome for yourself.
I also don't like games where you've become really attatched to the character you play as, and it ends with that character or even hero getting killed/dying "for the greater good".
However, I think the first example is acceptable if the game will be followed by another game picking up where the first one ended.
And I really hope that will be the case for Wolfenstein: TNO!
B.J. could have been saved and a new fight against the nazis could begin.
Like Anya said "Believe it" I will believe that this game wasn't the end of B.J's story and that we will eventually continue his quest in a new game.

Wolfenstein:TNO is like a 90s shooter, but it has nods to modern conveniences. Like, if you take insignificant damage, it regenerates back, and you always regen to at least 20 health so you never die in one tiny hit; but it has actual health, which is really fun; it keeps you avoiding damage even if you know you can easily win one specific trade, and it keeps the tension high when health is low.
This is also probably the most impressed I've been with a shooter engine since Far Cry. I think this represents a real turning point in 3D games. It's not that this engine can do anything that others can't, it's how it manages to milk every last ounce of performance out of my hardware to make it look better than seems hypothetically possible on my computer. I think this is the future: anyone nowadays can pack an engine full of more fancy lighting physics than a $1000 graphics card can ever handle; the new frontier is doing things more efficiently with what consumers actually have in their house.
That said, there are some engine issues. Some people have had problems launching the game at all with their video hardware (maybe check for issues with your card before you buy). I also occasionally started a mission and had a 20-second hang before things "got going"; and occasionally I would have some sort of issue where the game would run extremely slowly upon loading, and only restarting the game would resolve the issue. I encountered these problems roughly once per hour, but if I have to be perfectly honest, they didn't really bother me because the game in general is just THAT GOOD.
The story-telling is in fully-realized film style. It's clear that this was storyboarded shot for shot. Cuts and transitions, camera angles, and expert animation and voice actor delivery make the story everything it can be. Which, by the way, is in an interesting place: the themes are not "deep", but they are powerful. Scenes are expertly crafted to make you feel the full weight of each situation from start to hard-hitting finish, and I almost never felt "interrupted" by cutscenes, because they were actually worth watching. Fans of disheartened monologues, like those of westerns, Bastion, or Max Payne, will love B.J.'s take on the world. He also keeps these ideas to himself, which creates an interesting contrast between what we know about him and how the other characters interact with him. Overall the storytelling is a bizarre blend of frivolous action-movie fluff and serious, mature themes (and by "mature", I mean heartfelt and grown-up, not "explicit"). And against all expectations, the blend totally works.
They also seem to have gameplay kind of showing off their engine. They can arbitrarily cut pieces out of surfaces (in terms of both visual masking and collision), so they give you a torch that cuts through fences. Then you're drawing circles on fences and, oops, it's too small, let me hack off another piece...
They have really good destruction physics, so they hide random goodies in wooden crates and make the player break them open to get more health and ammo. This engine-oriented design plays to their strengths without being a hamfisted justification of the technology for its own sake. *cough* recent Nintendo games *cough*
So eventually I find myself playing a vehicle section with an overpowered superweapon that mows down wave after wave of enemies effortlessly. At first I thought the game did a 180 on me and went all "generic '00s shooter Call of Duty clone"...
...and then I notice a ♥♥♥♥ing number.
There's a number on my HUD. It represents the integrity of my vehicle. When people shoot me, the number goes down. And when the number goes down, it does not go back up by itself no matter how long I wait.

If you think of this as a standalone game, it's probably more enjoyable. As someone who never played or even heard of the other games in this series before playing The New Order, I found that the game did a great job giving the characters the depth and personality that they apparently lacked in previous games. Anyway, there are a lot of reasons why this game is one of the best I've ever played:
1. The storyline is EPIC. I don't want to give anything away, but in addition to all the nazi-killing, there are about 20 different unique missions that are all incredibly engaging. I doubt that there has ever been a linear video game that allows the player to do this much. Also, people complain that they shouldn't have added a romance aspect to the story, but it's very minor and doesn't make the game any duller. It's all about them actually trying to create actual characters, which I think is admirable.
2. The weapons are innovative. That's right. This is a (alternate) reality-based war game that has unique weapons. Almost every weapon has a dual-weild option. They let you dual weild automatic shotguns. They even rotate the different weapon types (assault rifles, shotguns, pistols) with other variants from mission to mission to keep the game from getting repetitive.
3. The collectibles are fun. There are 50 gold pieces in the game, some of them easy to find, others very well hidden. There are also files all over the place, hundreds  of newspaper clippings about the alternate reality (not to collect, just to read), and even vinyl records to pick up. You can keep track of everything to pick up easily and always go back and find it if you miss it.
4. Boss fights. There are lots of boss fights and lots of different types of bosses. They bring the right amount of challenge to the game without just piling on enemy after enemy like most games.
5. They implement stealth tactics well. You can either go out guns ablazing or take out enemies stealthily. Both methods are preferred at different moments in the game and both are very fun to do.
6. Graphics. It's a 40 gig game in 2014. Obviously the graphics are going to be fantastic.
7. Cinematic aspect. There are lots of cutscenes that seamlessly tie the missions together. Dialogue and facial expressions are both excellent in these cutscenes and it makes you feel like you're playing through a movie...in a good way.
8. Bugs. I've played through almost all of the game and I've had one actual bug show up: a temporary freeze-and-unfreeze that happened a few times over a five-minute stretch. Otherwise, the game is very polished.
9. The health and armor system is as good as any other system I've seen.
10. This can be a hard-core, intense game if you really commit to it. The series has been called shallow in the past, but this installment has plenty of depth and creativity if you care to see it. There's more to it than just killing Nazis.
Cons:
Screen tearing. Constant through the game. Worst in the cutscenes. Vsync doesn't work. Who knows? Maybe they'll fix it in a patch or something.
That's it. I can't think of a single thing wrong with this game apart from the screen tearing. Every mission is fun. Every weapon is useful. Every enemy is hateable. Every ally is likeable. Every boss is challenging. Every collectible is satisfying. Get the game. It's a 9.5/10. Without screen tearing its a perfect 10.

With Dirty Bomb, you get what you pay for (and it's free).
It isn't perfect but it is a fun game to play.
Yes, there are some balance issues and there isn't much depth to the characters like in Overwatch and there's no real customization ability to weapons or loadouts.
Regardless, it is a smooth running, action packed game that is only in beta.
Knowing that, changes are bound to come in the future to advance the game so no difinitive conclusions can be made now.
Many people say it's a pay-to-win game or a grind fest. Both are false. I haven't spent any money at all and I've had no trouble doing well at it. And once you play you can easily see the best ways to collect credits (missions) and level up (badges) which only get easier as you get better at the game. With that in mind, there's no hardcore grinding even necessary.
I usually play a few times a day to do the missions and can easily make 10,000 credits daily. Considering mercs only cost 50,000 credits, you can unlock them easily.
If it were a paid game I'd see where the issues lie but it's free and because of that it's a great game to try out.
Word of advice, though. There really is no need to spend money on this game unless you want a very specific loadout card which is pointless because they don't really make the game easier for you.
Regarding the DLC, same rule applies. DONT GET IT.
Down and Dirty Starter pack gives you 50,000 credits, 2 elite cases, and a credit booster (which could only last for 3 hours). Like I said before, you can easily make 50,000 credits. With that in mind, it is definitely NOT with $30.
Fire and Light Pack gives you two mercs permanently unlocked. It's not as bad as the one above, but still not worth it since you can get them easily just by doing your missions to earn credits.
I say not to spend money because THE MORE MONEY YOU SPEND IN A GAME, THE MORE YOU EXPECT FROM IT. That rule applies to just about all games and considering this one isn't perfect, best not pour your money into it.
Long review but should be helpful if you are thinking of investing some time in it.

Overall a damn solid shooter, better than I was expecting, but I bought it at 30 bucks--I don't think I'd have paid 60 for it due to the length.
Combat's solid--enemies are decently intelligent in groups, and the weapons were varied enough that I did have to think about what the right tool for the job was; weapon-switching interface could use some work, though. Many levels encourage stealth but it's not really a requirement--I was quite satisfied with either sneaking up and gutting guards with a knife or busting into a room with an assault rifle in each hand and lighting the place up.
The game looks really good, especially the environment design--some of the later levels are really impressive, and definitely a breath of fresh air compared to the gritty greybrown levels of so many other shooters. Spot-on story, presented intelligently--not so little that it seems forced, not so much that it upstages the combat.
As far as complaints, the difficulty settings seemed a bit lazy. I played on the second-highest difficulty ("I Am Death Incarnate!") and it just seemed like enemies had more health than they were supposed to and did more damage than they were supposed to--it did mean I couldn't Rambo through rooms constantly, but it felt like I died all but instantly if I was out of armor. Made fights more difficult, to be sure, but in a tedious way; I wish I had played on the Normal difficulty, just for a more streamlined experience. Beyond that, I found that checkpoints were a bit too few and far between in some levels, making for some obnoxious restarts, especially when there were a few bugs that caused me to get stuck in map geometry and be unable to move until I restarted. Lastly, I felt like some of the the non-combat levels were stretched out for the sake of padding. I don't mind having non-combat levels for a change of pace and/or character development opportunities, I totally respect that they wanted to actually do a legitimate story, and they really delivered on that, but too many of those levels would result in needless detours through sewers for no real reason--it felt like the result of somebody on the dev team mandating that every level must be at least twenty minutes long, even if there were only five minutes of actual content.
Oh, and to save you some trouble: every level has about a bazillion hidden collectibles, but most of them literally do nothing--they're only there for completion's sake. The only collectibles that actually do anything are the Codes, which unlock alternate difficulty settings (like "Max difficulty, only one life"); if you only plan on playing through the game once, you can skip all the collectibles without missing out on anything.
Those complaints aside, I did enjoy the game, and would recommend it to anybody interested, but grab it on sale.

Where to start... There is a LOT to be said about this game. Mostly good things, don't worry.
About the game and story:
Wow... I loved the game. The story is very strong, and I love how the game combines action, humor and romance. It's also a perfectly challenging game that really puts all of B.J's skills to the test.
I almost couldn't stop playing once I started, and within two days I had finished the game (and I don't usually like to finish the games that quickly).
The strong story really made me feel like "Okay, this is what I'm fighting for, Ima put my life on the line and I love it" and that got me really motivated to slay all those nazis and get past the obstacles. And it's not only endless fighting, there are also fun and joyful moments, which kept me going.
Also I'm very picky when it comes to games, but this definitely makes my list of top 5 best games ever!
About the marketing of the game:
I truly got my eyes opened to this game after the actual release. But I emidiately thought this is a game I could possibly like. As I watched more trailers and also videos of some gameplay, I knew I would love to try it out!
The only hesitation I had was the fact that "minimun requirements" were set really high, requiring a PC with with Intel Core i7 and a fairly new graphics card.. My PC was built in 2011, and I don't get that many FPS in most games, so the high requirements were a huge turn-off for me, not knowing if it would be a waste of money if I shouldn't be able to even run the game.
Finally I decided to buy the game anyway since it was on sale.
And to my suprise I've been able to run the game fine from the very beginning, not lowering settings. Never had troubes launching or lag, it just runs very smoothly.
I'm on a PC with Intel core i5-2500 @ 3.30 GHz (4 cores) and a pretty old graphics card; AMD Radeon HD 5670.
So I really had my doubts, but it ran fine! Okay, I'm definitely not close to this games ideal 60 FPS (rather half of that), but I think at least the "minimum requirements" should be changed to "recommended specs", since minimum sounds as if it's not possible to run the game if you dont meet these requirements, which clearly it is.
About the ending of the game (*SPOILERS* DON'T CONTINUE READING IF YOU DIDN'T FINISH THE GAME):
I don't fancy games that leaves you wondering "what happened?" and where you have to imagine the actual outcome for yourself.
I also don't like games where you've become really attatched to the character you play as, and it ends with that character or even hero getting killed/dying "for the greater good".
However, I think the first example is acceptable if the game will be followed by another game picking up where the first one ended.
And I really hope that will be the case for Wolfenstein: TNO!
B.J. could have been saved and a new fight against the nazis could begin.
Like Anya said "Believe it" I will believe that this game wasn't the end of B.J's story and that we will eventually continue his quest in a new game.

Wolfenstein:TNO is like a 90s shooter, but it has nods to modern conveniences. Like, if you take insignificant damage, it regenerates back, and you always regen to at least 20 health so you never die in one tiny hit; but it has actual health, which is really fun; it keeps you avoiding damage even if you know you can easily win one specific trade, and it keeps the tension high when health is low.
This is also probably the most impressed I've been with a shooter engine since Far Cry. I think this represents a real turning point in 3D games. It's not that this engine can do anything that others can't, it's how it manages to milk every last ounce of performance out of my hardware to make it look better than seems hypothetically possible on my computer. I think this is the future: anyone nowadays can pack an engine full of more fancy lighting physics than a $1000 graphics card can ever handle; the new frontier is doing things more efficiently with what consumers actually have in their house.
That said, there are some engine issues. Some people have had problems launching the game at all with their video hardware (maybe check for issues with your card before you buy). I also occasionally started a mission and had a 20-second hang before things "got going"; and occasionally I would have some sort of issue where the game would run extremely slowly upon loading, and only restarting the game would resolve the issue. I encountered these problems roughly once per hour, but if I have to be perfectly honest, they didn't really bother me because the game in general is just THAT GOOD.
The story-telling is in fully-realized film style. It's clear that this was storyboarded shot for shot. Cuts and transitions, camera angles, and expert animation and voice actor delivery make the story everything it can be. Which, by the way, is in an interesting place: the themes are not "deep", but they are powerful. Scenes are expertly crafted to make you feel the full weight of each situation from start to hard-hitting finish, and I almost never felt "interrupted" by cutscenes, because they were actually worth watching. Fans of disheartened monologues, like those of westerns, Bastion, or Max Payne, will love B.J.'s take on the world. He also keeps these ideas to himself, which creates an interesting contrast between what we know about him and how the other characters interact with him. Overall the storytelling is a bizarre blend of frivolous action-movie fluff and serious, mature themes (and by "mature", I mean heartfelt and grown-up, not "explicit"). And against all expectations, the blend totally works.
They also seem to have gameplay kind of showing off their engine. They can arbitrarily cut pieces out of surfaces (in terms of both visual masking and collision), so they give you a torch that cuts through fences. Then you're drawing circles on fences and, oops, it's too small, let me hack off another piece...
They have really good destruction physics, so they hide random goodies in wooden crates and make the player break them open to get more health and ammo. This engine-oriented design plays to their strengths without being a hamfisted justification of the technology for its own sake. *cough* recent Nintendo games *cough*
So eventually I find myself playing a vehicle section with an overpowered superweapon that mows down wave after wave of enemies effortlessly. At first I thought the game did a 180 on me and went all "generic '00s shooter Call of Duty clone"...
...and then I notice a ♥♥♥♥ing number.
There's a number on my HUD. It represents the integrity of my vehicle. When people shoot me, the number goes down. And when the number goes down, it does not go back up by itself no matter how long I wait.
This game is ♥♥♥♥ing awesome.

If you think of this as a standalone game, it's probably more enjoyable. As someone who never played or even heard of the other games in this series before playing The New Order, I found that the game did a great job giving the characters the depth and personality that they apparently lacked in previous games. Anyway, there are a lot of reasons why this game is one of the best I've ever played:
1. The storyline is EPIC. I don't want to give anything away, but in addition to all the nazi-killing, there are about 20 different unique missions that are all incredibly engaging. I doubt that there has ever been a linear video game that allows the player to do this much. Also, people complain that they shouldn't have added a romance aspect to the story, but it's very minor and doesn't make the game any duller. It's all about them actually trying to create actual characters, which I think is admirable.
2. The weapons are innovative. That's right. This is a (alternate) reality-based war game that has unique weapons. Almost every weapon has a dual-weild option. They let you dual weild automatic shotguns. They even rotate the different weapon types (assault rifles, shotguns, pistols) with other variants from mission to mission to keep the game from getting repetitive.
3. The collectibles are fun. There are 50 gold pieces in the game, some of them easy to find, others very well hidden. There are also files all over the place, hundreds  of newspaper clippings about the alternate reality (not to collect, just to read), and even vinyl records to pick up. You can keep track of everything to pick up easily and always go back and find it if you miss it.
4. Boss fights. There are lots of boss fights and lots of different types of bosses. They bring the right amount of challenge to the game without just piling on enemy after enemy like most games.
5. They implement stealth tactics well. You can either go out guns ablazing or take out enemies stealthily. Both methods are preferred at different moments in the game and both are very fun to do.
6. Graphics. It's a 40 gig game in 2014. Obviously the graphics are going to be fantastic.
7. Cinematic aspect. There are lots of cutscenes that seamlessly tie the missions together. Dialogue and facial expressions are both excellent in these cutscenes and it makes you feel like you're playing through a movie...in a good way.
8. Bugs. I've played through almost all of the game and I've had one actual bug show up: a temporary freeze-and-unfreeze that happened a few times over a five-minute stretch. Otherwise, the game is very polished.
9. The health and armor system is as good as any other system I've seen.
10. This can be a hard-core, intense game if you really commit to it. The series has been called shallow in the past, but this installment has plenty of depth and creativity if you care to see it. There's more to it than just killing Nazis.
Cons:
Screen tearing. Constant through the game. Worst in the cutscenes. Vsync doesn't work. Who knows? Maybe they'll fix it in a patch or something.
That's it. I can't think of a single thing wrong with this game apart from the screen tearing. Every mission is fun. Every weapon is useful. Every enemy is hateable. Every ally is likeable. Every boss is challenging. Every collectible is satisfying. Get the game. It's a 9.5/10. Without screen tearing its a perfect 10.

Not really a wolfenstein game, but it's still really good.
I give it a 7/10
+Great graphics & effects (bloody as hell)
+Fun gameplay
+Long campaign, took me about 9 hours to complete (Also has an alternate timeline, depending on your choices, but it is basically the same story)
+Good story
+Cool cutting mechanic for the laser gun thing
+Character development of Blazkowicz fits his Nazi killing style
+Good AI
+Easter egg where you get to play the first level of Wolfenstein 3D, sucky graphics and all, but with the new weapons.
-Due to the long campaign it can get repetitive at times
-Doesn't feel like a Wolfenstein game, too much duel weilding mayhem
-Forced fighting in some levels, instead of being able to use stealth
-No multiplayer
-Can no longer kick things above head
-Story seems a little far fetched at times (such as the badass grandparents hell bent on killing nazis, which makes no sense at all)
-Story has a lot of unnecessary slow moments (finding lost toys, cutting a chunk of moldy brick, falling into a sewer)
-The weapons I liked the most were only in the game for the first mission and never used again (Thompson sub-machine gun)
-60 bucks is a lot to ask for a singleplayer only game
-Textures load slowly, but not as bad as Rage
-Low replayability
-43.5 GB file size
I would also like to mention that I played this game on the lowest graphics settings, using a Radeon HD 6850, which is the graphics card listed on the minimum requirements. It ran at around 50-60 FPS, but looked like absolute crap (as expected for low graphics). Textures also loaded very slow when doing a quick spin, sometimes certain textures took 5-6 seconds to load.
I bought it for 30 dollars in the summer sale, and I believe it was worth that price. However, I would not recommend it for the current price of 59.99.

This is delicious vintage 90s RTS. Get it if you like Warcraft II or Starcraft.
A few things that stand out to me in AOEIIHD. The first is massive groups of units, the second is how they can be crushed with very effective area of effect attacks. The gameplay itself is very fast-paced and challenging; if you're finding yourself waiting around when playing you aren't playing right: this game will challenge you to complete as many actions as possible as quickly as possible. The maps have a good variety and unique challenges for the players.
The game includes a non-military victory option, wherein you build a "wonder" and a timer counts down from 250. I have mixed feelings about this mechanic. On one hand it gives a "multiple routes to victory" flavor like the Civilization series, but on the other hand it encourages a very defensive playstyle, which might work against the AI, but will leave you very poorly prepared for multiplayer matches, which are still very popular. Did I mention resource gathering and management is constant and frantic? It is and it's awesome.

This is still one of my favorite casual fps games to play. There are a good variety of mercs and I find the game balancing to be pretty good (the devs constantly working on the balancing the mercs, weapons and gameplay).
I really like the selection of both female and male mercs who all have a "cheekiness" about them. They all have distinctive sounds and catch phrases which I find quite amusing. The sound is also spot on. You can always hear clearly what direction a sound is coming from.
I have found that this game has alot more teamwork going on when compared to other fps games.. just my opinion.
The graphics are good but the responsiveness is even better! Playing a smaller, faster mercs, like Proxy really shows off how responsive this game is.... So much joy to be had from running and gunning, jumping off walls and smashing skulls with cricket bats lol
Dirty Bomb can be tough when first starting out as the damage takes a bit of getting used to (it takes quite a few shots to kill someone depending on the character/merc). Don't let this phase you as this is part of the games cheekiness! It encourages team play so don't feel you have to get a load of kills to find success.
After 265 hours of game play and also the purchase of the down n dirty starter pack I have all the mercs that I want along with a silver load out card for each merc that I own.
For Players wondering about "the grind" (the effort it takes to purchase new mercs and load out cards). I would say that its not too bad. You are given objectives every 3-4 hours to help you earn the credits you need to buy more mercs and of course if the grind id not for you then there is always the option to purchase whatever you want with real money.
Personally, I struggle to see how people can find fault with this free to play game. It delivers on what it promises.. it knows it limits.. not overambitious... just as straight up fun and cheeky little game.

PS2 is a great game, and I highly recommend it, if you've got a strong enough PC to play it smoothly.  Been playing on and off for the past couple of years, not on Steam (I had 389 hours in on the Miller European server before I switched to the U.S. West Coast server, for a grand total of 418 as of this writing).
A big thing for me is that the player base tends to be considerably more decent than that of a lot of other competitive shooter-type MMOs I've played.  And DBG seems to be really on top of hackers and cheaters lately.  They tend to announce in-game when they've booted a cheater; I recently saw a broadcast message to all players a few sessions ago that "Ding Dang Dong has been Bing Bang Banned for cheating."  I guess the guy's name was that, or something like that, and the admin online was feeling frisky.  Got a kick out of that.  Anyway.
But, of course, the real kick of the game is the massive battles involving 100-150 players, with bombers and fighters sparring overhead as the tanks and sundies (troop transports/mobile spawn points) roll across the battlefield amid the blips of players on foot.  It really accomplishes something there, and the feel is great.
As with any free-to-play game, progression is painfully slow if you don't spend *some* money on the game to get a few important goodies, like a heavy pistol, anti-aircraft guns for your MAX and light tank, and some heavier weaponry for your heavy tank, but the beginning weapons are noted as being competitive.  In all honesty, I really don't know if I'd continue to enjoy the game nearly as much if I'd never spent a cent on it (and I've been pretty cheap -- we're on a tight budget, so I've spent $30 total on it), but I suppose it's a matter of patience.
I can say, though, that if you can, the game is worth the money you'll spend on it.
Unless you're on a Core 2 Duo or something.  In that case, just...  no.  You're going to be very frustrated with this.  I am not sure -- I think they have optimized it better, but it is still very heavy-feeling, at least on our 4GB core 2 duo clunker.
Those caveats aside, it's a great game, and I highly recommend it.

2. The concept of the story is awesome, but I don't think they have fully used its potential. SPOILER ALERT! SPOILER ALERT! All you do is: fight in the war for a little bit -> wake up and fight to get to a prison and help prisoners escape -> kill the boss. That's the way the game feels, and once again this is not satisfying enough for such an expensive game.
3. Things are too clearly shown in the game. It should be a challenge to find an exit, or certain items, so please don't buy this game if you are looking for a FPS/puzzle-ish kind of game. Everything is clearly highlighted and there is absolutely no fun in searching for anything.
4. The game is too short. It's as simple as that. I finished the campaign in 8 hours, and I suppose that is mostly because of me not searching for collectables, but I didn't feel the need to find them as there wouldn't be that big of a challenge in it.
Final judgement
Don't buy this game. I bought it during the summer sale for 25 euro's and if there was a way to get my money back, I would. It is just not worth it, it's too short, there's no challenge in finding anything etc. Sure, the graphics, storyline and fighting itself are awesome but not exceptional for a modern-day FPS game and therefore I do not judge this game as worthy of its price. Value for money to me is a 4/10.
Buy this for yourself and once you beat it buy copy for a friend and enjoy more in co-op.

Wolfenstein. What more is there to say about it? The game is thrilling from start to end.
Shall I elaborate?
The combat in Wolfenstein: The New Order may seem like your average triple A shooter, but it's not. It's better. It flows seemlessly from stealth to gunplay and to hectic firing and hope you hit things. Every stage there are usually more ways than one to reach your objective. Whether it's storm in through the front doors and just introduce the inhabitants of the room to your bullet spittin' pals or take a hidden airduct and introduce everyone to your knife friend with a fond hug.
The story however, is where this game shines. There's no multiplayer (thank God) so more fuel for the developers to make an engaging story for once. The entire story campaign was a wonderful take on alternative history and immersing yourself isn't that hard. Think a bit during the game and sometimes, some things make a whole lot more sense than the other things.
The soundtrack is also fantastic. It's not music that's out of place like some rock song as you are driving along a linear river to your destination. It fits the era well and what else is there to say about it?
It's a fairly large expansive game that rewards those well for exploring the environments from top to bottom. Those who treat it like a linear shooter miss out on a lot more than just upgrades.
It may be a 40GB download, but it's a fantastic download. It's a fantastic download that will leave you wanting more and as someone who is sick and tired of the concept of DLCs, would benefit more from more Nazi stabbin' fun in the future. It's definitely a favourite of mine and probably one of my or is already the best game of 2014.
Advice for AMD users though:
make sure you have AMD 14.4 Catalyst installed. It's so handy and a lot less stressful on your AMD card. Tried playing without it installed (cause I'm smart like that) and I did not make it past the starting cutscene cause it was too heavy to render.

PS2 is a great game, and I highly recommend it, if you've got a strong enough PC to play it smoothly.  Been playing on and off for the past couple of years, not on Steam (I had 389 hours in on the Miller European server before I switched to the U.S. West Coast server, for a grand total of 418 as of this writing).
A big thing for me is that the player base tends to be considerably more decent than that of a lot of other competitive shooter-type MMOs I've played.  And DBG seems to be really on top of hackers and cheaters lately.  They tend to announce in-game when they've booted a cheater; I recently saw a broadcast message to all players a few sessions ago that "Ding Dang Dong has been Bing Bang Banned for cheating."  I guess the guy's name was that, or something like that, and the admin online was feeling frisky.  Got a kick out of that.  Anyway.
But, of course, the real kick of the game is the massive battles involving 100-150 players, with bombers and fighters sparring overhead as the tanks and sundies (troop transports/mobile spawn points) roll across the battlefield amid the blips of players on foot.  It really accomplishes something there, and the feel is great.
As with any free-to-play game, progression is painfully slow if you don't spend *some* money on the game to get a few important goodies, like a heavy pistol, anti-aircraft guns for your MAX and light tank, and some heavier weaponry for your heavy tank, but the beginning weapons are noted as being competitive.  In all honesty, I really don't know if I'd continue to enjoy the game nearly as much if I'd never spent a cent on it (and I've been pretty cheap -- we're on a tight budget, so I've spent $30 total on it), but I suppose it's a matter of patience.
I can say, though, that if you can, the game is worth the money you'll spend on it.
Unless you're on a Core 2 Duo or something.  In that case, just...  no.  You're going to be very frustrated with this.  I am not sure -- I think they have optimized it better, but it is still very heavy-feeling, at least on our 4GB core 2 duo clunker.
Those caveats aside, it's a great game, and I highly recommend it.
