As someone who's never played the older Wolfenstein games, I came into this expecting a blood soaked, kill 'em all that relies on old school mechanics in a modern game. What I didn't expect was probably the best AAA game to come out this year, and one of the few games that I started over as soon as I finished because I still wanted more. Aside from being visually stunning, the combat is smooth and engaging, the soundtrack is flawless and every character you meet both sounds and behaves like a real person, something most shooters, and games in general don't quite get. Another huge plus in it's favor are it's handling of cinematics. While most games will cut the action out of nowhere and make you watch your character do cool things, Wolfenstien's cinematics only activate when you trigger them, and the game makes it clear when your action will do so. In addition, if Blaskowicz is going to do anything of importance, the game will cut back to first person and let you do it. Perhaps the biggest part, is when a scene ends instead of having everyone standing in static positions, all characters will be continuing the same movements they were doing during the cut scene, adding a new layer of believeablity that you won't find in most first person games.
My only complaints towards the game is the huge download size and the fact that Blazkowicz whispers constantly, but both are inconsequential in comparison to the rest of the game.

In this game, as you can see, you build robots and send them into battle. That seems easy enough, but there is a lot of depth into building. During building, there are three compulsory item types you need to place on your robot. Cubes for the structure, movement parts for moving around and haardware that range from offensive to defensive items. Optional items are in the speacial and cosmetic categories that range from modules to give you special abilities, radars and recievers for you to know about enemy position, jammers to counter radars, and cosmetics which make you look cool.
Some nice things you can build are:
Planes equipped with plasma launchers aka plasma bombers to bomb ground enemies
Rail walkers/tanks if you really want to be that guy who camps at a cliff
A swiss army knife mech full of weapons, modules and backup rotor blades for it to fly
There are 4 gamemodes in this game which are:
Elimination: Either cap the enemy base or kill all the bad guys. Like world of tanks
Battle arena: Destroy the enemy crystal while protecting yours. Capture all the towers to deactivate the           enemy shield. Similar to mobas
TDM: Your team has to kill the target number of enemies first to win
The pit: Without teammates, you need to reach 20 points to win by getting kills
Economy in this game works differently. Instead of getting credits after a match, you get a crate. The crates all have grade which in order from worst to best are:
Rusted, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Diamond, Protonium
Better crates give you better items. Rarity is classified in 5 grades which are:
Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary
These are what items are in which rarity
Common items are blocks
Uncommon items are low tier weapons, movement systems, radars, recievers and some cosmetics
Rare items are Rods, Helium, Mid tier weapons, movement systems, radars, recievers and some cosmetics
Epic items are Struts, High tier weapons, movement systems, radars, recievers and speedo/altimeters
Legendary items are Giant wheels, hover blades, mech legs, Weapons like the Aeroflak Guardian, Missile launcher, Ion Distorter, and all the modules
The update which released the crates infuriated many people in the community and people has complained about the game being pay to win. Freejam took steps to improve them. About the game being pay to win,it is not. Th robocraft, there are no such things as paid items that you cannot get/unlock without paying a single cent. This game is pay to skip and not pay to win.
Robocraft has a wide variety of weapons to choose from, each of them meant for different playstyles. You used to only be able to put one type of weapon on your robot. However, now, you can place up to 6 types on one robot. Modules also take up a weapon slot. The weapons and modules available are:
Lasers/SMGs: Like rifles
Plasma: Explosive cannons
Rails: Sniper rifles
Nanos: Medi guns
Tesla: Point blank highly damaging melee weapons
Flak: Anti air cannons
Ion: Shotguns deadly at point blank range and useless at mid to long ramge
LOML: Look at an enemy for 2.5 secs, and fire the missiles
CSH: Spin up miniguns which fires at great speed
DSM: Forms a temporary shield at the shape of a disc to block all fire
BLM: Think Tracer's blink from overwatch
EMP: Target an area to EMP, robots caught in the area will be stunned if they get hit
Power Module: Refills all of your power
GHM: Cloaks you but drains power over time when cloaked
Overall, this game is easy to play at first but needs lots of building skill to build functional robots and good targeting in battle as you need to find the enemy robot weakspots to shred them quick.

I did not know what to expect of this game when I bought it. I hadn't played the previous Wolfenstein games, but the game looked awesome and most of the reviews I read were really positive. So I started playing, and I wasn't disappointed. The graphics look awesome, there's no denying that. The storyline couldn't have been better, agreed. But then we get to the negative part of the game.
1. It feels like you spend more time watching cutscenes than actually playing the game. There's way too little action and gameplay for a 50 euro game.
2. The concept of the story is awesome, but I don't think they have fully used its potential. SPOILER ALERT! SPOILER ALERT! All you do is: fight in the war for a little bit -> wake up and fight to get to a prison and help prisoners escape -> kill the boss. That's the way the game feels, and once again this is not satisfying enough for such an expensive game.
3. Things are too clearly shown in the game. It should be a challenge to find an exit, or certain items, so please don't buy this game if you are looking for a FPS/puzzle-ish kind of game. Everything is clearly highlighted and there is absolutely no fun in searching for anything.
4. The game is too short. It's as simple as that. I finished the campaign in 8 hours, and I suppose that is mostly because of me not searching for collectables, but I didn't feel the need to find them as there wouldn't be that big of a challenge in it.
Final judgement
Don't buy this game. I bought it during the summer sale for 25 euro's and if there was a way to get my money back, I would. It is just not worth it, it's too short, there's no challenge in finding anything etc. Sure, the graphics, storyline and fighting itself are awesome but not exceptional for a modern-day FPS game and therefore I do not judge this game as worthy of its price. Value for money to me is a 4/10.

Wolfenstein. What more is there to say about it? The game is thrilling from start to end.
Shall I elaborate?
The combat in Wolfenstein: The New Order may seem like your average triple A shooter, but it's not. It's better. It flows seemlessly from stealth to gunplay and to hectic firing and hope you hit things. Every stage there are usually more ways than one to reach your objective. Whether it's storm in through the front doors and just introduce the inhabitants of the room to your bullet spittin' pals or take a hidden airduct and introduce everyone to your knife friend with a fond hug.
The story however, is where this game shines. There's no multiplayer (thank God) so more fuel for the developers to make an engaging story for once. The entire story campaign was a wonderful take on alternative history and immersing yourself isn't that hard. Think a bit during the game and sometimes, some things make a whole lot more sense than the other things.
The soundtrack is also fantastic. It's not music that's out of place like some rock song as you are driving along a linear river to your destination. It fits the era well and what else is there to say about it?
It's a fairly large expansive game that rewards those well for exploring the environments from top to bottom. Those who treat it like a linear shooter miss out on a lot more than just upgrades.
It may be a 40GB download, but it's a fantastic download. It's a fantastic download that will leave you wanting more and as someone who is sick and tired of the concept of DLCs, would benefit more from more Nazi stabbin' fun in the future. It's definitely a favourite of mine and probably one of my or is already the best game of 2014.
Advice for AMD users though:
make sure you have AMD 14.4 Catalyst installed. It's so handy and a lot less stressful on your AMD card. Tried playing without it installed (cause I'm smart like that) and I did not make it past the starting cutscene cause it was too heavy to render.

Another great game from Rockstar. Max is back and miserable as ever. Graphics are lush, though you may get a bit of a headache with all the blurring in and out, and the dizzying CRT interlacing-style transitions (you'll know when you see them). Sometime we just want to stare at the visuals without all the fancy special effects!
The mechanics of the game are slightly better from Max Payne 2, namely in using cover. For people who like collectables, you can collect gun parts and make golden guns and act like a detective by finding hidden clues in the story.
However, one aspect of the game made me a little disappointed, though I imagine it was to keep it as realistic as possible when compared to the 'true game world' of Max Payne 2. Bullet time, not the dodge mode, is worse in this game, it runs out too fast and doesn't have the same bonus as 2 by killing people in Bullet time mode to slow time even further. Reloading here doesn't do a fancy twirl with instant replenishment either, a lost chance in my opinion.
Yet, the game makes up for it with last gasp shots to kill someone who felled you, gaining you a bit of life once more. The locations are varied and the story is long enough to get you involved, with plenty of twists and turns, as per the Payne series.
However I really didn't get as emotionally invested in the characters as with the first two games. In fact, I liked the few moments Max was in New Jersey more than other parts of the game. This was a shame, perhaps there were too many characters to like or hate, and not enough time given for them to develop further.
I haven't played the multiplayer yet but if you are interested in frantic gunplay, then this is for you.

Max Payne 3
I'm a huge fan of the Max Payne franchise, I loved the whole dark and gritty feeling, so I was really excited about this game, and I wasn't disappointed at all, I finished it twice because I loved it so much!
and now, I've decided to write a review about it and share my thoughts about this great game!
Story
So, if you don't have a clue about who is Max Payne... you ought to be ashamed!
I'll just start from this game, so, after the last game, Max left the police force and settled in a New Jersey, where he was just drinking himself to death and been haunted by the loss of his family,
one day, while he was drinking a friend finds him in the bar, and offers him a job, to protect a well known family in Rio De Janeiro, Brazil, he accepts the job, and leaves USA to protect the family.
And from here the story twists and turns...
Graphics
The graphics are amazing imo, really good, they've thought of everything (Rockstar), even the smallest details,
the animations are crazy good, the effects of the bullet-time is sweet!... I've nothing to add, really the graphics are sweet!
Gameplay
Max Payne is a third-person shooter, and the first Max Payne where the first to introduce the Bullet-Time feature, and so, it's also in this game, and they've taken the game to the next level,
I mean it, everything, you can jump to each side while the effect is on, you can move from cover to cover, you can blind-fire, and there's also a slow-motion effect when you kill dudes (like Fallout 3, Skyrim etc)... everything you look in a third-person shooter, Max Payne 3 got!
and my favourite one is that when you prone you actually roll over and the player turns 360 degrees to maintain his sight on target, I found that really nice and making me feel like they've thought of everything in the game.
now, I heard from people that actually didn't like the game because of the long cut-scenes, I really don't understand this, cause the game itself is story driven and the cut-scenes are a must!
the story it self is amazing, and the cut-scenes are just like a movie, Rockstar knows how to make this kinda games, from GTA to Red Dead Redemption, L.A. Noire and Max Payne.
I loved the gameplay, it's full of action and fun!
Conclusion
I LOVE THIS GAME!
The game is well built! they've put thought of every small detail, and just made it perfect!
The gameplay is fun and full of action! and I just couldn't get enough of it! the single player is long and delivers a movie-like story, with twists and turns, it took me about 13 hours or so to complete the game,
The graphics are amazing! had no bugs at all, the game worked fluently with no lags at all, and I had GTS 8800 320MB GPU, which wasn't the best at the time I played it.
I can really go on and on praising this game, and I really think the game deserves it, Rockstar made an excellent game, they maintained the feeling of the original games and just made it even better!
If you didn't play this game at all, put it in the top of your list, and if you already played it and stopped, give it another go!
for me, I'm waiting for the next Max Payne to come out, I really hope they're making one :)

First off, as you can see from the decent amount of hours i've wasted on this game, I think it is pretty good.  Many oppurtunites to troll people, many oppurtunites to be trolled, and countless headshots to be made.  That being said, my personal favorite weapon is the AF-8 Railjack.
Now, down to business, this game is amazing, even on its lowest graphics setting.  The gameplay is smooth and there are only about 10 hackers at any given time across the entire game.  Aimbot is nowhere to be found, and ironsights often win the day.  Grenades fly thru window openings just to ricochet off of crates back outside, and even though a MAX is a walking tank, it still get blown up nicely with a pack or two of c4 (or an anti-tank mine).  Side note: took me about a full week to figure out that higby was actually the f word being censored (thank you devs).
Snipers make up about 33% of the total player population, so if you're looking to make some headshots, be prepared to take a few of those yourself.  Light assaults make up the bulk of the initial assault forces, with heavy assaults trailing right behing, with medics and engineers throughout their midst.  MAXes trod along well behind, their bulky armor hindering their maneuverability.  Snipers hang far back while they pick off enemies at a distance (or rush ahead under cloak to lay tank mines ON tanks), all in all an excellent gameplay experience... BUT WAIT!!!
I'm sorry, I forgot about the ONE THING that all Planetside 2 players have in common, the need to be glory hounds.  Yes my fellow comrades, it's completely true, once you get on the battlefield you try to rack up as many kills as possible before dying, sometimes failing to even move an inch before a well placed sniper picks you off as you spawn next to the sundy.  This has lead to many mad attempts at revenge, only to be picked off by auto-turrets and heavy assaults in the process.  Tempers run short and craftiness runs deep as players do everything they can to get an edge for their faction in combat.  Whether it is parking their sundy inside of a defense tower, or perching atop a high-rise plateau to get a sniper's perspective of the battlefield, players are doing whatever they can to make sure that YOU, yes I mean YOU specifically don't make it past their base walls.  Anti-personal mines lay in wait as you cross into the base, detonating and releasing a hailstorm of shrapnel as you press on through.  And that's not even the best part.
Sometimes, if your lucky enough, you'll get put in a galaxy or libby that has a screwup for a pilot who rams into EVERYTHING.  Yeah, I suck at flying as well.  I've been in my share of fails as well, where the pilot miscalculates and rams headfirst into a mountain, or the ground (if he's THAT bad).  Tank to Phalanx Turret combat is extremely frequent, and often ends in silent raging for many.  Also doesn't help when someone with a good aim with turrets (like myself) enters one and starts sniping random enemies from a distance.  Such fun!  Pistols are a core part of the game as well, for who wouldn't gladly switch to a tiny revolver when he guns out of ammo for his big gatling gun?  I sure would, as pistols have saved my life quite a few times.

This is more or less the game Rage wanted to be. It's an interesting story premise, and although it boils down to beefy American war hero vs puppy-killing baby-punting Nazis, that seems pretty intentional. Mechanically it's pretty sound, you can dual-wield damn near anything and rip turrets off their mounts to carry around manually. You do run out of ammo for all your guns remarkably quickly, though, which is both an incentive to keep moving and an easy way to get killed.
For some reason a big element of this Wolfenstein is stealth, which is kind of hit or miss. It usually works when it's supposed to, at least. A good handful of the levels offer you the choice of taking the stealthy route or just running in balls-out with guns blazing, but there are also a few aggravating forced stealth sections and a few largely uninteresting infiltration sections to serve as exposition dumps for the characters.
No really remarkable weapons although a couple nifty ones, a few neat setpieces, much better game than Rage, lasts maybe 10-12 hours, more if you go stealthy or hunt for the extra game mode unlocks. Mostly it's just pretty competent and doesn't ♥♥♥♥ anything up horribly.

The best  Online Shooter on the market even if it's a few years old, the continents in this game are massive, approach enemy bases the way you want, join other people, battles of massive scale almost every time you log in, watch your back contantly or get headshot by snipers , there is a nice set of ground and air vehicles, 3 factions, 5 infantry classes + Max robot like armor per faction with unique abilities, a large selection of weapons, a lot of bases scattered around continents.
- Pro -
Huge maps
scifi theme
F2P
Server admins regularly ban hackers/aimbotters
- Cons -
Only one game mode (conquer enemy bases)
Aimbotters and hackers as in every other game
glitches and bugs (not many but it can still be annoying at times)
Unbalanced as hell sometimes  in my opinion (the biggest army always win on the other)
Some features are gamebreaking,enemy spotting is a good example, start shooting or get spotted by an enemy, the entire enemy faction will instantly have an aim to your head, there is no tactical advantage in trying to hide, you have to be lucky. Spotting works even if you don't see target, people can sometimes get spotted through corners and sometimes through  barriers by just spamming q or the key you decide to use for spotting, this function is abused by a lot of players and in my opinion it completely breaks the gameplay, it makes things too easy for the faction spotting the enemy and it ruins the tactical gameplay to the point the game can't be played as a tactical shooter.
Weapons are unbalanced, some people will be able to headshot you with a hand gun from 200m away. Weapons you buy get nerfed after a few months so that you are forced to buy a new one, this is my opinion based on experienced, my weapons bought at the beginning don't seem to be as effective as they used to be, however there have been a new damage model patch after release, maybe it affected many weapons
Since they added implants and energy packages the game has become P2W to some extent in my opinion, these implants give you advantages like having enemies on radar regardless you see them or not, Health automatically restored when not hit for some seconds.
The game started great but many new features like implants ruined it, also the physics need rework as well as the enemy spotting machanics which in my opinion should only be for infiltrators and not for the whole faction, too easy to spot an enemy and see your whole faction overkill the enemy , imagine being a soldier and you approach an enemy, this enemy instantly spots you, even if you manage to kill the enemy in front of you , you have to then deal with a whole army that doesn't only know where the fight happened but also the direction you are trying to escape to for many seconds, it makes the gameplay unfair and stupid, even a noob will be able to shoot you since you suddenly become a huge red and white arrow on the minimap
Verdict : Yes definitely try it out since it's free but I suggest to avoid spending money on it until you are sure you like the game.

Sound 8/10
Gameplay 7/10

Don't try to lonewolf into bases unless you are sure no enemy is around,

To take a game so devoid of plot like Wolfenstein and a character so lacking in depth as B.J. Blazkowicz and create such a fantastic story and cinematic experience is one thing. But the experience itself is action packed, the stealth is tense and fun if you choose that route when available, and the gameplay is just seeped in all the proper elements of old school shooters while utilizing first person in a way I haven't seen any other game do so well.
It took a formerly silent protagonist and breathed life into him, immersing the player in his shoes and surrounding him with characters you'd genuinely care for and antagonists you love to hate. Uber difficulty is challenging, so no worries there if you're looking for a bit of masochism like me. The graphics are breathtaking and the locations vary significantly in this bleak, alternative-history Nazi killing dystopia.
The folks at Machinegames have outdone themselves. They absolutely deserve a chance at a sequel. I for one would be quite happy (and relieved since it seems like it's in development hell) if they went over to id software and helped them out with Doom 4. They know what they're doing, and they delivered a reboot I didn't know I wanted until I played it. 10/10

It's been over a year since the release of Max Payne 3 and I decided to replay the game once again and share a few of my insights. First off, I can definitely say I'd recommend this game, since it carries the very essence of the previous parts of the franchise. The RAGE engine looks gorgeous and making headshots in bullet time is as fun as ever. The game runs pretty darn well on most systems. The storytelling is great and Max's monologues reveal the self-pity he's fighting after the loss of his family. What I did not like is the amount of cutscenes which interupt the fun you're having over and over again. Of course, those who intend to run through the game just once - will find the cutscenes to be a great addition. On the other hand, those, who are planning to complete the game on different difficulty levels, or just hunt for achievements, are bound to watch the unskippable cutscenes. The soundtrack adds up to the memorable shooting sequences and provides a few classy tracks which may find their way into your MP3 player. Conclusion: go get this game, it's worth it! 9/10

I was remarkably impressed by Wolfenstein: The New Order, and not just because my expectations for a Wolfenstein game were set so low that I was willing to settle for an ancient pack of Wolf3D levels on 5.25 floppies unearthed from John Romero's attic for $60. I was impressed because this game actually does interesting things with its characters and world-building - Deathshead believes he's the hero because the Nazis won the war and therefore SCIENCE, and the Resistance characters are actually sympathetic and fun to be around rather than just boring NPCs. It captures that awesome gothic technological feel that I love playing id Software games for. And also Jimi Hendrix is in this game. All of this is enough to keep me from recognizing just how shoe-stringy the actual story progression is. The actual gameplay is standard 'chuck some old-school elements into this new-school cover shooter' gameplay, but it brings back my favorite part of a first-person shooter: Secrets, and the finding thereof. I have a feeling it's going to go over like a damp piece of toilet paper for the hardcore players looking for an actual challenge, because I picked the highest difficulty and died less than fifty times in ten hours, which comes out to less than five deaths an hour. Other than that, Machine Games just created the game that id Software and Raven Software wish they could make. It's not a great game, but it's good and interesting enough.

This is the Wolfenstein game I think many of us have waited a long time for.
The game has so many strengths going for it: amazing music, fantastic voice actors, dialogue that isn't cheesy, and the reason we play such games; solid enjoyable gun-play. I personally think that their devotion to single-player only is what allowed for such a well rounded experience.
I want to get the 'cons' out of the way, as they are few, and really are more quibbles than anything. The story, at points, feels a little rushed. Could have used a little slower pacing. The shotguns, while pretty devestating, sound and feel a bit underwhelming, especially when compared to the assault rifle. Then again, the Brutal Doom mod has set the personal bar in regards to how shotguns should sound.
I think the game blends very well elements of 'old-school shooters' and the current mechanics of todays. The health system is like that of Far Cry 3's: each health 'chunk' (5 in this case, each worth 20 health) regenerates within its own 'chunk'.
I also like how it brings elements of the old-school in regards to the levels. To survive, you need to find health kits, armor, ammo, and so forth. There's also a lot of hidden goodies to find; secrets, as they used to be called. The levels are well varied and nicely designed.
I could go on with all the various nuances with the game, or how many great homages it pays; especially with the final boss. I can't decide between my two favorite moments: dropping acid with Jimi Hendrix, or finding the mattress to have a nightmare, and have it be Wolfenstein 3D.

Have you loved games such as Battlefield or Call of Duty? Well, this game takes both of those contents and adds more. PlanetSide 2 puts you into a literal world of battlefield, you travel from place to place fighting for your different Empires.. Of course there are different Empires, 3 to be exact, the New Conglomerate, Terran Republic, or the Vanu Sovereignty. As choosing one of the races you get through the basic training session and then into the battlefield. You can choose from multiple classes with different specialities, such as a Bolt Action - One Shot One Kill sniper, a Tough - Explosive heavy assualt, a Caring - Healing medic, ect.., and while entering this battlefield and choosing a class, you get many different places to capture and control, you and your teamates must work all together and attack/take over each of these specific places.
What I think is cool about this game is that EVERY shot makes a difference, either it's damaging a player so another could kill that player, throwing a grenade into a room full of light and heavy assualt infantry, or blowing up the first quad that comes into sight. The one shot makes a whole difference into this very game, all you know if that you are killing the player in front of you, while really, your team should be thanking you for making that opening gap to make it into that objective.
This game is very different from most I've ever played before, very interesting, fun, challenging... And very rage filling. But other then that, this game is recommended for anyone who wants a different kind of first person shooter. But remember, Every Shot Counts.

AoE II is a 1999 2D isometric RTS game that marked an era on the RTS genre and this new version, luckily, just revamps it with widescreen/HD patches, a few bugfixes, reworked water/effects and steam workshop integration.
While widescreen/HD graphic support was a must have and there was no actual need for water or effects reworks, steam workshop integration is what makes this new version worth buying.
On the workshop you're able to mod almost every part of the game, this increases even further the decennial longevity of this game. A few examples of currently available steam workshop items are: complete texture packs, water/coast mods, entire campaigns, extremely well made maps, ...
So, game system is exactly how AoE II was, one of the best ones ever among RTS games, extremely balanced and quite various, with slight but substantial differences between civilizations.
Graphic is good, not what you would expect from a 2013 game but strictly speaking about the HD port quality I couldn't think of any way it could have been done better.
Music got some nice remixes, most of them made it sound more "medieval", which as far as I'm concerned it really nice.
In the end I'd say that even at full price (which is maybe 30%~35% more than you may expect from an HD port of a 10+ year old game) I'd recommend buying this game, mostly because of steam workshop integration that really made (and still makes) the difference on my gameplay experience.

A true classic, you need to play it. It’s one of those games where the sequel is better then the original.
Portal 2’s story is better, the puzzles are better, it’s a longer and it’s more polished. It imporves on all of those things, so if you liked the first one, you will enjoy this even more.
In the original game, the story was simple and straightforward. Now there is a little more to it, but I won’t talk to much about it to prevent spoilers. You also get to learn more about Aperture Science's history and an exclusive behind the scenes look on how those darn puzzle rooms are build. All this is topped with a hefty amount of humor.
The puzzles are better, not only are several new mechanics introduces that were not present in the first game, but all those pesky timed puzzles are gone. In the first game I got stuck a few times because you only had this 1.5 second (or less) window to perform several actions in a row, these are no longer there. This is a good thing in my book, because they were a source of frustration in an otherwise excellent game. That’s not to say that the puzzles have become easier, in fact they might even be more complicated because all the newly introduced elements, like the blue, orange and gray gels (they provide different extra capabilities such as speed up, bounce, …) combine those with the portals and you’ve got some crazy puzzle solving to do.
The voice acting is spot on, JK Simons does an excellent job, but so does Merchant as the hopeless hilarious Wheatly and ofcourse Ellen McLain as GlaDOS is as brilliant as she was in the first game.
The graphics are pretty much on the same level as the first game, which is just perfect, I have nothing bad to say about it, they still hold up very well these days, despite being a +5 year old game. Everything does look more polished though, there is at least a lot more going on, making the environment so much more feel alive.
As a PC or SteamOS gamer you cannot miss this game, it is essential gaming material.
Runs like nothing else on Linux/SteamOS and plays very, very well with the Steam Controller. Streaming to the Steam Link is problemless.

I'm actually super impressed with this game. I wasn't expecting as much as I got.
This game took a bold, bold, move, by taking Captain B.J. Blazkowicz, and putting an emotional spin on his character. And you know, amazingly, it worked. The plot here, is that, in 1946, the Allied forces are fighting a losing battle against the invading Axis forces. The Nazi war machine is on the cusp of global victory, under the military leadership as well as technological advancements of General Wilhelm 'Deathshead' Strasse, who is both genius, and sadistic to the extreme. The Allied forces ultimately lose, and the whole world is bent to the will of the Nazi regime. You are Captain B.J. Blazkowicz, who has been comatose since 1946 due to a piece of shrapnel lodged into his brain. You regain your ability to move in the year 1960, after the German army has brought the world to its knees.
Now, the gameplay is pretty archaic, but it's charming. You have a set of roughly 7 weapons you have on hand at all times, and you collect ammo, health, and armor as loot on the ground. It sounds bizarre, in the wake of modern games, but it works well, and I had no real complaints with it. The combat was smooth and fun, and dual wielding all weapons except for the laser cutter is possible. There is no iron sights while dual wielding. This game also is heavy on stealth. It gives you the option to go guns blazing, and risk trigging an alarm and fighting a larger group, or going in quiet, and eliminating you foes one by one. The AI is pretty oblivious, they'll walk past corpses of their comrades like it's a normal happening, but I don't have any other complaints about the AI other than that.
So I've only played through the game once, and apparently, there are two completely different playthroughs, depending on who you save at the beginning, Fergus or Wyatt. I think this is a really interesting thing, and I intend to play it again, to see what changes.
Is this game worth $59.99? No. The story runs at around 8-10 hours, and you can play through it twice, and, unless you wanna go collectible hunting, that's the replay value. But, I got it on sale at $29.99 and it was worth it, I would say.
There were many moments in this game that got me enganged and involved, it's a pretty damn emotional story, regardless of how absurd a lot of the things that happen are. Such as Nazi war robots or cyborg dogs.
I enjoyed it through and through, though. I would suggest this game when it drops price, or if it goes on sale again.

AoE II is a 1999 2D isometric RTS game that marked an era on the RTS genre and this new version, luckily, just revamps it with widescreen/HD patches, a few bugfixes, reworked water/effects and steam workshop integration.
While widescreen/HD graphic support was a must have and there was no actual need for water or effects reworks, steam workshop integration is what makes this new version worth buying.
On the workshop you're able to mod almost every part of the game, this increases even further the decennial longevity of this game. A few examples of currently available steam workshop items are: complete texture packs, water/coast mods, entire campaigns, extremely well made maps, ...
So, game system is exactly how AoE II was, one of the best ones ever among RTS games, extremely balanced and quite various, with slight but substantial differences between civilizations.
Graphic is good, not what you would expect from a 2013 game but strictly speaking about the HD port quality I couldn't think of any way it could have been done better.
Music got some nice remixes, most of them made it sound more "medieval", which as far as I'm concerned it really nice.
In the end I'd say that even at full price (which is maybe 30%~35% more than you may expect from an HD port of a 10+ year old game) I'd recommend buying this game, mostly because of steam workshop integration that really made (and still makes) the difference on my gameplay experience.

Alright, so I waited until completion of the game before making a review on it. While my initial reaction of the game was great, I wanted to play the whole way through before sharing my thoughts.
As my budget was thight, paying 60$ for a new game wasn't very appealing to me so I decided to wait. Recently, as part of the summer sale, the game dropped to a very appealing 30$ (which is insane) so I decided to bite the bullet and OH BOY! am I glad I did.
I don't judge a game based on the value it gives me. With that being said I don't mind paying full price for a single player only game that takes, in this case, around 15 hours to complete. If you only play games to get incredible amount of value (MMOs, online FPS, MOBAs, etc) then you will probaly be disapointed. Sure the game might get a second or even 3rd playthrough out of you but know that you won't be playing this game for more thand 45-50 hours and that's a stretch. If that bothers you then I suggest either avoiding the game or wait for it to drop in price.
For anyone else, Wolfenstein is a really fun and fast paced shooter with old school roots that doesn't take itself seriously while still giving you a good story focused around a handful of interesting characters. The weapons both look and sound amazing and are extremwly satisfaying to use. You have the choice to go either go fully commando and blast your way through a segment and feel like a complete badass with your dual shotguns (I know) or make your way trhough a level as silently possible picking off guards one by one with your knives and silent pistol using the pretty robust stealth system.
Like I said before, the game takes around 15 hours to beat and does warrant atleast a second playthrough in my opinion.
So if you are interested in anyway in this game and have the money to spend, I urge you to buy this game and support a good development team that took a risk in making a great singleplayer only FPS. You won't be disapointed.
Also, I think it's important to inform you that the download size is a gigantic 41gb, so if that's not achievable to you, I suggest looking into buying a physical copy of the game instead.

This game is incredible and is now one of my favourites, heres 5 reasons why
It really is free to play - I cant believe a game this good is completely free to play, i keep expecting to come up against a paywall but there is none. Everything can be achieved without the use of money. Too many games lately are marked as free to play but they put a bunch of paywalls in your way. This is NOT one of them.
This game is completely open world - The map is huge and if you don't like the battle your in, just walk the other direction and you'll find something else going on. Or use instant action to drop right into the battle from orbit.
The visuals are epic - If you can find a moment when your not being shot at, take a look at the landscape, it really is breathtaking, but dont let it destract you. let your guard down too long and you'll get taken out.
The community is really good - I joined a squad at random, no one was yelling or raging like you see in alot of free games, and we were able to coordinate our forces really well.
The battles are absolutely epic - The battles in this game seamlessly transition from fighting in a dense city to fighting in the air in a huge dogfight to fighting on the countryside with tanks, trucks and infantry.
And i do mean seamlessly, I spawned in a research facility which is covered by a large dome, after fighting for about 5 minutes, our team had secured the facility and cleaned up the remaining enemies, but they were flying in from one of their bases. I ran to the launch pad and got in a fighter, i managed to take down their troop transports before they could land but a fighter got behind me and started shooting me down. i ejected with about one second to spare and used my jetpack to slow down and land safely, i took cover in a building and waited for the fighter to leave. I managed to catch up with a tank heading to the next enemy base, he took me back to get my own tank and we fought our way along the road to the next objective. We got to the walls of the base and used the jetpacks to get over. After about 5 minutes of holding the position, 4 people were able to take the base.
This game is awesome and i highly recommend you get it and support the developers if you like it.

I'm actually super impressed with this game. I wasn't expecting as much as I got.
This game took a bold, bold, move, by taking Captain B.J. Blazkowicz, and putting an emotional spin on his character. And you know, amazingly, it worked. The plot here, is that, in 1946, the Allied forces are fighting a losing battle against the invading Axis forces. The Nazi war machine is on the cusp of global victory, under the military leadership as well as technological advancements of General Wilhelm 'Deathshead' Strasse, who is both genius, and sadistic to the extreme. The Allied forces ultimately lose, and the whole world is bent to the will of the Nazi regime. You are Captain B.J. Blazkowicz, who has been comatose since 1946 due to a piece of shrapnel lodged into his brain. You regain your ability to move in the year 1960, after the German army has brought the world to its knees.
Now, the gameplay is pretty archaic, but it's charming. You have a set of roughly 7 weapons you have on hand at all times, and you collect ammo, health, and armor as loot on the ground. It sounds bizarre, in the wake of modern games, but it works well, and I had no real complaints with it. The combat was smooth and fun, and dual wielding all weapons except for the laser cutter is possible. There is no iron sights while dual wielding. This game also is heavy on stealth. It gives you the option to go guns blazing, and risk trigging an alarm and fighting a larger group, or going in quiet, and eliminating you foes one by one. The AI is pretty oblivious, they'll walk past corpses of their comrades like it's a normal happening, but I don't have any other complaints about the AI other than that.
So I've only played through the game once, and apparently, there are two completely different playthroughs, depending on who you save at the beginning, Fergus or Wyatt. I think this is a really interesting thing, and I intend to play it again, to see what changes.
Is this game worth $59.99? No. The story runs at around 8-10 hours, and you can play through it twice, and, unless you wanna go collectible hunting, that's the replay value. But, I got it on sale at $29.99 and it was worth it, I would say.
There were many moments in this game that got me enganged and involved, it's a pretty damn emotional story, regardless of how absurd a lot of the things that happen are. Such as Nazi war robots or cyborg dogs.
I enjoyed it through and through, though. I would suggest this game when it drops price, or if it goes on sale again.
